records.definition_text: to take something in, especially gradually

records.learnerexamples_text: sexual/psychological/mental abuse; The rescued dogs had been victims of physical abuse.; The one side opposes this treatment as an abuse of living creatures while the other side denies any suffering and points at the values of zoos for people.

records.definition_text: the use of a substance in an unsuitable and harmful way or for the wrong purpose

records.definition_text: relating to schools, colleges and universities, or to subjects which involve thinking and studying and not technical or practical skills

records.definition_text: a mark written or printed over a letter to show you how to pronounce it

records.learnerexamples_text: an American accent; He speaks with a broad/heavy/strong Yorkshire accent.; Our teacher is a middle-aged lady with a kind smile and [a] British accent.

records.definition_text: to allow someone to join an organization or become part of a group
records.learnerexamples_text: She's been accepted by two universities.; He was accepted as a full member of the society.; His fellow workers refused to accept him.; When I returned home I check[ed] my mail and I ha[d] a new message from my uncle, saying that the university have accepted me.

records.definition_text: good enough

records.definition_text: to admit that you caused something bad that happened

records.definition_text: the right or opportunity to use or look at something

records.definition_text: the way in which you can enter a place or get to a place
records.learnerexamples_text: disabled access; The only access to the village is by boat.; I think it would be better if you stayed in a small village which has easy access to the city centre.

records.definition_text: to find or see information, especially using a computer
records.learnerexamples_text: You can access the files over the Internet.; We have more time to stay together at home, because we can access [the] internet at home.

records.definition_text: able to be reached or easily got
records.learnerexamples_text: The resort is easily accessible by road, rail and air.; It is very accessible because it is situated in the centre.

records.definition_text: happening by chance

records.definition_text: by chance or by mistake
records.learnerexamples_text: She accidentally knocked over a glass of water.; I accidentally broke one of your vases - the most beautiful one.

records.definition_text: a place where you live or stay

records.definition_text: to go somewhere with someone

records.definition_text: in a way that agrees with

records.definition_text: a written or spoken description of something that has happened

records.definition_text: to change something slightly so that it works better, fits better, or is more suitable

records.definition_text: to change the way you behave or think in order to suit a new situation

records.definition_text: a small change that you make to something so that it works better, fits better, or is more suitable

records.definition_text: when you admire someone or something

records.definition_text: to find someone or something attractive and pleasant to look at

records.definition_text: to respect or approve of someone or something

records.definition_text: the money that you pay to enter a place or an event

records.definition_text: to accept or start to use something new

records.definition_text: legally taken by another family to be looked after as their own child
records.learnerexamples_text: They've got two adopted children and one of their own.

records.definition_text: the process of legally becoming the parents of someone else's child
records.learnerexamples_text: She couldn't have children, so they were considering adoption.

records.definition_text: an amount of something, often something unpleasant

records.learnerexamples_text: a dose of bad news; You ought to plan your work and mainly learn in the morning when your brain is ready to accept a great dose of knowledge.

records.definition_text: new discoveries and inventions

records.definition_text: modern and well developed

records.definition_text: something good about a situation that helps you

records.definition_text: something that will help you to succeed

records.definition_text: willing to try new and often difficult or dangerous things

records.definition_text: an area containing temporary buildings or tents used for soldiers/prisoners/refugees
records.searchterms_text: an army/prison/refugee etc camp;an army/prison/refugee, etc. camp;army/prison/refugee, etc. camp;camp;camps
records.learnerexamples_text: This year I think I'd rather go to a refugee camp to organise a program for children.

records.definition_text: a very large amount
records.searchterms_text: an awful lot (of sth);an awful lot of sth;awful;awful lot (of sth)
records.learnerexamples_text: It cost an awful lot of money.; First of all, I want to highlight that we see an awful lot of mobile phone[s] in our daily life.

records.definition_text: a relative who lived a long time ago
records.learnerexamples_text: My ancestors came from Ireland.; We are living in a technologically advanced world where we are surrounded by all sorts of devices, which would seem fantastic to our ancestors.

records.definition_text: from a long time ago
records.learnerexamples_text: ancient Greece/Rome/Egypt; ancient monuments/ruins; People have lived in this valley since ancient times.; I would recommend you to visit Rome, because you shouldn't miss [seeing] the huge monuments, the ancient Roman ruins and the Vatican.

records.definition_text: used between two words which are the same to make their meaning stronger
records.learnerexamples_text: She spends hours and hours on the telephone.; The sound grew louder and louder.; We laughed and laughed.; The situation became harder and harder.

records.definition_text: used for saying that other similar things are included or that the whole of a situation is considered
records.learnerexamples_text: He told us about his school and all that.; We decided to stay in bed, with it being a holiday and all that.; I really enjoy shopping for clothes, but not only for clothes, also for things like earrings and all that!

records.definition_text: used for saying that other similar things are included or that the whole of a situation is considered
records.learnerexamples_text: He told us about his school and all that.; We decided to stay in bed, with it being a holiday and all that.; I really enjoy shopping for clothes, but not only for clothes, also for things like earrings and all that!

records.definition_text: a spiritual creature in stories or some religions, usually represented as a human with wings
records.learnerexamples_text: According to the Bible, an angel told Mary that she would have God's son, Jesus.; I like to wear a top with a picture of an angel that my mother bought for me as my birthday present.

records.definition_text: a strong feeling against someone who has behaved badly, making you want to shout at them or hurt them
records.learnerexamples_text: I think he feels a lot of anger towards his father who treated him very badly as a child.; The people showed no surprise or anger at their treatment.; Trisha, who had invited us there, looked like she was about to explode with anger or burst into tears.

records.definition_text: in an angry way
records.learnerexamples_text: "Don't do that!" she shouted angrily.; Demonstrators protested angrily following the jury's verdict.; The Prime Minister reacted angrily to claims that he had lied to the House of Commons.; "How dare she do that [to] me?" I thought, angrily.

records.definition_text: anything that lives and moves, including people, birds, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: Are humans the only animals to use language?; I think the human is [an] animal that want[s] to [do] amusing things.

records.definition_text: An animated film is one in which drawings and models seem to move.
records.learnerexamples_text: He makes animated films.; It's a funny animated film about a superhero family.

records.definition_text: an animated film, or the process of making animated films
records.learnerexamples_text: a course in computer animation; It's a comedy animation about penguins.

records.definition_text: the joint between the foot and the leg, or the thin part of the leg just above the foot
records.learnerexamples_text: I fell over and sprained/twisted my ankle.; I have broken my ankle and I need to stay in bed during the day.

records.definition_text: the day on which an important event happened in a previous year
records.learnerexamples_text: We always celebrate our wedding anniversary with dinner in an expensive restaurant.; Tomorrow is the fiftieth anniversary of the revolution.; She and her husband are touring Europe for a second honeymoon, [on the] 10th anniversary of their marriage.

records.definition_text: to tell people about something officially or with force or confidence
records.learnerexamples_text: The Prime Minister has just announced that public spending will be increased next year.; The company has announced plans to open six new stores.; After dinner, they announced the winner of the competition.; [The] TV has just announced a bus-drivers strike for tomorrow morning.

records.definition_text: something that someone says officially, giving information about something
records.learnerexamples_text: The President made an unexpected announcement this morning.; I heard about this club in [a] radio announcement.

records.definition_text: to make someone angry
records.learnerexamples_text: Tim really annoyed me in the meeting this morning.; I'm sorry - is my cough annoying you?;  It annoys me that she just expects us to help.;  It really annoys me when people expect me to tip as well as pay a service charge in a restaurant.; My bed makes a loud noise when I lie down on it. It annoys me.

records.definition_text: angry
records.learnerexamples_text: I was so annoyed with him for turning up late.; He was annoyed at the way she tried to take over the whole meeting.; My parents were rather annoyed (that) I hadn't told them about the accident.; She was annoyed to discover that her husband had taken her car keys.; I was a bit annoyed when I [found out], but it's all right.

records.definition_text: making you feel annoyed
records.learnerexamples_text: It's really annoying when a train is late and there's no explanation.; He's got a really annoying laugh.; Do you like going shopping with your mom? They are sometimes annoying, aren't they?

records.definition_text: happening once every year, or relating to a period of one year
records.learnerexamples_text: an annual event/visit/holiday; annual income/salary; I never miss the annual sale at the department store near my place.

records.definition_text: once every year
records.learnerexamples_text: Your starting salary is £28,000 per year and will be reviewed annually.; Dear Mr Benson, I am writing with regard to your letter, in which you asked me to give you some pieces of advice for the special events which take place in the College annually.

records.definition_text: a way of solving a problem
records.learnerexamples_text: It's a difficult situation and I don't know what the answer is.; So what's the answer to the problem?; There's no easy answer to the problem.; Should wild animals be kept in cages, and denied their freedom so that we can have the pleasure of watching them [in] zoos? Well, there's no simple answer to that question.

records.definition_text: to write or say something as a reply to a question in a test, exercise, competition, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: I couldn't answer the last three questions.; That was to be my first interview, and I had never before answered a test of personality so I felt insecure.

records.definition_text: a small, black or red insect that lives in groups on the ground
records.learnerexamples_text: There were ants crawling all over the ground.; I [have] know[n] Larry since I was five years old and he couldn't hurt an ant, I am sure about it.

records.definition_text: an object that is old, and often rare or beautiful
records.learnerexamples_text: an antique shop; My mother collects antiques.; First we drove to the old city wh[ere] there were lots of different shops [selling] clothes, shoes, antiques, and jewellery.

records.definition_text: old and often rare or beautiful
records.learnerexamples_text: antique furniture; antique silver/jewellery; There's a nice, cosy lobby, with antique furniture and a fireplace.

records.definition_text: several
records.searchterms_text: a number of sth;number;number of sth;numbers
records.learnerexamples_text: There were a number of journalists present at the public meeting.; We've had quite a number of complaints about the programme.; There are a number of errors in your article.

records.definition_text: the feeling of being very worried
records.learnerexamples_text: Children normally feel a lot of anxiety about their first day at school.; That explains his anxiety over his health.; On the other hand, if we consider this statement in general, we could infer that [the] teenage [years are] quite a good time in a person's life, as there is no stress or anxiety that is usually encountered later on in life.

records.definition_text: worried and nervous
records.learnerexamples_text: He's very anxious about his exams.; My mother always gets a bit anxious if we're late.; I saw my sister's anxious face at the window.; I am a bit anxious about my mum's reaction, but I am sure she'll enjoy this party.

records.definition_text: wanting to do something or wanting something to happen
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm anxious to hear her news.; I'm anxious that we get there on time because I don't think there'll be many seats left.; I am very anxious [for you] to tell me what type of competition you managed to win.

records.definition_text: in an anxious way
records.learnerexamples_text: We waited anxiously by the phone.; I am waiting for your reply anxiously.

records.definition_text: used in questions and negatives to emphasize a comparative adjective or adverb
records.learnerexamples_text: Do you feel any better?; I can't walk any faster.; Those trousers don't look any different from the others.; Houses in this area used to be a real bargain, but they're not cheap any more.; This radio isn't any good - I'll have to buy another.

records.definition_text: any person or any people
records.learnerexamples_text: Anybody can join the club and the membership is free.; The competition is open to anybody under the age of 16.; Anybody [could] understand it!

records.definition_text: used to say that something will happen very soon
records.searchterms_text: any day/minute/time etc now;any day/minute/time, etc. now;now
records.learnerexamples_text: We're expecting our second child any day now.; The evil creatures who were bound to come out of the dark [w]ould see Carla any minute now.

records.definition_text: despite that
records.learnerexamples_text: He hates carrots but he ate them anyhow.; It wasn't a great support, but anyhow I consider my choice to be the best I could have [made].

records.definition_text: used when you are returning to an earlier subject
records.learnerexamples_text: Anyhow, as I said, I'll be away next week.; After that we drove for about one hour before we had to take a lunch break. It was still very hot when we continued our trip and we had to stop once more. Anyhow, we [got] to Munich the same day, where we stayed for two days.

records.definition_text: used to give a more important reason for something that you are saying
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't need a car and I can't afford one anyhow.; We both thought that it was a good idea to have that stop-over at your place as it was on our route to Norway anyhow.

records.definition_text: any person or any people
records.learnerexamples_text: Anyone can go - you don't have to be invited.; Anyone could dress well with all that money.; The third programme was a joke competition. Anyone could come there and tell his joke.

records.definition_text: used in questions and negatives to mean 'at all similar to'
records.learnerexamples_text: Does he look anything like his brother?; Even in my dreams I haven't seen anything like it.

records.definition_text: used to give a more important reason for something that you are saying
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't have time to go and anyway it's too expensive.; Of course I don't mind taking you home - I'm going that way anyway.; I'm going to buy a new bed, because the old one has broken, [and] anyway it wasn't very comfortable.

records.definition_text: separated by a space, distance or period of time
records.learnerexamples_text: Stand with your feet wide apart.; How far apart should the speakers be?; We were asked to stand in two lines three metres apart.; I forget the exact age difference between Mark and his brother - they're two or three years apart.; They are situated on the same street, only a hundred metres apart, on each side of the street.

records.definition_text: If two people are apart, they are not in the same place together.
records.learnerexamples_text: By this time my parents were living apart.; I'll always remember those two days which we spent together after such a long time living apart.

records.definition_text: into separate, smaller pieces
records.learnerexamples_text: I took the motor apart to see how it worked.; My jacket is so old, it's coming apart.

records.definition_text: except for or in addition to
records.learnerexamples_text: Apart from the low salary, it's a great job!; He works until nine o'clock every evening, and that's quite apart from the work he does over the weekend.; So, when he started to speak, I couldn't understand anything apart from "thanks".

records.base_text: a pile of/ piles of sth
records.definition_text: a lot of something
records.searchterms_text: a pile of/ piles of sth;pile;pile of/ piles of sth;piles
records.learnerexamples_text: I've got a pile of things to do today.; He's got piles of money.; He was very disappointed, he didn't want to leave but he had to because he had a pile of work waiting for him.

records.definition_text: to tell someone that you are sorry about something you have done
records.learnerexamples_text: I must apologise to Isobel for my behaviour.; Trains may be subject to delay - we apologise for any inconvenience caused.; She apologised for having to leave early.; I'm writing to apologise because I won't be at tomorro[w]'s class.

records.definition_text: something you say or write to say that you are sorry about something you have done
records.learnerexamples_text: I have an apology to make to you - I'm afraid I opened your letter by mistake.; I owe you an apology, Chris.; "Was he at all sorry for what he'd done?" "Oh he was full of apologies."; Hi Zita, Please accept my apology for this belated letter which you're holding in your hands.

records.definition_text: the punctuation mark ' that shows when a letter or a number has been left out, or is used before or after 's' to show possession
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm Ian.; She was born in '65. ; Helen's laugh; Charles' cooking; a baby's hand

records.definition_text: obvious or easy to notice
records.learnerexamples_text: Her unhappiness was apparent to everyone.;  It was becoming increasingly apparent that he could no longer look after himself.; I was on the metro this morning when for no apparent reason the man opposite suddenly screamed.; This was my Dad, always doing weird things for no apparent reason.

records.definition_text: used to say you have read or been told something although you are not certain it is true
records.learnerexamples_text: Apparently it's going to rain today.; Apparently he's had enough of England and is going back to Australia.; Apparently he was planning to visit me and su[r]prise me for my birthday, w[h]ich was the following day.

records.definition_text: used to say that something seems to be true, although it is not certain
records.learnerexamples_text: There were two apparently unrelated deaths.; An eighty-year-old woman was badly hurt in what the police describe as an apparently random attack.; People found it important and still do but apparently, today, we don't appreciate reading as much as our ancestors.

records.definition_text: the quality in someone or something that makes them attractive or interesting
records.learnerexamples_text: sex appeal; Spielberg films have a wide appeal.; Parties on river-boats have lost their appeal since one sank last year.; In my opinion, computer games are so popular because the games have developed their graphics and they have more appeal to youngsters.

records.definition_text: to attract or interest someone
records.learnerexamples_text: Cycling has never really appealed to me.; It's a programme designed to appeal mainly to 16 to 25 year-olds.; In addition, books appeal to our imagination.

records.definition_text: to start to be seen
records.learnerexamples_text: He suddenly appeared in the doorway.; Then a bright light appeared in the sky.; Suddenly the singer of the band appeared.

records.definition_text: to seem
records.learnerexamples_text: He appeared calm and relaxed.;  There appears to be some mistake.; But, [the] reality is, that life appears very short to me.

records.definition_text: to start to exist or become available
records.learnerexamples_text: Laptop computers first appeared in the 1980s.; The story appeared in all the major newspapers.; In almost every city fast-food restaurants [have] appear[ed], which have a big group of fans.

records.definition_text: the way a person or thing looks to other people
records.learnerexamples_text: The buildings are very similar in appearance.; You can alter/change the whole appearance of a room just by lighting it in a certain way.; She gives the appearance of being very efficient.; I usually buy fashionable clothes, because I think [your] appearance is really important.

records.definition_text: when someone appears in public, on television, in a film, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: It was his first appearance on television/television appearance as president.; She made two appearances during her visit.; She will be making a public appearance, signing copies of her latest novel.; You probably know him, because he [made] an appearance [i]n the film "Bad Boys."

records.definition_text: when something starts to exist or becomes available
records.learnerexamples_text: The appearance of new products on the market has increased competition.; The appearance of the car has facilitated our lives.

records.definition_text: to perform in a film, play, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: She appears briefly in the new Bond film.; What I like the most is that I'm going to appear on T.V.

records.definition_text: an official request for something, usually in writing
records.learnerexamples_text: a letter of application; I've sent off applications for four different jobs.; Have you filled in the application form for your passport yet?; After having filled [in] the application form, the master pilot took us on a short trip around the hangars showing the planes used for training.

records.definition_text: a piece of computer software designed for a particular purpose
records.learnerexamples_text: Typical examples of software applications are spreadsheets, media players and database applications.; I am [an] exp[e]rienced user of [the] Internet and know all application programs for Windows '95 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PinPoint etc).

records.definition_text: to relate to a particular person or situation
records.learnerexamples_text: That bit of the form is for UK citizens - it doesn't apply to you.; He seems to think that the normal rules of behaviour don't apply to him.; Those were old regulations - they don't apply any more.; The same doesn't apply to a teenager who lives in illness and poverty and whose family and friends constantly mistreat him.

records.definition_text: to request something, usually officially, especially by writing or sending in a form
records.learnerexamples_text: By the time I saw the job advertised it was already too late to apply.; I've applied for a job there.; Please apply in writing to the address below.; I applied for this course and went to my first lesson last week.

records.definition_text: to understand how good something or someone is and be able to enjoy them
records.learnerexamples_text: There's no point buying him expensive wines - he doesn't appreciate them.; I don't think you appreciate how much time I spent preparing this meal.; It's like wine, it's impossible to drink a glass of wine quickly, you can't appreciate it.

records.definition_text: when you understand how good something or someone is and are able to enjoy them
records.learnerexamples_text: You've done so much to help us so, to show our appreciation, we've bought you a little gift.; The crowd cheered in appreciation.; Children rarely show any appreciation of/for what their parents do for them.; My appreciation of art has increased as I've got older.; To show our appreciation, we would also like to invite you to dinner afterwards at the Red Baron.

records.definition_text: to come close in distance or time
records.learnerexamples_text: Ladies and gentlemen, we are now approaching Paddington Station.; Christmas is fast approaching.; [The] holidays are approaching.

records.definition_text: to deal with something
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm not sure how to approach the problem.; This is the right way to approach the issue.

records.definition_text: when something or someone gets nearer in distance or time
records.learnerexamples_text: The siren signalled the approach of an ambulance.; Please fasten your seat belts, the plane is now making its final approach (in)to Heathrow Airport.

records.definition_text: a way of doing something
records.learnerexamples_text: In Sweden they have a different approach to the problem.; I thought we'd adopt/take a new approach.; This will show the contrast in teaching methods, different approaches to students and [the] techniques used by different teachers.

records.definition_text: suitable or right for a particular situation or occasion
records.learnerexamples_text: Is this film appropriate for small children?; I didn't think his comments were very appropriate at the time.; I will explain why I am an appropriate person for this job.

records.definition_text: in a way that is appropriate
records.learnerexamples_text: She didn't think we were appropriately dressed for a wedding.; I enjoyed reading it and I think it appropriately describes the atmosphere of that lovely town.

records.definition_text: when you have a positive opinion of someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: He showed his approval by smiling broadly.; Sam always tried hard to win his father's approval.; Does the wine meet with your approval?; I hope this meets [with] your approval and I am looking forward to hearing from you as soon as possible.

records.definition_text: official permission
records.learnerexamples_text: The project has now received approval from the government.; The teacher gave the student a nod of approval.; Besides the questionable approval given by governmental authorities, the situation might be useful to us.

records.definition_text: to allow or officially agree to something
records.learnerexamples_text: The council has approved plans for a new shopping centre.; The court approved the sale of the property.; "Congratulation[s], your scholarship to [the] UK is approved."

records.definition_text: to think that something is good or right
records.learnerexamples_text: She doesn't approve of my friends.; He doesn't approve of smoking.; The head of department seems to approve of what I am doing.; Woods didn't approve of the government's attitude to them.

records.definition_text: not completely accurate but close
records.learnerexamples_text: The train's approximate time of arrival is 10.30.; Can you give me an approximate idea of the numbers involved?; The approximate figure is about 5000 people.

records.definition_text: close to a particular number or time although not exactly that number or time
records.learnerexamples_text: The job will take approximately two weeks, and cost around £1000.; The college has approximately 700 students.; From the airport of Larnaka you need approximately forty-five minutes by taxi, to Agia Napa.

records.definition_text: someone who works quickly/slowly/well, etc.
records.searchterms_text: a quick/slow/good etc worker;a quick/slow/good, etc. worker;quick/slow/good, etc. worker;worker;workers
records.learnerexamples_text: He's rather a slow worker, but he is very thorough.; I'll recom[men]d you [as] a hard worker and a very nice person.

records.definition_text: someone whose job is to design buildings
records.learnerexamples_text: He trained as an architect in Edinburgh and then moved to London to find work.; He kn[e]w that I wanted to be an architect.

records.definition_text: the design and style of buildings
records.learnerexamples_text: Roman architecture; modern architecture; There are beautiful places like Merarejonban, which is outstanding in its architecture.

records.definition_text: the skill of designing buildings
records.learnerexamples_text: He studied architecture.; I want to study architecture in the U.K. but English is a problem, so I need spend a lot of time learn[ing] it.

records.definition_text: a part of a building or piece of land used for a particular purpose
records.learnerexamples_text: a play/picnic area; I'm staying in a very big hotel; it ha[s] a swimming pool, a golf area, gardens, and also a children['s] area.

records.definition_text: a part of a subject or activity
records.learnerexamples_text: Marketing is Paul's area.; Software is not really my area of expertise.; I am a 30-year-old Swedish male with a diploma in gardening. I have 6 years experience of the area since I have been employed by a Swedish fruit supplier.

records.definition_text: to speak angrily to someone, telling them that you disagree with them
records.learnerexamples_text: My parents are always arguing.; Kids, will you stop arguing with each other?; They were arguing over/about which film to go and see.; Peter told her his parents had argued and he came with his mother to London.

records.definition_text: to give reasons to support or oppose an idea, action, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: The minister argued for/in favour of making cuts in military spending.; She argued against tax cuts.; The minister argued that cuts in military spending were needed.; It is often argued that family life is not important.

records.definition_text: an angry discussion with someone in which you both disagree
records.learnerexamples_text: The children had an argument about/over what game to play.; He got into an argument with a man in the pub last night.; I wrote a song last week. It's about my boyfriend and an argument he had with his parents about our relationship.

records.definition_text: a reason or reasons why you support or oppose an idea, action, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: There are many arguments for and against nuclear energy.; I don't think that's a very strong/powerful argument.; An argument in favour of this statement is that shopping is very tiring.

records.definition_text: using or carrying weapons
records.learnerexamples_text: an armed robbery; armed conflict; armed guards/police; I could clearly understand that the two armed men would catch us within [a] few minutes.

records.definition_text: in a circle or with circular movement
records.learnerexamples_text: She passed a plate of biscuits around.; This switch makes the wheels go around.; Hello, everybody. Please gather around.

records.definition_text: to the opposite direction
records.learnerexamples_text: Jonny turned around and looked at her.; The pianist spun around on the stool and faced his audience.; As the concert finished, I heard someone call my name. I turned around.

records.definition_text: to make the necessary plans and preparations for something to happen
records.learnerexamples_text: The meeting has been arranged for Wednesday.; They arranged to have dinner the following month.; I've already arranged with him where to meet.; She's arranged for her son to have swimming lessons.; I'd arranged that they should arrive at the same time.

records.definition_text: to put objects in a particular order or position
records.learnerexamples_text: She arranged her birthday cards along the shelf.; Who arranged these flowers so beautifully?; His books are neatly arranged in alphabetical order.; Before the pop concert [started], I arranged the seats and carried some musical instruments.

records.definition_text: plans for how something will happen
records.learnerexamples_text: They'd made all the arrangements for the party.; Arrangements were made to move the prisoners to another jail.; What are your current childcare arrangements?; I'll make all [the] arrangements.

records.definition_text: an agreement between two people or groups
records.learnerexamples_text: We had an arrangement that he would clean the house and I would cook.; I'm sure we can come to an arrangement.; You can only withdraw money from this account by (prior) arrangement  with the bank.; I didn't know if you would be in the house or not so you need to contact him for a new arrangement [on] this telephone number 333-30.30.

records.definition_text: a group of objects in a particular order or position
records.learnerexamples_text: a flower arrangement; Dear Mrs. Anderson, I have learned from a friend that your club gives advanced courses in flower arrangement.

records.definition_text: If the police arrest someone, they take them away to ask them about a crime which they might have committed.
records.learnerexamples_text: She was arrested for drinking and driving.; He was arrested when customs officers found drugs in his bag.; To my horror, they arrested me.

records.definition_text: when the police take someone away to ask them about a crime which they might have committed
records.learnerexamples_text: Police made twenty arrests at yesterday's demonstration.; She was stopped outside the shop and placed/put under arrest.; When I came around, Mr Smith was under arrest and fortunately, thing[s] finished well for me.

records.definition_text: when someone or something arrives somewhere
records.learnerexamples_text: Hundreds gathered to await the boxer's arrival at the airport.;  On arrival at the police station, they were taken to an interview room.; We regret the late arrival of Flight 237.; Can you confirm your arrival time next week?

records.definition_text: believing that you are better or more important than other people
records.learnerexamples_text: I found him arrogant and rude.; Chubby, arrogant and filthy were the words that described him best. Every time they met, a bitter feeling of hatre[d] bloomed in her throat.

records.definition_text: a symbol used on a sign, on a computer, etc. to show direction
records.learnerexamples_text: I followed the arrows to the car park.; I followed its arrow and believe it or not I found mum!

records.definition_text: a weapon that is like a long thin stick with a sharp point at one end and often feathers at the other, shot from a bow
records.learnerexamples_text: Robin Hood asked to be buried where his arrow landed.; The museum has many old axes, crossbows, bows and arrows.

records.definition_text: a piece of writing on a particular subject in a newspaper or magazine
records.learnerexamples_text: There was an interesting article on climate change in the paper yesterday.; I read an article about this zoo in the newspaper.

records.definition_text: in grammar, used to mean the words 'a', 'an' and 'the'
records.learnerexamples_text: There's a definite article missing before the noun.

records.definition_text: not natural, but made by people
records.learnerexamples_text: an artificial flower/lake; artificial flavourings; First, most shop[p]ing centres use artificial illumination, which is bad for our health.

records.definition_text: in an artificial way
records.learnerexamples_text: Most mushrooms sold in supermarkets have been grown artificially in manure.; Zoos are part of nature, despite the fact that they are created artificially.

records.definition_text: showing skill and imagination in creating things, especially in painting, drawing, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: Both children are very artistic.; artistic talent; If the museum is a place were they can say how they feel, or express it in an abstract or artistic way, they will start to like it.

records.definition_text: relating to any form of art, including painting, literature, theatre, music, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: the artistic director of the theatre; a work of artistic merit; That would be perfect to improve the artistic and cultural life of Turin.

records.definition_text: creative areas including painting, drama, dance, music, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: fine/decorative arts; She's doing a course in the performing arts.; You can enjoy both traditional and contemporary performing arts in Osaka.

records.definition_text: being or appearing to be a particular thing

records.definition_text: to cause people to pay attention/be interested, etc.

records.definition_text: to make someone notice you
records.learnerexamples_text: I waved at her to get her attention.; The bank is near the school, so the lady was trying to get people's attention while the others [robbed] the bank.

records.definition_text: something that makes people come to a place or do a particular thing
records.learnerexamples_text: tourist attractions; The opportunity to travel is one of the main attractions of this job.; At first I only wanted to see the many attractions in Balboa Park.

records.definition_text: interesting or useful
records.learnerexamples_text: an attractive offer/idea; We want to make the club attractive to a wider range of people.; In fact, all of my work-mates make fun of me when I talk about my collection of stamps. I want to demonstrate [to] them that it is a very attractive hobby.

records.definition_text: at a time that is convenient to you
records.learnerexamples_text: We can meet at your convenience.; I look forward to hearing from you at your earliest convenience.

records.definition_text: an oval, purple vegetable that is white inside
records.learnerexamples_text: The dish is made with aubergines and cheese.

records.definition_text: the people who sit and watch a performance at a theatre, cinema, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: There were a lot of children in the audience.; The audience was/were clearly delighted with the performance.; All the [people in the] audience looked at me, I was very excited. The band called me, so I went to the stage and they started to play a very popular song.

records.definition_text: the type of people who watch a particular TV show, read a particular book, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: This magazine is aimed at a teenage/young audience.; The above-mentioned restaurants are totally different from each other and suit completely different customers. Pasta+, to begin with, is best suited [to a] younger audience.

records.definition_text: the writer of a book, article, play, etc.

records.definition_text: the power to make decisions or to control other people

records.definition_text: An automatic machine works by itself or with little human control.
records.learnerexamples_text: automatic doors; It has both manual and automatic functions so it has a lot of possibilities.

records.definition_text: If a machine does something automatically, it does it independently, without human control.
records.learnerexamples_text: The camera adjusts the shutter speed automatically.; [The] television will be automatically switched on in time for [the] breakfast news.

records.definition_text: If you do something automatically, you do it without thinking about it.
records.learnerexamples_text: I automatically put my hand out to catch it.; There was a strange envelope between the others, so automatically, she picked it up and [looked at] the stamp. The letter came from Australia.

records.definition_text: when something or someone is available
records.learnerexamples_text: I checked the availability of flights online and there's plenty of choice.; Therefore, it is essential that you take account of my availability when booking the trip.

records.learnerexamples_text: an average age/temperature; The weather on this mountain is fantastic, with an average temperature of 17°C.

records.definition_text: typical and usual
records.learnerexamples_text: The average person in the street is a lot better off than they were forty years ago.; a student of average ability; This makes people beli[e]ve that a lot of the food we eat is fast-food, but it's not true at all, in fact it's a very small part of our average diet.

records.definition_text: the result you get by adding two or more amounts together and dividing the total by the number of amounts
records.learnerexamples_text: Prices have risen by an average of 4% over the past year.; On the table was my mark sheet with the average as 90%.

records.definition_text: the usual or typical amount

records.definition_text: to stay away from a person, place, situation, etc.

records.definition_text: knowing that something exists, or having knowledge or experience of a particular thing

records.base_text: call off sth or call sth off

records.definition_text: in a quiet or relaxed way

records.definition_text: a large animal that lives in the desert and has one or two raised parts on its back

records.definition_text: a matter to be decided by a judge in a court of law

records.learnerexamples_text: I caught up with him in Singapore a few years later.; I'll catch up with you later!; You should catch up with me in Sicily, where you will be able to walk on the best beaches you have ever seen.

records.definition_text: a group of people or things of the same type

records.definition_text: providing food and drinks for people
records.learnerexamples_text: Who did the catering for the party?; a high-class catering company; All food, appetizers and refreshments will be provided by a catering company.

records.definition_text: male and female cows kept on a farm for their milk or meat
records.learnerexamples_text: beef/dairy cattle; He was born in Australia, where his father has a big cattle station.

records.definition_text: the reason why something, especially something bad, happens

records.definition_text: to make something happen, especially something bad

records.definition_text: taking care to avoid risks or danger

records.definition_text: a large hole in the side of a hill, cliff or mountain, or one that is underground
records.learnerexamples_text: The area is also home to one of the largest underground cave and lake systems in Latin America.; The next day I went to see a cave with a blue lake inside it.

records.definition_text: to stop

But it didn't cease, making me realize it was something else, from outside the room.

records.definition_text: to do something enjoyable because it is a special day, or because something good has happened

records.definition_text: a special social event, such as a party, when you celebrate something, or the act of celebrating something

records.definition_text: someone who is famous, especially in the entertainment business
records.learnerexamples_text: It's a celebrity gossip magazine.; The walls are painted blue and hung with posters of my favourite celebrities.

records.definition_text: the smallest basic unit of a plant or animal

records.definition_text: a small room in a prison or police station where a prisoner is kept

records.definition_text: a room under the ground floor of a building, usually used for storage
records.learnerexamples_text: He keeps his wine in the cellar.; We were in the cellar of the old castle without a candle or even matches.

records.definition_text: a large, wooden musical instrument with four strings that you hold between your knees to play
records.learnerexamples_text: She plays the cello.; It was Beethoven, the 9th symphony. The cellos [and] violins, followed by the timpani...

records.definition_text: a place where dead people are buried
records.learnerexamples_text: She went to the cemetery where her grandfather was buried.; It was Halloween night and almost midnight, and Steve had the idea of going out to the nearest cemetery to catch some ghosts or vampires.

records.definition_text: a measurement of temperature in which water freezes at 0° and boils at 100°
records.learnerexamples_text: Water boils at 100° centigrade.; The last few days I prefer[red] to go swimming, because the temperature was above thirty degrees centigrade.

records.definition_text: in or near the centre of a place or object
records.learnerexamples_text: central Europe/London; Of course, you pay more for premises with a central location.; We could go for a walk to the park in the central area of my town.

records.learnerexamples_text: The house had no central heating so in winter it was freezing.; I like this restaurant because it's cheap, big and tidy, [and] at the same time it has central heating and air condition[ing].

records.definition_text: a formal event that is performed on important social or religious occasions
records.learnerexamples_text: a wedding/graduation ceremony; In July I'm going to [get] married to my girl friend, and the wedding ceremony is on 7th of July.

records.definition_text: completely sure of something, or knowing without doubt that something is true

records.definition_text: sure to happen, to do something, or to be true
records.learnerexamples_text: It now looks certain that she will resign.; One thing is certain: she's not coming to my party.; How can we make certain that she sees the note?; If I were you I'd choose the large school because it's certain that you'll find people [there] that think like you.

records.definition_text: used to refer to a particular person or thing without naming or describing them
records.learnerexamples_text: The museum is only open at certain times of the day.; The last one I saw was called 'Spelling' and it was a kind of quiz where the competitors had to spell difficult words fast and finish at a certain time.

records.definition_text: when you are completely sure about something
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm unable to answer that question with any certainty.; I can say with certainty that this town is just a treasure of Polish culture.

records.definition_text: an official document that gives details to show that something is true
records.learnerexamples_text: a birth/marriage/death certificate; an examination certificate; a doctor's/medical certificate; You must have the PET certificate and you should speak another language.

records.definition_text: a number of similar shops, restaurants, etc. owned by the same company
records.learnerexamples_text: a chain of hotels/shops/supermarkets; a fast-food chain; These days children [have] grown up with McDonalds and other fast-food chains.

records.definition_text: a series of things that happen one after the other
records.learnerexamples_text: a chain reaction; His arrival set off a surprising chain of events.; The problem began to increase because all her friends knew her secret. It was like a "chain reaction".

records.definition_text: something that is difficult and that tests someone's ability or determination
records.learnerexamples_text: Finding a solution to this problem is one of the greatest challenges faced by scientists today.; You know me - I like a challenge.; It's going to be a difficult job but I'm sure she'll rise to the challenge.; I went with two friends from school, we had a big adventure there and we had to face many challenges.

records.definition_text: to express disagreement with ideas, rules, or someone's authority
records.learnerexamples_text: Children challenge their parents' authority far more nowadays than they did in the past.; His daughter had just challenged him and he was struggling for a decision.

records.definition_text: difficult, in a way that tests your ability or determination
records.learnerexamples_text: This has been a challenging time for us all.; Like cavaliers we ride across the country looking for adventures and challenging activities.

records.definition_text: a person, animal, or team that wins a competition
records.learnerexamples_text: an Olympic champion; She is the world champion for the third year in succession.; The defending champion will play his first match of the tournament tomorrow.; Who are the European football champions?; Last week I played with a person who was the world chess champion!

records.definition_text: a competition to find the best team or player in a particular game or sport
records.learnerexamples_text: the British Diving Championship; The world championships will be held in Scotland next year.; He has been playing championship tennis for three years now.; I have a sailing championship, in which I must participate.

records.definition_text: the possibility that something will happen
records.learnerexamples_text: There's a chance (that) he'll still be there.; Does she have any chance of winning?; You'd have a better chance of passing your exams if you worked a bit harder.; There's a good chance (that) I'll have this essay finished by tomorrow.; What are the chances of getting tickets for the Olympics?

records.definition_text: a risk

records.definition_text: the place on a website where you order and pay for goods
records.learnerexamples_text: After you've chosen what you want, click here to proceed to checkout.

records.definition_text: to leave a hotel after paying and returning your room key

records.definition_text: slightly rude or showing no respect, but often in a funny way

records.definition_text: highest in rank
records.learnerexamples_text: He is the chief economic adviser to the government.; Bob Wilson, the chief accountant, had resigned.

records.definition_text: the time when someone is a child
records.learnerexamples_text: She had an unhappy childhood.; Childhood is not always a happy time.; The e-mail was from somebody who I haven't heard about since my childhood.

records.definition_text: Childish behaviour is silly, like that of a small child.
records.learnerexamples_text: Don't be so childish!; In comparison with other countries' tourists, they seem to be a little childish, just like a group of duckling[s] or chickens.

records.definition_text: typical of a child
records.learnerexamples_text: childish handwriting; I heard a childish voice saying to me "Take my hand."

records.definition_text: to relax completely, or not allow things to upset you
records.learnerexamples_text: Chill out, Dad - if we miss this train there's always another one.; I just can't wait to get there, grab some Coke and chill out!

records.definition_text: a hollow structure that allows the smoke from a fire inside a building to escape to the air outside
records.learnerexamples_text: Factory chimneys belched dense white smoke into the sky.; The reason is half for my own health and fitness and half for the health of my town, which is polluted by lead, the smoke from chimneys and other artificial poisons.

records.definition_text: the bottom part of a person's face, below their mouth
records.learnerexamples_text: Fasten the strap beneath your chin.; She sat behind the table, her chin resting in her hands.; I'm just about 20cm taller and I've grown whiskers on my chin, which is quite an uncommon look.

records.definition_text: a very small part of a computer that stores information
records.learnerexamples_text: a silicon chip; Even in cars and wash[ing] machines there're computer chips.

records.definition_text: when you can choose between two or more things, or the decision to choose one thing or person and not someone or something else
records.learnerexamples_text: If I had a choice, I'd give up work.; I had to go - I had no choice.; It's a difficult choice to make.; It's your choice/The choice is yours.; It was a choice between black or brown.

records.definition_text: the range of different things from which you can choose
records.learnerexamples_text: There wasn't much choice on the menu.; The evening menu offers a wide choice of dishes.; The dress is available in a choice of colours.; There is a very wide choice of activities!

records.definition_text: a person or thing that has been chosen or that can be chosen
records.learnerexamples_text: Harvard was not his first choice.; He wouldn't be my choice as a friend.; This type of nursery care may well be the best choice for your child.; For me, the best choice is to come to the city.

records.definition_text: a group of people who sing together, often in a church or a school
records.learnerexamples_text: He sings in the church choir.; choir practice ; I have sung in the church's choir for three years, and I have had singing classes at school since first grade.

records.definition_text: to decide to do something
records.learnerexamples_text: Manuela chose to take a job in Paris.

records.definition_text: to cut something into pieces with an axe, knife, or other sharp instrument
records.learnerexamples_text: He was chopping wood in the yard.; Add some fresh parsley, finely chopped.; Chop (up) the onions and carrots roughly.; You would use them to chop vegetable[s].

records.definition_text: a group of people with family, work or social connections
records.learnerexamples_text: She's not one of my close circle of friends.; It's a technical term used in medical circles.; His name is Omar Naber and he has quite [a] big circle of fans in Slovenia, although most of them are kids.

records.definition_text: to draw a circle around something
records.learnerexamples_text: Circle the answer you think is correct.

records.definition_text: shaped like a circle
records.learnerexamples_text: a circular rug ; People who congratulate the marrying [couple] take a circular sweet.

records.definition_text: a fact or event that makes a situation the way it is
records.learnerexamples_text: I think she coped very well under the circumstances.; She died in suspicious circumstances.; We oppose capital punishment in/under any circumstances.;  Under no circumstances should you approach the man.; The meeting has been cancelled due to circumstances beyond our control.

records.definition_text: a show in which a group of people and animals perform in a large tent
records.learnerexamples_text: a circus ring; The children loved being taken to the circus.; In the afternoon you can just go walking if you are not in a mood to do something exciting, but if are, you can go to the circus.

records.definition_text: someone who lives in a particular town or city
records.learnerexamples_text: The citizens of Moscow woke up this morning to find they had a new government.; I think that it is a really good idea to make a film about our town and its citizens.

records.definition_text: someone who has a legal right to live in a particular country
records.learnerexamples_text: He applied to become an American citizen.; I'm an American citizen because my mother comes from Queens, New York.

records.definition_text: human society with its well developed social organizations, or the culture and way of life of a society or country at a particular period in time
records.learnerexamples_text: Some people think that nuclear war would mean the end of civilization.; Cuzco was the centre of one of the world's most famous civilizations, that of the Incas.; ancient civilizations; Since the beginning of civilization, man has been looking for co[m]fort and better ways to do things.

records.definition_text: to say that something is true or is a fact, although you cannot prove it and other people might not believe it
records.learnerexamples_text: The company claims (that) it is not responsible for the pollution in the river.; He claims to have met the President, but I don't believe him.; An unknown terrorist group has claimed responsibility for this morning's bomb attack.; All parties have claimed success in yesterday's elections.; Bicycle supporters claim that it is silent and keeps owners fit.

records.definition_text: to ask for something because it belongs to you or you think you have the right to have it
records.learnerexamples_text: She claimed £1,500 in expenses.; Don't forget to claim (for) your travelling expenses after the interview.; The number of people claiming unemployment benefit has risen sharply this month.; If the shop won't give me a replacement TV, I'll claim my money back.; I also would like to claim [a] refund for the evening.

records.definition_text: a written request asking an organization to pay you a sum of money which you believe they owe you
records.learnerexamples_text: an insurance claim; a claim for compensation; I've made a claim on my insurance.; This wasn't "my perfect evening out", and I [would like to] make a claim for half the money back.

records.definition_text: to hit your hands together, often repeatedly, especially in order to show you enjoyed a performance
records.learnerexamples_text: The audience clapped and cheered for more.; "When I clap my hands, you must stand still," said the teacher.; Every[thing] was nice till I clapped my hands to call the waiter to [get] the bill.

records.definition_text: a group of people within society who have the same economic and social position
records.learnerexamples_text: The Labour Party has lost a lot of support among the working class.; We live in a middle class neighbourhood.; She belonged to the rich American upper class.; The second film is called "Upper class first" and it describes how rich people live.

records.definition_text: A classic book, film, etc. is one that has been popular for a long time and is considered to be of a high quality.
records.learnerexamples_text: a classic film/novel/story; I am fond of reading different books, especially classic literature.

records.definition_text: a piece of writing, a musical recording or a film which has been popular for a long time and is considered to be of a high quality
records.learnerexamples_text: Jane Austen's 'Pride and Prejudice' is a classic of English literature.; Many of the Rolling Stones' records have become rock classics.; Wuthering Heights [is] a classic, which everybody knows about.

records.definition_text: a group of words containing a subject and a verb, that is usually only part of a sentence
records.learnerexamples_text: In the sentence 'I can't cook very well but I make quite good omelettes', both 'I can't cook very well' and 'I make quite good omelettes' are main clauses.; In the sentence 'I'll get you some stamps if I go to town', 'if I go to town' is a subordinate clause.

records.definition_text: certain or obvious
records.learnerexamples_text: Are you clear about how to get there?; It's clear that she's not interested.; I'm still not clear what I'm supposed to do.; Are you clear about the questions?

records.definition_text: A clear sky does not have any clouds.
records.learnerexamples_text: clear blue skies; When we went to San Martin de los Andes, we could see seven lakes and different kinds of trees and the sky [was] always clear.

records.definition_text: to remove all the objects or people from a place
records.learnerexamples_text: It took several hours to clear the road after the accident.; I'll make the coffee if you'll clear the table.; I cleared the snow from the path.; Could you clear your things off the sofa?; I cleared the stage before the concert, but you [ca]n't imagine how it looked after it?!!! Full of flowers, hats, underwear, etc.

records.definition_text: used to show that you think something is obvious or certain
records.learnerexamples_text: The accident was clearly the lorry driver's fault.; Clearly, he's very talented.; It was clearly not for me, because it came from a girl called Carol who wanted to talk to some guy named John.

records.definition_text: If the weather clears up, the cloud and rain disappears.
records.learnerexamples_text: I hope the weather clears up before this afternoon.; For the first two days the weather was so bad that we couldn't reach the beach but finally the sky cleared up.

records.definition_text: to make a place tidy by removing things from it or putting them where they should be
records.searchterms_text: clear;clear up (sth) or clear (sth) up;clear up sth or clear sth up
records.learnerexamples_text: Dad was clearing up the kitchen.; I also helped to clear up the place after the concert.

records.base_text: clear up sth or clear sth up
records.definition_text: to give an explanation for something, or to deal with a problem or argument
records.searchterms_text: clear;clear up sth or clear sth up;clear up sth or clear sth up
records.learnerexamples_text: Before we sign the contract, there are a few points we should clear up.; I hope this will clear up your problem.

records.definition_text: effective and showing intelligence
records.learnerexamples_text: a clever idea; I've got a clever little gadget for opening jars.; My friend told me that he saw [a] really nice loft bed. I think it's [a] clever idea.

records.definition_text: someone who pays someone else for services or advice
records.learnerexamples_text: We're losing a lot of our clients.; The mot[t]o of the staff there is: "the client is always right."

records.definition_text: a high area of rock with a very steep side, often on a coast
records.learnerexamples_text: Keep well away from the edge of the cliff.; the cliff edge; This hotel is [on] a cliff, and has good [views].

records.definition_text: the weather conditions that an area usually has
records.learnerexamples_text: a hot/dry/cold/wet climate; The Mediterranean climate is good for growing citrus fruits and grapes.; The climate of Brazil is typically tropical so the weather is gorgeous.

records.definition_text: the way the Earth's weather is changing
records.learnerexamples_text: Climate change is the greatest environmental challenge facing the world today.

records.definition_text: to go up, or to go towards the top of something
records.learnerexamples_text: The plane climbed quickly to a height of 30 000 feet.; As it leaves the village, the road climbs steeply up the mountain.; The sun climbed higher in the sky.

records.definition_text: to move into or out of a small space, often with difficulty or effort
records.searchterms_text: climb;climb into/out of/through etc;climb into/out of/through, etc.;climbed;climbing;climbs
records.learnerexamples_text: The baby had managed to climb out of his cot.; They climbed into the truck and drove away.; I went to my car, climbed into it and wanted to drive, but nothing happened.

records.definition_text: a building, often part of a hospital, where people go for medical treatment or advice
records.learnerexamples_text: Bring your baby to the clinic and we'll take a look at her.; Antenatal clinics provide care for pregnant women.; Ahmed [was] travelling to attend a fair of medical equipment, to get what he [needed] for his clinic.

records.definition_text: If a business or organization closes, or if someone or something closes it, it stops operating.
records.learnerexamples_text: The factory closed over ten years ago.; A lot of restaurants/shops are closing because they can't afford to pay the rent.; In addition, I would like you to know that the Hotel Astrid closed last year.

records.definition_text: A close relative is someone who is directly related to you, for example, your mother, father or brother.
records.learnerexamples_text: There weren't many people at the funeral - just close family/relatives.; Tomson has [a] close family, his son lives with them, [and] his company makes a good profit.

records.definition_text: seeing or communicating with someone a lot
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm still in close contact with my school friends.; Our school has close links with a school in China.; Being in close touch with me for such a long time, you should have known everything about the band.

records.definition_text: near in distance
records.learnerexamples_text: Come a bit closer.; He stayed close to his mother.; There's a great beach close by.; Aunty told me that there is a Hindu temple close by.

records.definition_text: If a business or organization closes down or someone closes it down, it stops operating.
records.searchterms_text: close;close down (sth) or close (sth) down;close down sth or close sth down
records.learnerexamples_text: All the mines in this area were closed down in the 80s.; Our local butcher is closing down.; I must tell you that unfortunately "Hotel Astrid" closed down last year.

records.definition_text: in a way that is directly connected or has a strong relationship
records.learnerexamples_text: English and German are closely related.; Both politicians have been closely associated with the movement for some time.; We are working closely with the police.; The main reason I am applying for this job is that this job would be very rewarding on [a] personal level and would give me useful experience closely related to my field of study.

records.definition_text: material made from cotton, wool, etc. and used, for example, to make clothes or curtains
records.learnerexamples_text: a piece/length of cloth; We [will] probably be wearing dresses made of synthetic cloth in 2100.

records.definition_text: a small piece of material used for cleaning or drying things
records.learnerexamples_text: a washing-up cloth

records.definition_text: clothes, especially of a particular type
records.learnerexamples_text: Protective clothing must be worn at all times.; You can only take three articles/items of clothing into the changing room.; Nowadays the aim in clothing is not just for covering and protecting ourselves.

records.definition_text: a mass of something such as dust or smoke that looks like a cloud
records.learnerexamples_text: A huge cloud of smoke from burning oil tanks stretched across the sky.; Some of them leave behind a large cloud of smoke and it damage[s] our health.

records.definition_text: a team of sports players
records.learnerexamples_text: Stockport County Football Club; The Orioles are an exciting club this year.; The club is Juventus and as you know, [it] is my favo[u]rite football team.

records.definition_text: a place open late at night where people can dance
records.learnerexamples_text: After the show, we went to a club.; As regards the food, you can ask for any kind of food and after midnight it turns into a club where you can dance [to] any kind of music.

records.definition_text: a sign or some information that helps you to solve a problem or answer a question
records.learnerexamples_text: Police are searching the area for clues to the murder.; Police are still looking for clues in their search for the missing girl.; I'm never going to guess the answer if you don't give me a clue.; They found it and they started looking for more clues.

records.definition_text: Clumsy people move in a way that is not controlled or careful enough, and often knock or damage things.
records.learnerexamples_text: That's the third glass you've smashed this week - you're so clumsy!; I was cleaning the house, and as you know, I'm very clumsy, so I was dusting the table, and, accidentally, I dropped the vase.

records.definition_text: to teach someone so they improve at a sport, skill, or in a school subject
records.learnerexamples_text: She coaches students in French, usually for exams.; I have also been coaching a girls team for 3 years.

records.definition_text: someone whose job is to teach people to improve at a sport, skill, or school subject
records.learnerexamples_text: a tennis/maths coach; Then the coach wanted to know some facts about me.

records.definition_text: additional teaching of a sport, a skill or a school subject
records.learnerexamples_text: She has extra coaching in maths.; In Poland basketball is getting more and more popular and we feel the lack of coaching.

records.definition_text: the land next to or close to the sea
records.learnerexamples_text: Rimini is a thriving holiday resort on the east coast of Italy.; The accident happened three miles off the coast.; We spent a week by/on the coast.; I think it's best to spend your time visiting our coast in the North East of Brazil.

records.definition_text: situated on, or relating to the coast
records.learnerexamples_text: a coastal town; I love to spend time at the beach and that is the reason why I live in a coastal area.

records.definition_text: a very large nut with a hard, hairy shell, a white part that you eat, and liquid in the centre
records.learnerexamples_text: Thai food uses a lot of coconut.; I forgot to tell you that they have a special dessert with coconut and ice cream.

records.definition_text: a large sea fish that can be eaten
records.learnerexamples_text: I'll have cod and chips, please. ; I suggest 'batatas com bacalhau', which is cooked cod served with boiled potatoes.

records.definition_text: a system of words, letters or signs which is used to represent a message in secret form
records.learnerexamples_text: The message was written in code.; She managed to break/crack the code.; Everyone had already heard of me getting the secret access code for the 'Secret Society' organisation.

records.definition_text: a small, flat, usually round piece of metal used as money
records.learnerexamples_text: a 10p/ten pence coin; a pound coin; a ten-cent coin; gold coins; I asked for ten pounds in 20p coins.

records.definition_text: when two very similar things happen at the same time but there is no reason for it
records.learnerexamples_text: You chose exactly the same wallpaper as us - what a coincidence!; Just by coincidence, I met my old school-mate again fifty years later.;  It was pure coincidence that we met.; What a coincidence, don't you think so?

records.definition_text: unfriendly or showing no emotion
records.learnerexamples_text: She became quite cold and distant with me.; a cold stare/voice; Suddenly, I heard the same, cold voice behind me again.

records.definition_text: to fall down suddenly because of pressure or having no strength or support
records.learnerexamples_text: Thousands of buildings collapsed in the earthquake.; The chair collapsed under her weight.; Then a sudden wave of fire made their heads explode and many buildings collapsed instantly.

records.definition_text: If someone collapses, they fall down, usually because they are ill or weak.
records.learnerexamples_text: He collapsed and died of a heart attack.; He desperately tried to keep the stalking sharks at bay, but he couldn't succeed, for the long fight exhausted him and he collapsed.

records.definition_text: the sudden failure of a system, organization, business, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: A poor economy has caused the collapse of thousands of small businesses.; Negotiations between the two countries are on the brink/verge of collapse.; He suffered a mental collapse after ten years' teaching.; After your nervous collapse last year I really worry about you.

records.definition_text: the part of a shirt, coat, etc. that is usually folded over and goes round your neck
records.learnerexamples_text: a shirt collar; a fur collar; It's a new, fashionable one with [a] high collar and short sleeves.

records.definition_text: a strap made of leather or other strong material which is put around the neck of an animal, especially a dog or cat
records.learnerexamples_text: a dog collar; I grabbed the dog by its collar and dragged it out of the room.

records.definition_text: to get things from different places and bring them together
records.learnerexamples_text: Police collected a good deal of information during the investigation.; I collected up twenty bottles from various parts of the house.; The majority of people collect their own rubbish separately in their home, but they d[o] not separate the paper and the cardboard.

records.definition_text: to ask people to give you money for something, for example a charity
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm collecting on behalf of Oxfam.; We're collecting (money) for the homeless.; And I think it's a perfect way to collect money for our poor people.

records.definition_text: a group of objects of one type that have been collected by one person or in one place
records.learnerexamples_text: a private art collection; a valuable stamp collection; I'm going to buy the DVD named "Lord of the Rings" because I like it very much and want to have it in my DVD collection.

records.definition_text: a group of things or people
records.learnerexamples_text: There's quite a collection of toothbrushes in the bathroom.; I [wear] long t-shirts and I have a collection of sweaters.

records.definition_text: when something is taken away from a place
records.learnerexamples_text: rubbish collection; We need a different organisation for the waste collection.

records.definition_text: someone who collects objects because they are interesting or beautiful
records.learnerexamples_text: a collector of modern art; a stamp collector; Anne has been a collector for many years and she knows almost everything about Swedish stamps.

records.definition_text: a word or phrase that sounds natural or correct when it is used with another word or phrase, or the combination formed when two or more words are frequently used together in a way that sounds natural
records.learnerexamples_text: 'Heavy traffic' is a collocation.

records.definition_text: a mark (:) used before a list, an example, an explanation, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: There's a colon missing in that sentence.

records.definition_text: having bright colours
records.learnerexamples_text: a colourful painting; She wears colourful clothes.

records.definition_text: interesting and unusual
records.learnerexamples_text: a colourful character; Computers make our modern life more colourful.

records.definition_text: one of the blocks of print into which a page of a newspaper, magazine, or dictionary is divided
records.learnerexamples_text: I didn't have time to read the whole article - just the first column.; To the editor, I am puzzled by the report which appeared on yesterday's page 2, second column, concerning the Westfield Music Festival.

records.definition_text: a tall, solid, usually stone post which is often used to support a roof or as decoration in a building
records.learnerexamples_text: The roof of the temple was held up by a row of thick stone columns.; Nelson's Column in Trafalgar Square; There are a lot [of] columns outside and inside the restaurant, in Doric [style].

records.definition_text: to tidy your hair using a comb
records.learnerexamples_text: She combed her hair and put on some lipstick.; I've been trying to comb out the knots in her hair.; I want to buy [a] mirror for my room because I need to see myself while I'm combing my hair.

records.definition_text: the mixture you get when two or more things are combined
records.learnerexamples_text: Strawberries and cream - a perfect combination.; A combination of tiredness and boredom caused me to fall asleep.; This drug can be safely used in combination with other medicines.; Her experience and energy are a winning combination in business.; It has the winning combination of adventure in strange, far-off places, scientific discovery and humour.

records.definition_text: to become mixed or joined, or to mix or join things together
records.learnerexamples_text: My wages combined with your savings should just about pay for it.; The band combines jazz rhythms and romantic lyrics.; Boys wear jeans or longer shorts than girls, combined with patterned, cotton shirts.

records.definition_text: to happen
records.learnerexamples_text: Spring has come early.; The worst problems are still/yet to come.; The announcement came at a bad time.; But worse was yet to come!

records.definition_text: to meet someone or find something by chance
records.learnerexamples_text: He came across some of his old love letters in his wife's drawer.; Luckily, I've come across an advertisement of a well-known computer trader.

records.definition_text: to have or achieve a particular position in a race, competition, list, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: She came second in the 100m race.; Z comes after Y in the alphabet.; Which king came after Edward?; April comes before May.

records.definition_text: to go somewhere with someone
records.learnerexamples_text: We're going to the cinema. Do you want to come along?; I'm really expecting you guys to come along.

records.definition_text: to arrive or appear at a place
records.learnerexamples_text: A taxi never comes along when you need one.; Luckily someone came along soon afterwards and they went off to phone for an ambulance which brought us here.

records.definition_text: someone who entertains people by telling jokes
records.learnerexamples_text: Then, he went to London to become a comedian and now he is one of the [most] famous stars [in] that field.

records.definition_text: If a price or a level comes down, it becomes lower.
records.learnerexamples_text: House prices have come down recently.; Inflation is coming down.; The GDP (Gross Domestic Product) has come down from 0.3% to 0.2%.

records.definition_text: to drop to the ground or floor
records.learnerexamples_text: A lot of trees came down in the storm.; Our plane came down in a field.; The snow came down during the night.; Luckily, the curtain came down and the play was postponed.

records.definition_text: to become ill
records.learnerexamples_text: The whole family came down with food poisoning.; I must apologize for writing so late, but my sister came down with flu and I had to visit her.

records.definition_text: entertainment such as a film, play, etc. which is funny
records.learnerexamples_text: His latest film is described as a romantic comedy.; I prefer Shakespeare's comedies to his tragedies.; Everybody agreed to see that comedy with Jim Carrey and I know that you would like it.

records.definition_text: to say what you want to immediately and directly
records.learnerexamples_text: I'll come straight to the point, we've run out of money.; Can you get straight to the point? We need to go home!; I will come straight to the point, Mark. I think you're just killing yourself with your work.

records.definition_text: said to encourage someone to do something, especially to hurry or try harder
records.learnerexamples_text: Come on or we'll be late!; Come on, help me to find it.

records.definition_text: If a book, record, film, etc. comes out, it becomes available for people to buy or see.
records.learnerexamples_text: When does their new album come out?; We're going to se[e] "Blade". It came out just yesterday.

records.definition_text: When the sun, the moon, or a star comes out, it appears in the sky.
records.learnerexamples_text: It's really warm when the sun comes out.; When we were coming back, the sun came out.

records.definition_text: If results or information come out, they are given to people.
records.learnerexamples_text: The exam results come out in August.; The results finally came out at the beginning of October.

records.definition_text: to be a particular total when numbers or amounts are added together
