records.learnerexamples_text: That comes to £50, please.; [If] a bill c[ame] to £1000, you would be shocked and regret what you had done.

records.definition_text: to reach a state, or change to a different state
records.learnerexamples_text: I was sad when the evening came to an end.; I came to the conclusion that the relationship wasn't working.; That was when the Labour party came to power.; That's why I came to the conclusion that the motorb[i]ke, together with anti-smog equipment, is the [only way] to get to work, unless you want [to] spend hours in a traffic jam.

records.definition_text: If a dream or hope comes true, it really happens.
records.learnerexamples_text: I'd always dreamt of owning my own house, but I never thought it would come true.; After all the problems I'd had, Oliver's birth was a dream come true.; I had been dreaming of going to London since I started learning English, and now that my dream had come true, I was overhelmed by joy and feeling very lucky.

records.definition_text: If a dream or hope comes true, it really happens.
records.learnerexamples_text: I'd always dreamt of owning my own house, but I never thought it would come true.; After all the problems I'd had, Oliver's birth was a dream come true.; I had been dreaming of going to London since I started learning English, and now that my dream had come true, I was over[w]helmed by joy and feeling very lucky.

records.definition_text: to move towards someone
records.learnerexamples_text: A young girl came up to me and asked for money.; A tall slim Soc came up and said:- "I will, Daryl old bud." It was James, Daryl's old school friend.

records.definition_text: to be mentioned or talked about in conversation
records.learnerexamples_text: What points came up at the meeting?; From time to time the discussion about keeping animals in zoos comes up.

records.definition_text: When the sun or moon comes up, it rises.
records.learnerexamples_text: We watched the sun come up over the ocean.

records.definition_text: to suggest or think of an idea or plan
records.searchterms_text: come;come up with sth;come up with sth
records.learnerexamples_text: She's come up with some amazing scheme to double her income.; Together with my teacher we came up with the idea of asking you to come to the college in order to give a talk about your latest book and about the experiences you have had as a novelist.

records.definition_text: a pleasant feeling of being relaxed and free from pain
records.learnerexamples_text: She evidently dresses for comfort.; It's a little too hot for comfort.; Now you can watch the latest films in the comfort of your own room.; When the weather is bad, I need the comfort of my car.

records.definition_text: relaxed and free from pain
records.learnerexamples_text: Are you comfortable perched on that seat?; I don't feel comfortable in high heels.; Do sit down and make yourself comfortable.; But when she started the lesson, everybody was comfortable and relaxed.

records.definition_text: If you are comfortable in a situation, you do not have any worries about it.
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't feel comfortable about leaving the children here alone.; Those children maybe they don't feel comfortable away from home.

records.definition_text: in a comfortable way
records.learnerexamples_text: We slept very comfortably that night.; I was sitting comfortably on the couch watching TV when suddenly all the lights went out, [and] everything became silent.

records.definition_text: funny
records.learnerexamples_text: a comic actor/performance; I think it's a bit long for a comic film (3 hours!!) but it's very [funny]: you must see it.

records.definition_text: a mark (,) used to separate parts of a sentence, or to separate the items in a list
records.learnerexamples_text: Put a comma before his name.

records.definition_text: an order to do something, especially one given by a soldier
records.learnerexamples_text: He hated being in the army because he had to obey commands.; When I give the command, fire!; Under the red lights of his command room, the first question that the captain wanted to a[sk] was to know if the boat was safe.

records.definition_text: knowledge of a subject, especially a language
records.learnerexamples_text: She had a good command of Italian.; Besides, I have a good command of French and I speak English fluently, which might be useful during the voyage around the world.

records.definition_text: something that you say or write that expresses your opinion
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't want any comments on/about my new haircut, thank you!; Tell us what you think - go to our web page and post/leave/add a comment.; He made negative comments to the press.; Write me a comment.

records.definition_text: to make a comment
records.learnerexamples_text: My mum always comments on what I'm wearing.; He commented that the two essays were rather similar.; The official refused to comment on the matter.; I will only comment on some points, the others may be viewed as agreed upon.

records.definition_text: the activities involved in buying and selling things
records.learnerexamples_text: the world of commerce and industry; In the old days, when the only mean[s] of transport were horses, there were many difficulties in communication between people, in commerce, [and] in life generally.

records.definition_text: related to buying and selling things
records.learnerexamples_text: a commercial organization/success; The commercial future of the company looks very promising.; Unfortunately, as long as their private life is interesting for ordinary people and it brings commercial gain to publishers, journalists and photographers, famous people will just have to get use[d] to this living "under a microscope".

records.definition_text: an advertisement on the radio, on television, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: I tend to switch off during the commercials.; Nearly every one of us has to confess that on some days it is simply relaxing to sit in front of the TV just watching without using the brain at all, but we have to wonder if television is also able to educate us, especially regarding the senseless commercials.

records.definition_text: to do something that is considered wrong, or that is illegal
records.learnerexamples_text: He was sent to prison for a crime that he didn't commit.; to commit suicide; to commit a crime/an offence/murder; She is willing to be [a] witness for the prosecution and states that her husband [was] not with her at the time the crime was committed.

records.definition_text: when you are willing to give your time and energy to something that you believe in, or a promise or firm decision to do something
records.learnerexamples_text: She is known chiefly for her commitment to human rights.; I'd like to thank the staff for having shown such commitment.; I really admire your stamina, your commitment and your eagerness to pursue a career as one of the youngest vice presidents ever in the company (and the only female I guess), but is it really worth it?

records.definition_text: something that you must do or deal with that takes your time
records.learnerexamples_text: family/work commitments; I've got too many commitments at the moment to do an evening class.; Please tell me also the terms of [the] possible job so I can plan my future work commitments.

records.definition_text: a small group of people chosen to represent a larger organization and either make decisions or collect information for it
records.learnerexamples_text: She is on the school's development committee.; The local council have just set up a committee to study recycling.; I'm pleased to help and to present these films to the club committee.

records.definition_text: happening often or existing in large numbers
records.learnerexamples_text: It's quite common to see couples who dress alike.; The surname 'Smith' is very common in Britain.; The city is so noisy and it's possible that you [will] get lost, it's very common.

records.definition_text: belonging to or shared by two or more people or things
records.learnerexamples_text: a common goal/interest; English has some features common to many languages.; I invited her to dinner for all her trouble and we found out that we have a lot of common interests.

records.definition_text: something that a lot of people know
records.learnerexamples_text: It's common knowledge that he spent time in jail.; It is common knowledge that such attention [in the mass-media] inevitably tells on relationships in the family.

records.definition_text: something that a lot of people know
records.learnerexamples_text: It's common knowledge that he spent time in jail.; It is common knowledge that such attention [in the mass-media] inevitably tells on relationships in the family.

records.definition_text: the natural ability to be practical and to make good decisions
records.learnerexamples_text: The children shouldn't be in any danger as long as they use their common sense.; In fact she is very nice, funny, [and] full of common sense.

records.definition_text: to share information with others by speaking, writing, moving your body or using other signals
records.learnerexamples_text: We can now communicate instantly with people on the other side of the world.; Has the news been communicated to the staff yet?; Unable to speak a word of the language, he communicated with his hands.; Finally, I decided to join a new English class in order to improve my English because [a] few weeks ago I met someone who is really interesting, so I would like to be able to communicate properly with him.

records.definition_text: to be understood by someone when you tell them about your feelings and thoughts
records.learnerexamples_text: He can't communicate with his parents.; I think I can communicate with children and make them happy.

records.definition_text: the act of communicating with people
records.learnerexamples_text: Television is an increasingly important means of communication.; We are in direct communication with Moscow.; With an hour's walk to the nearest telephone, communication is difficult.; There's very little communication between mother and daughter.; a course on communication skills

records.definition_text: open and willing to talk to people
records.learnerexamples_text: She's never very communicative in the morning.; First of all, I would like to say I am a very communicative person and I enjoy being surrounded by many people.

records.definition_text: a group of people with the same interests, way of life, nationality, job, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: the black/white/Chinese/Jewish community; the business community; As a member of our academic community, and a representative of [the] student's senate, I'm very glad to hear that our college will have a surplus in its annual budget.

records.definition_text: the people living in one particular area
records.learnerexamples_text: a rural/small community; He's well-known in the local community.; Drug trafficking is a matter of considerable concern for the entire international community.; He supported some projects in our community.

records.definition_text: someone you spend a lot of time with or go somewhere with
records.learnerexamples_text: a travelling companion; Dan has been her constant companion these past ten years.; Jane and her companion felt absolutely foolish and muttered something about a wrong address.

records.definition_text: when you are with a person or people, or the person or people you are with
records.learnerexamples_text: I just enjoy his company.; Do you want company or would you rather go on your own?; I didn't realize you had company.; Margot came to stay for a week as company for my mother while I was away.; Fortunately a friend of mine came with me for company.

records.definition_text: to examine the ways in which two people or things are different
records.learnerexamples_text: If you compare house prices in the two areas, it's quite amazing how different they are.; That seems expensive - have you compared prices in other shops?; Compare some recent work with your older stuff and you'll see how much you've improved.; Teachers always used to compare me with my sister.; Our lives are so different, it's interesting to compare.

records.definition_text: used when saying how one person or thing is different from another
records.learnerexamples_text: This road is quite busy compared to ours.; Children seem to learn more interesting things compared with when we were at school.; To my surprise it was very cheap compared with other restaurants.

records.definition_text: when two or more people or things are compared
records.learnerexamples_text: They made a comparison of different countries' eating habits.;  By/In comparison with the French, the British eat far less fish.; I always drink fresh coffee, not instant. There's no comparison.; Nowadays we can see a very different world from the one our grandparents were living in. Whereas they used to talk about how their daily life had changed in comparison with previous generations', we remain astonished [at] how our li[v]es are changing frenetically.

records.definition_text: to try to be more successful than someone or something else
records.learnerexamples_text: It's difficult for a small supermarket to compete against/with the big supermarkets.; Both girls compete for their father's attention.; Most small cities like ours think that we have to compete with big cities by building new houses and shopping centres.

records.definition_text: to take part in a race or competition
records.learnerexamples_text: She's competing for a place in next year's Olympics.; Are you competing in the 100 metres?; There's gonna be a competition and I want to compete, but you know that my bicycle is a mess and very old.

records.definition_text: when someone, or a company, is trying to win something or be more successful than someone else
records.learnerexamples_text: Competition for jobs is intense.; There's a lot of competition between computer companies.; The two companies are in competition with each other.; Different opening times mean[s] competition between the shops.

records.definition_text: involving competition
records.learnerexamples_text: competitive sports; a highly competitive industry; Nowadays people live in [a] very competitive society.

records.definition_text: wanting very much to win or be more successful than other people
records.learnerexamples_text: She's very competitive.; I think that I am a very competitive player.

records.definition_text: as good as or better than other prices, services, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: They offer good quality goods at competitive prices.; I stayed at Riverside Hotel w[h]ich [is] great value because of the food and the competitive prices they offer.

records.definition_text: a person, team or company that is competing against others
records.learnerexamples_text: How many competitors took part in the race?; Their prices are better than any of their competitors.; The last one I saw was called 'Spelling' and it was a kind of quiz where the competitors had to spell difficult words fast and finish at a certain time.

records.definition_text: to say that something is wrong or that you are annoyed about something
records.learnerexamples_text: Lots of people have complained about the noise.; He's always complaining!; He complained that she never listened to him.; If the service was so bad why didn't you complain to the manager?; If we are bad, they complain to our manager or they tell the head office.

records.definition_text: to tell other people that something is making you feel ill
records.learnerexamples_text: She's been complaining of a headache all day.; I asked her if he [had] complained of any pains or aches?

records.definition_text: when someone says that something is wrong or not satisfactory
records.learnerexamples_text: We've received a complaint from one of our listeners about offensive language.; I've made a complaint to the police about the noise.; We've had complaints that you've been playing your radio too loud.; I hope you give my complaint serious consideration and I would be very pleased if you would print a correction in the next issue of your magazine.

records.definition_text: with all the parts
records.learnerexamples_text: the complete works of Oscar Wilde; The report comes complete with diagrams and colour photographs.; Sun, sand and romance - her holiday was complete.; I can send you [a] complete map.

records.definition_text: very great or to the largest degree possible
records.learnerexamples_text: It was a complete waste of time.; He's a complete idiot!; I made a complete and utter mess of it!; It was a complete disaster!

records.definition_text: in every way or as much as possible
records.learnerexamples_text: I completely forgot I'd said I would call him.; He'd completely changed and I didn't recognize him.; I agree with you completely.; She's completely mad.; In the middle of the journey there was one of [those] summer rain [showers] and we got completely wet.

records.definition_text: involving a lot of different but connected parts in a way that is difficult to understand
records.learnerexamples_text: a complex network of roads; a complex procedure; The film's plot was so complex that I couldn't follow it.; It took us two weeks to modify the results in a very complex operation.

records.definition_text: involving a lot of different parts, in a way that is difficult to understand
records.learnerexamples_text: complicated instructions; I had to fill in this really complicated form.; The rules are rather complicated to follow.; The relationship is a bit complicated. He's my mother's cousin's daughter's child.; Life is getting easier but more complicated - I could have written a letter in a bottle but waiting for the answer would take a decade, now it's just a click of a button.

records.definition_text: to be the parts that something consists of
records.learnerexamples_text: The committee was composed of elected leaders and citizens.; It is composed of more than 50 members and they have various taste[s] [in] film: old and modern, comedy, action and so on.

records.definition_text: to write a piece of music
records.learnerexamples_text: Who composed the music for the film?; I've been composing music on a computer for over five years and I have a lot of knowledge when it comes to hardware.

records.definition_text: someone who writes music
records.learnerexamples_text: a famous composer; I also met a lot of famous composers, singers and even my favourit[e] violin player, Ann Sophie Mutter, because I had to interview them.

records.definition_text: a short piece of writing about a particular subject, done by a student
records.learnerexamples_text: a 500-word composition; I have [to] do a composition in English to cover the work I missed.

records.definition_text: a piece of music that someone has written
records.learnerexamples_text: This concerto is one of her later compositions.; He sang Schubert's "Die Winterreise" although it's already Spring - this composition [can be heard in] every season.

records.definition_text: to agree to something that is not exactly what you want
records.learnerexamples_text: In a relationship, both people have to compromise.; I'm not going to compromise on quality.; The famous stars and the journalists should compromise and respect each other's rights.

records.definition_text: when you agree to something which is not exactly what you want
records.learnerexamples_text: It is hoped that a compromise will be reached in today's talks.; You've both got to be willing to make compromises.; In a compromise between management and unions, a 4% pay rise was agreed in return for an increase in productivity.; I hope that we'll find a compromise.

records.definition_text: If something is compulsory, you must do it because of a rule or law.
records.learnerexamples_text: Wearing seat belts in cars is compulsory by law.; Swimming was compulsory at my school.; We have asked participants to wear a typical traditional dress/suit from their country - of course, this is not compulsory but everyone is warmly invited to do so.

records.definition_text: to think very carefully about something you are doing and nothing else
records.learnerexamples_text: Come on, concentrate! We haven't got all day to do this.; I can't concentrate on my work with all that noise.; I'm going to concentrate on my writing for a while.; I can't concentrate on studying.

records.definition_text: the ability to think carefully about something you are doing and nothing else
records.learnerexamples_text: The noise outside made concentration difficult.; There was a look of intense concentration on her face.; I find that yoga improves my powers of concentration.; I found it hard to follow what the teacher was saying, and eventually I lost concentration.; First of all, in my opinion, watching a film is more relaxing, because you don't have to concentrate to[o] much on it. You only have to watch the screen, while books require more concentration.

records.definition_text: a principle or idea
records.learnerexamples_text: the concept of free speech; I failed to grasp the film's central concept.; I had been trying very hard to get the point of the concept.

records.definition_text: to be important to someone or to involve someone directly
records.learnerexamples_text: Matters of pollution and the environment concern us all.; There are one or two other matters that don't concern you.; Fitness and health are two important issues in life which concern all of us.

records.definition_text: to be about a particular subject
records.learnerexamples_text: The next item on the agenda concerns staffing levels.; Your other question concerns clothes.

records.definition_text: when you feel worried or nervous about something, or something that makes you feel worried
records.learnerexamples_text: Concern for the safety of the two missing teenagers is growing.; There's a lot of public concern about/over dangerous toxins recently found in food.; The situation has been causing concern for some time now.; My concern is that you're not getting enough work done.; There's a matter of some concern that I have to discuss with you.

records.definition_text: something that is important to you, or when something is important
records.learnerexamples_text: Our primary concern is safety.; My concern is what present to buy for Mr Brown.

records.definition_text: worried
records.learnerexamples_text: He's very concerned about her health.; I'm concerned that sales figures haven't improved; Concerned parents have complained about the dangerous playground.; We are getting more and more concerned about our health and how to get and keep fit nowadays.

records.definition_text: about
records.learnerexamples_text: I've had a letter from the tax authorities concerning my tax payments.; I am writing in reply to your letter concerning the prize I won in your competition, which is two weeks at Camp California in the U.S.A.

records.definition_text: the opinion you have after considering all the information about something
records.learnerexamples_text: At first I thought he was a bit rude but I've come to/reached the conclusion that he's just shy.; Dear Jack and Ben: I['ve] been thinking about your last letter for quite a long time and I came to the following conclusion.

records.definition_text: a very hard building material made by mixing together cement, sand, small stones and water
records.learnerexamples_text: reinforced concrete; a concrete floor/path; a grey concrete building; Some of our children, brought up in modern cities, in a world of concrete, cars, motorways and supermarkets, when asked: "What is a fish?" are only able to answer: "a square piece of white flesh we take from the freezer".

records.definition_text: the particular state that something or someone is in
records.learnerexamples_text: My bike's a few years old, but it's in really good condition.; They left the flat in a terrible condition - there was mess everywhere.; He's in no condition to drive home.; It's very beautiful and in good condition.

records.definition_text: an illness
records.learnerexamples_text: a medical condition; He suffers from a rare heart condition.; Besides, all the fats we eat every day plus the accumulated stress of a job, makes us the perfect candidates [for] a heart condition.

records.definition_text: the physical situation that someone or something is in and affected by
records.learnerexamples_text: The prisoners were kept in the most appalling conditions.; Severe weather conditions are making driving difficult.;  What are their living/working conditions like?;  Under what conditions do plants grow best?; Althoug[h] I had fun the weather conditions were horrible - it was raining all the time and the road was too wet to ride on.

records.definition_text: to organize and perform a particular activity
records.learnerexamples_text: We are conducting a survey to find out what our customers think of their local bus service.; The experiments were conducted by scientists in New York.; This is based on a questionnair[e] conducted in the school and our English department's investigation.

records.definition_text: to stand in front of a group of musicians and control their performance
records.learnerexamples_text: The orchestra was conducted by Charles Miller.; The o[r]chestra conducted by Mr Miller was just superb.

records.definition_text: someone who stands in front of a group of musicians or singers and controls their performance
records.learnerexamples_text: a famous conductor; I am fifty five years old and have experience [as] a conductor of a choir.

records.definition_text: a large, formal meeting, often lasting a few days, where people discuss their work, politics, subjects they are studying, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: a conference on women's rights; the annual sales conference; They frequently hold conferences at the hotel.; I'm speaking at/attending a conference next week.; As you know, I went to Canada in order to take part in an environmental conference.

records.definition_text: to admit that you have done something wrong or something that you feel guilty or bad about
records.learnerexamples_text: She confessed to her husband that she had sold her wedding ring.; He has confessed to the murder.; He confessed to sleeping through most of the film.; I have to confess, I was a little confused at first.; I found it all very confusing, I must confess.

records.definition_text: when you admit that you have done something wrong or illegal
records.learnerexamples_text: He made a full confession to the police.; I have a confession to make - I've lost that book you lent me.; I also have a confession to make.

records.definition_text: when you are certain of your ability to do things well
records.learnerexamples_text: He's got the confidence to walk into a room of strangers and immediately start a conversation.; The training has given me the confidence to deal with any situation that arises.; She has ability but she lacks confidence.; I have every/complete confidence in her. She'll be perfect for the job.; As a result of such a bad appearance he lacks confidence.

records.definition_text: certain about your ability to do things well
records.learnerexamples_text: Be a bit more confident in yourself!; It was a confident performance.; He feels confident of winning.; But I soon felt more confident, as I saw what activities they were doing: some people were playing tennis, others were sunbathing in the garden.

records.definition_text: being certain that something will happen
records.learnerexamples_text: Are you confident that enough people will attend the event?; They don't sound confident about the future of the industry.; All in all, I'm confident that a solution will be found and our town will soon regain its former attractive look.

records.definition_text: with confidence or in a confident way
records.learnerexamples_text: Try to act confidently, even if you feel nervous.; I am quite [a] hard worker and I can confidently say that I am quite [a] reliable person.

records.definition_text: to make an arrangement or meeting certain, often by telephone or in writing
records.learnerexamples_text: Six people have confirmed that they will be attending and ten haven't replied yet.; Flights should be confirmed 48 hours before departure.; I've accepted the job over the phone, but I haven't confirmed in writing yet.; I just want to confirm that we're going to the ABC cinema tonight.

records.definition_text: to say or show that something is true
records.learnerexamples_text: His wife confirmed that he had left the house that morning.; The leader's speech was impressive and confirmed her faith in the party.; Besides, it was confirmed by scientists that consum[er]ism may develop [in]to a compulsion.

records.definition_text: a statement, often written, that an arrangement or meeting is certain
records.learnerexamples_text: a letter of confirmation; We've only had five confirmations for the conference so far.; We will send you written confirmation of our offer shortly.; I look forward to receiving your confirmation.

records.definition_text: serious disagreement between people with opposing opinions or principles
records.learnerexamples_text: There was a lot of conflict between the two parties.; The Government was in conflict with the unions over pay.; It was an unpopular policy and caused a number of conflicts within the party.; As you know I was in conflict with myself, should I buy a computer or a bicycle?

records.definition_text: fighting between two or more groups of people or countries
records.learnerexamples_text: armed conflict; In these years, Europe was in conflict with China, which meant war.

records.definition_text: to think that one person or thing is another person or thing
records.learnerexamples_text: I think you're confusing me with my sister - we look quite similar.; It's easy to confuse his films, because he tends to use the same actors.; I had confused the two words, "uvas", which means grapes, and "huevos", which means eggs and said "huevas", which unfortunately means testicles, instead...

records.definition_text: to make someone unable to think clearly, or to make something difficult to understand
records.learnerexamples_text: You're confusing him! Tell him slowly and one thing at a time.; Stop confusing the issue!; When the corpse was found he - successfully - tried to confuse Mrs. Marple, Scotland Yard and the members of the family where he was the doctor.

records.definition_text: not clear
records.learnerexamples_text: The witnesses gave confused accounts of what happened.; What can a child [think], hearing such confused explanations about animals that don't live where they s[h]ould live, that don't live how they should live.

records.definition_text: unable to think clearly or to understand something
records.learnerexamples_text: People keep telling me different things and I'm getting very confused.; Sorry, I'm a bit confused - are we meeting here or in town?; She seemed a bit confused about the arrangements.; At first I felt very confused.

records.definition_text: difficult to understand
records.learnerexamples_text: I found the instructions very confusing.; As a secret agent I was prepared [for] this sort of thing but it was surprising and confusing.

records.definition_text: when people do not understand what is happening, what they should do or who someone or something is
records.learnerexamples_text: There seems to be some confusion about/over who is actually giving the talk.; This caused some confusion because the courses were not completely prepared.

records.definition_text: a situation, often with a lot of activity and noise, in which people do not know what to do
records.learnerexamples_text: In the confusion after the bomb blast, I lost my bag.; In the confusion someone pushed her against the wall and she hurt her shoulder.

records.definition_text: a feeling of not being able to think clearly
records.learnerexamples_text: He could see the confusion on Marion's face.; Then I thought he recognised my confusion; therefore, he opened the box, picking up something from [it].

records.definition_text: to tell someone that you are happy because they have done something good or something good has happened to them
records.learnerexamples_text: I was just congratulating Ceri on winning her race.; Needless to say, everybody congratulated her and she spent all evening answering questions such as: "Why did you choose water jumping?" or "Isn't it difficult for a teenager to train five hours a day and to study?"

records.definition_text: a word such as 'and', 'but', 'while' or 'although' that connects words, phrases and clauses in a sentence
to join or be joined with something else
records.learnerexamples_text: Can I connect my printer to your computer?; Where does the cooker connect (up) to the electricity?; Has the water/electricity/gas/telephone been connected in your new place yet?; I want to buy [a] computer to play games and connect to [the] Internet as well as listen to music in my free time.

records.definition_text: something that joins things together
records.learnerexamples_text: Many companies now offer free connection to the Internet.; Moreover, some portable phones have a connection to the web, so it is easy to read newspapers if one hasn't enough money to buy [them].

records.definition_text: when someone or something is involved with or related to someone or something else
records.learnerexamples_text: The connection between smoking and heart disease is well known.; He has denied having any connection with the terrorists.; They're sisters, are they? I knew their surname was the same, but I never made the connection.; If you are aware of the connection between food and health you can start changing your eating habits.

records.definition_text: a train, bus or aircraft that leaves a short time after another arrives, so people can continue their journey
records.learnerexamples_text: The train was half an hour late and I missed my connection.; Because of bad bus connections it's not easy to get there.

records.definition_text: when someone is awake and can think and notice things
records.learnerexamples_text: He lost consciousness for several minutes.; He never regained consciousness after the accident.; He lost consciousness and lay there on the floor just in front of me.

records.definition_text: the result of a particular action or situation, especially a bad result
records.learnerexamples_text: The ship sank with disastrous consequences.; Excessive drinking can have serious consequences for a person's health.; If you neglect your relationships like that, you'll suffer the consequences.; My work was the best because I drew a big drawing about [the] consequences of us not caring [for the] environment.

records.definition_text: as a result
records.learnerexamples_text: I spent most of my money in the first week and consequently had very little to eat by the end of the holiday.;  Because of their job or school, people are much more stress[ed]. Consequently, they don't take [the] time to eat correctly.

records.definition_text: the protection of nature
records.learnerexamples_text: wildlife conservation; conservation groups; I think that trying to save the wildlife in your area is a great aim because you don't have conservation areas and people can easily go hunting without telling anyone and in that way they destroy the wildlife.

records.definition_text: to think carefully about something, often before you decide what to do
records.learnerexamples_text: Have you considered what you'll do if you don't get the job?; We're considering selling the house.; She's being considered for the job.; I'd like some time to consider before I make a decision.; I must say thanks to you for your birthday money for me to buy a DVD. After considering [what to buy], I decided to buy 'The Legend of Narnias'.

records.definition_text: large or important enough to be noticed
records.learnerexamples_text: It's a considerable sum of money.; The effect on the region has been considerable.; I have considerable experience as a worker on [a] farm, having worked on my father's farm from 1956 to 1986.

records.definition_text: in a way that is large or important enough to be noticed
records.learnerexamples_text: Rates of pay vary considerably.; He's considerably fatter than he was when I knew him.; The departures are at 8 am. and 10 a.m. daily, but I suggest that your group be there at the time of the first departure because it is considerably less crowded.

records.definition_text: when you think about something very carefully
records.learnerexamples_text: After careful consideration, we decided to offer her the job.; The whole matter needs to be given careful consideration.; Please give this your careful consideration.

records.definition_text: something that you have to think about when you make decisions or plans
records.learnerexamples_text: Safety is our main consideration.; Cost, of course, is another consideration.; The next consideration is the activities.

records.definition_text: used for saying that you have a particular opinion about something, because of a particular fact about it
records.learnerexamples_text: She did really well, considering how little experience she'd had.; Considering the weather, we got here quite quickly.; Considering all the above, I think that your article was completely misleading.

records.definition_text: to have a particular opinion about someone or something
records.searchterms_text: consider;consider sb/sth (to be) sth;consider sb/sth to be sth;considered;considering;considers
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't consider myself to be a great athlete.; I consider myself to be punctual, hard-working, reliable and responsible.

records.definition_text: to be made of or formed from something
records.learnerexamples_text: The team consists of four Europeans and two Americans.; It's a simple dish to prepare, consisting mainly of rice and vegetables.; Our team consists of 15 girls, who are all between 16 and 18.

records.definition_text: one of the speech sounds or letters of the alphabet which is not a vowel
happening a lot or all the time
records.learnerexamples_text: He's in constant trouble with the police.; These machines are in constant use.; As for me, constant practice in [the] English language is quite important, it is the essence of my life.

records.definition_text: all the time or often
records.learnerexamples_text: He's constantly changing his mind.; She has the television on constantly.; I stood up and walked around the house, constantly bumping into things!

records.definition_text: to build something from several parts
records.learnerexamples_text: The building was constructed in 1930.; The walls are constructed of concrete.; You need this information to construct a basic sentence.; Using some wood, we constructed small seats and tables.

records.definition_text: the work of building something, especially houses, offices, bridges, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: the construction industry; The next decade saw the construction of many more office blocks.; She works in construction.; This website is currently under construction.; It [is] worth mentioning that a huge gym is under construction.

records.definition_text: The construction of a sentence or phrase is the way the words are arranged.
records.learnerexamples_text: Pay attention to sentence construction and check word order.

records.definition_text: something that is built
records.learnerexamples_text: a large steel construction; It would be a pity to build a modern construction there.

records.definition_text: someone who advises people on a particular subject
records.learnerexamples_text: a management/financial consultant; a firm of public relations consultants; I work in a bank as a consultant.

records.definition_text: to eat or drink something
records.learnerexamples_text: People generally consume far too much sugar.; People who eat fresh vegetables and meat tend to have good digestion and tend to consume less salt.

records.definition_text: a person who buys goods or services for their own use
records.learnerexamples_text: The new telephone rates will affect all consumers including businesses.; consumer rights/advice; Some people might argue that this system is convenient for consumers as they can go shopping whenever they would like to, and it makes the shops more secure against burglary and vandalism since the shops are packed with people inside.

records.definition_text: communication with someone, especially by speaking or writing to them regularly
records.learnerexamples_text: Do you still keep in contact with Peter?; I'm still in contact with Sarah - we write a couple of times a year.; There isn't enough contact between teachers and parents.; I'd hate to lose contact with my old school friends.; If you manage to make contact with her, do let me know.

records.definition_text: If one thing contains another, it has it inside it.
records.learnerexamples_text: a box containing a diamond ring; How much liquid do you think this bottle contains?; I've lost a file containing a lot of important documents.; So he asks the man if that suitcase is his, [and] the man runs to get it but the security guards don't let him until he shouts: "It contains my daughter's wedding dress!"

records.definition_text: to have something as a part
records.learnerexamples_text: Does this drink contain alcohol?; Try to avoid foods which contain a lot of fat.; The allegations contained in this report are very serious.; [The] food was not wonderful, but it was healthy and contained a lot of vitamins.

records.definition_text: an object such as a box or a bottle that is used for holding something
records.learnerexamples_text: an airtight container; a plastic drinks container; As a result, a mountain of plastic containers and harmful chemical fluid is [ruin]ing mother earth.

records.definition_text: existing or happening now
records.learnerexamples_text: contemporary music/literature/art/fashion; Although it was written hundreds of years ago, it still has a contemporary feel to it.; I always read a lot of different magazin[e]s and know a lot about contemporary writers.

records.definition_text: pleased with your situation and not hoping for change or improvement
records.learnerexamples_text: He seems fairly content with life.; They're content to socialize with a very small circle of people.; He looked really content and happy.

records.definition_text: the ideas that are contained in a piece of writing, a speech or a film
records.learnerexamples_text: the content of the article; It's a very stylish and beautiful film, but it rather lacks content.; We've discussed the unusual form of the book - now, what about the content?; I suggest explaining the content of the film.

records.definition_text: everything that is contained within something
records.learnerexamples_text: The contents of his bag spilled all over the floor.; He hardly needed to open the letter because he already knew the contents.; He looked for the owner and gave him the suitcase. He also asked about its contents.

records.definition_text: the information or ideas that are written in a book, letter, document, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: the contents of his will; In the first lesson the teacher explaine[d] the rules and [the] contents of the course, and finally we d[id] a group activity.

records.definition_text: a list in a book that tells you what different parts the book contains
records.learnerexamples_text: a table of contents

records.definition_text: a competition to do better than other people, usually in which prizes are given
records.learnerexamples_text: a dance/sports contest; She's won a lot of beauty contests.; Next week there will be a "Freestyle Battle", a rap contest, where [a] rapper can mess with others.

records.definition_text: all the facts, opinions, etc. relating to a particular thing or event
records.learnerexamples_text: This small battle is very important in the context of Scottish history.; It is important to see all the fighting and bloodshed in his plays in historical context.; It is interesting to see wild animals in their natural surroundings but for a number of reasons this is mostly impossible. In this context, I think a zoo is a good alternative.

records.definition_text: one of the seven main areas of land on the Earth, such as Africa, Asia, Europe or South America
records.learnerexamples_text: the North American continent; Asia and Africa are the two biggest continents.; Brazil is a large country, almost as big as a continent.

records.definition_text: to start doing or saying something again, after stopping for a short period
records.learnerexamples_text: We'll have to continue this discussion tomorrow.; It's getting late - why don't we continue tomorrow?; After stopping for a quick snack, they continued on their way.; He paused for a moment to listen and then continued eating.; We continued our journey early in the morning.

records.definition_text: to keep happening, existing or doing something
records.learnerexamples_text: It continued to snow heavily for two days.; If the rain continues, we'll have to cancel tonight's plans.; The article continues on page ten.; I'll continue working until the end of June.; Shall I continue with this task?

records.definition_text: being the form of a verb used to show that an action is continuing to happen
records.learnerexamples_text: the present/past continuous; The lesson was about the present continuous form.

records.definition_text: happening or existing without stopping
records.learnerexamples_text: continuous pain; My computer makes a continuous low buzzing noise.; A continuous white line in the middle of the road means no overtaking.; Since the development of nuclear weapons, the Earth's fate has been in continuous danger.

records.definition_text: without stopping
records.learnerexamples_text: You can't work continuously for six hours without a break!; They continuously claim that [the] destruction of the environment is totally all human beings' responsibility.

records.definition_text: a legal agreement between two people, two organizations or a person and an organization
records.learnerexamples_text: a contract of employment; a temporary/permanent contract; My solicitor is drawing up a contract.; Don't sign/enter into any contract before examining its conditions carefully.; He went to the 1994 World Cup in the USA and Brazil's victory helped him to sign a contract to play in Holland.

records.definition_text: an obvious difference between two or more things
records.learnerexamples_text: The contrast between their lifestyles couldn't be greater.; The busy north coast of the island is in sharp contrast to the peaceful south.; The contrast between the wild mountains and the crowded but charm[ing] beach on the ocean shore would have pleased you.

records.definition_text: to give something, especially money, in order to provide or achieve something together with other people
records.learnerexamples_text: Are you going to contribute towards Jack's leaving present?; Her family have contributed £50, 000 to the fund.; Do come to the meeting if you feel you have something to contribute.; Furthermore, it is unfair to judge other performers as second-rate, as they did their best to contribute.

records.definition_text: something that you do or give to help produce or achieve something, or to help make something successful
records.learnerexamples_text: This invention made a major contribution to road safety.; She didn't make much of a contribution at today's meeting, did she?; All contributions, no matter how small, will be much appreciated.; a generous contribution to charity; I am willing to make a significant contribution to the club.

records.definition_text: to make someone or something do what you want
records.learnerexamples_text: If you can't control your dog, put it on a lead!; This switch controls the temperature.; The movie was about a ring which [was] found in the river and used to control the world.

records.definition_text: to stop yourself expressing strong emotions or behaving in a silly way
records.learnerexamples_text: You're going to have to learn to control your temper.; I tried to control myself and started to speak politely and in a friendly way.

records.definition_text: to limit the number, amount or increase of something
records.learnerexamples_text: Fire crews struggled to control the blaze.; No attempt was made to control the spread of the disease.; We have to control the [number of] cars, we can't allow as many car[s] as we drive [now].

records.definition_text: to rule or govern an area
records.learnerexamples_text: The whole area is controlled by rebel forces.; BRAVE NEW WORLD The part of the book I have read and I remember best is when John, the savage, comes into the New World [State] controlled by several World Controllers from the savage reservation.

records.definition_text: when you make someone or something do what you want, or the power to do this
records.learnerexamples_text: She's got no control over that child.; He lost control of the vehicle.; The police are in control of the situation. ; Ap[p]arently he lost control of the wheel, so the car crashed into a tree.

records.definition_text: a switch or other device used to operate a machine such as a vehicle
records.learnerexamples_text: Where's the volume control on your stereo?; The main instruments are in the centre of the control panel.; The captain sat at the controls of the aircraft.; He touched a switch on the control panel and heard that characteristic hiss.

records.definition_text: a rule or law that limits something
records.learnerexamples_text: He wants the government to impose strict controls on dog ownership.; [It is important] to find a way to regulate the information show[n] [o]n the internet, because right now there is no control over the information.

records.definition_text: a place where something official, usually a document, is checked
records.learnerexamples_text: passport/immigration control; I kissed my parents and went to passport control.

records.definition_text: causing disagreement or discussion
records.learnerexamples_text: a controversial issue/decision/speech/figure; The book was very controversial.; From my point of view it is a very controversial issue.

records.definition_text: the quality of being convenient
records.learnerexamples_text: the convenience of credit cards;  I like the convenience of living so close to the shops.; I think the first reason is its convenience. [...] Just by sitting in front of it, you can enjoy TV program[me]s.

records.definition_text: easy to use or suiting your plans well
records.learnerexamples_text: We could meet at either place - whichever is more convenient for you.; A bike's a very convenient way of getting around.; I find it more convenient to be able to do my banking by phone.; What would be a convenient time for me to come round?; If it would be possible for you, I can attend another class at any time which is convenient for you.

records.definition_text: near or easy to get to
records.learnerexamples_text: My new house is more convenient for the station.; It is near the train station [so] it is very convenient to get there.

records.definition_text: in a way that is convenient
records.learnerexamples_text: The house is conveniently situated near the station and the shops.; First of all, your group has been booked into the Palace Hotel, which is conveniently situated in the centre of Nymegen.

records.definition_text: traditional and ordinary
records.learnerexamples_text: conventional behaviour/attitudes/clothes; conventional medicine/farming; I find his art rather dull and conventional.; The accommodation wasn't bad, however our rooms were quite small and conventional.

records.definition_text: to change the appearance, form, or purpose of something
records.learnerexamples_text: Could we convert the small bedroom into a second bathroom?; What's the formula for converting pounds into kilos?; Even some medieval castles have been converted into museums.

records.definition_text: to persuade someone or make them certain
records.learnerexamples_text: She tried to convince me that I needed a new car.; I hope this will convince you to change your mind.; He managed to convince the jury of his innocence.; She was the one who convinced me to go, and I am glad she did.

records.definition_text: certain
records.learnerexamples_text: My boyfriend says I'd enjoy a walking holiday, but I'm not convinced.; I'm convinced (that) she is lying.; I'm convinced that I would benefit from this experience in the future.

records.definition_text: slightly cold, but not too cold
records.learnerexamples_text: cool water; a nice cool breeze; Sometimes a cool wind blows [in Bodrum].

records.definition_text: to become less hot, or to make something become less hot
records.learnerexamples_text: Allow the bread to cool before slicing it.; In the summer many people were delighted by fountains which cooled the air.

records.definition_text: to become less hot, or to make someone or something become less hot
records.searchterms_text: cool;cool down/off (sb/sth) or cool (sb/sth) down/off;cool down/off sb/sth or cool sb/sth down/off
records.learnerexamples_text: She waited until her coffee had cooled down and then took a sip.; We went for a swim to cool off.; The pool is a very popular place to cool down [in].

records.definition_text: to become calmer, or to make someone become calmer
records.searchterms_text: cool;cool down/off (sb/sth) or cool (sb/sth) down/off;cool down/off sb/sth or cool sb/sth down/off
records.learnerexamples_text: Just leave her to cool off and then talk to her.; It seemed to me that you were stressed. If I were you, I would cool down a little.

records.definition_text: to help someone or do what they ask
records.learnerexamples_text: I find it very hard to dress my two-year-old when she refuses to cooperate.; Moreover, I am in favour of rules at school because it is very important for children to learn how to cooperate with others.

records.definition_text: to work together with someone in order to achieve the same aim
records.learnerexamples_text: The Spanish authorities cooperated with the British police in finding the terrorists.; Several companies are cooperating in the relief effort.; Lime has become a sort of monster, with no consideration for life any more, and Martins decides to cooperate with the police to catch and kill him.

records.definition_text: when you work together with someone or do what they ask you
records.learnerexamples_text: This documentary was made with the cooperation of Rails UK.; There's very little cooperation between the two countries.; We thank you in advance for your cooperation.; The clubs work in close cooperation  with the Football Association.; Thank you in advance for your cooperation in this respect.

records.definition_text: willing to help or do what people ask
records.learnerexamples_text: I found them very cooperative.; You can rely on me - I love children and I am energetic and cooperative.

records.definition_text: to deal successfully with a difficult situation
records.learnerexamples_text: How does she cope with three small children and a job?; It was too stressful and eventually he just couldn't cope.; Tyres generally don't cope well on wet roads.; Moreover she can't cope with life.

records.definition_text: a reddish-brown metal used especially for making wire and coins, or the reddish brown colour of this metal
records.learnerexamples_text: copper wire/pipes; Rosie's hair shone like copper in the sunlight.; Its domes are made of pure copper, inside there's a big bell called "Zygmunt".

records.definition_text: to cheat by looking at and using someone else's work
records.learnerexamples_text: He was always copying from/off other children, but never got caught.; I'm certain she thought we had copied in the test.

records.definition_text: to behave like someone else
records.learnerexamples_text: He tends to copy his brother in the way he dresses.; He has to eat salads now, in [the] hope [that] the kids'll copy his attitudes and eat fresh and healthy food instead of sweets and unhealthy st[u]ff.

records.definition_text: a single book, newspaper, etc. of which many have been produced
records.learnerexamples_text: Over a million copies of the book have been sold.; The single with her new song sold more than 15 million copies, now she was a powerful star.

records.definition_text: something that has been made to be exactly like something else
records.learnerexamples_text: This painting is only a copy - the original hangs in the Louvre.; I always keep a copy of any official or important letters that I send off.; Could you make a copy of this for tomorrow's meeting, please?; For covering the work I missed, I will ask May on Thursday if I can borrow her exercise book and make a copy.

records.definition_text: a crop of grain, or the seed from this crop used to make flour or feed animals
records.learnerexamples_text: fields of corn; [My sister] is a farmer and we have to plant yams, corn, beans and other crops.

records.definition_text: a large company or group of companies that is controlled together as a single organization
records.learnerexamples_text: a multinational corporation; the British Broadcasting Corporation; She didn't want to work for a big corporation where everything was so impersonal.; Since I was a child, I've always dreamed about being a car designer in a large and powerful corporation like Ferrari, Porsche, Mercedes-Benz, etc.

records.definition_text: to show someone the mistakes in something they have said or written
records.learnerexamples_text: Our teacher normally corrects our pronunciation.; Until now, I have never had someone really teaching me and correcting my mistakes.

records.definition_text: suitable for a particular situation
records.learnerexamples_text: correct behaviour; I think that is the correct option because I really like this [kind of] film!

records.definition_text: to make a mistake or problem right or better
records.learnerexamples_text: The new software finds and corrects any errors on the hard disk.; For example if I have to write a formal letter or something like this, I use my 'PC' because the paper looks nicer and [the] computer corrects my mistakes.

records.definition_text: a change made to something in order to correct or improve it, or when you make such a change
records.learnerexamples_text: I made some corrections before handing in my essay.; She was disappointed to see her essay returned with a mass of corrections in red ink.; My new teacher is friendlier and he is more careful [with his] correction [of] the work and exams we do.

records.definition_text: in a correct way
records.learnerexamples_text: Have I pronounced your name correctly?; I don't speak English correctly.

records.definition_text: to be the same or very similar
records.learnerexamples_text: The money I've saved corresponds roughly to the amount I need for my course.; The American FBI corresponds to the British MI5.; His story of what happened that night didn't correspond with the witness's version.; Therefore, I would like to ask you for my entrance fee, as this evening did not correspond to your advertisement.

records.definition_text: to communicate with someone by writing letters
records.learnerexamples_text: They had corresponded ever since the war.; Dear Tom It would be wonderful to see you because we've been corresponding for a long time but I've never had [the] pleasure [of meeting] you.

records.definition_text: a long passage in a building or train
records.learnerexamples_text: Her office is at the end of the corridor.; The invigilator left the room and walked down the corridor looking for some help.

records.definition_text: something that you give or lose, in order to get or achieve something else
records.learnerexamples_text: He rescued four people at the cost of his own life.; She finally got the job she wanted, but at great personal cost.; It's not worth getting into an argument with Tim, as I learned to my cost.; We wanted to travel by car and, to my cost, my friend began to drive the car.

records.definition_text: to cause someone to lose or destroy something valuable
records.learnerexamples_text: Drinking and driving costs lives.; His affairs cost him his marriage.; However, many people are talking about car accidents which cost human lives.

records.definition_text: a set of clothes worn in order to look like someone else, especially for a party or a film or play
records.learnerexamples_text: actors in costume; a clown costume; The children were dressed in Halloween costumes.; Everything becomes alive with music and dancing, and everybody wears amazing costumes.

records.definition_text: the set of clothes typical of a particular country or period of history
records.learnerexamples_text: Japanese national costume; You also can take some terrific [ph]otographs of national costumes, hear music and take part in dances.

records.definition_text: comfortable and warm
records.learnerexamples_text: This room is nice and cosy in the winter.; He showed me into a cosy little room.; I have a very tiny but cosy bedroom.

records.definition_text: a small house, usually in the countryside
records.learnerexamples_text: They live in a country cottage, with roses round the door.; I live in a typical Norwegian cottage with a huge fireplace, and everything is natural and simple.

records.definition_text: cloth or thread made from the fibres of the cotton plant
records.learnerexamples_text: a shirt made of pure cotton;  a simple cotton dress; a reel of cotton ; Normally, I would prefer my blouses to be made of cotton or silk as these materials make me [feel] comfortable.

records.definition_text: to force air out of your lungs through your throat with a short loud sound
records.learnerexamples_text: The smoke made me cough.; I coughed all night long.; I kept coughing, my nose kept running!

records.definition_text: when you cough or an illness that makes you cough
records.learnerexamples_text: a dry cough; Emily has a nasty cough.; Because of swimming so much I got a terrible cough and so I had to be sent back to school so that I could be treated properly.

records.definition_text: used for making a suggestion
records.learnerexamples_text: We could go for a drink after work tomorrow, if you like.; You could always call Susie and see if she might babysit.; I could take you to a nice hotel.

records.definition_text: used to talk about what will possibly happen or is possibly true
records.learnerexamples_text: She could arrive any time now.; A lot of crime could be prevented.; This new drug could be an important step in the fight against cancer.; This could be a big advantage but on the other [hand], books contain more details and sometimes some parts of the book are cut out [in] the film.

records.definition_text: used as a more polite form of 'can' when asking for permission
records.learnerexamples_text: Could I speak to Mr Davis, please?; Excuse me, could I just say something here?; Could I bring you the missing work [to the] next class?

records.definition_text: used to talk about things that possibly happened in the past or might possibly have happened by some time in the future
records.learnerexamples_text: She could have been killed.; Let's go to the coast anyway - the rain could have stopped by the time we get there.; Then they thought about the situation and tried to [develop] a theor[y] about what could have happened with the dead body and who could be the murderer.

records.definition_text: used to express certainty that something in the past was impossible or didn't happen
records.learnerexamples_text: He couldn't have damaged your bike - he was with me all evening.; That book couldn't have been on sale last week - it's only come out today!; The blood froze in our veins, and we were all sure that it couldn't have been anything but a ghost!

records.definition_text: the group of people elected to govern a particular area, town or city, and organize services for it
records.learnerexamples_text: Edinburgh City Council; The local council has/have decided not to allocate funds for the project.; The town/city council is/are responsible for keeping the streets clean.; Rubbish collecting needs to be arranged more regularly by the city council.

records.definition_text: to see how many people or things there are
records.learnerexamples_text: The teachers counted the students as they got on to the coach.; Count your money carefully to make sure it's all there.; We're still waiting for the votes to be counted (up).; I counted them and there were 5 suitcases.

records.definition_text: to say numbers in their correct order
records.learnerexamples_text: Can you count to ten in French?; What he told me is "If you have any wishes, count 1 to 100 every Sunday for one month".

records.definition_text: to be important
records.learnerexamples_text: I've always believed that happiness counts more than money.; My opinion doesn't count for anything around here.; It wasn't romantic, there were no flowers but Carla knew [that] what counts is in the h[e]art.

records.definition_text: a long flat narrow surface or table in a shop, bank, restaurant, etc. at which people are served
records.learnerexamples_text: There was nobody at/behind the counter when I went into the bank, and I had to wait to be served.; When I was at the counter, I put down my bags and paid for the serviettes.

records.definition_text: a noun that can be used in the singular and the plural
records.learnerexamples_text: Count nouns are shown here with [C].

records.definition_text: to have confidence in someone because you know they will do what you want
records.learnerexamples_text: I can always count on my parents to help me.; So Jan, I'm sure I can count on you.

records.definition_text: to expect something to happen and make plans based on it
records.learnerexamples_text: I didn't count on so many people coming to the party.; This town can always count on the same quality and variety of films as any other city in the world.

records.definition_text: the largest political division of a state or country
records.learnerexamples_text: County Antrim; Westchester County; A county usually consists of several cities and towns and the rural areas surrounding them.; Rutland used to be the smallest county in England, but in 1974 it became part of Leicestershire.; Texas is divided into 254 counties.

records.definition_text: two or a few
records.learnerexamples_text: He'll be better in a couple of days.;  I'm going away with a couple of friends.; We'll have to wait another couple of hours for the paint to dry.; She'll be retiring in a couple more years.; The weather's been terrible for the last couple of days.

records.definition_text: two people who are married or in a romantic or sexual relationship, or two people who are together for a particular purpose
records.learnerexamples_text: a married couple; A young couple walked into the bar.; The couple skated well throughout the competition.; The couple can say what they want to eat on their [wedding] day.

records.definition_text: the ability to deal with a dangerous or difficult situation without being frightened
records.learnerexamples_text: I wanted to talk to him, but I didn't have the courage.; People should have the courage to stand up for their beliefs.; He [had] wanted to do it for a long time but never had the courage.

records.definition_text: a long green vegetable that is white inside
records.learnerexamples_text: We had fried courgettes and onions.; I really like hot and spicy chicken with courgette.

records.definition_text: an area of land or water used for a sports event
records.learnerexamples_text: a golf course; It is a very nice club, it has 20 tennis courts, 2 soccer fields and an 18-hole golf course.

records.definition_text: the place where a judge decides whether someone is guilty of a crime
records.learnerexamples_text: He's due to appear in court again on Monday.; Please describe to the court exactly what you saw.; the European Court of Human Rights; The lack of evidence means that the case is unlikely to go to court.; Two days after, I went to the law court as a witness.

records.definition_text: an area drawn out on the ground which is used for playing sports such as tennis and basketball
records.learnerexamples_text: a tennis/basketball/squash court; They were penalized for having too many players on the court.; I stayed in a hotel with [a] swimming pool, tennis court and private beach.

records.definition_text: polite behaviour
records.learnerexamples_text: Hotel staff must at all times treat guests with courtesy.; He could at least have had the courtesy to say sorry.; On balance, I think McDonalds should improve the courtesy of members of staff, as well as keeping up the speedy service.

records.definition_text: to deal with or include a subject or piece of information
records.learnerexamples_text: This leaflet covers what we've just discussed in more detail.; The book covers European history from 1789-1914.; Dear Teacher, I'm sorry but I won't be able to go to the English class tomorrow. But I can go another day to cover the work I've missed.

records.definition_text: to form a layer on the surface of something
records.learnerexamples_text: Snow covered the hillsides.; Cover the pasta with a layer of sauce.; The bandages were covered with/in blood.; The hills are covered by the snow.

records.definition_text: to be a particular size or area
records.learnerexamples_text: The town covers an area of 15 square kilometres.; The other suggestion is the flower market, wh[ich] is very famous for tourists because it covers 2 acres and there are plenty of flowers to buy.

records.definition_text: to travel a particular distance
records.learnerexamples_text: We covered 700 km in four days.; Secondly, travelling by car is a very effective way of saving time - for instance you cannot cover long distances with your bicycle.

records.definition_text: the outer part of a book, magazine, etc., that protects the pages
records.learnerexamples_text: Her picture is on the cover of several magazines.; I received it for Christmas [in] 1991, and I immediately decided to write [my name and my address on] the cover.

records.definition_text: something you put over something else, usually to protect it
records.learnerexamples_text: I keep my computer printer under a protective plastic cover.; an ironing board cover

records.definition_text: someone who is not brave and tries to avoid dangerous or difficult situations
records.learnerexamples_text: You didn't talk to her? You coward!; Instead of behaving like a wise grown-up, I behaved like a coward.

records.definition_text: behaving in a way that shows you are not brave
records.learnerexamples_text: This was a particularly brutal and cowardly attack.; Bernard was usually weak, depressed, cowardly and pessimistic, but, on the other hand, when he became popular and famous by taking advantage of John, he was so boastful.

records.definition_text: a sea creature with ten legs and a round, flat body covered by a shell, or the meat from this animal
