records.learnerexamples_text: a dead battery; The phone suddenly went dead.; I tried to phone my sister, but the phone was dead.

records.definition_text: a time or day by which something must be done
records.learnerexamples_text: There's no way I can meet that deadline.; We're working to a tight deadline.; I'm afraid you've missed the deadline - the deadline for applications was May 30th.; My last question is about the deadline of your offer.

records.definition_text: likely to cause death
records.learnerexamples_text: a deadly virus; a deadly weapon ; Caught without cover, they were quickly eliminated by a burst of Bull's deadly machine gun.

records.definition_text: unable to hear, either completely or partly
records.learnerexamples_text: He's been totally/partially deaf since birth.; She should take care of her family, especially her deaf three-year-old daughter.

records.definition_text: an agreement or an arrangement, especially in business
records.learnerexamples_text: a business deal; I'll make/do a deal with you - you wash the car and I'll let you use it tonight.; "I want to make a deal with you," he went on.

records.definition_text: a person who trades in something
records.learnerexamples_text: a second-hand car dealer; an antiques dealer; drug dealers; The computer dealer in our street offered me a special combination package.

records.definition_text: to talk to someone or meet someone, especially as part of your job
records.learnerexamples_text: She's used to dealing with difficult customers.; In my previous job, I used to deal with many, many people.

records.definition_text: to take action in order to achieve something or in order to solve a problem
records.learnerexamples_text: How do you intend to deal with this problem?; General enquiries are dealt with by our head office.; Sorry about such [a] late reply, but I've had some problems to deal with.

records.definition_text: liked very much
records.learnerexamples_text: She was a very dear friend.; He's one of my dearest friends.;  My dear Gina - how lovely to see you!; I decided to go to my dear friend Mary's house after writing a letter saying where I was and why.

records.definition_text: a way of beginning a formal letter to a woman whose name you do not know
records.learnerexamples_text: Dear Madam, I am writing to inform you...; Dear Sir or Madam, With reference to your newspaper report of 17th July, I am writing to correct some points in this report.

records.definition_text: a way of beginning a formal letter to a man whose name you do not know
records.learnerexamples_text: Dear Sir, I am writing to...; Dear Sir or Madam, With reference to your advertisement in the Wall Street Journal [...]

records.definition_text: the end of life
records.learnerexamples_text: The disease causes thousands of deaths a year.; Do you believe in life after death?; He never got over the death of his daughter.; death threats; After his father's death, he didn't want to study.

records.definition_text: (a) discussion or argument about a subject in which many people take part
records.learnerexamples_text: Education is the current focus of public debate.; How we proceed from here is a matter for debate.; Over the year we have had several debates about future policy.; Public debates are shown on television and television is the best way for politicians to explain their actions and projects.

records.definition_text: money taken out of a bank account, or a record of this
records.learnerexamples_text: The statement shows your most recent debits.

records.definition_text: to take money out of a bank account
records.learnerexamples_text: £20 has been debited from my account.

records.definition_text: a plastic card used to pay for things directly from your bank account
records.learnerexamples_text: I can use my debit card in most of the local shops.

records.definition_text: an amount of money that you owe someone
records.learnerexamples_text: He managed to pay off his debts in two years.; The firm ran up huge debts.; She thought of getting a loan but she already had huge debts.

records.definition_text: when you owe money to someone
records.learnerexamples_text: They are in debt to the bank.; He ran/got into debt after he lost his job.; The company is deep in debt.; The consequence is that I'm in debt.

records.definition_text: a period of ten years, especially a period such as 1860 to 1869, or 1990 to 1999
records.learnerexamples_text: The building was due to be knocked down decades ago.; Life has centred around fast food chains during the last decade and continues to do so.

records.definition_text: to become gradually damaged or to cause something to become gradually damaged
records.learnerexamples_text: Sugar makes your teeth decay.; Pollution has decayed the surface of the stonework on the front of the cathedral.; The historic buildings are starting to decay.

records.definition_text: to make someone believe something that is not true
records.learnerexamples_text: The company deceived customers by selling old computers as new ones.; The sound of the door closing deceived me into thinking they had gone out.; So if you don't want to feel deceived or offended, think twice before you decide to go shopping.

records.definition_text: of a satisfactory quality or level
records.learnerexamples_text: He earns a decent salary.; I haven't had a decent cup of coffee since I've been here.; I think it's a decent place for us to stay for a night.

records.definition_text: honest and morally good
records.learnerexamples_text: Decent people have had their lives ruined by his behaviour.; She should do the decent thing and apologize.; In fact, it had such [a] bad reputation that nobody "decent" went there any longer.

records.definition_text: a choice that you make about something after thinking about several possibilities
records.learnerexamples_text: She has had to make some very difficult decisions.; The company will reach/come to/make a decision shortly.; Let me have a/your decision by next week.; It was his decision to leave.; We need to take a lot of factors into account in our decision-making.

records.definition_text: able to make decisions quickly and confidently, or showing this quality
records.learnerexamples_text: You need to be more decisive.; a decisive reply; They were attractive, handsome, brave and decisive men.

records.definition_text: the flat area of a ship or boat that is not covered
records.learnerexamples_text: We sat on deck until it was dark.; When I woke up and went on the deck, I saw the skipper who [was coming] back from the village in the small boat.

records.definition_text: to announce something publicly or officially
records.learnerexamples_text: They declared their support for the proposal.; America declared war on Japan in 1941.; The country declared independence in 1952.; We should declare [the city centre] a pedestrian zone.

records.definition_text: to officially tell someone the value of goods you have bought, or the amount of money you have earned, because you might have to pay tax
records.learnerexamples_text: Have you got anything to declare?

records.definition_text: to gradually become less or worse
records.learnerexamples_text: His interest in the project declined after his wife died.; The party's popularity has declined in the opinion polls.; It had slightly declined to about 88 per cent in 1992.

records.definition_text: to refuse politely
records.learnerexamples_text: I invited him to the meeting but he declined.; He declined my offer.; We thank you for your offer of accommodation, but we decline it.

records.definition_text: when something becomes less in amount, importance, quality or strength
records.learnerexamples_text: industrial decline; Home cooking seems to be on the/in decline.; a sharp decline in sales; She seemed to be recovering and then she went into a decline.; For the 25-34 age group, a decline can be seen from 2006 to 2010.

records.definition_text: to add attractive things to an object or place, often for a special day or period
records.learnerexamples_text: They decorated the wedding car with ribbons and flowers.; The church always is decorated with beautiful flowers and other things.

records.definition_text: to put paint or paper on the walls or other surfaces of a room
records.learnerexamples_text: We're going to decorate the kitchen next week.; I hate the smell of paint when I'm decorating.; It is all decorated in blue.

records.definition_text: when the walls or other surfaces of rooms or buildings are covered with paint or paper
records.learnerexamples_text: This place is badly in need of decoration.; I will start with the new decoration [of] my bedroom next week.

records.definition_text: something that you put on something to make it look attractive or special, or the activity of putting things on something to make it look more attractive or special
records.learnerexamples_text: Christmas/party/table/cake decorations; He's good at cake decoration.; In November I joined a day course to learn how to make Christmas decorations.

records.definition_text: made to look attractive
records.learnerexamples_text: a decorative display of plants and flowers; a mirror in a decorative frame; It seems that the decorative role of clothes will have disappeared by the year 2050.

records.definition_text: to become less, or to make something become less
records.learnerexamples_text: During the summer months, rainfall decreases.; The aim to satisfy different interests should not [allow] the quality [to] decrease.

records.definition_text: a reduction
records.learnerexamples_text: There has been a steady decrease in the number of visitors.; Their yellow and black stripe has a mysterious beauty (which is the main reason for the huge decrease [in the] tiger population).

records.definition_text: A deep colour is strong and dark.
records.learnerexamples_text: deep purple; He is tall and has got black hair and beautiful deep brown eyes.

records.definition_text: A deep sound is low.
records.learnerexamples_text: a wonderfully deep voice ; "I'm not Gary," a strange and deep voice answered, "I'm someone who wants to warn you that tomorrow, you are going to die."

records.definition_text: A deep feeling or experience is very strong.
records.learnerexamples_text: deep regret ; Their son has been a deep disappointment to them.; I fell into a deep depression, and took an extremely long time to recover.

records.definition_text: a long way into something from the top or outside
records.learnerexamples_text: They travelled deep into the forest.; He thrust his hands deep in(to) his pockets.; I just fall deep into the story, into the writer's own world.

records.definition_text: If you know or feel something deep down, you are certain that it is true, or you feel it strongly although you do not admit it or show it.
records.learnerexamples_text: Deep down, I knew that I was right.; No, because I [feel] deep down that it's wrong to put animals behind bars.

records.definition_text: extremely or strongly
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm deeply grateful to you.; He found her comments deeply irritating/annoying/offensive.; We don't want to get too deeply involved with these people.; After 20 years of marriage, they're still deeply in love.; I was deeply impressed by the long-term cooperation between the zoo and the school.

records.definition_text: a large, wild animal that is sometimes hunted for food and has antlers (= long horns) if it is male
records.learnerexamples_text: a deer park ; It would be even nicer if there would be some wildlife in the par[k], like deer, walking free all over.

records.definition_text: to cause someone or something to fail
records.learnerexamples_text: The proposal to change the rules was narrowly defeated by 201 votes to 196.; I'm afraid anything that involves language learning has always defeated me.; But it was useless, Tina's friends had defeated their plan, and her.

records.definition_text: to win a victory over someone in a fight, war or competition
records.learnerexamples_text: Napoleon was defeated by the Duke of Wellington at the battle of Waterloo.; If we can defeat the Italian team, we'll be through to the final.; I still remember when Marcelo became [number] 1 in 1998 after he defeated Andre Agassi in the final of the "fifth Grand Slam".

records.definition_text: when someone or something is made to fail
records.learnerexamples_text: At the last General Election, they suffered a massive defeat.; The company was not ready to admit defeat.; After long negotiations with the police, Linda admitted defeat and gave up.

records.definition_text: when someone loses against someone else in a fight, war or competition
records.learnerexamples_text: After their defeat in battle, the soldiers surrendered.; Norwich City have suffered their worst defeat of the season.; The whole team will face serious problems, which may lead to big defeats.

records.definition_text: the part of a sports team which tries to prevent the other team from scoring points
records.learnerexamples_text: I play best in defence.; I did basketball exercises for defence.

records.definition_text: protection or support against attack, criticism or infection
records.learnerexamples_text: When Helen criticized me, Chris came/rushed to my defence.; She argued strongly in defence of her actions.; A good diet helps build the body's natural defences.; Movie stars like Brigitte Bardot started strong campai[g]ns against zoos as part of wider battles in defence of animal rights.

records.definition_text: to support someone or something that is being criticized
records.learnerexamples_text: The newspaper's editor defended his decision to publish the photos.; They are fighting to defend their beliefs/interests/rights.; Do we know a lot of people nowadays who would be able to take the risk of being a prisoner for 10 or 20 years "just" to defend his beliefs?

records.definition_text: to protect someone or something from being attacked, especially by fighting
records.learnerexamples_text: How can we defend our homeland if we don't have an army?; I'm going to karate lessons to learn how to defend myself.; White blood cells help defend the body against infection.; In the fourth one, you learn to defend yourself by doing Karate and in the last section, you could learn fencing.

records.definition_text: someone in a sports team who tries to prevent the other team from scoring points, goals, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: The Brazilian attack put France's defenders under pressure.; I'm mostly a defender, so scoring a goal for the first time gave me great pleasure!

records.definition_text: to say exactly what something means, or what someone or something is like
records.learnerexamples_text: In the dictionary 'reality' is defined as 'the state of things as they are, rather than as they are imagined to be'.; Your duties are clearly defined in the contract.; I guess you would have to define the word 'fit' to answer that question.

records.definition_text: certain, fixed and not likely to change
records.learnerexamples_text: The date for the meeting - is that definite?; We need a definite answer by tomorrow.; I'm really excited about your definite plans to come.

records.definition_text: the grammatical name for the word 'the' in English, or the words in other languages which have a similar use
records.learnerexamples_text: 'The City', referring to the financial area of London, takes a definite article.

records.definition_text: without any doubt
records.learnerexamples_text: Have you definitely decided to go to America?; He definitely said he'd be here.; So if I were you, I would definitely stay in the city.

records.definition_text: an explanation of the meaning of a word or phrase
records.learnerexamples_text: a dictionary definition; What is the definition of 'mood'?; He tried to give a definition of friendship.

records.definition_text: a qualification given for completing a university course
records.learnerexamples_text: "What degree did you do at York?" "Geography."; She's got a physics degree/a degree in physics from Oxford.; I completed my languages degree course at U.P.N University.

records.definition_text: an amount or level of something
records.learnerexamples_text: This job demands a high degree of skill.; A good society depends on the degree to which people are able to trust each other.; Can you imagine the degree of pollution you absorb in crossing London every morning by bicycle?

records.definition_text: to cause someone or something to be slow or late
records.learnerexamples_text: I was delayed by traffic.; The roads were crowded with a lot of traffic, so I got really delayed.

records.definition_text: to remove something, especially from a computer's memory
records.learnerexamples_text: All names have been deleted from the report.; I didn't take notice of [the email] and deleted it again.

records.definition_text: done intentionally or planned
records.learnerexamples_text: a deliberate attack/insult/lie;  This was a deliberate attempt to mislead us.; I'm sure that his deliberate intention with this was to make us get closer.

records.definition_text: intentionally
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm sure he says these things deliberately to annoy me.; Many of them choose the bicycle deliberately, just to have at least a small amount of exercise before and after [the] hours they spend sitting at their desks.

records.definition_text: soft, light or gentle
records.learnerexamples_text: a delicate flavour; a delicate shade of pink; She liked his delicate skin and his body's warmth.

records.definition_text: easy to damage or break
records.learnerexamples_text: delicate china; Delicate plants need to be kept in a greenhouse during the winter.; Although you told me I can make use of anything, I'd like to make sure that it isn't a problem to use such delicate things as the computer and the CD player?

records.definition_text: having a very pleasant taste or smell
records.learnerexamples_text: a delicious cake; The delicious smell of freshly-made coffee came from the kitchen.; This wine is delicious.; I love it because they make delicious hamburgers.

records.definition_text: (something or someone that gives) great pleasure, satisfaction or happiness
records.learnerexamples_text: The children screamed with delight.; My sister's little boy is a real delight.; I read your letter with great delight.; He seems to take great delight in teasing his sister.; At midnight fireworks covered the concert hall and I, as well as the rest of [the] spectators, felt excitement and delight.

records.definition_text: very pleased
records.learnerexamples_text: We're delighted with our new house.; I was delighted at/by your news.; I'm absolutely delighted that you can come.; We'd be delighted to come to dinner on Friday.; I've just seen your letter and I'm really delighted to have won the first prize in your competition.

records.definition_text: very pleasant, attractive, or enjoyable
records.learnerexamples_text: We had a delightful evening.; A table was laid with a lot of delightful food and a beautiful cake was in the centre of it.

records.definition_text: to take things such as goods, letters and parcels to people's houses or places of work
records.learnerexamples_text: Mail is delivered to our office twice a day.; The shop is delivering our new bed on Thursday.; You have to deliver newspapers to the town centre's shops.

records.definition_text: to speak formally to a group of people
records.searchterms_text: deliver;deliver a speech/talk etc;deliver a speech/talk, etc.;delivered;delivering;delivers
records.learnerexamples_text: The priest delivered a passionate speech against war.; Then, he delivered a speech to the public.

records.definition_text: when things such as goods, letters, or parcels are taken to people's houses or places of work
records.learnerexamples_text: a delivery van ; We get two deliveries of mail a day.; You can pay for the carpet on delivery.; We expect to take delivery of our new car next week.; I called for a delivery [from] Pizza Hut and after that went to study.

records.definition_text: to need something such as time or effort
records.learnerexamples_text: This job demands a high level of concentration.; I would say that driving a car demands a lot of responsibility.

records.definition_text: to ask for something in a way that shows that you do not expect to be refused
records.learnerexamples_text: I demanded an explanation.; I demand to see the manager.; She demanded that he return the books he borrowed from her.; I demand a full refund or I will be forced to take this matter further.

records.definition_text: a strong request
records.learnerexamples_text: You can't give in to children's demands all the time.; The government is unlikely to agree to the rebels' demands for independence.; They received a final demand for payment.; Of course only when my demands are logical.

records.definition_text: a need for something to be sold or supplied
records.learnerexamples_text: There was little demand for tickets.; I believe we [have] to stop the demand for ivory!

records.definition_text: needing a lot of time, attention or energy
records.learnerexamples_text: She's a very demanding child.; a demanding job ; Although the job was demanding I enjoyed it.

records.definition_text: a system of government in which people elect their leaders, or a country with this system
records.learnerexamples_text: The early 1990s saw the spread of democracy in Eastern Europe.; From then on it represented democracy and freedom until Hitler took over power in January 1933.

records.definition_text: based on the principles of democracy
records.learnerexamples_text: We must accept the results of a democratic election.; If we regard ourselves as modern people, we must be democratic enough to release them.

records.definition_text: to completely destroy a building, especially in order to use the land for something else
records.learnerexamples_text: A number of houses were demolished so that the supermarket could be built.; The building was demolished, and so was the dream of a house of the[ir] own.

records.definition_text: to show or prove that something exists or is true
records.learnerexamples_text: These problems demonstrate the importance of strategic planning.; These figures clearly demonstrate the size of the economic problem facing the country.; Research has demonstrated that babies can recognize their mother's voice very soon after birth.; The results were amazing, the group man[a]ged to demonstrate that the learning capacity increased a lot with respect to traditional methods.

records.definition_text: to march or stand with a group of people to show that you disagree with or support someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: Thousands of people gathered to demonstrate against the new proposals for universities.; Maybe the RSPCA should demonstrate, to show that it's not [accept]able. We have to stand up for their rights! Yesterday I heard that animal rights activists have met the prime minister.

records.definition_text: when a group of people march or stand together to show that they disagree with or support something or someone
records.learnerexamples_text: The students are holding a demonstration to protest against the increase in their fees.; Protesters staged an anti-war demonstration in front of the US embassy.; There were many demonstrations and violence.

records.definition_text: thick, strong, cotton cloth, often blue in colour, used especially for making jeans
records.learnerexamples_text: a denim jacket and jeans; If you have time to go shopping you could buy me a pair of blue denim jeans (size 30).

records.definition_text: thick and difficult to see through
records.learnerexamples_text: dense fog ; a dense forest; "Don't [be afraid] and don't run" shouted someone from the dense forest.

records.definition_text: with a lot of things close together
records.learnerexamples_text: England was once a densely wooded country.; Mexico City is one of the most densely populated cities in the world.; It's densely populated and with that the ugliness [of] densely populated places follows.

records.definition_text: relating to the teeth
records.learnerexamples_text: dental treatment ; In Kingsthorp you have lots of GPs and dental surger[ie]s.

records.definition_text: to say that something is not true
records.learnerexamples_text: Neil denies that he broke the window, but I'm sure he did.; Neil denies breaking the window.; We cannot deny that technology has changed our lives.

records.definition_text: to not allow someone to have or do something
records.learnerexamples_text: Her request for time off work was denied.; No one should be denied a good education.; The goalkeeper denied him his third goal.; I was denied the opportunity of learning French at school.; Should wild animals be kept in cages, and denied their freedom so that we can have the pleasure of watching them at zoos?

records.definition_text: to go away or leave, especially on a journey
records.learnerexamples_text: The plane departs at 6.00 a.m.; The train for London departs from Platform 2.; The boat departs from King's Bridge.

records.definition_text: when someone or something leaves a place, especially to start a journey to another place
records.learnerexamples_text: There are several departures for Paris every day.; Our departure was delayed because of bad weather.; departure time ; Now I am just waiting for the day of departure.

records.definition_text: needing the support of something or someone in order to continue existing or operating
records.learnerexamples_text: He has three dependent children.; It's very easy to become dependent on sleeping pills.; If I went to school by car I would be dependent on my father.

records.definition_text: If something depends on someone or something, it is influenced by them, or changes because of them.
records.learnerexamples_text: The choice depends on what you're willing to spend.; But, [o]n the other hand, you should explain to your parents what you want to do because you know that your decision depends on what they say.

records.definition_text: to need the help and support of someone or something in order to exist or continue as before
records.learnerexamples_text: She depends on her son for everything.; The country depends heavily on foreign aid.; I don't want to depend on my parents any more.

records.definition_text: to trust someone or something and know that they will help you or do what you want or expect them to do
records.learnerexamples_text: You can always depend on Michael in a crisis.; I'm depending on you to keep your promise.; You can't always depend on the trains arriving on time.; I hope you'll let me join your foundation because I could be a member you can depend on.

records.definition_text: a payment that you make immediately when you decide to buy something, as proof that you will really buy it
records.learnerexamples_text: They've put down a deposit on a house.; How many days in advance do we have to make our reservation? I also wonder if there is a deposit that we have to pay.

records.definition_text: unhappy and without hope for the future
records.learnerexamples_text: He seemed a bit depressed about his work situation.; She became deeply depressed when her husband died.; I felt depressed and decided to go to live in another city.

records.definition_text: making you feel unhappy and without hope for the future
records.learnerexamples_text: I find this weather so depressing.; Her letter made depressing reading.;  It was very depressing watching the news on television tonight.;  It's depressing to think that we've got five more years of this government!; It was really depressing, seeing people drinking and having fun [when] I just had to work.

records.definition_text: when you feel very unhappy, or a mental illness that makes you feel very unhappy and anxious for long periods
records.learnerexamples_text: If you suffer from depression, it's best to get professional help.; My mum always worried about my sister because of her shyness and depression.

records.definition_text: to take something, especially something necessary or pleasant, away from someone
records.learnerexamples_text: He claimed that he had been deprived of his freedom/rights.; You can't function properly when you're deprived of sleep.; We shouldn't deprive our music fans of this wonderful event, that can only enrich our city's cultural life.

records.definition_text: the distance down either from the top of something to the bottom, or to a distance below the top surface of something
records.learnerexamples_text: the depth of a lake/pond; There are very few fish at depths below 3000 metres.; The river froze to a depth of over a metre.; But suddenly Laura did not feel any fear anymore and within a second she jumped into the air and fell into the endless depth of the Grand Canyon.

records.definition_text: when you have serious qualities or the ability to think seriously about something
records.learnerexamples_text: Terry lacks depth - he's a very superficial person.; Her writing shows astonishing depth.; Jo has hidden depths.; I think that the main reason why someone has to read this book twice is the strength and depth of the two main characters: Donald Woods and Steve Biko.

records.definition_text: to go or come down
records.learnerexamples_text: The path descended steeply into the valley.; Jane descended the stairs.; Paul slowly descended to the river and sat down on the grassy bank.

records.definition_text: something that tells you what something or someone is like
records.learnerexamples_text: Write a description of your favourite seaside resort.; Your essay contains too much description, and not enough discussion of the issues.; She has given the police a very detailed/full description of the robber.; Here's a description of [my bedroom].

records.definition_text: If you deserve something good or bad, it should happen to you because of the way you have behaved.
records.learnerexamples_text: After all that hard work, you deserve a holiday.; Chris deserves our special thanks for all his efforts.; I hope they get the punishment they deserve.; They certainly deserved to win that match.; I wish you happiness, you deserve it.

records.definition_text: the art of making plans or drawings for something
records.learnerexamples_text: She's an expert on kitchen/software design.; He's studying design at college.; You know that my subject is design.

records.definition_text: a pattern or decoration
records.learnerexamples_text: a floral design; Last year I made and sold more than 200 pairs of knitted socks and because of that I got a prize from The Swedish Handcraft Company for [the] wonderful and original design on my socks.

records.definition_text: the way in which something is planned and made
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't like the design of this kettle.; The building was originally Victorian in design.; a serious design fault ; The car has some excellent design features.; I was looking to find a good bicycle with a nice design.

records.definition_text: to draw or plan something before making it
records.learnerexamples_text: Who designed this building/dress/furniture?; This range of clothing is specially designed for shorter women.; It was built in 1570 and designed by [the] Italian architect Morando.

records.definition_text: someone who draws and plans how something will be made
records.learnerexamples_text: a fashion/software designer; After five months, she was working as a co-designer with the best Italian designer, although she was just a student.

records.definition_text: made by a famous or fashionable designer
records.learnerexamples_text: designer jeans/sunglasses; I can't afford designer labels/designer label clothes.; People like designer clothes like Armani, Chanel [and] so on.

records.definition_text: worth having and wanted by most people
records.learnerexamples_text: Reducing class sizes in schools is a desirable aim.; It's regarded as a highly desirable job.; The house is in a very desirable area of the city.; It is desirable that they include showers, although a bath tub would be nice, too.

records.definition_text: a strong feeling that you want something
records.learnerexamples_text: I certainly have no desire to have children.; There is a strong desire for peace among the people.; She had a strong desire to go back to her home country before she died.; Several people have expressed a desire to see the report.; I had such a desire to go to the disco that I decided to go even without [my] parents' permission.

records.definition_text: a computer screen that contains icons that represent files, programs and other features of the computer
records.learnerexamples_text: The menu bar with its windows is one of the features of the desktop.

records.definition_text: a computer that is small enough to fit on a desk
records.learnerexamples_text: I can download from my desktop to my mobile phone.; The computer I bought is a beautiful, new, white desktop.

records.definition_text: a feeling of having no hope
records.learnerexamples_text: a mood/sense of despair; They're in the depths of despair over/about the money they've lost.; Almost in despair, I came out of the bathroom and tried my best to look for a candle.

records.definition_text: extremely worried or frightened and ready to do anything to change the bad situation you are in
records.learnerexamples_text: The doctors made one last desperate attempt/effort to save the boy's life.; They made a desperate appeal for help.; I was almost desperate, trying to think about any possible solution to my problem, but the more I thought, the bigger was my problem, because hours went by.

records.definition_text: needing or wanting something very much
records.learnerexamples_text: They are desperate for help.; He was desperate to tell someone his good news.; She was 19 and in desperate need of a boyfriend.

records.definition_text: in a way that shows you are frightened and ready to try anything to change a situation
records.learnerexamples_text: They fought desperately for their lives.; He desperately tried to keep the stalking sharks at bay, but he couldn't succeed.

records.definition_text: extremely or very much
records.learnerexamples_text: He was desperately ill.; I'm not desperately keen on football.; He was desperately in love with her.; They desperately wanted a child.; I desperately need a bicycle as a bicycle competition is going to take place in our city.

records.definition_text: used to say that something happened or is true, although something else makes this seem not probable
records.learnerexamples_text: I still enjoyed the week despite the weather.; Despite claims that the product is safe, many people have stopped buying it.; He managed to eat a big lunch despite having eaten an enormous breakfast.; Despite having to share a bedroom with my three cousins, I feel very comfortable.

records.definition_text: used to refer to a situation which is surprising in relation to something that is true or happens
records.learnerexamples_text: The company has been forced to reduce its price, despite the fact that the offer has been very popular.; The advantages of the kind of life that people ha[d] years ago is that they could eat more fruit and vegetables than us. However, there are advantages for us too, because despite the fact that we eat more fast food, we do more exercise than they [did].

records.definition_text: used to refer to a situation which is surprising in relation to something that is true or happens
records.learnerexamples_text: The company has been forced to reduce its price, despite the fact that the offer has been very popular.; The advantages of the kind of life that people ha[d] years ago is that they could eat more fruit and vegetables than us. However, there are advantages for us too, because despite the fact that we eat more fast food, we do more exercise than they [did].

records.definition_text: the place where someone or something is going
records.learnerexamples_text: We arrived at our destination tired and hungry.; His letter never reached its destination.; The Caribbean is a popular tourist/holiday destination.; The journey to the destination lasted about an hour.

records.definition_text: to damage something so badly that it does not exist or cannot be used
records.learnerexamples_text: Most of the old part of the city was destroyed by bombs during the war.; The accident seemed to have completely/totally destroyed his confidence.; The film described a terrible period of our history when a lot of people died and a lot of cities were destroyed.

records.definition_text: when something is destroyed
records.learnerexamples_text: Many people are very concerned about the destruction of the rainforests.; Unusually high winds left a trail of destruction over southern Britain.; weapons of mass destruction; With the ongoing industrialisation and, for example, the destruction of the rain forest men have taken or destroyed the natural places of several hundred species all over the world.

records.definition_text: one of many facts or pieces of information about something
records.learnerexamples_text: She insisted on telling me every single detail.; We don't know the full/precise details of the story yet.; Consequently we [want] to know every single detail about them and their lives.

records.definition_text: giving a lot of information
records.learnerexamples_text: A witness gave a detailed description of the man.; We ran until we arrived at the police station where we gave a detailed description of that man and what had happened.

records.definition_text: someone, especially a police officer, whose job is to discover information about a crime
records.learnerexamples_text: a private detective; detective stories ; I know that you love detective stories.

records.definition_text: when someone continues trying to do something, although it is very difficult
records.learnerexamples_text: Andy Murray will need great determination and skill to win this match.; Mandela tried to better the political situation of South Africa [-] he was strong enough to fight, he had determination.

records.definition_text: wanting to do something very much, and not letting anyone stop you
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm determined to get this piece of work finished today.; She's sure to get the job she wants - she's a very determined person.; I am determined to study computer engineering and pursue my education oversea[s].

records.definition_text: in grammar, a word which is used before a noun to show which particular example of the noun you are referring to
records.learnerexamples_text: In the phrases 'my first boyfriend' and 'that strange woman', the words 'my' and 'that' are determiners.

records.definition_text: to make something new such as a product
records.learnerexamples_text: Scientists are developing new drugs all the time.; The company is spending $650 million on developing new products/technology.; With more free time we can develop new tec[h]nology, learn more about ourselves and the world that surrounds us.

records.definition_text: to (cause something to) grow or change and become more advanced
records.learnerexamples_text: The baby develops inside the mother for nine months.; Over time, their acquaintance developed into a lasting friendship.; This exercise is designed to develop the shoulder and back muscles.; I'm looking for a job which will enable me to develop my skills/talents.; Therefore it's an important tool that is used to develop new friendships.

records.definition_text: If you develop an illness or problem, or if it develops, you start to suffer from it.
records.learnerexamples_text: The study showed that one in twelve women is likely to develop breast cancer.; She's developed some very strange habits lately.; They often developed the same symptoms as can be seen among mentally disturbed human beings.

records.definition_text: describes a country or region of the world with an advanced level of technology, industry, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: a developed country/nation ; To conclude I would like to say that the gover[n]ments of all developed countries wouldn't have been so concerned about [the] so-called "problem 2000" if the computer had not been so important for modern society.

records.definition_text: describes a country or region of the world which is poor and has few industries
records.learnerexamples_text: the developing world/countries/nations; Nowadays, both developed and developing countries spend a lot of money on computeriz[ation].

records.definition_text: when someone or something grows or changes and becomes more advanced
records.learnerexamples_text: healthy growth and development; The programme traced the development of popular music through the ages.; a development project in Pakistan; There are some machines which have helped in my development, and others which help to make my life easier.

records.definition_text: the process of developing something new
records.learnerexamples_text: the development of new drugs; Mr Berkowitz is in charge of product development.; Owing to the great speed of technological development, people need to lead a faster life.

records.definition_text: something new that happens and changes a situation
records.learnerexamples_text: an important development in the fuel crisis; Phone me if there are any new developments.; There have been impressive developments in technology lately.

records.definition_text: a piece of equipment that is used for a particular purpose
records.learnerexamples_text: an electronic device; Rescuers used a special device for finding people trapped in collapsed buildings.; I have much more time for many other things during the day thanks to [the] devices modern technology offers us.

records.definition_text: an evil being, often represented in human form but with a tail and horns
records.learnerexamples_text: This film is about a devil who meets a priest.

records.definition_text: extremely loving or caring very much about someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: a devoted fan/husband/wife; Lucy is devoted to her cats.; I am devoted to reading and I can say this book is wonderful.

records.definition_text: to use time, energy, etc. for a particular purpose
records.searchterms_text: devote;devote sth to sb/sth;devote sth to sb/sth
records.learnerexamples_text: He resigned from his job to devote more time to his family.; At that time, everyone should have devoted their life to the nation.

records.definition_text: to use a space or area for a particular purpose
records.searchterms_text: devote;devote sth to sb/sth;devote sth to sb/sth
records.learnerexamples_text: Most of the magazine was devoted to celebrity gossip.; And we ha[ve] come [up with] the idea of building a drama theatre at our college and a new department for our library devoted to music.

records.definition_text: a simple picture showing what something looks like or explaining something
records.learnerexamples_text: The teacher drew a diagram showing how the blood flows through the heart.; The first diagram tells us that the number of Japanese tourist[s] travelling abroad increased dramatically from about 5 million in 1985 to about 11 million in 1990.

records.definition_text: to make a telephone call to a particular number
records.learnerexamples_text: Can I dial this number direct, or do I have to go through the operator?; Dial 0 for the switchboard.; So he picked up the phone and dialled the number written in the letter.

records.definition_text: (a) conversation which is written for a book, play or film
records.learnerexamples_text: The play contained some very funny dialogue.; Act Two begins with a short dialogue between father and son.; However, she shows her courage during her first dialogue with Joss.

records.definition_text: an extremely hard valuable stone which is used in jewellery, and in industry for cutting hard things
records.learnerexamples_text: a diamond ring/necklace ; He had worked in the diamond mines of South Africa.; She found a gorgeous diamond ring on her finger.

records.definition_text: a shape with four straight sides of equal length, forming two opposite angles which are wide and two which are narrow
records.learnerexamples_text: Joe's socks had diamond patterns on them.

records.definition_text: to become more and more rare and then disappear completely
records.learnerexamples_text: Dinosaurs died out about 65 million years ago.; A second point is that [a] lot of animals are going to die out because of pollution.

records.definition_text: the type of food that someone usually eats
records.l_topic_text_text: body and health, food and drink
records.learnerexamples_text: a healthy/balanced diet; The children seem to exist on a diet of burgers and chips.; You can try our fresh farm food, which [is] very good for your diet.

records.definition_text: when someone eats less food, or only particular types of food, because they want to become thinner or for medical reasons
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm going on a diet next week and hope to lose two kilos before Christmas.; The doctor put me on a low-salt diet to reduce my blood pressure.; I'm on a serious diet, and I have to exercise.

records.definition_text: to be not like something or someone else, either physically or in another way
records.learnerexamples_text: The twins look alike, but they differ in personality.; His views differ considerably from those of his parents.; The findings of the various studies differ greatly/widely.; People's opinions on this matter differ widely.

records.definition_text: the amount by which one thing is different from another
records.learnerexamples_text: a(n) age/price/temperature difference; There's a big difference in age between them.; This age difference was too big!

records.definition_text: used to talk about separate things or people of the same type
records.learnerexamples_text: I had to go to three different shops to find the book she wanted.; I have three different teachers for three different things, one for the grammar, [an]other for the lis[ten]ing and finally [one] for my writing.

records.definition_text: in a different way
records.learnerexamples_text: We want to do things differently.; Are girls treated differently?; I had always pictured it quite differently.

records.definition_text: to be very different
records.learnerexamples_text: Prices vary widely from shop to shop.; People's opinions on the protection of the environment differ widely.

records.definition_text: not friendly or easy to deal with
records.learnerexamples_text: The manager is difficult to deal with/a difficult person to deal with.; His wife is a very difficult person.; Please children, don't be so difficult!; I'm not a difficult person and I can cook very [well].

records.definition_text: when something is not easy to do or understand
records.learnerexamples_text: We finished the job, but only with great difficulty.; The difficulty of the task excited them.; She had great difficulty finding a job.; They would have difficulty in sleeping outdoors.

records.definition_text: something that is not easy to deal with
records.learnerexamples_text: financial difficulties; to have/experience difficulties; children with learning difficulties; As you know my family has financial difficulties and we can't afford this.

records.definition_text: to break up and move soil using a tool, a machine or your hands
records.learnerexamples_text: Digging (in) the garden is good exercise.; I started digging, but it was useless.

records.definition_text: to form a hole by moving soil
records.learnerexamples_text: The tunnel was dug with the aid of heavy machinery.; The dog was digging a hole to hide its bone in.; I was ready to dig a hole and jump into it, because when you are at that age and your best friend's father sees you kissing your boyfriend in the dark, [it is] just the most embarr[a]ssing thing which can happen to you.

records.definition_text: showing information in the form of an electronic image
records.learnerexamples_text: a digital clock/display; a digital watch; The alarm clock was flashing with the annoying digital zeros.

records.definition_text: a situation in which a difficult choice has to be made between two different things you could do
records.learnerexamples_text: The President is clearly in a dilemma about/over how to tackle the crisis.; She faces the dilemma of disobeying her father or losing the man she loves.; a moral/ethical dilemma; Actually I think it's a typical female dilemma: we try to do many things by ourselves and at the same time!

records.definition_text: a particular part of a situation, especially something that affects how you think or feel
records.learnerexamples_text: Music has added a new dimension to my life.; I had never felt this way before, it was like being part of another life, another dimension!

records.definition_text: a measurement of the length, width, or height of something
records.learnerexamples_text: The dimensions of the photo should be no larger than 30cm by 20cm.; Also I [want to] take a big mirror, the dimensions are 0.70 x 1.20 m.

records.definition_text: to put something into a liquid for a short time
records.learnerexamples_text: Dip the fish in the batter, then drop it into the hot oil.; She dipped her toe into the pool to see how cold it was.; I recommend little sandwiches, chips and other things to dip [into sauces].

records.definition_text: to become lower in level or amount
records.learnerexamples_text: The number of students taking sciences has dipped sharply.; Cinema attendance in th[is] age group dipped to 88%.

records.definition_text: an official whose job is to represent one country in another, and who usually works in an embassy
records.learnerexamples_text: a Spanish/British diplomat; The owner of the restaurant was a diplomat, and he invited the refugees to eat at the restaurant.

records.definition_text: going straight from one place to another without stopping or changing direction
records.learnerexamples_text: a direct route/line ; Is there a direct train to Edinburgh?; I'm looking for a direct flight from Zurich to Botswana.

records.definition_text: with no other person or thing involved or between
records.learnerexamples_text: She decided to take direct control of the project.; Have you any direct experience of this kind of work?; He left as a direct result/consequence of what she said.; There is a direct link/connection between smoking and lung cancer.; I think that there are huge dangers today such as war, violence, crime, pollution, etc. that have a direct influence on our lives.

records.definition_text: to tell the actors in a film or play what to do
records.learnerexamples_text: He wanted to give up acting and start directing (his own films).; 'Jaws' was directed by Steven Spielberg.; We plan to see an action film which was directed by Tarantino.

records.definition_text: to show or tell someone how to get to a place
records.learnerexamples_text: Can you direct me to the manager's office please?; He directed me to a room where other guests were waiting.

records.definition_text: the way that someone or something is moving or facing
records.learnerexamples_text: "No, go that way," I said, pointing in the opposite direction.; He was going in the direction of the bedroom.; They drove away in opposite directions.; I walked for hours in the same direction I [had] walked before.

records.definition_text: with no other person or thing involved or in between
records.learnerexamples_text: Our hotel room was directly above a building site.; The disease is directly linked to poor drainage systems.; The sun shone directly in my eyes.; The Youth Hostel was directly beside the sea.

records.definition_text: clearly and honestly
records.learnerexamples_text: Let me answer that question directly.; While being interviewed, try to answer the questions directly and look into [the] interviewer's eyes.

records.definition_text: an important manager in an organization or company
records.learnerexamples_text: the board of directors; She has become the director of the new information centre.; It was from my school teacher and she was saying the most horrible things about the school, the director and other teachers.

records.definition_text: someone who tells the actors in a film or play what to do
records.learnerexamples_text: a famous film/movie director; We want to see the latest film by our favourite director - Oliver Stone.

records.definition_text: dust, soil or any substance that makes a surface not clean
records.learnerexamples_text: His coat was covered with dirt.; Maybe in the future they'll find a new fabric which protects you from dirt and dangerous sunshine.

records.definition_text: an illness, injury or condition that makes it difficult for someone to do the things that other people do
records.learnerexamples_text: a physical/learning disability; Trying to change attitudes to disability is a real struggle.; Such [problems] as cancer, heart attack, [or] mental disability are very likely to bother you in the future.

records.definition_text: having an illness, injury or condition that makes it difficult to do the things that most people do
records.learnerexamples_text: The accident left him severely disabled.; The library does not have disabled access.; I have done a lot of work looking after disabled people in the local area.

records.definition_text: something which makes a situation more difficult, or makes you less likely to succeed
records.learnerexamples_text: One disadvantage of living in the town is the lack of safe places for the children to play.; We need to consider whether the disadvantages of the plan outweigh the advantages.; After that we discussed the advantages and disadvantages of public transport.

records.definition_text: to have a different opinion from someone else about something
records.learnerexamples_text: I disagree with most of what he said.; Experts disagree about / on the causes of the disease.; Few people would disagree that something should be done to reduce the level of crime in the area.; I strongly disagree with the decision that has been taken.; We saw "Harry Potter" [and] the film was good but I think the book is better. Carlos disagreed with me.

records.definition_text: when people have a different opinion about something or have an argument
records.learnerexamples_text: They had a disagreement about/over money.; There was some disagreement with this view.; Literary critics were in total disagreement about the book.; I am writing to express my disagreement with your article "Failure of Festival", as I attended the festival last weekend.

records.definition_text: to become impossible to see
records.learnerexamples_text: The sun disappeared behind a cloud.; We looked for her but she had disappeared into the crowd.; They saw my mother's shadow [on] the stairs and disappeared.

records.definition_text: to become impossible to find
records.learnerexamples_text: She disappeared from her home over a month ago.; I can't find my keys anywhere - they've completely disappeared.; I noticed that my wallet had disappeared.

records.definition_text: to no longer exist
records.learnerexamples_text: These flowers are disappearing from our countryside.; This is a way of life that is fast disappearing.; It seems that the decorative role of clothes will have disappeared by the year 2050.

records.definition_text: when someone or something disappears
records.learnerexamples_text: A man was being questioned in connection with her disappearance.; After his disappearance lots of people were looking for him and [in] the end they tracked him down!

records.definition_text: to make someone feel unhappy because someone or something was not as good as they had expected
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm sorry to disappoint you, but I'm afraid I can't come after all.; We don't want to disappoint the fans.; I've always got along very well with little kids and I'm sure I won't disappoint you.

records.definition_text: unhappy because someone or something was not as good as you hoped or expected, or because something did not happen
records.learnerexamples_text: She was disappointed (that) they hadn't phoned.; We were deeply disappointed at/about the result.; His parents were bitterly disappointed in/with him.; He was disappointed to find they'd already gone.; I feel so disappointed.

records.definition_text: making you feel disappointed
records.learnerexamples_text: What a disappointing performance/result!; The response to our advertisement has been very disappointing.; I started my new English class last week, which was [a] really disappointing experience since the teacher was not a native speaker.

records.definition_text: the feeling of being disappointed
records.learnerexamples_text: Book early to avoid disappointment.;  To my (great) disappointment, he decided to leave.; However, to my disappointment, the restaurant was closed because it was being redecorated.

records.definition_text: something or someone that disappoints you
records.learnerexamples_text: The party turned out to be a big / huge / great disappointment.; I'm afraid I've been rather a disappointment to my parents.; It was all a big disappointment!

records.definition_text: to feel that something or someone is bad or wrong
records.learnerexamples_text: The survey showed that 32% of respondents approve, 54% disapprove and the rest are undecided.; I strongly disapprove of under-age drinking.; Since the system has more disadvantages than advantages, I disapprove of [the] "open 24 hours a day, seven days a week" system.

records.definition_text: something that causes great harm or damage
records.learnerexamples_text: An inquiry was ordered into the recent rail disaster.; This is one of the worst natural disasters ever to hit the area.; Everything was going smoothly until suddenly disaster struck.; Secondly, we have to save our planet from disaster.

records.definition_text: something that is a failure or has a negative result
records.learnerexamples_text: His idea was a total disaster.; Inviting James and Ivan to dinner on the same evening was a recipe for disaster - they always argue with each other.; For very shy people who have trouble communicating even in everyday situations it would be a disaster to become famous, watched by curious fans and recognised while walking in the streets.

records.definition_text: a CD
records.learnerexamples_text: Both songs are on their latest disc.; Then after the movie, we went to a CD shop and I bought the new Foo Fighters' disc.

records.definition_text: a flat, round shape or object
records.learnerexamples_text: The dog had a small, metal disc attached to its collar.

records.definition_text: when people's behaviour is controlled using rules and punishments
records.learnerexamples_text: parental/military/school discipline; There should be better discipline in schools.; I don't know if that is because of their age, but whatever it is, I think teachers should change the methods of discipline they use.

records.definition_text: someone who plays music on the radio or at live events
records.learnerexamples_text: a radio 2 disc jockey; I found out that there would be a special event with disc jockeys like DJ Quicksilver.

records.definition_text: to make someone less confident or enthusiastic about something
records.learnerexamples_text: The thought of how much work she had to do discouraged her.; It should include the prices of the tickets. If not, it will discourage people.

records.definition_text: to try to persuade someone not to do something
records.searchterms_text: discourage;discourage sb from doing sth;discourage sb from doing sth ;discouraged;discourages;discouraging
records.learnerexamples_text: Her parents tried to discourage her from seeing him.; Yet there are also disadvantage[s] which might discourage you from buying a mobile phone.

records.definition_text: to find out something or to find a place or an object, especially for the first time
records.learnerexamples_text: Who discovered America?; Scientists have discovered how to predict an earthquake.; We searched all morning for the missing papers and finally discovered them in a drawer.; She discovered (that) her husband was having an affair.; I have discovered that horses are wonderful animals.

records.definition_text: when someone discovers something
records.learnerexamples_text: the discovery of electricity; Leonardo made many scientific discoveries.; a journey/voyage of discovery; The discovery of a body in the woods started a murder enquiry.; How will this affect our lifestyles and homes in the future if scientists go on making new discoveries?

records.definition_text: when people talk about something and tell each other their ideas or opinions
records.learnerexamples_text: They were having a discussion about football.; I can say nothing - the matter is still under discussion.; Management are holding/having discussions with the union about possible redundancies.; Jane told us something about the Civil War and after that we had a discussion about the rights of black people in th[o]se days.

records.definition_text: (an) illness caused by infection or by a failure of health rather than by an accident
records.learnerexamples_text: heart disease; a common/rare disease; They reported a sudden outbreak of the disease in the south of the country.; The first symptom of the disease is a very high temperature.; Starvation and disease have killed thousands of refugees.

records.definition_text: when someone does something very bad that makes people stop respecting them or their family, team, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: They were sent home in disgrace.; He brought disgrace on the whole team.; When we came back, it felt like we were sinking in[to] a miserable life, full of disgrace.

records.definition_text: clothes and other things that you wear to change the way you look so that people cannot recognize you
records.learnerexamples_text: She usually goes out in disguise to avoid being bothered by the public.; There will be a big parade in the first week of the month with people in disguise.

records.definition_text: to give a new appearance to a person or thing, especially in order to hide its true form
records.learnerexamples_text: He disguised himself by shaving his head and wearing a false beard.; Minor skin imperfections can usually be disguised with make-up.; We tried to disguise the fact that it was just a school hall by putting up coloured lights and balloons.; This writer that we are going to welcome is a brilliant woman, because she had the courage to disguise herself as an [im]migrant to see and to feel how those poor and miserable Turkish [im]migrants live in Germany.

records.definition_text: extremely unpleasant or unacceptable
records.learnerexamples_text: It's disgusting that there are no schools or hospitals for these people.; Passengers were kept for hours in a disgusting waiting room.; Personally I don't like the special food that they do sometimes, because it's disgusting.

records.definition_text: not honest and likely to lie or do something illegal
records.learnerexamples_text: a dishonest lawyer; a dishonest way of making money; He's been dishonest in his dealings with us/about his past.; Both of them are dishonest men: Joss organizes the smuggling, and Jem is a horse-thief.

records.definition_text: when someone is not honest
records.learnerexamples_text: Her dishonesty landed her in prison.; He is so open in his dishonesty that Mary can't be angry with him.

records.definition_text: a machine that washes dirty plates, cups, forks, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: I was just loading the dishwasher.; Finally, modern technology has changed my way of spending the free time that is provided by household appliances [such] as the dishwasher [and] the washing machine.

records.definition_text: a piece of computer equipment that records and stores information electronically
records.learnerexamples_text: the hard disk; How much disk space is there?; I bought a brand new, state of the art computer which is equipped with a 300 Mhz PENTIUM Processor, a 300 GB hard disk, a 17" monitor and so on.

records.definition_text: to not like someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: Why do you dislike her so much?; I dislike walking and I hate the countryside.; I generally prefer reading newspapers, but I don't dislike books.

records.definition_text: when you do not like someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: a dislike of cold weather; The main reason for my dislike is that it's so unnatural.

records.definition_text: not planned or organized well
records.learnerexamples_text: The whole conference was totally disorganized - nobody knew what they were supposed to be doing.; Even though it was rather disorganized, most of [the] audience seemed to be [pleased] with it.

records.definition_text: not good at planning or organizing things
records.learnerexamples_text: He's impossible to work for - he's so disorganized.; Apart from that, I am a disaster working in offices and I am very disorganised.

records.definition_text: a collection of objects or pictures arranged for people to look at
records.learnerexamples_text: a display of children's paintings; I decided to visit a museum which has a special display on Friday.

records.definition_text: when something is shown electronically such as on a computer screen
records.learnerexamples_text: The display problems might be due to a shortage of disk space.; The phone has many facilities like games and color display.

records.definition_text: a performance or show for people to watch
records.learnerexamples_text: a firework display; One of the high points of our exciting and well organised event was the fireworks display.

records.definition_text: to arrange something somewhere so that people can see it
records.learnerexamples_text: Family photographs were displayed on the wall.; The problem [with] some museums is that the way in which the pieces of art are displayed is not right.

records.definition_text: to show something electronically such as on a computer screen
records.learnerexamples_text: The text can be displayed and edited on screen.; The timetable is hidden somewhere in a submenu which, I think, should be displayed on the main page.

records.definition_text: when you get rid of something, especially by throwing it away
records.learnerexamples_text: waste disposal; the disposal of hazardous substances; Nowadays waste disposal and environmental protection has become one of the most important questions of our life in a world with environmental catastrophes.

records.definition_text: to interrupt something and stop it continuing as it should
records.learnerexamples_text: A heavy fall of snow had disrupted the city's transport system.; The meeting was disrupted by a group of protesters who shouted and threw fruit at the speaker.; On the other hand the beep on your mobile phone sometimes disrupts the most romantic moment or the best scene in the cinema.

records.definition_text: when someone is dissatisfied
records.learnerexamples_text: At the moment she's experiencing a lot of dissatisfaction with her job.; I expect a full refund plus compensation for my dissatisfaction and discomfort which I suffered.

records.definition_text: not pleased or happy with something
records.learnerexamples_text: If you're dissatisfied with the service, why don't you complain to the hotel manager?; However, I must say that museums are really useful, to understand the history of the world, and that's why people keep going there even though they're sometimes dissatisfied.

records.definition_text: the amount of space between two places
records.learnerexamples_text: What's the distance between Madrid and Barcelona/from Madrid to Barcelona?; He travels quite a distance to work every day.; Does she live within walking distance of her parents?; There are also caves to explore a short distance away.

records.definition_text: somewhere that is far away, but close enough for you to see or hear the things that are there

records.definition_text: far away

records.definition_text: to be able to see, hear or understand something

records.definition_text: to make someone stop giving their attention to something

records.definition_text: making you feel extremely worried or upset

records.definition_text: to interrupt what someone is doing by making noise or annoying them

records.definition_text: when you enter water head-first with your arms held out above your head

records.definition_text: when you spend some time swimming under water

records.definition_text: someone who swims under water, usually with breathing equipment
records.learnerexamples_text: a deep-sea diver; I've got [the qualification] of "open water diver''.

records.definition_text: varied or different

records.definition_text: the activity of swimming under water, usually with breathing equipment

records.definition_text: when something is separated into parts or groups, or the way that it is separated

records.definition_text: one of the groups in a business or organization

records.definition_text: used to avoid repeating a verb that has just been used

records.definition_text: to be unsuccessful/successful

records.definition_text: a piece of text produced electronically on a computer

records.definition_text: a film, television or radio programme that gives facts and information about a subject

records.definition_text: to cause damage/harm, etc.

records.definition_text: relating to a person's own country

records.definition_text: belonging or relating to the home, house or family

records.definition_text: to have control over a place or a person

records.definition_text: to give money or goods to help a person or organization

records.definition_text: an animal like a small horse with long ears
records.learnerexamples_text: The donkey struggled with its heavy burden.; You can use animals like donkeys for transportation.

records.definition_text: used to tell someone that you do not know the answer to a question and that you are surprised they have asked you

records.definition_text: used to encourage someone to do something
records.learnerexamples_text: Please don't hesitate to get in touch if you need any more advice.; If you have mo[re] questions, do not hesitate to contact me.

records.definition_text: to have a good effect on someone

records.definition_text: to be useful or helpful to someone
records.learnerexamples_text: A holiday in the sun will do you good.; I think that living and studying in another country will do you good.

records.learnerexamples_text: The full stop at the end of this sentence is a dot.; Her skirt was blue with white dots.; On the map we have marked a black dot on the place where you will find the hotel.

records.definition_text: twice as much or as many
