records.learnerexamples_text: an entertaining story/film/talk ; His books aren't particularly well-written, but they're always entertaining.; It is obvious that some people prefer reading books, [while] others claim that watching films is much more entertaining.

records.definition_text: shows, movies, television, or other performances or activities that entertain people
records.learnerexamples_text: There is live entertainment in the bar every night.; There's not much in the way of entertainment in this town - just the cinema and a couple of pubs.; You can find cinemas, discos and night clubs for entertainment.

records.definition_text: a feeling of energetic interest in a particular subject or activity and an eagerness to be involved in it
records.learnerexamples_text: One of the good things about teaching young children is their enthusiasm.; After the accident he lost his enthusiasm for the sport.; I am filled with enthusiasm about [spend]ing two weeks at Camp California in the U.S.A.

records.definition_text: showing enthusiasm
records.learnerexamples_text: You don't seem very enthusiastic about the party - don't you want to go tonight?; I've got a lot of friends who are really enthusiastic about cycling and we often go cycling [together].

records.definition_text: in an enthusiastic way
records.learnerexamples_text: She responded very enthusiastically to the idea.; She accepted my suggestion enthusiastically.

records.definition_text: whole or complete, with nothing missing
records.learnerexamples_text: Between them they ate an entire cake.; He'd spent the entire journey asleep.; On behalf of the entire school, I would like to put forward a num[b]er of suggestions in regard to the improvement of the reception area.

records.definition_text: completely
records.learnerexamples_text: I admit it was entirely my fault.; I'm not entirely convinced it will work.; The company is run almost entirely by middle-aged men.; I would like to do something entirely different before I start to study again.

records.definition_text: to give someone the right to do or have something
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm entitled to apply for citizenship.; Being unemployed entitles you to free medical treatment.; In conclusion, I believe that I am entitled to a partial refund.

records.definition_text: the right to enter a place or join an organization
records.learnerexamples_text: Entrance is free, but you have to pay for your drinks.; If you've [got] membership, you don't need to pay for entrance. You only pay for the drinks and the food.

records.definition_text: the right or ability to come into or go into a place
records.learnerexamples_text: She was refused entry.; A flock of sheep blocked our entry to the village.; I can't go down that street - there's a 'No entry' sign.; There's free entry to the exhibition for students after 6 pm.

records.definition_text: a separate piece of information that is recorded in a book such as a dictionary, or on the Internet
records.learnerexamples_text: They've updated a lot of the entries on the website.; As his illness progressed, he made fewer entries in his diary.; Later I got my own entry on their Clan-home-page.

records.definition_text: when you join an organization or take part in a competition
records.learnerexamples_text: Are there lots of exams for entry into the legal profession?; Have you filled in your entry form yet?; You can do anything in this club from football to chess. If you ever come to visit, I could organise an entry form [for] you.

records.definition_text: a piece of work that you do to try to win a competition
records.learnerexamples_text: There have been a fantastic number of entries for this year's poetry competition.; the winning entries

records.definition_text: the conditions that you live or work in and the way that they influence how you feel or how effectively you can work
records.learnerexamples_text: The office is quite bright and airy - it's a pleasant working environment.; As a parent you try to create a stable home environment.; They need to live in a friendly environment with their relatives and their friends.

records.definition_text: relating to the environment
records.learnerexamples_text: People are becoming far more aware of environmental issues.; As you know, I went to Canada in order to take part in an environmental conference.

records.definition_text: in a way that is related to the environment
records.learnerexamples_text: environmentally damaging chemicals; We need our industries to work in an environmentally responsible way.; All these [things] were made possible because we have the world's most dedicated and environmentally adaptable government, spearheaded by Lee Kuan Yew decades ago.

records.definition_text: not harmful to the environment
records.learnerexamples_text: environmentally-friendly washing powder; A lot was said about creating more environmentally-friendly products.

records.definition_text: to wish that you had something that someone else has
records.learnerexamples_text: I envy her ability to talk to people she's never met before.; I don't envy you the job of cooking for all those people.; I really envy you, Pete.

records.definition_text: the feeling that you wish you had something that someone else has
records.learnerexamples_text: I watched with envy as she set off for the airport.; Sam, your last letter has filled me with envy.

records.definition_text: a single event or group of related events
records.learnerexamples_text: This latest episode in the fraud scandal has shocked a lot of people.; The drugs, the divorce and the depression - it's an episode in his life that he wants to forget.; This little episode happened when I was seven years old.

records.definition_text: one of the single parts into which a story is divided, especially when it is broadcast on the television or radio
records.learnerexamples_text: I missed the first episode.; I watch[ed] the news and one episode of "Friends".

records.definition_text: the same in amount, number or size
records.learnerexamples_text: The sides are of equal length.; One litre is equal to 1.76 imperial pints.; We are a well-mixed class with equal numbers of boys and girls, all about 20 years old.

records.definition_text: the same in importance and deserving the same treatment
records.learnerexamples_text: All people are equal, deserving the same rights as each other.; They've got a long way to go before they achieve equal pay/opportunities for men and women.; Then Napoleon did whatever he wanted to do under the motto of "all animals are equal", which was false.

records.definition_text: someone or something that has the same importance as someone or something else and deserves the same treatment
records.learnerexamples_text: The good thing about having her as a boss is that she treats us all as equals.; We must respect and treat them as our equals.

records.definition_text: the right of different groups of people to have a similar social position and receive the same treatment
records.learnerexamples_text: equality between the sexes;  racial/sexual equality; That's why I think people who fight to defend equality are amazing, especially Nelson Mandela because he spen[t] part of his life in jail for that.

records.definition_text: fairly and in the same way
records.learnerexamples_text: Everyone should be treated equally.; In [the] festival, all the performers were treated equally.

records.definition_text: to provide someone or something with what is needed for a particular purpose
records.learnerexamples_text: They're raising money to equip the hospital.; The new trains are equipped with all the latest technology.; We were equipped with crampons, ropes, ice axes, gloves, sunglasse[s] and so on.

records.definition_text: the set of necessary tools, clothing, etc. for a particular purpose
records.learnerexamples_text: office/camping/kitchen equipment;  electrical equipment; This is a really useful piece of equipment.; You can rent equipment or take your own.

records.definition_text: a period of time in history that is special for a particular reason
records.learnerexamples_text: the Clinton era; the post-war era; They had worked for peace during the long era of conflict.; The fall of the Berlin wall marked the end of an era.; The world is paddling through the era of technology.

records.definition_text: a mistake
records.learnerexamples_text: He admitted that he'd made an error.; The letter contained a number of typing errors.;  Human error has been blamed for the air crash.; The document was destroyed in error by the police.; There are a lot [of] factual errors in this article.

records.definition_text: moving stairs that take people from one level of a building to another
records.learnerexamples_text: I'll meet you by the up/down escalator on the second floor.; Shall we use the lift or take the escalator?; The newly decorated section is fairly modern [in] style with escalators and touch-screen ticket machine[s].

records.definition_text: to succeed in getting away from a place where you do not want to be
records.learnerexamples_text: The two prisoners escaped from prison last night.; There were reports that a lion had escaped from its cage at a nearby zoo.; You also get to meet people there, interesting people - for example, I met a really weird guy who claims to have escaped from an asylum, twice!

records.definition_text: to avoid a dangerous or unpleasant situation
records.learnerexamples_text: She was lucky to escape serious injury.; Chelsea only just escaped defeat in the second round of the cup.; Happily they were found by some hunters and escaped with minor injuries.

records.definition_text: something that helps you to forget about your usual life or problems
records.learnerexamples_text: I love old movies - they're such an escape from the real world.; Going on holiday is a great idea and I think it's the best way to relax and have fun, but it would also be an escape from the daily routine and a break from your tiring job.

records.definition_text: for one particular person, purpose, or reason
records.learnerexamples_text: I cooked this meal especially for you.; I remember the taste of the pineapple cake that you baked especially for me and your home-made goos[e]berry wine.

records.definition_text: a short piece of writing about a particular subject, especially one done by students
records.learnerexamples_text: For homework I want you to write an essay on endangered species.; I could write an extra essay.

records.definition_text: very important and necessary
records.learnerexamples_text: Government support will be essential if the project is to succeed.; Computers are an essential part of our lives.; Water is essential for/to living things.;  It is essential that our prices remain competitive.; For the experiment to be valid, it is essential to record the data accurately.

records.definition_text: relating to the most important characteristics or ideas of something
records.learnerexamples_text: It's essentially a dictionary but it differs in one or two respects.; What he's saying is essentially true.; Although we are essentially a rock band, we integrate elements of traditional Indian music (such as sitar).

records.definition_text: to start a company or organization that is likely to continue for a long time
records.learnerexamples_text: The brewery was established in 1822.; The first restaurant, which was established 10 years ago, is called Paris.

records.definition_text: a large area of land in the country which is owned by a family or an organization and is often used for growing crops or raising animals
records.learnerexamples_text: a country estate; There is a special law in Sweden which allows everyone to wander [through] any private estate unless one causes harm.

records.definition_text: a group of houses or factories built in a planned way
records.learnerexamples_text: a housing estate; an industrial estate; I live [o]n a big housing estate.

records.definition_text: to guess the cost, size, value, etc. of something
records.learnerexamples_text: Government sources estimate a long-term 50% increase in rail fares.; They estimate that the journey will take at least two weeks.;  It was difficult to estimate how many trees had been destroyed.; The number of dead is estimated at over three hundred.; I estimate it will take only 7 minutes to walk from the conference center to the hotel.

records.definition_text: a guess of what the size, value, amount, cost, etc. of something might be
records.learnerexamples_text: The number of people who applied for the course was 120 compared with an initial estimate of between 50 and 100.; This is only a rough estimate.

records.definition_text: guessed
records.learnerexamples_text: an estimated cost/value ; My estimated [time of] arrival [at] Heathrow airport is nine o'clock in the morning and my flight number is OK 1312.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize a comparison
records.learnerexamples_text: Her last film was even better.; The next 36 hours will be even colder, with snow showers just about everywhere.; I think Alex is going to be even taller than his father.; It's even more difficult to find work.; When I saw her getting off the train I really was close to break[ing] down because she looked even more beautiful.

records.definition_text: whether or not
records.learnerexamples_text: Even if you take a taxi, you'll still miss your train.; I often go to parks, with or without the children, even if the weather is not good.

records.definition_text: something that happens, especially something important or unusual
records.learnerexamples_text: Local people have been shocked by recent events in the town.; The police are trying to determine the series of events that led up to the murder.; I like this book because I like the description of historical events.

records.definition_text: a race, party, competition, etc. that has been organized for a particular time
records.learnerexamples_text: Over two thousand people took part in the event.; They stage big sporting events here.; They organize a lot of social events.; When there are parties or important social events, I usually choose a dress to wear.

records.definition_text: although
records.learnerexamples_text: Even though he left school at 16, he still managed to become a millionaire.; He still smokes even though he's got asthma.; They didn't give up hope even though they were tired and wet to the bone.

records.definition_text: although
records.learnerexamples_text: Even though it was getting dark, we decided to walk on to the next village.; He still smokes even though he's got asthma.; They didn't give up hope even though they were tired and wet to the bone.

records.definition_text: in the end, especially after a long time
records.learnerexamples_text: Eventually they reached an agreement.; He eventually got round to fixing the bike.; Anyway Pat eventually apologized to me.

records.definition_text: continuously since that time
records.learnerexamples_text: We met at school and have been friends ever since.; He's been depressed ever since he got divorced.; The pen was given [to me] by my father on my birthday and I have treasured it ever since.

records.definition_text: very
records.learnerexamples_text: It was ever so kind of you to meet us at the airport.; It was ever so kind of you to take the trouble and make room for us although we arrived quite unexpectedly.

records.definition_text: as much as is possible
records.learnerexamples_text: I'd like to wish you every success in your new job.; She has every reason to be unhappy after losing her job and her home.; You had every opportunity to make a complaint.; Every effort is being made to minimise civilian casualties.; She has every right to be proud of her tremendous achievements.

records.definition_text: sometimes but not often
records.searchterms_text: (every) once in a while;every once in a while;once
records.learnerexamples_text: We do go to the beach once in a while.; She did not say very much except for "oh" and "yes, yes" every once in a while.

records.definition_text: sometimes but not often
records.searchterms_text: (every) once in a while;every once in a while;while;whiles
records.learnerexamples_text: We do go to the beach once in a while.; She did not say very much except for "oh" and "yes, yes" every once in a while.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize that you are talking about each one of a group or series
records.learnerexamples_text: I call him every single day.; The decision affected every single one of them.; But we used to play together every single day!

records.definition_text: something that makes you believe that something is true or exists
records.learnerexamples_text: evidence of global warming; There is no evidence that the theory is true.; New evidence suggests/shows this argument is flawed. ; There is scientific evidence that the drug is addictive.;  All the evidence points to a substantial rise in traffic over the next few years.

records.definition_text: obvious to everyone and easy to see or understand
records.learnerexamples_text: The full extent of the damage only became evident the following morning.;  From the smell it was evident that the drains had been blocked for several days.; In conclusion, it is evident that it is better to do shopping in big supermarkets or shopping centres than small local shops in terms of time, money, working hours and family life.

records.definition_text: in a way that is easy to see
records.learnerexamples_text: He evidently likes her.; There are, evidently, points in favour and points against.

records.definition_text: something that is very bad and harmful
records.learnerexamples_text: Drug-addiction is one of today's great social evils.; The theme of the play is the battle between good and evil.; It is not simply [the] confronting of good and evil.

records.definition_text: very cruel, bad or harmful
records.learnerexamples_text: an evil monster; These people are just evil.; She is a very dark and evil person who can't forget the first Mrs. de Winter.

records.definition_text: the way in which living things change and develop over millions of years
records.learnerexamples_text: Darwin's theory of evolution; I think it is good to have zoos, but we shouldn't try to control natural evolution as we have done until now.

records.definition_text: a gradual process of change and development
records.learnerexamples_text: the evolution of language; [Leonardo's] studies and projects on mechanics puzzle us and foresee the future evolution of science and technology.

records.definition_text: completely correct in every detail
records.learnerexamples_text: The exact distance is 1.838 metres.; I'm afraid I can't give you exact details.; The exact location of the factory has yet to be decided.; They've lived here a long time - 25 years to be exact.; I am looking forward to your next letter to know the exact time of your [arrival].

records.definition_text: used to emphasize what you are saying
records.learnerexamples_text: I've found some shoes that are exactly the same colour as that dress.; Do exactly what I tell you and no-one will get hurt!; That's exactly why I didn't go.; That is exactly one of the reasons [why] I decided to join a new English class.

records.definition_text: something you say when you agree completely with someone
records.learnerexamples_text: "Surely they should have told us about this problem sooner?" "Exactly!"

records.definition_text: when someone looks at or considers something carefully in order to discover something
records.learnerexamples_text: a medical examination; I had to have a medical examination when I started my new job.; The evidence is still under examination.; I thought it was paint at first, but on closer examination I realised it was dried blood.; Finally we went to the hospital for a medical examination and fortunately we were all right.

records.definition_text: to look at or consider a person or thing carefully and in detail in order to discover something about them
records.learnerexamples_text: She picked up the knife and examined it closely.; He was examined by a doctor as soon as he arrived.; Experts are examining the wreckage for clues about the cause of the explosion.; I examined both of them and finally I discovered [that it] was a virus changed genetically in order to kill people.

records.definition_text: someone who tests how much you know about something, or how well you can do something
records.learnerexamples_text: The writing paper is marked by trained examiners.; When the examiner said that I had passed, I could not believe it.

records.definition_text: someone or something that is very good and should be copied
records.learnerexamples_text: He is a very good example to the rest of the class.; You are a shining example for you[r] colle[a]gues.

records.definition_text: someone or something that is not included in a rule, group or list or that does not behave in the expected way
records.learnerexamples_text: There are exceptions to every rule.; I like all kinds of films with the exception of horror films.; Her books are always entertaining and this one is no exception.; You must report here every Tuesday without exception.; The animals looked so sad to me. So I decided to set them free, all of them, without exception.

records.definition_text: extremely good
records.learnerexamples_text: He really is an exceptional student.; This trip constitutes an exceptional challenge for me.

records.definition_text: used to give a reason why something is not possible or true
records.learnerexamples_text: I want to go, except that I'm tired.; She would have passed the exam, except that she was ill on the day.

records.definition_text: when you give something to someone and they give you something else
records.learnerexamples_text: an exchange  of ideas/information ; They were given food and shelter in exchange for work.; So, it was a very interesting exchange of ideas.

records.definition_text: an arrangement by which students and teachers from one country go to stay with students and teachers in another country
records.learnerexamples_text: Are you going on the French exchange this year?; His name is Rob and, [like] me, [he] applied to the student exchange program.

records.definition_text: to give something to someone and receive something similar from them
records.learnerexamples_text: It's traditional for the two teams to exchange shirts after the game.; We exchanged addresses and telephone numbers.; She moved to another part of town and we forgot to exchange our addresses.

records.definition_text: to take something back to the shop where you bought it and change it for something else
records.learnerexamples_text: Goods can only be exchanged on production of the original receipt.; Could I exchange this shirt for a larger size?

records.definition_text: If two people exchange looks, opinions, views, etc., they look at each other, talk to each other, etc.
records.searchterms_text: exchange;exchange looks opinions views etc;exchange looks, opinions, views, etc.;exchanged;exchanges;exchanging
records.learnerexamples_text: The group meets every month to exchange their views on a book they have all read.; You can exchange opinions with them as to the way of life in Japan and your country.

records.definition_text: the rate at which the money of one country can be changed for the money of another country
records.learnerexamples_text: The Money Ready Reckoner gives the exchange rate for any country you plan to visit and shows how much currency you will get.; I looked around and saw a shop with the notice "Currency exchange". I decided to [go] in [to find out] the exchange rate.

records.definition_text: in an excited way
records.learnerexamples_text: She ran excitedly down the hall to greet her cousins.; We talked excitedly about it all the way home.

records.definition_text: when people feel very happy and enthusiastic
records.learnerexamples_text: The competition is causing a lot of excitement.; If you want excitement, you should try parachuting.; However, if you are looking for fun and excitement, I would go for the city.

records.definition_text: a punctuation mark (!) used at the end of a sentence that expresses surprise, excitement or shock
records.learnerexamples_text: Her emails are full of exclamation marks.; The day was wonderful as I got two A's with [an] exclamation mark.

records.definition_text: expensive and only for people who are rich or of a high social class
records.learnerexamples_text: an exclusive club/hotel/shop ; an exclusive part of town; We can also discern sophisticated, exclusive shops with expensive clothes in the city centres.

records.definition_text: to forgive someone
records.learnerexamples_text: Please excuse me for arriving late - the bus was delayed.; Please excuse my appearance - I've been painting.; I hope you'll excuse me now, I have to do my homework.

records.definition_text: to be given as a reason for someone's bad behaviour, so that it does not seem so bad
records.learnerexamples_text: Nothing can excuse that sort of behaviour.; Their main goals are to save the animals and/or to show the animals to the public in order to make us take an interest in the animals and in ecology. I think that these purposes can excuse [the fact] that the animals are locked up, if they [have] enough space and [are] treated very well.

records.definition_text: a reason that you give to explain why you did something wrong
records.learnerexamples_text: What was his excuse for being late?; He'd better have a good excuse for not being here!; I've never known him to miss a meeting - I'm sure he'll have an excuse.; There's no excuse for that sort of behaviour.; I had no excuse to give [for] being late with this report.

records.definition_text: a false reason that you give to explain why you do something
records.learnerexamples_text: Nick was just looking for an excuse to call her.; Any excuse for a holiday!; Also shopping for clothes is an excuse to go out with girls!!

records.definition_text: to do physical activities to make your body strong and healthy
records.l_topic_text_text: body and health, people: actions, shopping
records.learnerexamples_text: She exercises most evenings, usually by running.; A work-out in the gym will exercise all the major muscle groups.; It's funny how I heard about that; I was at the gym with Sarah, we were exercising when we heard Tom talking about it with John.

records.definition_text: extremely tired
records.learnerexamples_text: By the time they reached the summit they were exhausted.; Exhausted, they fell asleep.; When we got back home I was absolutely exhausted.

records.definition_text: making you feel extremely tired
records.learnerexamples_text: I've had an exhausting day.; We will also have the opportunity to drink a coffee or have a snack after an exhausting day in the swimming pool!!

records.definition_text: when you are extremely tired
records.learnerexamples_text: She felt ill with exhaustion.; The tennis star is said to be suffering from exhaustion.; Eighty kilometres is a pretty long distance and there is a threat that our trip would turn out to be a gruelling experience because of physical exhaustion.

records.definition_text: when objects such as paintings are shown to the public
records.learnerexamples_text: to see/visit an exhibition; an exhibition centre ; There's a new exhibition of sculpture on at the city gallery.; We went to the Royal Academy to see the Kandinsky exhibition.

records.definition_text: to be present or real
records.learnerexamples_text: Poverty still exists in this country.; Ghosts don't exist anyway.; Buses will not exist any more and everyone will have his own car and his own computer too.

records.definition_text: when something or someone exists
records.learnerexamples_text: Many people question the existence of God.; According to modern cosmology, the Universe came into existence about fifteen billion years ago.; The theatre company that they started is still in existence today.; The book gives explanations about all these popular beliefs about ghosts and their supposed existence among living people.

records.definition_text: describes something that exists now
records.learnerexamples_text: The existing church was built in the sixteenth century.; The existing laws are inadequate.; The computer upgraded most of the existing inventions, and made them more efficient, faster and [more user-friendly].

records.definition_text: to stop using a program on a computer
records.learnerexamples_text: Press escape to exit the game.

records.definition_text: unusual, interesting and often foreign
records.learnerexamples_text: exotic flowers/fruits ; Even if you do not have any cooking skills you can enjoy exotic meals.

records.definition_text: to increase in size or amount, or to make something increase in this way
records.learnerexamples_text: The air in the balloon expands when heated.; They expanded their retail operations during the 1980s.; I would like to expand my library.

records.definition_text: when something increases in size or amount
records.learnerexamples_text: These years saw the rapid expansion of the software industry.; More effective ways includ[e] the construction of bridges [in] heavy traffic areas and the expansion of METRO to even more areas of Athens.

records.definition_text: to think or believe that something will happen
records.learnerexamples_text: We are expecting a lot of applicants for the job.; I expect (that) she'll be very angry.; He didn't expect to see me.; I expect that it is going to be sunny because in the hotel there is a swimming-pool.

records.definition_text: to think that someone should behave in a particular way or do a particular thing
records.learnerexamples_text: You will be expected to work some weekends.; You have to satisfy your boss [but] you do not have to do more than you are expected to.

records.definition_text: when you expect good things to happen in the future
records.learnerexamples_text: The holiday lived up to all our expectations.; I have high expectations for this job.; We did so well - beyond all our expectations.; The talks given by writers were up to my expectations and it was a pleasure to attend all of them.

records.definition_text: thought likely to happen or be true
records.learnerexamples_text: The expected power cuts never happened.; I went into the theatre on time but became a little bit angry [at having to] wait until 20:15, forty-five minutes after the expected starting time.

records.definition_text: an organized journey, especially a long one for a particular purpose
records.learnerexamples_text: Shackleton led several expeditions in the Antarctic.; I was with my father on Mount Tahan [and] I had the best time of my life during this expedition.

records.definition_text: the money that you spend on something
records.learnerexamples_text: Buying a bigger car has proved to be well worth the expense.; We've just had a new garage built at great expense.; It's silly to go to the expense of buying new clothes when you don't really need them.; You have to pay/cover your own medical expenses.; We couldn't afford the expense of a new car [at] that time.

records.definition_text: knowledge that you get from doing a job, or from doing, seeing, or feeling something
records.learnerexamples_text: She has a lot of teaching experience.; You become more confident in your work as you get more experience.; Do you have any experience of working with children?; I know from experience that you can't trust him.; In my experience, people smile back if you smile at them.

records.definition_text: something that happens to you that affects how you feel
records.learnerexamples_text: I had a rather unpleasant experience at the dentist's.; My trip to Australia was an experience I shall never forget.; It was a great experience, we talked for 3 hours about lots of thing[s].

records.definition_text: If you experience something, it happens to you, or you feel it.
records.learnerexamples_text: We experienced a lot of difficulty in selling our house.; It was the worst pain I'd ever experienced.; We had three fantastic days [- the best] we have ever experienced.

records.definition_text: having skill or knowledge because you have done something many times
records.learnerexamples_text: an experienced teacher; She is very experienced in marketing.; You can go to the nearest village, where you can [do a] mountain walk led by experienced guides.

records.definition_text: a test, especially a scientific one, that you do in order to learn something or to discover whether something is true
records.learnerexamples_text: Some people believe that experiments on animals should be banned.; Scientists are carrying out/doing experiments to test the effectiveness of the new drug.; In the chemistry lab experiments are often set up.

records.definition_text: to try something in order to discover what it is like
records.learnerexamples_text: Did he ever experiment with drugs?; Last year I started to take a lot of black and white photos and I wanted to follow the process all the way through so I bought an enlarger. I was now able to experiment with all sorts of te[chniq]ues.

records.definition_text: someone who has a lot of skill in something or a lot of knowledge of something
records.learnerexamples_text: a computer/gardening/medical expert; He's an expert on Japanese literature.; My "personal" trainer is Peter, he is a real expert in running.

records.definition_text: having or showing a lot of knowledge or skill
records.learnerexamples_text: The centre provides expert advice for people with financial problems.; What's your expert opinion?; We're not expert cyclists and we could [get] tired before we get to the Mountain Hostel.

records.definition_text: the details or reasons that someone gives to make something clear or easy to understand
records.learnerexamples_text: What was her explanation for why she was late?; Could you give me a quick explanation of how it works?; There must be some kind of explanation.

records.definition_text: If something such as a bomb explodes, it bursts with noise and force, and if you explode it, you make it burst with noise and force.
records.learnerexamples_text: A bomb exploded at one of London's busiest railway stations this morning.; He was driving so fast that his car tyre exploded.; A bomb had exploded and that boy rescued me from the accident.

records.definition_text: to treat someone unfairly for your own advantage
records.learnerexamples_text: Laws exist to stop companies exploiting their employees.; I suppose those people are often exploited and do not have real friends with whom they can share feelings and emotions. Therefore I believe being a famous person is also synon[y]mous [with] being lonely.

records.definition_text: to use or develop something to your advantage
records.learnerexamples_text: We need to make sure that we exploit our resources as fully as possible.; John would certainly exploit this unique opportunity and meet the interviewer's expectations easily.

records.definition_text: to go around a place where you have never been in order to find out what is there
records.learnerexamples_text: The best way to explore the countryside is on foot.; The children have gone exploring in the woods.; You can walk and explore in the jungle.

records.definition_text: to find out more about something, often something that you might do in the future
records.learnerexamples_text: We're exploring the possibility of buying a holiday home.; It is a great camera and I still [have] not explore[d] all [the] possibilities it holds.

records.definition_text: when something such as a bomb explodes
records.learnerexamples_text: Forty people were killed in the explosion.; The fire was thought to have been caused by a gas explosion.; I was doing my homework when I heard an explosion.

records.definition_text: to send goods to another country for sale
records.learnerexamples_text: French cheeses are exported to many different countries.; Our clothes sell so well in this country that we have no need to export.; And of course, while Italy is exporting pizza, spaghetti and food like that, Italian people are able to try different food from foreign countries, like hamburger[s], Chinese food, or pudding.

records.definition_text: a product that you sell in another country or the business of selling products in another country
records.learnerexamples_text: Coffee is one of Brazil's main exports.; The export of ivory is now strictly controlled.; India grows tea for export.; We are planning to develop our export market.; At present I work for a Multinational company as export officer.

records.definition_text: to make public something bad or dishonest
records.learnerexamples_text: The review exposed widespread corruption in the police force.; The newspaper story exposed him as a liar.; If I do not receive full satisfaction, I will expose your operation by writing to the newspaper.

records.definition_text: to show what you think or how you feel using words or actions
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm simply expressing my opinion.; I would like to express my thanks for your kindness.; I'm sorry, I'm not expressing myself very clearly.; Words can't express how happy I am.; Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to express my dissatisfaction about the show you presented two weeks ago at your theatre.

records.definition_text: the look on someone's face, showing what they feel or think
records.learnerexamples_text: facial expressions; He had such a sad expression on his face.; I could tell from her expression that something serious had happened.; He had a funny expression on his face.

records.definition_text: a word or phrase
records.learnerexamples_text: He uses a lot of informal expressions.; 'A can of worms' is an expression which means 'a difficult situation'.; With th[ese] kind[s] of videos, they could learn words and expressions used every day by normal people talking to normal people.

records.definition_text: when you show what you think or how you feel using words or actions
records.learnerexamples_text: He wrote her a poem as an expression of his love.; We've received a lot of expressions of support for our campaign.;  Freedom of expression is a basic human right.; It's better to give expression to your anger, rather than hiding it.; It always thrilled me, the energy and expression this dance had.

records.definition_text: to make something bigger or longer
records.learnerexamples_text: We have plans to extend our house.; They've extended their range of products.; The existing lighting loop would be extended and [the] capacity of the illumination would be increased.

records.definition_text: to make an activity, agreement, etc. last for a longer time
records.learnerexamples_text: They have extended the deadline by one week.; A lot of shops have extended their opening hours.; I need to extend my visa.; If we decide to extend our stay for two more days, does the offer still stand?

records.definition_text: extra time that you are given to do or use something
records.learnerexamples_text: I've applied for an extension to my visa.

records.definition_text: a telephone that is connected to the main telephone in an office or other large building
records.learnerexamples_text: Call me on extension 3104.; For further information call 990-643 extension 93.

records.definition_text: something that has developed as a result of something else
records.learnerexamples_text: The book is an extension of ideas he set out in an earlier article.; So we might say the computer is the extension of our brain.

records.definition_text: large in amount or size
records.learnerexamples_text: Fire had caused extensive damage to the building.; This is probably the most extensive modern art collection in Europe.; The school has extensive grounds. ; The motorway was in need of extensive repairs.; Both events received extensive coverage in the newspapers.

records.definition_text: the size or importance of something
records.learnerexamples_text: They are just beginning to realize the full extent of the damage.; Her face was injured to such an extent that we didn't recognize her.; Rosie's teacher was impressed by the extent of her knowledge.; The River Nile is over 6500 kilometres in extent.; [For the] past couple of decades, TV has been diffused in Japan to such an extent that nowadays, one household is likely to have more than 2 TV sets that [show] a wide range of programmes nearly 24 hours [a day].

records.definition_text: relating to the outside part of something
records.learnerexamples_text: the external walls of the house; This cream is for external use only.; If you see all this external decoration, you will probably fall in love [with] this art.

records.definition_text: coming from or relating to another country, group, organization, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: Most news magazines have a section devoted to external affairs.; All exams are marked by an external examiner.

records.definition_text: more
records.learnerexamples_text: They pay her extra to work nights.; Will there be any special events that cost extra?

records.definition_text: something that you can get with something else if you pay a little more money
records.learnerexamples_text: A sunroof is an optional extra on this model of the car.; The DVD contains many extras.

records.definition_text: to remove or take out something
records.learnerexamples_text: The oil which is extracted from olives is used mainly for cooking.; The tooth was eventually extracted.; I'm really sorry, but I can't come on the day before because I need to have my teeth extracted.

records.definition_text: a short part of a book, poem, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: They published an extract from his autobiography.; The number of copied and read articles or book extracts ha[s] increased steadily.

records.definition_text: very
records.learnerexamples_text: She is, it must be said, extraordinarily beautiful.; Besides, the trip will be extraordinarily helpful for my course at school.

records.definition_text: very special, unusual or strange
records.learnerexamples_text: He told the extraordinary story of his escape.; She was an extraordinary young woman.; On the next day there was an extraordinary thunderstorm!

records.definition_text: the most unusual or the most serious possible
records.learnerexamples_text: extreme weather conditions ; In extreme cases, the disease can lead to blindness.; It seems to be an extreme case but it is a fact that modern children have no more contact with animal life.

records.definition_text: very large in amount or degree
records.learnerexamples_text: extreme pain/danger/wealth ; This time I promise that I will take extreme caution [with] your things.

records.definition_text: very, or much more than usual
records.learnerexamples_text: They played extremely well.; She's extremely beautiful/intelligent.; The film was extremely funny.

records.definition_text: a sport or activity that is exciting and dangerous
records.learnerexamples_text: I love most extreme sports, such as bungee jumping and white-water rafting.; You can go camping, climb mountains or learn a lot of extreme sports.

records.definition_text: the thin line of hair that is above each eye
records.learnerexamples_text: He's got really bushy eyebrows.; He woke up and cleaned off the blood from his injured eyebrow.

records.definition_text: one of the short hairs which grow from the edge of your eyelids
records.learnerexamples_text: false/long eyelashes

records.definition_text: the piece of skin that covers your eyes when you close them
records.learnerexamples_text: His eyelids drooped with tiredness.

records.definition_text: the ability to see
records.learnerexamples_text: My eyesight is getting worse.; I had some trouble with my eyesight, so he advised me to wear glasses and not to strain my eyes.

records.definition_text: If you face a problem, or a problem faces you, you have to deal with it.
records.learnerexamples_text: This is one of the many problems faced by working mothers.; Passengers could face long delays.; You're faced with a very difficult choice there.; Grandparents are experienced people and they can help their child[ren] to avoid a lot of problems which they have faced.

records.definition_text: to be or turn in a particular direction
records.learnerexamples_text: Our house faces north/south/east/west.; She turned to face him.; The café faces (towards) the sea.; There is a desk [to] the right of the room which faces my bed.

records.definition_text: to accept that something unpleasant is true and start to deal with the situation
records.learnerexamples_text: I think Phil has to face the fact that she no longer loves him.; We have to face facts here - we simply don't have enough money.; He's dying but he refuses to face the truth.; But Mary has a strong personality, she faces the facts.

records.definition_text: directly, meeting someone in the same place
records.learnerexamples_text: We need to talk face to face.; I need to talk to her face to face.

records.definition_text: involving two people who are meeting in the same place
records.learnerexamples_text: a face-to-face meeting

records.definition_text: to accept that a difficult situation exists
records.searchterms_text: face;face up to sth;face up to sth
records.learnerexamples_text: Eventually, he faced up to his money problems.; She has to face up to the fact that he's not coming back.; However, she had to face up to the fact that it was her duty to question the serial killer, to find out what his motives were.

records.definition_text: the buildings, equipment and services provided for a particular purpose
records.learnerexamples_text: childcare facilities;  sports facilities; The city has more facilities than the countryside.

records.definition_text: a part of a system or machine which makes it possible to do something
records.learnerexamples_text: an overdraft facility; I would suggest free Internet access as an extra facility in our library.

records.definition_text: real events and experiences, not things that are imagined
records.learnerexamples_text: It's sometimes hard to separate fact from fiction.

records.definition_text: one of the things that has an effect on a situation, decision, event, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: Money was an important factor in their decision to move.; Price is an important/key/major factor in the success of any product.;  economic factors; [Modern technology] is another important factor which affects our life.

records.definition_text: to become less bright, strong or clear, or to make something become less bright, strong or clear
records.learnerexamples_text: If you hang your clothes out in the bright sun, they will fade.; My suntan is already fading.; They arrived home just as the light was fading.; The music began to fade.; The sun had faded the blue walls.

records.definition_text: to gradually become less strong or clear and then disappear
records.learnerexamples_text: With time, memories of that painful summer would fade away.; These memories would never fade away, she knew it.

records.definition_text: to not be successful
records.learnerexamples_text: She moved to London in the hope of finding work as a model, but failed.; He failed in his attempt to break the record.; This method of growing tomatoes never fails.; I tried to make him give up, but all my attempts failed.

records.definition_text: to stop working normally, or to become weaker
records.learnerexamples_text: Two of the plane's engines had failed.; The sound system failed.

records.definition_text: to not do what is necessary or expected
records.learnerexamples_text: He failed to turn up for football practice yesterday.; He failed to mention that we wouldn't be paid for the work.; Your advertisement also failed to mention the fact that there w[ere] no discounts.

records.definition_text: when someone or something does not succeed
records.learnerexamples_text: Their attempt to climb Everest ended in failure.; I'm a bit of a failure at making cakes.; I feel such a failure.; David told her that the reason [for] his failure was her, because she used to press him and she couldn't accept that he wanted to be an actor.

records.definition_text: when something does not work, or stops working as well as it should
records.learnerexamples_text: All trains were delayed due to a power failure.; He died of heart/liver failure.; [There] has been a power failure but it will be solved in [a] few minutes.

records.definition_text: when you do not do something that you are expected to do
records.learnerexamples_text: Failure to pay within 14 days will result in interest being charged.; It was his failure to return her phone call that told her that something was wrong.

records.definition_text: slight and not easy to notice, smell, hear, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: a faint sound/noise/smell ; She gave me a faint smile.; I heard a faint sound.

records.definition_text: to suddenly become unconscious for a short time, usually falling down
records.learnerexamples_text: He faints at the sight of blood.; I nearly fainted in the heat.; The young girl was about to faint.

records.definition_text: treating everyone in the same way, so that no one has an advantage
records.learnerexamples_text: That's not fair! You always go first!; It's not fair to make me do all the work.; a fair trial; I can't spend all my time with one child - it wouldn't be fair on the others.; Even though she thought her m[u]m wasn't being fair, she decided to go and try to have a nice day with her family.

records.definition_text: acceptable, reasonable or right
records.learnerexamples_text: a fair deal ; He offered a fair price for the car.; That's a fair comment/question.; You may ask yourself: "What do you do in a club?" Well, it's a fair question!!!

records.definition_text: an event outside where you can ride large machines for pleasure and play games to win prizes
records.learnerexamples_text: The children spent all their money on rides at the fair.; For example in the morning we can go to a fair, like Six Flags. I think that it will be exciting.

records.definition_text: used for saying that you can understand and accept someone's opinion or decision
records.learnerexamples_text: "He says he'll only work on Sunday if he gets paid extra." "Fair enough."; Most of the streets are open [to] cars and therefore people tend to escape to a little area around the pedestrian streets. Fair enough, but it make[s] those streets terribly overcrowded.

records.definition_text: used for saying that you can understand and accept someone's opinion or decision
records.learnerexamples_text: "He says he'll only work on Sunday if he gets paid extra." "Fair enough."; Most of the streets are open [to] cars and therefore people tend to escape to a little area around the pedestrian streets. Fair enough, but it make[s] those streets terribly overcrowded.

records.definition_text: more than average, but less than very
records.learnerexamples_text: a fairly big family; She's fairly tall.; We get on fairly well.; I saw her fairly recently.; The weather was fairly warm.

records.definition_text: If you do something fairly, you do it in a way which is right and reasonable and treats people equally.
records.learnerexamples_text: He claimed that he hadn't been treated fairly by his employers.; Officials will ensure that the election is carried out fairly.

records.definition_text: great trust or confidence in something or someone
records.learnerexamples_text: She has no faith in modern medicine.; You'll be fine - I have great faith in you.; After the trial, his family said they had lost all faith in the legal system.; We must do our best to help [these children] to have faith in their future.

records.definition_text: strong belief in a god or gods
records.learnerexamples_text: Even in the bad times she never lost her faith.; Her faith in God was shattered when her baby died.; It's my faith that keeps me going.; Your story about Christianity was very interesting and I was shocked at your deep faith in God.

records.definition_text: a particular religion
records.learnerexamples_text: the Muslim/Christian/Jewish faith; a multi-faith society; Everybody was praying, asking for help according to their faith or religion.

records.definition_text: loyal
records.learnerexamples_text: a faithful friend ; They are faithful supporters of the Labour Party.; His faithful old dog accompanied him everywhere he went.; An ideal pet should be a faithful friend [to] people, especially [to] its owner.

records.definition_text: to become lower in size, amount or strength
records.learnerexamples_text: Demand for new cars has fallen recently.; The standard of his work has fallen during the year.; The temperature could fall below zero overnight.; Average temperatures fell by ten degrees.; The pound has fallen to its lowest-ever level against the dollar.

records.definition_text: when the size, amount or strength of something gets lower
records.learnerexamples_text: the recent fall in the price of petrol; a fall in the unemployment rate; We could hear the rise and fall of voices in the other room.; There is a fall in job vacancies.

records.definition_text: when someone or something falls down to the ground, often without intending to or by accident
records.learnerexamples_text: He had a nasty fall and hurt his back.; The boulder smashed several small trees during its fall.; I was terrified and I heard the noise of a fall just by my side.

records.definition_text: to break into pieces
records.learnerexamples_text: My poor old boots are falling apart.; It looks like it [is] going to fall apart any day.

records.definition_text: to start having problems that you cannot deal with
records.learnerexamples_text: The deal fell apart because of a lack of financing.; Their marriage fell apart when she found out about her husband's affair.; All her dreams and wishes fell apart.

records.definition_text: to start to sleep or become ill
records.learnerexamples_text: I fell asleep on the sofa watching TV.; I planned to go with my cousin but unfortunately she fell ill, so I had to go with my friend.

records.definition_text: to fall onto the ground
records.learnerexamples_text: Our apple tree fell down in the storm.; He stumbled and fell down.; When I got up in the morning, I slip[ped] on a piece of soap and fell down.

records.definition_text: to fall over so that your face hits the ground, often in an embarrassing way
records.learnerexamples_text: I stepped on the ice and fell flat on my face.; You can guess what happened next - I fell flat on my face right in the mud and I have never felt more embarrassed in my life!

records.definition_text: to suddenly have strong romantic feelings about someone
records.learnerexamples_text: She fell for a tall, handsome Frenchman when she was on holiday in Paris.; I saw a handsome boy [and] I fell for him.

records.definition_text: to start to love someone
records.learnerexamples_text: I was 20 when I first fell in love.; I fell in love with David.

records.definition_text: to argue with someone and stop being friendly with them
records.learnerexamples_text: She's fallen out with her sister.; They fell out over money.; My husband always blame[s] me and we fall out over my incapacity to cook.

records.definition_text: If someone or something falls over, they fall to the ground or onto their side.
records.learnerexamples_text: She tripped and fell over.; The fence fell over in the wind.; I nearly fell over because the corridor was very dark.

records.definition_text: If a plan or agreement falls through, it fails to happen.
records.learnerexamples_text: Our plans to go on holiday together fell through when Jamie became ill.; All our plans fell through and I hope it will never happen to me again.

records.definition_text: not true or correct
records.learnerexamples_text: a false name; false information; The rumour later turned out to be false.; You'll get a false impression/idea of the town if you only visit the university.; I must say that the advertisement for the show included a lot of false information.

records.definition_text: not real, but made to look or seem real
records.learnerexamples_text: false eyelashes/teeth ; false documents; Asking what made her do so she answered that she had forgotten her false teeth, without which she couldn't have faced the fire-brigade.

records.definition_text: when you are known by many people because of your achievements, skills, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: She first rose to fame as a singer at the age of 16.; She moved to London in search of fame and fortune.; It is certain that these people have fame, fortune and success, and that many of them are very rich.

records.definition_text: easy to recognize because of being seen, met, heard, etc. before
records.learnerexamples_text: There were one or two familiar faces.; The house looked strangely familiar, though she knew she'd never been there before.; The street was familiar to me.; Someone started to wave and then I saw a familiar face.

records.definition_text: the children of a family
records.learnerexamples_text: Single parents have to raise a family on their own.; Paul and Alison are hoping to start a family soon.; Some people also want to [have] a family because they want to be a father or a mother.

records.definition_text: one part of someone's existence
records.learnerexamples_text: I never talk about my private life.; my working life; We interviewed senior politicians, famous writers and others in public life.; The film [is] about family life.

records.definition_text: something that is used to move the air around so that it feels cooler, such as a machine or an object that you move with your hand
records.learnerexamples_text: There was no air conditioning, just a ceiling fan turning slowly.; Since it's quite hot here I brought a fan. I have to use it at night otherwise I can't get to sleep.

records.definition_text: to want to have or do something
records.learnerexamples_text: Do you fancy a drink this evening?; I didn't fancy swimming in that water.; Do you fancy eating at the restaurant together?

records.definition_text: to feel sexually attracted to someone
records.learnerexamples_text: I fancied him the first time I saw him.; He had 3 very nice boys and everybody in my class knew that I fancied his youngest son Nicolai.

records.definition_text: extremely
records.learnerexamples_text: They're fantastically rich.; They're doing fantastically well.; We spent three fantastically romantic days later.

records.definition_text: a situation or event that you imagine, which is not real or true
records.learnerexamples_text: Steve's favourite fantasy was to own a big house and a flashy car.;  sexual fantasies; She retreated into  a fantasy world, where she could be anything she wanted.; Reading a book stimulates one's fantasy and imagination.

records.definition_text: very much
records.learnerexamples_text: This car is far better than our old one.; It cost far more (money) than I could afford.; He loses his temper far too often.; I'd far rather/sooner go to the theatre than watch a DVD.; I think restaurant B is far better than restaurant A.

records.definition_text: describes the part of something that is most distant from the centre or from you
records.learnerexamples_text: His office is at the far end of the corridor.; The children ran to the far side/corner of the room.; The dark spot at the far end of the wall seemed to be coming after her this time.

records.definition_text: the money that you pay for a journey on a vehicle such as a bus or train
records.learnerexamples_text: Air/Bus/Train fares are going up again.; In fact, there are buses (number 843 and 845) which go [to] my village but the bus fare is very expensive for me.

records.definition_text: the activity of working on a farm or organizing the work there
records.learnerexamples_text: modern farming practices; I am interested in farming and hope to own a farm one day.

records.definition_text: extremely interested
records.learnerexamples_text: They were fascinated by his stories. ; I am sure you will be fascinated by his work and his multi-faceted character.

records.definition_text: extremely interesting
records.learnerexamples_text: a fascinating person/place ; I found the movie fascinating.; You can enjoy not only Hungarian food but also fascinating Hungarian music.

records.definition_text: making and selling clothes
records.learnerexamples_text: the fashion industry ; fashion magazines ; When I'm tired, I like reading fashion magazines.

records.definition_text: popular at a particular time
records.learnerexamples_text: a fashionable nightclub/restaurant ; fashionable clothes ;  It's no longer fashionable to smoke.; There are some fashionable cafes, restaurants and museums.

records.definition_text: to close or fix something together, or to become closed or fixed together
records.learnerexamples_text: Fasten your seat belt.; This shirt fastens at the back.; She fell fast asleep and only woke to the sound of the announcement: "Ladies and gent[le]men fasten your seat belts [-] in a couple of minutes we will be landing in Kingston".

records.definition_text: to fix one thing to another
records.searchterms_text: fasten;fasten sth on/to/together etc;fasten sth on/to/together, etc.;fastened;fastening;fastens
records.learnerexamples_text: He fastened the rope to a tree.

records.definition_text: a solid or liquid substance that is taken from animals or plants and used in cooking
records.learnerexamples_text: This product contains no animal fat.; I only use vegetable fats in cooking.; They should also consum[e] as much salad as they can, due to the fact that it does not contain fat.

records.definition_text: A fatal illness or accident causes death.
records.learnerexamples_text: This illness is fatal in almost all cases.; the fatal shooting of an unarmed 15-year-old; Paul received a fatal shot in [the] head.

records.definition_text: Fatal actions have very bad effects.
records.learnerexamples_text: He made the fatal mistake/error of believing what they told him.; That was a fatal mistake because that [person] was my teacher and he wasn't so pleased about my behaviour.

records.definition_text: what happens to someone, especially something bad
records.learnerexamples_text: We want to decide our own fate.; His fate is now in the hands of the jury.; No one as powerless as him deserves this fate.

records.definition_text: a power that some people believe decides what will happen
records.learnerexamples_text: When we met again by chance in Cairo, I felt it must be fate.; Fate has brought us together.; But, little we did know what fate had in store for us.

records.definition_text: the father of your husband or wife
records.learnerexamples_text: My father-in-law was a banker. ; My father-in-law, I'm pretty sure, [will] be able to answer all your questions.

records.definition_text: something that is wrong with something
records.learnerexamples_text: The car has a serious design fault.; They think the fire was caused by an electrical fault.; I went out of the house and I saw that the other houses had not got any lights, so it was not an electrical fault.

records.definition_text: something that is wrong with someone's character
records.learnerexamples_text: He has many faults, but dishonesty isn't one of them.; He had a fault: he talked a lot.

records.definition_text: not working correctly or not in perfect condition
records.learnerexamples_text: faulty brakes/goods ; Big supermarkets always [give] you a complete refund if an item is of poor quality or faulty.

records.definition_text: something that you do to help someone
records.learnerexamples_text: She rang up to ask me a favour.; Could you do me a favour - could you give this to Sean, please?; Could you do me a favour?

records.definition_text: showing that you like or approve of someone or something, or making you support or approve of someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: She made a very favourable impression on us.; It is the first thing people see from our village and if their first impression is favourable, they will feel like going further into the village.

records.definition_text: a thing that someone likes best or enjoys most
records.learnerexamples_text: How clever of you to buy chocolate chip cookies - they're my favourites.; We are going to see a thriller film, they are my favourites.

records.definition_text: to send a document using a fax machine
records.learnerexamples_text: Fax me your reply/Fax your reply to me.; I will ask one of my classmate[s] to fax me the work you [set], and I will try to do it.

records.definition_text: a strong, unpleasant feeling that you get when you think that something bad, dangerous, or frightening might happen
records.learnerexamples_text: her fear of snakes;  Shaking/Trembling with fear, she handed over the money to the gunman.; There are fears that the disease will spread to other countries.; Fears for her safety are growing.; The low profit figures simply confirmed my worst fears.

records.definition_text: to be worried or frightened that something bad might happen or might have happened
records.learnerexamples_text: Police fear (that) the couple may have drowned.;  It is feared (that) as many as two hundred passengers may have died in the crash.; Lots of changes which may occur during these next fifty years [might] make us fear that our sons' and grandsons' lives will not be as happy as ours.

records.definition_text: to be frightened of something or someone
records.learnerexamples_text: Most older employees fear unemployment.; What do you fear most?; I've always feared the dark.

records.definition_text: one of the soft, light things that grow from and cover a bird's skin
records.learnerexamples_text: I found a peacock's feather. ; Birds were cleaning their feathers [and singing] morning songs, monkeys were jumping [at] the top of an old tree in the corner of the mon[aste]ry yard.

records.definition_text: a typical quality, or an important part of something
records.learnerexamples_text: The town's main features are its beautiful mosque and ancient marketplace.; Our latest model of phone has several new features.; He explained the features of the new product to the rest of his colleagues.

records.definition_text: Someone's features are the parts of their face that you notice when you look at them.
records.learnerexamples_text: His eyes are his best feature.; They have similar figures, [and] the features of their faces are nearly the same.

records.definition_text: to include someone or something as an important part
records.learnerexamples_text: The film features James Dean as a disaffected teenager.; This week's broadcast features a report on victims of domestic violence.; My favourite song is "Candy Shop", by 50 Cent, featuring Olivia.

records.definition_text: annoyed or bored by something that you have experienced for too long

records.definition_text: to fill or enter a place in large numbers or amounts

records.definition_text: If something such as a liquid flows, it moves somewhere in a smooth, continuous way.

records.definition_text: to understand something

records.base_text: follow up sth or follow sth up

records.definition_text: expressing or causing happy feelings

records.definition_text: stupid and not wise

records.definition_text: being employed by or representing a company, country, etc.

records.definition_text: in support of or in agreement with
records.learnerexamples_text: I voted for the Greens at the last election.; So let's hear some applause for these talented young performers.; There are a lot of votes for and against keeping animals in cages.

records.definition_text: to order someone not to do something, or to say that something must not happen
records.learnerexamples_text: I forbid you to see that boy again!; The law forbids the sale of cigarettes to underage people.; He is forbidden from leaving the country.; But the worst effect is when someone is driving a car and [is at] the same time talking [on a] mobile phone: today, there is a law which forbids it.

records.definition_text: physical strength or power

records.definition_text: making you feel fear

records.definition_text: used when you are saying how similar or different two things, people or places are

happening or working for the whole of the working week and not only part of it
