records.learnerexamples_text: Dad hopes to retire next year. ; With this new class I hope to make progress.

records.definition_text: a piece of equipment used to make a loud sound as a warning or signal
records.learnerexamples_text: a car/fog horn ;  The taxi driver sounded/beeped his horn. ; How happy I was, hearing the sound of a car horn.

records.definition_text: a strong feeling of shock or fear
records.learnerexamples_text: She watched in horror as the car skidded across the road. ; The thought of speaking in front of so many people fills me with horror.; I then realized to my absolute horror, that I had forgotten the present.; I approached the door but to my horror, it was locked.

records.definition_text: someone who invites people to a meal or a party, or to stay in their home
records.learnerexamples_text: We thanked our hosts for the lovely evening.; My host family looked after me very well during my month in London.; My experience [of] liv[ing] with a host family was very good, so I suggest we should look for a nice place for both of us.

records.definition_text: a place like a cheap hotel, where you can live when you are away from home or have no home
records.learnerexamples_text: a youth hostel;  a hostel for the homeless; We'll stay in a hostel [be]cause it's cheap and we'll use public transport.

records.definition_text: Hot food contains strong spices which cause a burning feeling in your mouth.
records.learnerexamples_text: a hot curry; hot and spicy food; Here we have many restaurants to go [to], so it's hard to have a favourite, but we sometimes go to [the] Delhi restaurant, which serve[s] Indian food, because we like meals [that are] hot [with] various spices.

records.definition_text: done or happening every hour
records.learnerexamples_text: There's an hourly bus service into town.; A nurse checked him at hourly intervals.

records.definition_text: for each hour
records.learnerexamples_text: an hourly rate/wage; I'll also call the shop and ask [about] the hourly rate and the working hours.

records.definition_text: a long time
records.learnerexamples_text: I spent hours doing my homework. ; They kept us waiting for hours and hours.; We spent hours talking, but at ten o'clock he [took] me home.

records.definition_text: a family or group of people who live together in a house
records.learnerexamples_text: By the 1960s, most households had a TV.; household chores; household expenses; In Japan, for example, the vast majority of households have at least one car nowadays.

records.definition_text: the work of keeping a house clean and tidy
records.learnerexamples_text: I hate doing housework.; I ran out of vegetables and cans, [and] as I was not at home the housework wasn't done, and the children almost destroy[ed] my furniture.

records.definition_text: used to ask or talk about what an experience or event was like
records.learnerexamples_text: How was your flight?; How did you find the lecture?; How did you like the concert?; How was your birthday?

records.definition_text: used for emphasis
records.learnerexamples_text: I can't tell you how pleased I am that you came.; How nice to see you!; I was amazed at how quickly she finished.; It's quite amazing how quickly she could change my reason to learn English.

records.definition_text: used to ask for someone's opinion on a particular subject
records.learnerexamples_text: So the town was nice - how about the food?; I don't like shopping with my mum because she wants me to wear weird clothes. How about you?

records.definition_text: used to say that it does not make any difference how cold/difficult/slowly, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: We're not going to get there in time, however fast we drive. ; However hungry I am, I never seem to be able to finish off a whole pizza.; If Emma likes something she'll buy it however much it costs.; I'll see you after the show and give you £20 for the tickets, or however much they cost.; We think that we are careful and that we can avoid traffic accidents, but however careful we may be, some other people might be careless and hit us.

records.definition_text: used to ask for someone's opinion on a particular subject
records.learnerexamples_text: What about Ava - is she nice? ; So the town was nice - how about the food?; I also enjoy shopping for shoes, what about you?

records.definition_text: to put your arms around someone and hold them tightly, usually because you love or like them
records.learnerexamples_text: They hugged each other when they met at the station.; Emily hugged her teddy bear tightly to her chest.; She sat on the floor hugging her knees.; We walked in the street together and spoke [to] each other [for] more than for four hours and at the end we hugged and kissed.

records.definition_text: when you put your arms around someone and hold them tightly
records.learnerexamples_text: Come here and give me a big hug.; We always exchange hugs and kisses when we meet.; The singer of the band ,"Green Day" was coming to[wards] me. [He] took my hand and then gave me a hug.

records.definition_text: extremely large
records.learnerexamples_text: They live in a huge house.; The costs involved in building a spacecraft are huge.; A huge number of people attended.; I live in a huge old house in the suburbs with my family.

records.definition_text: relating to people or their characteristics
records.learnerexamples_text: the human body; human behaviour; The fault was due to human error.; As for me, the last good programme I saw was [a] scientific episode about [the] abilities of the human brain.

records.definition_text: a man, woman or child
records.learnerexamples_text: The greatest damage being done to our planet today is that being done by humans.; The programm[e]s I have enjoyed recently were about w[h]ales, sharks and humans.

records.definition_text: the basic rights that every person should have, such as justice and freedom to say what you think
records.learnerexamples_text: international laws protecting human rights; My main interest is the way of li[f]e during the so-called French Period; that period is very important for the foundation of human rights and the way parl[ia]ment ought to work.

records.definition_text: Humid air or weather is hot and slightly wet.
records.learnerexamples_text: It's very humid today.; [The] north of Iran is wet but [the] south of Iran is humid and hot.

records.definition_text: the quality of being funny
records.learnerexamples_text: There's a lot of humour in her work.; The film is really exciting with a bit of humour.

records.definition_text: a lot
records.learnerexamples_text: Hundreds of people wrote in to complain.; When she came back to reality she could see hundreds of people applauding..

records.definition_text: the feeling you have when you need to eat
records.learnerexamples_text: I can't believe that that enormous meal wasn't enough to satisfy your hunger.; By about 9 o'clock she started to feel faint from/with hunger.; It [wa]s [what] I expected, a baby crying f[rom] hunger.

records.definition_text: when you do not have enough food
records.l_topic_text_text: body and health, food and drink
records.learnerexamples_text: All over the world, people die of hunger every day.; Many changes are coming and many problems are coming too, because overpopulation, contamination, pollution, hunger, [and] poverty besides come with this technological revolution and that is something that the human being will have to solve soon.

records.definition_text: to chase and kill wild animals
records.learnerexamples_text: Some animals hunt at night.; Cats like to hunt mice and birds.; As I was saying, you can also go to jungle hotels - comfortable hotels in the middle of the forest, just crossing the Amazon River, where you can keep in touch with nature, feed monkeys and even "hunt" alligators (all sizes, believe me!).

records.definition_text: to search for something or someone
records.learnerexamples_text: I've hunted all over the place, but I can't find that book.; They are still hunting for the missing child.; I've hunted high and low for my gloves.; Police are hunting the terrorists who planted the bomb.; You don't have to hunt for a place to park your car and to worry what will happen when you're out of gas.

records.definition_text: the sport of chasing and killing animals
records.learnerexamples_text: deer hunting; She's very much against hunting of any sort.; And of course hunting won't be allowed.

records.definition_text: the need to move or do things more quickly than normal
records.learnerexamples_text: We left in such a hurry that we forgot our tickets.; "Can you wait a few minutes?" "Yes, I'm not in any hurry/I'm in no hurry."; Are you in a hurry to leave?; What's (all) the hurry (for)/Why (all) the hurry - we've got plenty of time.; "I'll let you have this back next week." "That's all right, there's no (great) hurry/there isn't any (great) hurry ."

records.definition_text: to do something more quickly
records.learnerexamples_text: Hurry up or we'll miss the train.; When I arrived, the other [basketball] club members [were] already dressed, so I had to hurry up.

records.base_text: hurry up sb/sth or hurry sb/sth up
records.definition_text: to make someone do something more quickly, or to make something happen sooner
records.searchterms_text: hurry;hurry up sb/sth or hurry sb/sth up;hurry up sb/sth or hurry sb/sth up
records.learnerexamples_text: Could you hurry the children up, or their dinner will get cold?

records.definition_text: to cause emotional pain to someone
records.learnerexamples_text: She criticized my writing quite severely and that hurt.; He was badly hurt by the end of his marriage.; I didn't mean to hurt your feelings.; My heart was hurt and nobody will [be able to] repair the damage.

records.definition_text: injured or in pain
records.learnerexamples_text: Let me help you up. Are you hurt?; Put that knife away before someone gets hurt.; Several people were seriously/badly hurt in the explosion.; There was an accident on the motorway but fortunately nobody was seriously hurt.

records.definition_text: upset or unhappy
records.learnerexamples_text: I feel very hurt by what you said.; "That was very unkind," he said in a hurt voice.; I know you got very hurt when [you and] Brian broke up.

records.definition_text: a small, simple building, often made of wood
records.learnerexamples_text: a mountain hut; a row of beach huts; Finally, we reached a hut near a river, where we stayed until the following day, when we returned home by bus.

records.definition_text: a mark (-) used to join two words together, or to show that a word has been divided and continues on the next line
records.learnerexamples_text: There should be a hyphen in 'short-sighted'.

records.definition_text: something that you say to show that you believe that something is true or will happen
records.learnerexamples_text: I bet you she's missed the bus.; I bet that he won't come.; The movie is amazing. I bet you'll see it soon.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize your feelings about something
records.searchterms_text: i can't tell you how;i can't tell you how ...;tell;telling;tells;told
records.learnerexamples_text: I can't tell you how grateful I am for your help.; I can't tell you how nervous I am.

records.definition_text: a game played on ice in which two teams try to hit a small hard object into a goal using long curved sticks
records.learnerexamples_text: He loves ice hockey.; I visited Kassel with some friends, to watch an ice hockey game.

records.definition_text: the activity or sport of moving across ice using ice skates
records.learnerexamples_text: We're going ice skating.; Last year, I went ice-skating with some friends and it was not as easy as I thought it would be, but I liked it anyway.

records.definition_text: a small picture on a computer screen that you choose in order to make the computer do something
records.learnerexamples_text: Click on the print icon.; He clicked on the icon on the screen which started the operation.

records.definition_text: a person or thing that is famous because it represents a particular idea or way of life
records.learnerexamples_text: a fashion icon; I think he is still very famous because he is an icon and kickboxing is still very popular because of him.

records.definition_text: covered in ice
records.learnerexamples_text: icy roads; She had fallen off it on an icy street and had got injured.

records.definition_text: extremely cold
records.learnerexamples_text: an icy wind; Fast as [the] wind, she was falling down and down, until her long thin finger touched the icy cold water.

records.definition_text: without showing any emotion
records.learnerexamples_text: an icy stare ; FOGG is the typical rich English man: cold with a[n] icy heart, uncommunicative.

records.definition_text: an opinion or belief
records.learnerexamples_text: We have very different ideas about the environment.; Leach puts forward the idea that it is impossible to spoil a child.; I'm not married - where did you get that idea?; You can talk beside the fireplace, or have a beer with your friends and share your ideas about Tolkien's works.

records.definition_text: an understanding, thought or picture in your mind
records.learnerexamples_text: Do you have any idea of what he looks like?; Can you give me an idea of the cost?; I don't like the idea of living so far away from my family.; I've got a pretty good idea why they left early.; For children it's great to get an idea of how these "big" animals eat, drink and live.

records.definition_text: perfect, or the best possible
records.learnerexamples_text: the ideal employer; She's the ideal person for the job.; The television also comes in a compact 36 cm screen size, ideal for bedroom or kitchen use.; It's the ideal opportunity to meet people.;  In an ideal world no one would go hungry.

records.definition_text: in a perfect way
records.learnerexamples_text: She seemed ideally suited for the job.; I believe I am ideally suited for this job.

records.definition_text: used to talk about how something would be in a perfect situation
records.learnerexamples_text: Ideally, I'd like to work at home.; Ideally, through this camp, I would like to teach Japanese songs and dance to them and I would also like to learn about their culture.

records.definition_text: exactly the same
records.learnerexamples_text: I've got three identical blue suits.; The two rooms were virtually identical.; The tests are identical to those carried out last year.; And suddenly you notice the identical but cheaper one in the next shop.

records.definition_text: when you recognize and can name someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: Identification of the victims of the plane crash still is not complete.; [In the home of the future,] we might even be using voice identification and fingerprints instead of keys.

records.definition_text: to recognize someone or something and say or prove who or what they are
records.learnerexamples_text: Even the smallest baby can identify its mother by her voice.; The gunman in Wednesday's attack has been identified as Lee Giggs, an unemployed truck driver.; After [a few] minutes I heard [a] noise which I couldn't identify.

records.definition_text: to find a particular thing or all the things of a particular group
records.learnerexamples_text: You need to identify your priorities.; The research will be used to identify training needs.; The purpose of this report is to identify which lessons or other activities should be filmed.

records.definition_text: to feel that you are similar to someone, and can understand them or their situation because of this
records.learnerexamples_text: Readers can easily identify with the hero's sense of frustration at the beginning of the novel.; Orwell give[s] the animals human characteristics and we can identify with them.

records.definition_text: who someone is
records.learnerexamples_text: to hide/protect your identity; to prove/reveal your identity; The witness was given a new identity for her protection.; The newspaper photo apparently showed him in Rome but it was a case of mistaken identity.; But this idea fell through when the real Martine revealed her identity.

records.definition_text: the things that make one person or group of people different from others
records.learnerexamples_text: cultural/national identity; I think my job gives me a sense of identity.; There were many people and many speakers who talked about all sorts of subject[s] such as politics, religion, gender identity, [and] art.

records.definition_text: a card that shows your name, photograph and information to prove who you are
records.learnerexamples_text: His identity card was stolen.; I lost my identity card, credit card and passport and I couldn't go to Rome.

records.definition_text: a group of words used together with a meaning that you cannot guess from the meanings of the separate words
records.learnerexamples_text: To "have bitten off more than you can chew" is an idiom that means you have tried to do something which is too difficult for you.; [Greek] has many verbs, adjectives and idioms and the grammar can be very complicated.

records.definition_text: a stupid person or someone who is behaving in a stupid way
records.learnerexamples_text: Some idiot left the tap running in the bathroom and there's water everywhere.; You stupid idiot - that's a month's work you've lost!; Everybody was treating me like a big idiot.

records.definition_text: used to show that you think something is likely to be true
records.learnerexamples_text: I expect Isabel's told you about me?; "Will you be coming to the party?" "I expect so."

records.definition_text: used to mean always or every time
records.learnerexamples_text: If water is heated to 100°C it turns to steam.; If I don't get enough sleep I get a headache.; If there is a world cup - e.g. football - then I spend more time watching television.

records.definition_text: used to talk about something that might happen
records.learnerexamples_text: If I won the lottery, I'd buy a boat.; What would you do if he moved away?; It would be great if you came to the city.

records.definition_text: whether
records.learnerexamples_text: I wonder if he'll get the job?; Mrs Kramer rang half an hour ago to ask if her cake was ready.; I don't care if he likes it or not - I'm coming!; But let's see if a friend can lend me his notebook, [as] that way I will c[atch] up easily.

records.definition_text: used to talk about what would/might/could, etc. have happened
records.learnerexamples_text: If we'd had the money, we'd have bought a new car.; If you'd mentioned this earlier, it might not have been necessary to call the doctor.

records.definition_text: used when you give someone advice
records.learnerexamples_text: If I were you, I'd probably go.; I think I'd take the money if I were you.; But you enjoy clubbing and discos, so, if I were you, I would [choose the] city.

records.definition_text: used when you want to say how doing something simple would make it possible to avoid something unpleasant
records.learnerexamples_text: If only she'd listen to what he's saying, I'm sure they could work it out.; If only I had been more careful.

records.definition_text: used when you want to say how doing something simple would make it possible to avoid something unpleasant
records.learnerexamples_text: If only she'd listen to what he's saying, I'm sure they could work it out.; If only I had been more careful.

records.definition_text: if this is the case
records.learnerexamples_text: It might rain this afternoon. If so, we'll have to have the party indoors.; Let me know if you [can] come, and if so, [whether] you prefer the 15th or 22nd of February.

records.definition_text: if this is the case
records.learnerexamples_text: It might rain this afternoon. If so, we'll have to have the party indoors.; Will you be in time for dinner? If so, I'll cook your favourite dish.

records.definition_text: to pay no attention to something or someone
records.learnerexamples_text: I smiled at her but she just ignored me.; She can be really irritating but I try to ignore her.; How can the government ignore the wishes of the majority?; Paul ignored it at first and continued his shopping but the dog kept following him.

records.definition_text: used when you think something is probably true or likely
records.learnerexamples_text: I've known her for about 12 years, I guess.; I guess that I love her although we do not know [each other] very well.

records.definition_text: used when you agree/disagree but are not completely certain about something
records.learnerexamples_text: "So they're still living in the same house?" "I guess so."

records.definition_text: used when you agree with something someone has just said
records.learnerexamples_text: "It's a lovely day, isn't it?" "I know - let's hope it lasts."

records.definition_text: used when you have an idea
records.learnerexamples_text: I know - let's go to Helen's house.

records.definition_text: not allowed by law
records.learnerexamples_text: Prostitution is illegal in some countries.;  It is illegal to drive a car that is not taxed and insured.; Cocaine, LSD and heroin are all illegal drugs/substances.; Although he has a very charming personality, he uses it to take part in illegal activities and he has been in trouble with the law several times.

records.definition_text: in a way that is not allowed by law
records.learnerexamples_text: They entered the country illegally.; an illegally parked car; He was afraid and bought a gun illegally.

records.definition_text: a disease of the body or mind
records.learnerexamples_text: He died at home after a long illness.; It's because my aunt has a terrible illness and I have to go and see her.

records.definition_text: when you are ill
records.learnerexamples_text: She had five days off work due to illness.; There was a little paper on the door which informed us that the restaurant was closed due to illness.

records.definition_text: to draw pictures for a book, magazine, etc. or to put pictures, photographs, etc. in a book, magazine, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: The book is beautifully illustrated by the author.; Last year I illustrated two children's books by H.J. Simons.

records.definition_text: the way that other people think someone or something is
records.learnerexamples_text: The aim is to improve the public image of the police.; They are trying to promote a more positive image of the whole industry. ; The company has made serious attempts to improve its image in recent years.; He's terribly image-conscious.; In conclusion, I do not think that there are many things to do for Turin, but what I said before could really improve the image of our wonderful town.

records.definition_text: a picture, especially on film or television or in a mirror
records.learnerexamples_text: television images of starving children; This is the image you see in the mirror.; [Films] also provide a clear idea of how people's lives were in a particular period by showing us the visual images of that time.

records.definition_text: the part of your mind that creates ideas or pictures of things that are not real or that you have not seen
records.learnerexamples_text: There's nothing out here - it's just your imagination.; For some reason the story captured/caught the imagination of the public.; There's a sex scene in the film which apparently leaves nothing to the imagination.; I thought it was my imagination, because it was very late and the concert had been so long.

records.definition_text: the ability to create ideas or pictures in your mind
records.learnerexamples_text: The job needs someone with creativity and imagination.; Endless imagination and [the] development of technology will lead us to future fashion.

records.definition_text: to form an idea or picture of something in your mind
records.learnerexamples_text: Imagine Robert Redford when he was young - that's what John looks like.; Imagine (that) you're eating an ice cream - try to feel how cold it is.; She imagined herself sitting in her favourite armchair back home.; Just imagine the sun, the sea and all that fun on the beach.

records.definition_text: to have an idea of what something is like or might be like
records.learnerexamples_text: Can you imagine how it feels to be blind?; I can't imagine wanting to go out if I don't really know anyone.; You can't imagine how tired I am.

records.definition_text: to think that you hear or see something which does not really exist
records.learnerexamples_text: "Did you hear a noise?" "No, you're imagining things."; I can't hear anything - you must be imagining it.; I turn[ed] back but I didn't [see] anyone, so I thought that I had imagined it.

records.definition_text: to believe that something is probably the case
records.learnerexamples_text: I imagine (that) he's under a lot of pressure at the moment.; I don't imagine (that) they have much money.; "Will they change it?" "I imagine so."; I imagine that it's a lot of money so my first suggestion would be to spend only part of [it] on a motorbike.

records.definition_text: happening or done without delay or very soon after something else
records.learnerexamples_text: We must make an immediate response.; The directors have demanded his immediate resignation.; Dioxin is a poison that takes immediate effect.; I hope you will give this matter your immediate attention.

records.definition_text: important now and needing attention
records.learnerexamples_text: We have no immediate plans.; Our immediate concern is getting food and water to the refugees.; It can't be an immediate objective, of course, but we mustn't give up.

records.definition_text: someone who comes to live in a different country
records.learnerexamples_text: a large immigrant population ;  Illegal immigrants are sent back across the border if they are caught.; Leonardo is an Italian immigrant who has a restaurant near the primary school.

records.definition_text: when someone comes to live in a different country
records.learnerexamples_text: immigration policy; There are strict limits on immigration (into the country).; [T]he purpose of [the] party is to give [a] treat to my family members, as my immigration [into] New Zealand is approved.

records.definition_text: the place where people's official documents are checked when they enter a country at an airport, port, border, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: After you've been through immigration (control), you can go and get your luggage.; immigration officers; The immigration officers looked at her as if she was [suspected of] doing something wrong.

records.definition_text: morally wrong
records.learnerexamples_text: immoral behaviour; At this time - [the] early 20's -, tango was considered an immoral type of music; but Carlos Gardel changed this belief.

records.definition_text: the effect that a person, event or situation has on someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: The anti-smoking campaign had/made quite an impact on young people.; The new proposals were intended to soften the impact of the reformed tax system.; I could live without watching TV, but it would make a serious impact on my life.

records.definition_text: easily annoyed by someone's mistakes or because you have to wait
records.learnerexamples_text: He's a good teacher, but inclined to be a bit impatient with slow learners.; You'd be hopeless looking after children - you're far too impatient!; Hours passed and she became impatient and thought he had forgotten about their date.

records.definition_text: wanting something to happen as soon as possible
records.learnerexamples_text: He's got a lot of exciting ideas and he's impatient to get started.; People are increasingly impatient for change in this country.; I'm impatient to discover this country.

records.definition_text: in an impatient way
records.learnerexamples_text: "Yes, you said that before," she said, impatiently.; We were waiting impatiently for the show to begin.; I hope you will come soon because we are all impatiently waiting for your talk.

records.definition_text: the form of a verb which is usually used for giving orders
records.learnerexamples_text: In the phrase 'Leave him alone!', the verb 'leave' is an imperative/is in the imperative.

records.definition_text: to make a law, system, plan, etc. start to happen or operate
records.learnerexamples_text: The changes to the national health system will be implemented next year.; Rare species protection, on the other hand, can be implemented, e.g. by means of wildlife reserves and national parks.

records.definition_text: not polite
records.learnerexamples_text: It is impolite to point at people.; Besides, [the] serving speed was too slow and some waiters were even impolite to customers.

records.definition_text: to buy or bring in products from another country
records.learnerexamples_text: We import a large number of cars from Japan.; Moreover they say we must be independent of the Near East countries from whom we import oil.

records.definition_text: how important someone or something is
records.learnerexamples_text: Your views are of great importance to us.; The report stresses the importance of fresh food in a diet.; He emphasized the importance of following safety procedures.; The company recognizes the importance of regular staff training.; Now I know the importance of electricity.

records.definition_text: having a lot of power, influence or effect
records.learnerexamples_text: He was one of the most important writers of that period.; an important person/decision; Recently I've read [two] good books, "La Coscienza di Zeno" and "Uno, Nessuno e Centomila", that are written by Svevo and Pirandello, two of the most important writers of the XX century in Italy.

records.definition_text: in a way that is important
records.learnerexamples_text: If we served more soft drinks, there would be fewer hangovers and, more importantly, fewer drink-driving incidents.; Lastly, and most importantly, what is the cost?

records.definition_text: If an action or event is impossible, it cannot happen or be done.
records.learnerexamples_text: It was impossible to sleep because of the noise.; It seems impossible that I could have walked by without noticing her.; He made it impossible for me to say no.; I tried to find it but it was impossible!

records.definition_text: to cause someone to admire or respect you
records.learnerexamples_text: He tried to impress me with his extensive knowledge of wine.; All groups did their best to impress the public and every group played professionally.

records.definition_text: feeling admiration or respect for someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: I was impressed by her professionalism.; He seemed suitably impressed by our efforts.; I am really impressed by your offer to paint me.

records.definition_text: the way that something seems, looks or feels to a particular person
records.learnerexamples_text: It makes/gives/creates a very bad impression if you're late for an interview.; He likes to give the impression (that) he's terribly popular and has loads of friends.; I was afraid of being late or saying something wrong because I really wanted to make a good impression on this man.

records.definition_text: an idea, feeling or opinion about something or someone
records.learnerexamples_text: I didn't get much of an impression of the place because it was dark when we drove through it.; What was your impression of Charlotte's husband?; I don't tend to trust first impressions.; When I first met him I got/had the impression that he was a shy sort of a guy.; You can look back fifty years to get an impression of what changes have happened.

records.definition_text: Someone or something that is impressive makes you admire and respect them.
records.learnerexamples_text: She's a very impressive public speaker.; That was an impressive performance from such a young tennis player.; an impressive collection of modern paintings; There are some very impressive buildings in the town.; I thi[n]k that the Westfield Music Festival was really impressive.
