records.definition_text: because of a possibility of something happening, being needed, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't think I'll need any money but I'll bring some just in case.; Bring a map in case you get lost.; I have my mobile with me just in case.

records.definition_text: a large Australian animal that moves by jumping on its back legs
records.learnerexamples_text: Kangaroos are a danger on the roads.; Furthermore it has been my dream since I was five years old to see a kangaroo and play with it.

records.definition_text: very interested or enthusiastic
records.learnerexamples_text: She's a keen tennis player.; She's keen on (playing) tennis.; We are both quite keen on sailing and skiing.

records.definition_text: wanting to do something very much
records.learnerexamples_text: The shop is keen to attract new customers.; He is very keen to write [a] report about crime.

records.definition_text: to delay someone or prevent them from doing something
records.learnerexamples_text: He's very late, what's keeping him?; She kept me talking on the phone for half an hour.; Don't let me keep you from your work.

records.definition_text: If food or drink keeps, it remains fresh.
records.learnerexamples_text: Once opened, this product will keep for three days if refrigerated.

records.definition_text: to have and look after animals
records.learnerexamples_text: Our neighbours keep chickens.; It is cruel to keep dogs, cats, [and] birds in flats.

records.definition_text: to not tell anyone a secret/ about something secret
records.learnerexamples_text: Mr Brown apparently delayed the announcement, and managed to keep it secret from the entire cabinet.; I [had] loved Sean since sixth grade but I was keeping it a secret.

records.definition_text: to do what you have promised to do
records.learnerexamples_text: James kept his promise and repaid all of the money he had borrowed.; She didn't keep her promise and she ruined my life.

records.definition_text: to do/not do what you said that you would do
records.learnerexamples_text: If I make a promise, I like to keep it.; In addition, you didn't keep your promise.

records.definition_text: to continue doing something without stopping, or to do it repeatedly
records.learnerexamples_text: He keeps trying to distract me.; I kept hoping that he'd phone me.; I don't know why I wanted to meet her so much but my heart just kept telling me to go after her.

records.base_text: keep down sth or keep sth down
records.definition_text: to stop the number, level, or size of something from increasing
records.searchterms_text: keep;keep down sth or keep sth down
records.learnerexamples_text: I have to exercise to keep my weight down.; That's also a way of keeping down the many accidents we have from fast cycling.

records.definition_text: a person who takes care of animals or is in charge of valuable objects, a building, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: a zoo keeper; a lighthouse-keeper; Tina was confused because she wasn't a dragon keeper, so normal[l]y dragons didn't speak with her.

records.definition_text: short for goalkeeper
records.learnerexamples_text: The keeper intends to stay with the club until the end of next season.; He is a very good keeper - before he play[ed] football, he was in a karate club.

records.definition_text: to stay healthy and physically strong
records.learnerexamples_text: It's important to keep in shape.; We want to keep in shape, and we are interested in a gym - do you have one or is there one close to there?

records.definition_text: to communicate or continue to communicate with someone, for example by email or telephone
records.learnerexamples_text: We've kept in touch by email for the last five years.; Please keep in touch with me.

records.definition_text: to write something down in order to remember it
records.learnerexamples_text: Remember to keep a record of how much you spend.; Furthermore, a computer helps us to keep records by saving file[s].

records.definition_text: to continue to do something, or to do something again and again
records.learnerexamples_text: She kept on asking me questions the whole time.; I kept on looking for him outside my building and in the park, but I still [haven't found] him.

records.definition_text: to keep someone interested and help them to have an enjoyable time
records.learnerexamples_text: How do you keep an 8-year-old boy amused?; I could keep them amused with my funny stories.

records.definition_text: to stay with someone so that they are not alone
records.learnerexamples_text: Come and keep me company, Isabel.; Usually I went with him to keep him company and because I liked it.

records.definition_text: to stay with someone so that they are not alone
records.learnerexamples_text: Come and keep me company, Isabel.; I wish you came and kept me company.

records.definition_text: to make a child stay inside, often as a punishment, or to make someone stay in hospital
records.learnerexamples_text: She kept the children in as it was so cold.

records.definition_text: to not go somewhere or near something, or to prevent someone from going somewhere or near something
records.learnerexamples_text: I told them to keep away from the edge of the cliff.; The traffic must be kept away from the centre of our town.

records.definition_text: to not go near something, or to prevent someone or something from going past a particular place
records.learnerexamples_text: The police struggled to keep the crowd back.

records.definition_text: to remember to consider someone or something that may be useful in the future
records.learnerexamples_text: I'll keep you in mind if another job comes up. ; But we should keep in mind that books improve our vocabulary and, what's more, our imagination.

records.definition_text: to not go onto an area, or to stop someone or something going onto an area
records.searchterms_text: keep;keep (sb/sth) off sth;keep (sb/sth) off sth ;keep sb/sth off sth;keep sb/sth off sth
records.learnerexamples_text: Keep off the grass.

records.definition_text: to not go into a place, or to stop someone or something from going into a place
records.learnerexamples_text: The building was unsafe so they put up a sign saying 'Danger - Keep out'.

records.definition_text: to be late so that someone has to wait for you
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm sorry to have kept you waiting.; The dentist kept me waiting for ages.; A week later, when we were going to have our second lesson, she kept us waiting for almost an hour.

records.definition_text: to be late so that someone has to wait for you
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm sorry to have kept you waiting.; The dentist kept me waiting for ages.; I'm sorry for keep[ing] you waiting.

records.definition_text: to stop something touching or harming someone or something
records.searchterms_text: keep;keep sth off (sb/sth);keep sth off sb/sth
records.learnerexamples_text: He put a cloth over the food to keep the flies off.

records.definition_text: If you keep to a plan/subject/path, etc., you stay with it.
records.learnerexamples_text: We must keep to the agenda or the meeting will take too long.; I wish you'd keep to the point!; She kept to the main roads and was home before dark.; I suffer from stomach-ache and have to keep to a diet.

records.base_text: keep up sth or keep sth up
records.definition_text: to not allow something that is at a high level to fall to a lower level
records.searchterms_text: keep;keep up sth or keep sth up
records.learnerexamples_text: Keep up the good work!; Make sure you eat properly - you've got to keep your strength up.; I joined because I wanted to keep up [my] English and also, to learn some more.

records.definition_text: to move at the same speed as someone or something that is moving forward so that you stay level with them
records.searchterms_text: keep;keep up (with sb/sth);keep up with sb/sth
records.learnerexamples_text: She was walking so fast I couldn't keep up with her.; Unfortunately he was too fast and I couldn't keep up with him.

records.definition_text: to be able to understand or deal with something that is happening or changing very fast
records.searchterms_text: keep;keep up (with sb/sth);keep up with sb/sth
records.learnerexamples_text: It's important to keep up with international news.; I live in London and I have to keep up with Turkish news for my job.

records.definition_text: to watch or look after someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: Could you keep an eye on this pan of soup for a moment?; You have to supply [e]verything they need and keep an eye on them all the time.

records.definition_text: to watch or look after someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: Could you keep an eye on this pan of soup for a moment?; You have to supply [e]verything they need and keep an eye on them all the time.

records.definition_text: to not talk about something
records.learnerexamples_text: If you don't keep your mouth shut, there'll be trouble.; She made every effort to keep her mouth shut but it disturbed her to be the only one to know the truth, apart from her brother.

records.definition_text: a covered metal or plastic container with a handle and a shaped opening for pouring, used for boiling water
records.learnerexamples_text: If I have an electric kettle in my bedroom, I won't need to go to the kitchen.

records.definition_text: one of the parts that you press with your fingers on a computer or musical instrument to produce letters, numbers, symbols or musical notes
records.learnerexamples_text: Press the shift key to write in capital letters.; piano keys; What is more, you can get the information you need in just one second by pressing the "enter" key [o]n a computer.

records.definition_text: a way of explaining or achieving something
records.learnerexamples_text: Hard work is the key to success.; To those who say that money can't buy happiness I answer that money is a key to happiness.

records.definition_text: very important in influencing or achieving something
records.learnerexamples_text: She was a key figure in the international art world.; a key factor in tackling the problem; Unfortunately one day I decided that it was time to become more independent and I didn't ask a key question.

records.base_text: key in sth or key sth in
records.definition_text: to put information into a computer using a keyboard
records.searchterms_text: key;key in sth or key sth in
records.learnerexamples_text: I've got all the data now but it still needs to be keyed in.; Just key in the appropriate information and in a few seconds you will receive prices and conditions.

records.definition_text: someone who kills another person
records.learnerexamples_text: Police are still hoping to find the dead woman's killer.; I opened the window to take a breath of fresh air and I saw the man again, the killer, smoking a cigarette and looking at me.

records.definition_text: when a person is murdered
records.learnerexamples_text: a series of brutal killings; During the film there were a lot of explosions, killings and action scenes.

records.definition_text: to do something while you are waiting for something else to happen or have nothing else to do
records.learnerexamples_text: We killed time playing video games.; When you are at home alone and have nothing to do, you can kill time watching television.

records.definition_text: in a kind way
records.learnerexamples_text: Stella has very kindly offered to help out with the food for the party.; He answers my simple questions kindly.

records.definition_text: the quality of being kind
records.learnerexamples_text: love and kindness; Thank you again for your kindness and hospitality.

records.definition_text: used to describe something approximately
records.learnerexamples_text: It's a kind of shed.; He was kind of half laughing and half crying.; I know that the Frene Hotel is kind of expensive, but it's just for one night so I think we can make it.

records.definition_text: a country ruled by a king or queen
records.learnerexamples_text: the kingdom of Sweden; The kingdom Chosun lasted until the beginning of [the] 20th century.

records.definition_text: a collection of things kept in a container for a particular use
records.learnerexamples_text: a first-aid/tool kit; I would rather buy a big travel kit, including a first-aid kit.

records.definition_text: a young cat
records.learnerexamples_text: Our cat's had two kittens.

records.definition_text: the middle part of your leg where it bends
records.learnerexamples_text: a knee injury; The baby was crawling around on its hands and knees.; He got/went down on his knees in front of the altar.; He entered the living room drunk and with blood over his knee.

records.definition_text: to go down into, or stay in, a position where one or both knees are on the ground
records.learnerexamples_text: She knelt (down) beside the child.; He knelt in front of the altar and prayed.; Robert knelt down by her, prono[u]ncing the simple words "Will you marry me?"

records.definition_text: women's underwear that covers the bottom
records.learnerexamples_text: There was one time when Pat and I had a fight. It all started when I accident[al]ly took the wrong bag back to my house, and there w[ere] lad[ies'] knickers inside.

records.definition_text: to make clothes, etc. by using two long needles to connect wool or another type of thread into joined rows
records.learnerexamples_text: She's forever knitting.; She's busy knitting baby clothes.; My granny knitted me some gloves/knitted some gloves for me.; I would really like to learn how to knit sweaters and hats.

records.definition_text: to repeatedly hit something, making a noise
records.learnerexamples_text: She knocked on the window to attract his attention.; There's someone knocking on/at the door.; Please knock before entering.; On Monday, a person knocked on my door.

records.definition_text: to hit, especially forcefully, and cause to move or fall
records.learnerexamples_text: He accidentally knocked the vase off the table.; She knocked her head against the wall as she fell.; She took a hammer and knocked a hole in the wall.; Falling down, I knocked my head on the pa[v]ement.

records.definition_text: to hit someone with a vehicle and injure or kill them
records.learnerexamples_text: She was knocked down by a bus.; The man explained that Lime was knocked down by a car and that he died immediately.

records.definition_text: to make someone become unconscious, usually by hitting them on the head
records.learnerexamples_text: He was knocked out halfway through the fight.; Chris knocked him out with a strong punch without doubting that he was a criminal.

records.definition_text: to defeat a person or team in a competition so they cannot take part any more
records.learnerexamples_text: The French team were knocked out in the semi final.

records.definition_text: to destroy a building or part of a building
records.learnerexamples_text: They've knocked down the old cinema.; Since many of the office building are almost empty I also think that we should have them knocked down and replaced by green parks or other areas where no cars are to be allowed.

records.definition_text: to hit or push something or someone, especially accidentally, so that they fall to the ground or onto their side
records.learnerexamples_text: I knocked a bottle of wine over while I was reaching for a dish.; He banged into me so hard that he nearly knocked me over.; I knocked over the girl's cup, which was still full of milk.

records.definition_text: to be familiar with or have experience and understanding of
records.learnerexamples_text: I've known Daniel since we were at school together.; She grew up in Paris so she knows it well.; I've seen the film 'Casablanca' so many times that I know a lot of it by heart.; Knowing Sarah, she'll have done a good job.; I knew him in London, and when I knew him I was very happy.

records.definition_text: If you know a subject, you are familiar with it and understand it.
records.learnerexamples_text: Do you know about computers?; If you want to know more about Peruvian history, I recommend you [visit] the city because you can see the old houses and museum[s].

records.definition_text: to have the intelligence or judgment not to do something
records.searchterms_text: knew;know;know better (than to do sth);know better than to do sth;knowing;known;knows
records.learnerexamples_text: She should have known better than to eat so much. No wonder she feels sick now.; I should have known better but I had to tell it to someone.

records.definition_text: information and understanding that you have in your mind
records.learnerexamples_text: Her knowledge of English grammar is very extensive.; He has a limited knowledge of French.; Actually, I wanted to improve my English knowledge, because I need a good job.

records.definition_text: recognised or known about by most people
records.learnerexamples_text: These people are known criminals.; He is known to the police because of his previous criminal record.

records.definition_text: to have heard of something or someone and have a little information about them
records.learnerexamples_text: I know of a good restaurant near the station.; I know of a good restaurant that has opened recently and it's near your new apartment, so I suggest we go and try out the marvellous Chinese dishes the day after the concert.

records.definition_text: a laboratory
records.learnerexamples_text: a science/computer lab; a lab technician; There are computer labs too.

records.definition_text: a small piece of paper or other material which gives information about the thing it is fixed to
records.learnerexamples_text: Remember to put some address labels on the suitcases.; Washing instructions should be on the label.; It was the price label hanging from the skirt belt.

records.definition_text: a company which produces goods for sale, the goods themselves, or the company's name or symbol
records.learnerexamples_text: Her favourite designer label is Armani.; Their own-label vegetarian products have been a huge success.; The group have just signed with a new record label.; Another style which I like is the clothes from big labels like Armani, Dolce and Gabanna and Hugo Boss, but they are very expensive.

records.definition_text: a room used for scientific work
records.learnerexamples_text: research laboratories; a computer laboratory; Laboratory tests suggest that the new drug may be used to treat cancer.; I was in my school, in a laboratory, when I lost it.

records.definition_text: to not have or not have enough of something that is needed or wanted
records.learnerexamples_text: He just lacks a little confidence.; What we lack in this house is space to store things.; We are lacking three members of staff due to illness.; He lacks confidence due to such a terrible appearance.

records.definition_text: not having something, or not having enough of something
records.learnerexamples_text: Her only problem is lack of confidence.; Lack of sleep had made him irritable.; If he fails it won't be for/through lack of effort.; We won't be going on holiday this year - lack of money, I'm afraid.; If you like nature, wish to see tropical birds, which are rare in your country, or just wish to have a pleasant time, the countryside is the best option, [despite] the lack of nightlife.

records.definition_text: a piece of equipment which is used to reach high places, consisting of short steps fixed between two long sides
records.learnerexamples_text: She was up a ladder, cleaning the window.; My grandfather fell down from the ladder yesterday while he [was] fixing the broken light bulbs.

records.definition_text: a polite or old fashioned way of referring to or talking to a woman
records.learnerexamples_text: There's a young lady here to see you.; Say "thank you" to the lady, children.; A very nice lady offer[ed] me a ride home but I refuse[d].

records.definition_text: a young sheep, or the flesh of a young sheep eaten as meat
records.learnerexamples_text: We were staying on a farm where there were newborn lambs.; roast lamb; I special[l]y like the eggs and rice, and the spicy lamb that they are quite good at.

records.definition_text: an area of ground, especially when used for a particular purpose such as farming or building
records.learnerexamples_text: This sort of land is no good for growing potatoes.; We want to buy a plot of land to build a house.; One man talked about how people can use their land properly, how they [should] take care of their poultry farm or dairy farm, [and] how they can take care of their trees and crops.

records.definition_text: the surface of the Earth that is not sea
records.learnerexamples_text: It is cheaper to drill for oil on land than at sea.; The treaty has led to a dramatic reduction in the number of land-based missiles in Europe.; Firstly, the car is the fastest way of transportation by land [that] we have.

records.definition_text: to arrive at a place in a plane or a boat, or to make a plane or a boat reach the land
records.learnerexamples_text: We should land in Madrid at 7am.; You can land a plane on water in an emergency.; We landed at Port Said in the early evening.; When we landed, my suitcase was not there.

records.definition_text: an arrival on the ground of an aircraft or boat
records.learnerexamples_text: One person has died after the pilot of a light aircraft was forced to make a crash/emergency landing in a field.; The company said our landing would depend on the weather forecast.

records.definition_text: a woman who you rent a room or a house from
records.learnerexamples_text: My landlady doesn't let us have guests.; The thing is our landlady loves money and we have to pay plenty of money excluding [the] accommodation fee.

records.definition_text: a man who you rent a room or house from
records.learnerexamples_text: I've asked our landlord to fix the window.; I came downstairs [and] saw my landlord, [who] seemed very angry.

records.definition_text: the appearance of an area of land, especially in the countryside
records.learnerexamples_text: a rural landscape; The castle dominates the landscape for miles around.; The landscape was beautiful with a lake, a lot of animals, birds, [and] many flowers.

records.definition_text: part of a road or track that is separated from the other parts, usually by a painted line
records.learnerexamples_text: the inside/middle/outside lane; the fast/slow lane; They're widening the road from two to three lanes.; For example, most buses drive [i]n an extra lane.

records.definition_text: a narrow road in the countryside or in a town
records.learnerexamples_text: He drives so fast along those narrow country lanes.; I think the best place to buy all this junk food is from my aunty's sweet shop, just 2 miles down your lane.

records.definition_text: communication between people, usually using words
records.learnerexamples_text: She has done research into how children acquire language.; Language is very important [for] communicat[ion] between people.

records.definition_text: Your lap is the top part of your legs when you are sitting down.
records.learnerexamples_text: Come on kids - sit on my lap and I'll read you a story.; Clara opened her eyes and she was sit[t]ing [o]n [a] comfortable sofa in her warm room, and in her lap was [a] history book.

records.definition_text: one complete turn around a race track or from one end of a swimming pool to the other
records.learnerexamples_text: He's two laps behind the leaders.; The race began and David was 2nd after 25 laps, behind Nilson's rear bumper.

records.definition_text: almost completely
records.learnerexamples_text: a largely male company; Their complaints have been largely ignored.; Until recently, the civil war had been largely unreported in the press.; What I'm trying to say is that images, film-frames, videos and sound clips would be largely accepted by the young people because we're moving into a new high-technology age.

records.definition_text: a machine that produces a strong beam of light that has medical and technical uses or a beam of light produced by a machine like this
records.learnerexamples_text: laser beam; laser surgery; These appliances have been the key to medical achievements, such as laser-based surger[y] or different kinds of diagnosis and treatment.

records.definition_text: only remaining
records.learnerexamples_text: Who wants the last piece of cake?; The cam[e]ras watch everybody in the house 24 hours [a day]. Every Friday, the public decide[s] who [should leave]. The last person wins this show.

records.definition_text: used to talk about the most recent time you did something
records.learnerexamples_text: When did you last see her?; I think it was July when I last spoke to him.; Write back soon and let me know what you [have been] up to since I heard from you last.

records.definition_text: after everything or everyone else
records.learnerexamples_text: I wasn't expecting to win the race but I didn't think I'd come last!; We've still got to check the figures but we'll do that last.; When I reached the other end of the pool, my heart suddenly stopped and I just couldn't move my legs to continue swimming. So, I arrived last.

records.definition_text: to continue to happen, exist, or be useful
records.learnerexamples_text: How long will the meeting last?; We don't get much sun - enjoy it while it lasts!; Most sessions last about an hour.; The batteries only last about five hours.; We saw a new film, "Signs", that I liked very much, even though I found it very long: it lasted about 3 hours!

records.definition_text: something that you say to introduce the last person or thing on a list
records.learnerexamples_text: This is Jeremy, this is Cath and, last but not least, this is Eva.; And, last but not least, some complaints were made [about] the entertainment the café provides.

records.definition_text: something that you say to introduce the last person or thing on a list
records.learnerexamples_text: This is Jeremy, this is Cath and, last but not least, this is Eva.; And, last but not least, some complaints were made [about] the entertainment the café provides.

records.definition_text: finally
records.learnerexamples_text: And lastly, I'd like to thank everyone who took part in the event.; Lastly, I'd like to say that it's very kind of you to suggest bringing something back for me.

records.definition_text: done at the latest possible opportunity
records.learnerexamples_text: a last-minute cancellation; I could come the following day to help you [with] the last-minute preparations if you want [me] to.

records.definition_text: near the end of a period of time
records.learnerexamples_text: We talked late into the night.; As late as the 1980s they were still using horses on this farm.; Firstly, he usually starts working at eight in the morning and he keeps on writing and phoning till late in the evening.

records.definition_text: recently
records.learnerexamples_text: Lately, I've been walking to work.;  I haven't been feeling so well lately.; I'm sorry I couldn't write back to you before but I've been very busy lately.

records.definition_text: happening at a time in the future, or after the time you have mentioned
records.learnerexamples_text: We could catch a later train.; You can always change your password at a later date.; He said he'll come at a later date.

records.definition_text: at a time in the future, or after the time you have mentioned
records.learnerexamples_text: What are you doing later on this evening?; Shall I go and fetch her later on?; Later on, we could go and have a meal if you like.; But later on, I could not beli[e]ve what actually happened.

records.definition_text: near or towards the end of something
records.learnerexamples_text: Building of the new library should begin in the latter part of next year.; In the latter stages of the fight he began to tire.; I agree with the latter opinion.

records.definition_text: the act or sound of laughing
records.learnerexamples_text: a loud/nervous laugh; I was embarrassed at the time, but I had a good laugh about it later.; There is a beautiful beach there where you can swim, play football and enjoy a good laugh with your friends.

records.definition_text: to show that you think someone or something is stupid
records.learnerexamples_text: I can't go into work looking like this - everyone will laugh at me.; If you say that, people will just laugh at you.; All my friends laughed at me.

records.definition_text: the act or sound of laughing
records.learnerexamples_text: She roared with laughter.; As we approached the hall we could hear the sound of laughter.; There was a roar of laughter.

records.definition_text: to begin an important plan or activity
records.learnerexamples_text: The scheme was launched by the government a year ago.; Dear Phil, I was very proud last Monday when you asked me to help you to launch this association.

records.definition_text: If a company launches a product or service, it makes it available for the first time.
records.learnerexamples_text: The book was launched last February.; The airline will launch its new transatlantic service next month.; The firm was launching a new product and Peter was the manager in charge [of] making this product the most desirable thing to buy.

records.definition_text: clothes, sheets, etc. that need to be washed
records.learnerexamples_text: to do the laundry; Does the camp have laundry facilities?

records.definition_text: the subject or job of understanding and dealing with the official laws of a country
records.learnerexamples_text: to study/practise law; a law school/firm; a specialist in commercial/criminal/international law; Her name is Martina, she is twenty-one years old and she studies law in Bologna.

records.definition_text: an official rule in a country
records.learnerexamples_text: There are laws against drinking in the street.; The laws governing the possession of firearms are being reviewed.; They led the fight to impose laws on smoking.; They have passed a new law to ban fox hunting.; I think it would be a good idea to let shop owner[s] decide themselves about opening time and not to constrict this by law.

records.definition_text: someone whose job is to give advice to people about the law and speak for them in court
records.learnerexamples_text: I want to see my lawyer before I say anything.; After that she thank[ed] me and she told me that she is a lawyer.

records.definition_text: If an animal lays eggs, it produces them out of its body.
records.learnerexamples_text: The hens have laid a lot of eggs this week.; The only thing they can do is to lay eggs.

records.definition_text: an amount of a substance covering a surface, or one of several amounts of substance, each on top of the other
records.learnerexamples_text: the ozone layer; A thick layer of dust lay over everything.; There was a thin layer of oil on the surface of the water.; We stripped several layers of paint off the door.; I think clothes will have many gadgets on them like a small oxygen mask [or] a hat designed to protect people from the strong rays of the sun at midday because the ozone layer will be destroyed in a hundred years' [time].

records.definition_text: to put plates, knives, forks, etc. on the table to prepare for a meal
records.learnerexamples_text: Could you lay the table for me, please?; Before she came to my home, I prepared everything perfectly, laying the table with silver spoons, flowers and candles.

records.definition_text: to put plates, knives, forks, etc. on the table to prepare for a meal
records.learnerexamples_text: Could you lay the table for me, please?; Before she came to my home, I prepared everything perfectly, laying the table with silver spoons, flowers and candles.

records.definition_text: being lazy
records.learnerexamples_text: I could go to the gym - it's just laziness that stops me.; Sorry I haven't dropped you a line before now - no excuses really, just laziness.

records.definition_text: slow and relaxed
records.learnerexamples_text: a lazy morning/weekend; All in all we spent a lazy holiday there with fine weather and a warm blue sea.

records.definition_text: to show someone where to go, usually by taking them to a place or by going in front of them
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't know the way, so you'd better lead.; She led them down the hall.; The waiter led us to our table.; Our guide led us through the mountains.; She took the child by the hand and led him upstairs to bed.

records.definition_text: to be winning a game or a competition
records.learnerexamples_text: After thirty minutes the challengers were leading by two goals.; With two laps to go Ngomo led by less than two seconds.; The Lions lead the Hawks 28 - 9.; Marseille led 1-0 versus Milan AC in the match which qualified the winner for the semi-finals.

records.definition_text: to be in control of a group, country, or situation
records.learnerexamples_text: I think we've chosen the right person to lead the expedition.; I've asked Gemma to lead the discussion.; Who will be leading the enquiry into the accident?; I also led a group of people cleaning the wood just outside the city.

records.definition_text: a winning position during a race or other situation where people are competing, or a position ahead of other people
records.learnerexamples_text: For the first time in the race Harrison is in the lead.; With a final burst of speed she went/moved into the lead.; After last night's win Johnson has taken the lead in the championship table.; By the end of the day's play Davies had a lead of three points.; The whole family walked down to the beach, with Mum in the lead.

records.definition_text: The lead performer or lead part in a performance is the main performer or part.
records.learnerexamples_text: Who played the lead role?; It was Dave Grohl, the lead singer of Foo Fighters!

records.definition_text: to live in a particular way
records.searchterms_text: lead;lead a busy/normal/quiet etc life;lead a busy/normal/quiet, etc. life;leading;leads;led
records.learnerexamples_text: He was able to lead a normal life despite his illness.; Owing to the great speed of technological development, people need to lead a faster life [than before].

records.definition_text: a person in control of a group, country, or situation
records.learnerexamples_text: a tour leader; The Russian leader wants to introduce further changes.; He's a natural leader.; She was elected as leader of the campaign group.; When I arrived there, the group leader introduced me to all the others, and they all were very friendly.

records.definition_text: very important or most important
records.learnerexamples_text: a leading expert on the country's ecology; the world's leading manufacturer of audio equipment; Indeed hard work plays the leading role concerning both family welfare and [the] national economy.

records.definition_text: If something, for example a path or road, leads somewhere, it goes in that direction.
records.learnerexamples_text: That path leads to the beach.; There's a track that leads directly to the reservoir.; A narrow trail of blood led directly into the cave.; I discovered a small path which led to an old castle we had never seen before.

records.definition_text: to cause something to happen or exist
records.learnerexamples_text: Reducing speed limits should lead to fewer deaths on the roads.; People who work very hard are often tired, which could influence their relationship with others. It might lead to unnecessary arguments and spoil the pleasant atmosphere among them for some time.

records.definition_text: a flat, green part of a plant that grows from a stem or branch
records.learnerexamples_text: a lettuce leaf; autumn leaves; He was sweeping up leaves in his garden.; One of the things that I like [about] goril[l]as is that they are strong and they eat leaves, and another thing is that they can move very fast through the trees.

records.definition_text: a piece of folded paper or a small book which contains information
records.learnerexamples_text: I picked up a useful leaflet on how to fill in tax forms.; Another idea is to place a table where students, staff and visitors can find some information about the school and their activities, some leaflets and brochures.

records.definition_text: a group of teams which compete against each other in a sport
records.learnerexamples_text: Who do you think will win the league championship this year?; Liverpool were top of the Football League that year.; They are currently bottom of the league.; For example, I like live football match[es] from [the] Premier league.

records.definition_text: If a liquid or gas leaks, it comes out of a hole by accident, and if a container leaks, it allows liquid or gas to come out when it should not.
records.learnerexamples_text: Water was leaking from the pipe.; Oil leaked out of the car.; The tin was leaking.; The car leaked oil all over the drive.; There is always a possibilit[y] that this tent is leaking.

records.definition_text: a hole in something that a liquid or gas comes out of, or the liquid or gas that comes out
records.learnerexamples_text: There's water on the floor - we must have a leak.; If you suspect a gas leak, phone the emergency number.; The theatre restaurant was closed because there was a serious leak in a [pipe] and the kitchen was flooded.

records.definition_text: to rest against something for support, or to move something into this position
records.searchterms_text: lean;lean (sth) against/on sth;lean sth against/on sth;leaned;leaning;leans;leant
records.learnerexamples_text: She leaned her head on his shoulder.; His spade was leaning against the fence.; She turned around and saw this boy leaning against the wall.

records.definition_text: to move the top part of your body in a particular direction
records.searchterms_text: lean;lean (sth) back/forward/out, etc.;lean sth back/forward/out etc;lean sth back/forward/out, etc.;leaned;leaning;leans;leant
records.learnerexamples_text: She leaned forward and whispered in my ear.; He was leaning out of the window.; Lean your head back a bit.; John loved figures, combining them into long lines, counting them and solving difficult problems. And he had a secret. He saw numbers in different colours. [...] John tried to hide his papers with a book but Mr. Robinson leaned forward and whispered: "My number one is always red".

records.definition_text: to make yourself remember a piece of writing by reading it or repeating it many times
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't know how actors manage to learn all those lines.; We were told to learn Portia's speech by heart for homework.; He was a very famous and popular actor. He's very funny and he shows us very useful tricks to [help us] learn our roles.

records.definition_text: to be told facts or information that you did not know
records.learnerexamples_text: We were all shocked to learn of his death.; I later learnt (that) the message had never arrived.; I only learnt about the accident later.; I was pleased to learn that you are coming to Switzerland.

records.definition_text: to start to understand that you must change the way you behave
records.learnerexamples_text: She'll have to learn that she can't have everything she wants.; She soon learnt not to contradict him.; He's not afraid to learn from his mistakes.; I am sure that the organis[e]rs will learn from their mistakes and that next year you will enjoy it.

records.definition_text: someone who is getting knowledge or a new skill
records.learnerexamples_text: learners of English; She is very shy, so her Japanese didn't improve very rapidly, but she was a very industrious learner.

records.definition_text: the process of getting knowledge or a new skill
records.learnerexamples_text: language learning; This technique makes learning fun.; For the first month in her new job she was on a steep learning curve.; Th[ese] events are not only to entertain students, they are also a part of the learning process, as by communicating with each other, students learn the language.

records.definition_text: to decide not to do something again because it has caused you problems in the past
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm not going out without my umbrella again - I've learnt my lesson!; She learnt her lesson and she won't go out before [an] exam any more.

records.definition_text: less than anything or anyone else
records.learnerexamples_text: I chose the least expensive dish on the menu.; This group is the least likely of the four to win.; Disaster struck when we least expected it.; It was the answer she least wanted to hear.; Every day was the same and I thought that nothing w[ould] change but I was wrong - something changed and that something happen[e]d on the day I least expected it to.

records.definition_text: less than anyone or anything else
records.learnerexamples_text: He contributed least to the workshop.; I like the green one least of all.; He's the relative I like (the) least.; Giving her a bed for the night was the least I could do.; Taking you to the airport was the least I could do for such a good friend.

records.definition_text: the smallest amount
records.learnerexamples_text: She earns the least money of all of us.; I spent the least time on the third question.; My favourite way to travel is by plane, because I think that the most important point when you are travelling is to arrive [at] your destination in the least time.

records.definition_text: to cause something to stay in a particular condition
records.learnerexamples_text: Leave that chair where it is.; Don't leave any lights on, will you?; I'll have to go back - I think I've left the iron on.; You can leave the window open.; And I heard my husband shouting: "Mag, do you always have to leave all the lights on?"

records.definition_text: to end a relationship with a husband, wife, or partner and stop living with them
records.learnerexamples_text: I'll never leave you.; She left him for a younger man.; Jose, who is a bus driver, was very unhappy, because his girlfriend [had] left him.

records.base_text: leave behind sb/sth or leave sb/sth behind
records.definition_text: to leave a place without taking someone or something with you
records.searchterms_text: leave;leave behind sb/sth or leave sb/sth behind
records.learnerexamples_text: We were in a hurry and I think I must have left my keys behind.; He got out of the country, but had to leave his wife and son behind.; I know you must be disappointed [at] having to move, leaving all your friends behind, but it's OK, I'm sure you'll make new ones.

records.base_text: leave out sb/sth or leave sb/sth out
records.definition_text: to not include someone or something
records.searchterms_text: leave;leave out sb/sth or leave sb/sth out
records.learnerexamples_text: You can leave the butter out of this recipe if you're on a low-fat diet.; I've made a list of names - I hope I haven't left anyone out.; None of the other children play with her, and I think she feels rather left out.; She felt so left out.

records.definition_text: to stop talking to someone or annoying them
records.learnerexamples_text: Leave him alone, he's tired.; "Leave me alone, you monster," I said in panic.

records.definition_text: to stop speaking to or annoying someone
records.learnerexamples_text: Leave me alone! I'm trying to work.; I asked [him] to leave me alone and [un]plugged the phone.

records.definition_text: a formal talk on a serious or specialist subject given to a group of people, especially students
records.learnerexamples_text: We went to a lecture on Italian art.; Who's giving the lecture this afternoon?; The film will start at 9.30pm, so you could reach us after your lectures at the university in the pub near the cinema.

records.definition_text: someone who teaches at a university or college
records.learnerexamples_text: a lecturer in psychology ; In addition, my lecturers can't give me particular explanations for my questions.

records.definition_text: a long white and green vegetable that smells and tastes similar to an onion
records.learnerexamples_text: leek soup; I had some roasted chicken pieces with some leek and broccoli and roasted potatoes and Jan had his favourite spaghetti with cream sauce.

records.definition_text: relating to the law
records.learnerexamples_text: legal advice; a legal obligation/requirement; your legal rights; Unless I hear from you within ten days, I shall have to take legal advice on the matter.

records.definition_text: allowed by the law
records.learnerexamples_text: Is abortion legal in your country?; Can anybody say how any enterprise should or must work? Is it legal?

records.definition_text: as stated or allowed by the law
records.learnerexamples_text: Children under sixteen are not legally allowed to buy cigarettes.; He already had a driving licence, so by that time he could legally drive his own Ferrari.

records.definition_text: an old story or set of stories from ancient times
records.learnerexamples_text: The dance was based on several Hindu legends.; She is writing a thesis on Irish legend and mythology.; Legend has it that he always wore his boots in bed.; You know I'm fond of medieval tales and legends, so while we're in Scotland, let's visit a haunted castle!

records.definition_text: the time when you are not working
records.learnerexamples_text: leisure activities; Most people only have a limited amount of leisure time.; The town lacks leisure facilities such as a swimming pool or squash courts.; Reading is my favourite leisure activity. I've already read fifteen books this year.

records.definition_text: If a bank lends money, it gives money to someone who then pays the money back in small amounts over a period.
records.learnerexamples_text: The bank refuses to lend to students.; The bank agreed to lend him $5000.

records.definition_text: the measurement or distance of something from one end to the other
records.learnerexamples_text: The boat is ten metres in length.; The length of the bay is approximately 200 miles.; The new one has a length of 2.10 metres.

records.definition_text: the amount of time something takes
records.learnerexamples_text: the length of a film/speech/play; He is unable to concentrate on his work for any length of time.; We will need you to start the talk at 7:00 p.m. with a length of one hour.

records.definition_text: a large wild cat that has yellow fur with black spots on it and lives in Africa and southern Asia
records.learnerexamples_text: We saw leopards in their natural habitat.; We saw different kinds of animals like a leopard, a buffalo and so on.

records.definition_text: an experience which teaches you how to behave better in a similar situation in the future
records.learnerexamples_text: There is a lesson for all parents in this tragic accident.; My parents made me pay back all the money and it was a lesson I never forgot.; We can learn important lessons from this disaster.; I think he learned a valuable lesson.

records.definition_text: to allow someone to do something, or to allow something to happen
records.learnerexamples_text: She wanted to go but her parents wouldn't let her.; He decided to let his hair grow long.; Let your shoes dry completely before putting them on.; I'm letting you stay up late, just this once.; Don't let it worry you.

records.definition_text: something that you say when you are offering to help someone
records.learnerexamples_text: Let me carry your cases.

records.base_text: let out sb/sth or let sb/sth out
records.definition_text: to allow a person or animal to leave a place, especially by opening a locked or closed door
records.searchterms_text: let;let out sb/sth or let sb/sth out
records.learnerexamples_text: I heard a voice from the cupboard shouting "Let me out!"; Then, hopefully, the animals can be let out in[to] their natural enviro[n]ment again.

records.base_text: let sb down or let down sb
records.definition_text: to disappoint someone by failing to do what you agreed to do
records.searchterms_text: let;let sb down or let down sb
records.learnerexamples_text: I've promised to go to the party with Beth and I feel I can't let her down.; I promise you that I am not going to let you down.

records.base_text: let sb off or let off sb
records.definition_text: to not punish someone who has done something wrong, or to not punish them severely
records.searchterms_text: let;let sb off or let off sb
records.learnerexamples_text: Instead of a prison sentence they were let off with a fine.; You won't be let off so lightly the next time.; Although the headmaster let me off with a warning when I explained the matter to him, I was very depressed because I was exhausted.

records.definition_text: to allow someone or something to move to a particular place
records.searchterms_text: let;let sb/sth in/past/through etc;let sb/sth in/past/through, etc.;lets;letting
records.learnerexamples_text: They won't let us past the gate.; The roof lets in a lot of rain.; I had got so drunk that I could not control myself, so the doorman would not let me in.

records.definition_text: a plant with large green leaves, eaten raw in salads
records.learnerexamples_text: Mix the lettuce and tomatoes together.; It contains two burgers, cheese, lettuce, tomato and [any]thing else that you want to put [i]n it.

records.definition_text: the amount or number of something
records.learnerexamples_text: Inflation is going to rise 2% from its present level.; Chess requires a very high level of concentration.; There is some danger of low level radiation.; Your body requires a high level of nutrients to keep body functions working smoothly.

records.definition_text: the height of something
records.learnerexamples_text: The water level in the lake is much higher after heavy rain.; Also, due to global warming, sea levels might rise and [the] risk of flooding will also rise.

records.definition_text: flat or horizontal
records.learnerexamples_text: Make sure the camera is level before you take the picture.; Before I fix it to the wall, would you say this shelf was level?

records.definition_text: someone who tells lies
records.learnerexamples_text: He's such a liar - you can't trust a word he says.; You liar - I never touched it!; The plan works: the jury thinks that the wife is a notorious liar and her husband is found innocent.

records.definition_text: the freedom to live as you wish or go where you want
records.learnerexamples_text: For most citizens, liberty means the freedom to practise their religious or political beliefs.; Hundreds of political prisoners are to be given their liberty.; Of the ten men who escaped this morning from Dartmoor Prison, only two are still at liberty.; Personally, I think [a zoo] is a cruel way to [im]prison them after such a long period of time [when] they have been useful to Man, who is now depriving them of their liberty, preventing them from hunting and forcing them to eat what they are given.

records.definition_text: to move your tongue across the surface of something
records.learnerexamples_text: He licked the chocolate off his fingers.; She licked the stamps and stuck them on the parcel.; As soon as I come home, she jumps on me and licks my face. [...] Princess is my ideal dog.

records.definition_text: a cover on a container, which can be lifted up or removed
records.learnerexamples_text: Can you get the lid off this jar?; Put a lid on the saucepan.

records.definition_text: to be on a particular surface
records.learnerexamples_text: A pen lay on the desk.; There were papers lying all over the floor.; I hurried into the airport to find my suitcase lying in one corner.

records.definition_text: to be in a particular place or position
records.learnerexamples_text: The river lies 30km to the south.; Cambridge United are lying third in the league.; It lies in the south of the Czech Republic and it's [a] lovely place where you can spend your holiday.

records.definition_text: to say or write something which is not true in order to deceive someone
records.learnerexamples_text: Are you lying to me?; Don't trust her - she's lying.; I suspect he lies about his age.; She lied [to] me and said she could not come with me because she had work.

records.definition_text: something that you say which you know is not true
records.learnerexamples_text: I told a lie when I said I liked her haircut.; The [e-]mail was full of lies about things that I had never done.

records.definition_text: everything which is alive
records.learnerexamples_text: human/marine/plant life; Recently, I've enjoyed watch[ing] programmes about sea life.

records.definition_text: a way of living
records.learnerexamples_text: You lead an exciting life.; I left home at 16 to see life.; Teaching has been her whole life.

records.definition_text: the existence of a person
records.learnerexamples_text: How many lives will be lost to AIDS?; A simple mixture of glucose and water can save lives in many parts of the world.; Finally if you witness an accident you [should] inform the police quickly, which can save lives.

records.definition_text: energy or enthusiasm
records.learnerexamples_text: She's so full of life.; Above all, I like children very much because the[y're] full of life [and] always make a great impression on me when I have a chat with them.

records.definition_text: the way that you live
records.learnerexamples_text: He doesn't have a very healthy lifestyle.; She needs a pretty high income to support her lifestyle.; an alternative lifestyle; I would like to go on a[n] advent[u]re like this, with a group of people with different backgrounds, cultures and lifestyles.

records.definition_text: the period of time that someone is alive
records.learnerexamples_text: We'll see a tremendous lot of technological changes during/in our lifetime.; Winners of the competition will receive the holiday of a lifetime.; I've only been working here two days, but it seems like a lifetime.; A watch of this quality should last a lifetime.; Marriage is no longer always seen as a lifetime commitment.

records.definition_text: to move something from a lower to a higher position
records.learnerexamples_text: Could you help me lift this table, please?; Could you lift your chair a bit - I've got my bag caught under it.; She lifted the cup (up) to her lips.; Then, we lift[ed] weight[s] to get stronger legs, arms, etc. I met different people [and] I made lots of friends.

records.definition_text: the brightness that comes from the sun, fire, etc. and from electrical devices, and that allows things to be seen
records.learnerexamples_text: bright light; Light was streaming in through the open door.; It's a north-facing room so it doesn't get much light.; We spent some wonderful days admiring the famous bright Nordic light which has made Shagen so popular amongst painters.

records.definition_text: lit by the natural light of the day
records.learnerexamples_text: It gets light very early these summer mornings.; Summer is coming and the evenings are getting lighter.; Let's finish the work while it's still light enough to see.; In the cent[re] of the town, streets are narrow and in many cases, they [ar]en't light enough.

records.definition_text: small in amount
records.learnerexamples_text: A light wind was blowing.; The traffic was quite light so we got through London quickly.; It's only light rain - you don't need an umbrella.; I don't eat much for lunch - just a light snack.; The weather here is very warm and sunny with [a] light breeze.

records.definition_text: to start to burn or to make something start to burn
records.learnerexamples_text: to light a fire; I can't get the cooker to light.; He lit his fifth cigarette in half an hour.; We [put up] the tents and lit the fire.

records.definition_text: to produce light somewhere so that you can see things
records.learnerexamples_text: The stage had been lit with candles.; Fireworks lit up the sky .; Lightning lit up my bedroom and I saw a shadow moving outside the house.

records.definition_text: a small object that produces a flame and is used to make cigarettes start burning
records.learnerexamples_text: Can I borrow your lighter?; It's a [silver] lighter, with a little spider on, that my best friend bought me for my birthday.

records.definition_text: the light created by electrical equipment, candles, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: We have put some lighting in the garden.; I fixed the lighting on the ceiling and attached several spotlights to the walls.

records.definition_text: gently
records.learnerexamples_text: She patted him lightly on the shoulder.; The weather here is wonderful, the sun is shining, the wind is blowing lightly, and the sky is also clear, clear, blue!

records.definition_text: a sudden flash of light in the sky during a storm
records.learnerexamples_text: thunder and lightning; a flash of lightning; That tree was struck by lightning.; She changed her clothes with lightning speed.; We were sitting in the car when the lightning hit the roof.

records.definition_text: such as
records.learnerexamples_text: She looks best in bright colours, like red and pink.; We have visit[ed] beautiful places like Chile, Patagonia, Iguazu.

records.definition_text: typical or characteristic of
records.learnerexamples_text: That's just like Maisie to turn up half an hour late to her own party!; It's not like you to be so quiet - are you all right?

records.definition_text: as if
records.learnerexamples_text: It looks like I'm going to be in the office until late tonight.; It sounds to me like you ought to change jobs.; You look like you've just got out of bed!; She acts like she's stupid!; It [sound]s like your trousers are really pretty, I would like to see them soon.

records.definition_text: describes something that will probably happen or is expected
records.learnerexamples_text: Do remind me because I'm likely to forget.; I suppose that might happen but it's not very likely.; It's quite/very likely that we'll be in Spain this time next year.; They start thinking that the suitcase is likely to contain a bomb.

records.definition_text: a lot
records.learnerexamples_text: The band practised like mad before their first concert.; It was raining like mad, so we were wet to the skin.

records.definition_text: a lot
records.learnerexamples_text: The band practised like mad before their first concert.; It was raining like mad, so we were wet to the skin.

records.definition_text: things that you do and do not like
records.learnerexamples_text: What are your top five likes and dislikes?; The teacher asked about our families, friends, [and] likes and dislikes and [then] the lesson finished.

records.definition_text: things that you do and do not like
records.learnerexamples_text: What are your top five likes and dislikes?; The teacher asked about our families, friends, [and] likes and dislikes and [then] the lesson finished.

records.definition_text: the largest amount of something that is possible or allowed
records.learnerexamples_text: Is there a limit on the amount of money you can claim?; I think we ought to put a limit on the amount of time we can spend on the project.; There's a limit to the number of times I can stop what I'm doing just so I can help him!; We set a time limit of thirty minutes for the test.; I always watch this programm[e], it's really interesting for anyone who enjoy[s] cooking. [...] Usually two chef[s] come in and prepare the food, and they hav[e] a time limit.

records.definition_text: to control something so that it is less than a particular amount or number
records.learnerexamples_text: I've been asked to limit my speech to ten minutes maximum.; Having so little money to spend on an apartment does limit you in your choice.; In general, kids and teenagers are, at home, allowed to do almost anything they want, wh[ich] sometimes put[s] parents in a very difficult position when trying to [e]stablish rules in order to limit the freedom of the young.

records.definition_text: small in amount or number
records.learnerexamples_text: a limited choice; limited resources; I like warm colo[u]rs, orange and yellow, but my choices are limited for outdoor clothes.

records.definition_text: kept within a particular size, range, time, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: Places on the bus are limited to fifty - so book early!; Free places on the course will be available for a limited period (of time).; Above all, [w]ould it possible to enjoy the offer in September or is it limited to July?

records.definition_text: a row of words on a page
records.learnerexamples_text: The same line is repeated throughout the poem.; Can you read the next line, please, Sonia?; In no more than ten lines, my mother explained that she was moving to Brazilia, the capital of our country, and that she would take me and my brother with her.

records.definition_text: the connection between two telephones
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm afraid your line's been disconnected because your last bill hasn't been paid.; If you want to air your opinions live on the radio, the lines will be open from eight o'clock.; I've got Chris Foster on the line for you. Do you want to take it now or call her back later?; Please hold the line. I'll see if she's available.; I have been told that if I also get a modem and connect to my telephone line and the PC, I could get in contact with different kinds of bulletin boards that your members use.

records.definition_text: a railway track
records.learnerexamples_text: The train was delayed, apparently due to leaves on the line.; The Northern Line is the worst on the London Underground.; The train line is closed between London and Lampton so now you have to use "ABC Coaches", which is also che[a]per.

records.definition_text: to arrange people or things in a row or to stand in a row
records.searchterms_text: line;line (sb/sth) up or line up (sb/sth);line sb/sth up or line up sb/sth
records.learnerexamples_text: A fight broke out behind me as we lined up to receive our food rations.; The soldiers lined us up against a wall and I thought they were going to shoot us.; A lot of customers had lined up after me.

records.definition_text: a connection between documents or areas on the Internet
records.learnerexamples_text: Click on this link to visit our online bookstore.; An au-pair friend of mine ha[s] given me a link to an au-pair homepage.

records.definition_text: to make a connection between two or more people, things or ideas
records.learnerexamples_text: The explosions are not thought to be linked in any way.; The use of CFCs has been linked to the hole in the ozone layer.; The technological revolution taking place today can be directly linked to the amazing evolution [of] communication.

records.definition_text: a connection between two people, things or ideas
records.learnerexamples_text: There's a direct link between diet and heart disease.; Their links with Britain are still strong.; There is a direct bus link between the two locations: this is bus line number six.

records.definition_text: one of the two soft edges of the mouth
records.learnerexamples_text: She kissed me on the lips.; He licked his lips.; We went to a restaurant and when I had to leave, he kissed me on my lips.

records.definition_text: a substance, such as water, that is not solid or a gas and that can be poured easily
records.learnerexamples_text: liquid fuel/nitrogen; Mercury is a liquid at room temperature.; Inside there were three samples of a nasty purple liquid.

records.definition_text: to make a list, or to include something in a list

records.definition_text: to discover the exact size or amount of something, or to be of a particular size

"I don't know - let's measure it."; He measured the flour into the bowl.; This machine measures your heart rate.; The area, measuring 5 miles by 3 miles, has been purchased by the army.; I measured how long they played [for], because I was one of the group's fans.

records.definition_text: a way of achieving something or dealing with a situation

records.definition_text: the exact size, shape, degree or strength of something which you discover by measuring it

records.definition_text: treatment for illness or injury, or the study of this

records.definition_text: relating to the period in Europe between about AD 500 and AD 1500

records.definition_text: in the middle of a group of different amounts or sizes

records.definition_text: the state of belonging to an organization

records.definition_text: If an occasion is memorable, you will remember it for a long time because it is so good.
records.learnerexamples_text: a memorable performance; a memorable evening; It was a memorable birthday party because they bought me a bass guitar that I couldn't buy because of its high price.

records.definition_text: your ability to remember
records.learnerexamples_text: You have a good memory.; She has an excellent memory for names.;  He had a photographic memory.;  memory loss; It's about a girl that lives in London and she lost her memory so everybody has to tell her everything about the past.

records.definition_text: something that you remember from the past

records.definition_text: to repair something that is broken, torn, or not working correctly

records.definition_text: connected with or related to the mind

records.definition_text: a brief remark
records.learnerexamples_text: When I ordered the catalogue, there was no mention of any payment.;  The report made no mention of the problem. ; The story didn't even get a mention in the newspaper.; In the advertisement there's no mention about getting any money back but I think it was such a disappointing evening that you should give it back to me.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize that something is not large or important
records.learnerexamples_text: It cost a mere twenty dollars.;  The mere thought of eating octopus makes me feel sick. ; The fight was just a mere coincidence.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize that you mean exactly what you are saying and nothing more
records.learnerexamples_text: I wasn't complaining, I merely said that I was tired.; I didn't say that you had to go - I merely suggested that you might like to go.; Of course this is merely a suggestion, and if you have got anything else in mind please don't hesitate to let me know.

records.definition_text: Something or someone that is a mess or is in a mess, looks dirty or untidy.
records.learnerexamples_text: My hair's such a mess!;  The house is in a mess.; He makes a terrible mess when he's cooking.; Go and clear up that mess in the kitchen.; Now my room is a mess because I have so much stuff.

records.definition_text: a situation that is full of problems

records.definition_text: the most important idea in a book, film or play
records.learnerexamples_text: The book conveys a complex message. ; The film's message is that ultimately, rich and poor are alike.; It has a clear message: if you desire something, you can [achieve] whatever you want, but [only] with enormous effort and the danger of losing everything you posses[s].

records.definition_text: a place on a website where you can leave messages for other people to read
records.learnerexamples_text: There's a lot of discussion on the message boards about this issue.

records.base_text: mess up sth or mess sth up

records.definition_text: untidy or dirty
records.learnerexamples_text: a messy kitchen; messy hair; His bedroom's always messy.; My kids are both really messy.; It's completely messy now, looks like a war in my bedroom, because my bed has broken and I need to buy a new bed quickly.

records.definition_text: a usually hard, shiny material such as iron, gold, or silver which heat and electricity can travel through
records.learnerexamples_text: Metal, paper and glass can be recycled.; Silver, gold and platinum are precious metals.;  Metals are used for making machinery and tools. ; It was made of metal and wood.

records.definition_text: a way of doing something, often one that involves a system or plan
records.learnerexamples_text: What's the best method of/for solving this problem? ; Travelling by train is still one of the safest methods of transport.;  traditional teaching methods; I think her teaching method is modern, up to date, and I hope I'll finally improve my English.

records.definition_text: a piece of equipment that you speak into to make your voice louder, or to record your voice or other sounds
records.learnerexamples_text: The interviewer asked her to speak into/use the microphone.; My laptop has a built-in microphone.; Then we had to plug [in] all [the] electric instruments, speakers, lights and microphones.

records.definition_text: in a central position
records.learnerexamples_text: The knives and forks are in the middle drawer. ;  Our company rents the middle warehouse. ; After some minute[s] and as I was going [along] in the middle l[a]ne, the car stopped.

records.definition_text: in the middle of your life before you are old
records.learnerexamples_text: a middle-aged couple/man/woman ; Our teacher is a middle-aged lady with a kind smile and British accent.

records.definition_text: used to talk about what is possibly true

records.definition_text: used to suggest doing something, often when there is nothing better to do
records.learnerexamples_text: We might as well walk there.; As you already know so much about the subject, you might as well skip this lecture.; In my opinion, you might as well ask your neighbours if they can look after your flat for one day.

records.definition_text: used to talk about things that possibly happened in the past or could possibly have happened by some time in the future
records.learnerexamples_text: It might have been Alex who called.; The rain might have stopped by lunchtime.; First of all, you might have been thinking you have to go to a sports club or somewhere and exer[c]ise very hard to keep fit.

records.definition_text: describes weather that is not very cold or not as cold as usual
records.learnerexamples_text: We've had a mild winter this year.; As you know, my country has got mild weather.

records.definition_text: describes food or a food flavour that is not very strong
records.learnerexamples_text: a mild chilli sauce; Korean food is quite hot and usually served with rice, but Thai food is mild and sometimes a little bit sour.

records.definition_text: a unit for measuring distance, equal to 1609 metres or 1760 yards
records.learnerexamples_text: a ten-mile drive; The nearest town is ten miles away.;  The latest high-speed trains can travel at 140 miles an/per hour.; I don't feel safe enough [any more], because the police station is 10 miles away and last week there was a burgl[ary] at my neighbour's house.

records.definition_text: relating to the army, navy, or air force
records.learnerexamples_text: military action/service; military uniform; military targets/forces; During my military experience I worked in the kitchen, so kitchen work is quite normal for me as well.

records.definition_text: a unit of length which is equal to 0.001 metres
records.learnerexamples_text: The ring has a width of three millimetres.

records.definition_text: a lot
records.learnerexamples_text: I've seen that film millions of times.; There are millions of things you can do with a computer.

records.definition_text: someone's memory or their ability to think, feel emotions, and be aware of things
records.learnerexamples_text: My mind was full of what had happened the night before, and I wasn't concentrating.; I just said the first thing that came into my mind.;  For some reason her words stuck in my mind. ;  She has a very logical mind.; At my first class he asked to me sing a [song] in English, so I sang "Always on my mind!"

records.definition_text: to be annoyed, unhappy or worried by something

records.learnerexamples_text: a coal/salt/gold mine; My grandfather used to work down the mines.; It is a more or less industrial region with many co[al] mines.

records.definition_text: The minimum amount of something is the smallest amount that is allowed, needed, or possible.

records.definition_text: the smallest amount that is allowed, needed, or possible

records.definition_text: not important or serious

records.definition_text: a herb whose leaves have a strong fresh smell and taste and are used for giving flavour to food and drinks such as tea
records.learnerexamples_text: a bunch of mint; I'd recommend his special lamb chop with mint sauce, it's just so delicious.

records.definition_text: something that is very surprising or difficult to believe

records.definition_text: great suffering or unhappiness

records.definition_text: to avoid doing or experiencing something

records.definition_text: in a moral way

records.definition_text: used to show that something happens a greater number of times than before

records.definition_text: almost or approximately
