records.learnerexamples_text: I was deeply moved by his speech. ;  Many people were moved to tears. ; I was very moved: it was so beautiful!

records.definition_text: to change the time or order of something
records.learnerexamples_text: We need to move the meeting back a few days.; Unfortunately, we have to move the time of our departure [be]cause of technical problems.

records.definition_text: to leave your home in order to live in a new one
records.learnerexamples_text: We're moving house in the spring.; I want to move house [as] soon as possible.

records.definition_text: to begin living in a new home
records.learnerexamples_text: She's just moved in with some friends.; They [have] organised part[ie]s almost every day since we moved in.

records.definition_text: a change of position or place
records.learnerexamples_text: He made a sudden movement and frightened the bird away.; For a long time after the accident, he had no movement in his legs.; Her movements were rather clumsy.; She must sit for two hours without any movement.

records.definition_text: to stop living in a particular home
records.learnerexamples_text: Her landlord has given her a week to move out.; I need to move out and find somethin[g] near the Business Park area.

records.definition_text: causing strong feelings of sadness or sympathy
records.learnerexamples_text: She read a moving speech at the funeral.; It was [a] really moving story.

records.definition_text: used mainly in questions or negative sentences to mean often or a lot
records.learnerexamples_text: Do you go to London much?; I don't like curry very much.; I wear skirts, too, but not very much.

records.definition_text: used before comparative adjectives such as 'better' and 'more beautiful' to mean 'a lot'
records.learnerexamples_text: Their old house was much bigger.; That's a much better idea.; It's a much more beautiful city.; This class is so much better than the old one.

records.definition_text: a thick liquid mixture of soil and water, or this mixture after it has dried
records.learnerexamples_text: You've got mud on your shoes.;  He'd been playing football and was covered in mud. ; It may sound funny, but mud, gravel and snow lying on the school's floors is not a nice sight, so we change our shoes without questioning that rule.

records.definition_text: covered by or containing mud
records.learnerexamples_text: a muddy stream; muddy boots; You've made the kitchen floor all muddy.; I went out into the kitchen. I looked around to see if I could see him, but he was gone, only the wet, muddy footprints were left.

records.definition_text: to speak too quietly and not clearly enough for someone to understand you
records.learnerexamples_text: He mumbled something about it being a waste of time.; I started mumbling something and I could feel I was red because my cheeks were hot.

records.definition_text: the crime of intentionally killing a person
records.learnerexamples_text: to commit murder;  She was charged with attempted murder.; Two sisters have been charged with murder.; a murder weapon ; It was about a murder which had taken place on the beach.

records.definition_text: to kill someone intentionally and illegally
records.learnerexamples_text: He was murdered by a former employee.;  She was accused/found guilty of murdering her husband. ; It's about the man who murdered a lot of people.

records.definition_text: someone who has committed murder
records.learnerexamples_text: a mass murderer; A few weeks later the police caught the murderer of my best friend.

records.definition_text: one of many pieces of tissue in the body that are connected to bones and which produce movement by becoming longer or shorter
records.learnerexamples_text: neck/back/leg/stomach muscles; facial muscles; These exercises build muscle and increase stamina.; It tones the muscles in this area and provides us with stamina and good health.

records.definition_text: a play or film in which singing and dancing tell part of the story
records.learnerexamples_text: a Broadway musical; A Little Night Music is one of Sondheim's greatest musicals.; It is always a great opportunity to enjoy a musical when you go on holiday to London.

records.definition_text: someone who plays a musical instrument, often as a job
records.learnerexamples_text: a talented jazz/classical musician ; The concert features dancers, singers and musicians of all nationalities.; The movie is about two musicians that had to dress like women to escape from the gangsters of Chicago.

records.definition_text: used to show that you think something is very likely or certain to be true
records.learnerexamples_text: Harry's been driving all day - he must be tired.;  It must have been very upsetting for her.; There's no food left - they must have eaten it all.;  She must be very wealthy.; I must have been seven years old at that time.

records.definition_text: used to show that you think it is a good idea for someone to do something
records.learnerexamples_text: You must come and stay with us some time.; We must meet for lunch.; You must come with me when you are in Germany.

records.definition_text: to speak quietly so that your voice is difficult to hear, often when complaining about something
records.learnerexamples_text: He was muttering (away) to himself.;  He muttered something about the restaurant being too expensive.; "Emile Zola is the best writer", he muttered.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize 'I' as the subject of a sentence
records.learnerexamples_text: I myself don't like a heavy meal at lunchtime.;  I'll tell her myself.; Dear editor of 'The Student Tourist Guidebook' [I am writing] regard[ing] your latest student tourist guidebook, which I myself found very useful on my latest trip to Lampton.

records.definition_text: strange or unknown, and not explained or understood
records.learnerexamples_text: a mysterious stranger;  the mysterious death of her son; He died in mysterious circumstances, and there is still a possibility that it was murder.; He went to the Hotel because he wanted to find out who was the person that had sent him a mysterious letter a few days ago.

records.definition_text: something strange or unknown which has not yet been explained or understood
records.learnerexamples_text: an unsolved mystery; How the massive stones were brought here from hundreds of miles away remains a mystery.;  He never gave up hope that he would solve the mystery of his son's disappearance.;  He's out of work, so how he pays his rent is a mystery to me. ; I have chosen this film because it has mystery in it and a lot of fun!!

records.definition_text: an ancient story about gods and brave people, often one that explains an event in history or the natural world
records.learnerexamples_text: ancient myths;  the gods and goddesses of Greek and Roman myth; I spent three days there thinking about myths and legends and having a lot of fun.

records.definition_text: a thin piece of metal with a sharp end, used to join pieces of wood together
records.learnerexamples_text: a three-inch nail; I stepped on a nail sticking out of the floorboards.;  Hammer a nail into the wall and we'll hang the mirror from it.; Sometimes in food given to animals by visitors you can find pieces of glass, nails or even poison.

records.definition_text: the hard surface at the end of your fingers and toes
records.learnerexamples_text: Stop biting your nails!; nail clippers; a nail file; She went to the hairdresser to have her hair cut, to the nails shop to have her nails done and finally she made her face up.

records.definition_text: not wearing clothes
records.learnerexamples_text: a naked man; naked bodies; He was naked to the waist.; The children were half naked.; I cried out in anger and that was a mistake, because the girls turned around and looked at me, standing there naked.

records.definition_text: the reputation that someone or something has
records.learnerexamples_text: She went to court to clear her name.; Their actions gave British football a bad name in Europe at that time.; They're trying to restore the good name of the manufacturer.; He's the only one concerned about the good name of the family.

records.definition_text: to give someone or something a name
records.learnerexamples_text: We named our dogs 'Shandy' and 'Belle'.; A man named Dennis answered the door.; She is named Maryam.

records.definition_text: to say what something's or someone's name is
records.learnerexamples_text: In the first question you had to name three types of monkey.; He couldn't name his attacker.; Not only "Tandoori dishes" but all the [dishes] are tasty, to name some there [are] Chinese, North Indian, and many others.

records.definition_text: to choose someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: Just name the time and the place and I'll be there.; Name your conditions/terms/price.; Ms Martinez has been named (as) the new Democratic candidate.; He has [been] named as the best Latin singer and he has [won] two Grammys.

records.definition_text: Narrow things measure a small distance from one side to the other.
records.learnerexamples_text: narrow streets; a narrow bridge/passage/gap; a narrow face; narrow feet; You will also see narrow streets with pubs and small cafes everywhere.

records.definition_text: only by a small amount
records.learnerexamples_text: He narrowly escaped death in the accident.; She narrowly missed winning an Oscar.; They narrowly escaped crash[ing] with the car in [the]opposite lane.

records.definition_text: bad or unpleasant
records.learnerexamples_text: a nasty shock/surprise; There's a nasty smell in here.; He had a nasty cut above the eye.; She has a nasty habit of picking on people in meetings.; Inside there were three samples of a nasty purple liquid.

records.definition_text: unkind
records.learnerexamples_text: Don't be so nasty to your brother - he's four years younger than you!; I though that it was a nasty joke made by a friend, but the ad[d]ress of the sender did not match with any that I knew.

records.definition_text: very angry or violent
records.learnerexamples_text: When I asked for the money, he turned really nasty.; He can sometimes be very nasty and say and do horrible things on and [off] the pitch.

records.definition_text: a country or the people living in a country
records.learnerexamples_text: the industrial nations; All the nations of the world will be represented at the conference.; Practically the whole nation watched the ceremony on television.; At that time, everyone should have devoted their life to the nation.

records.definition_text: existing or happening in all parts of a particular country
records.learnerexamples_text: a nationwide network/chain of shops; a nationwide survey; The nationwide blackout was the first in the past decade.

records.definition_text: in all parts of a country
records.learnerexamples_text: Schools nationwide are experiencing a shortage of teachers.; On Thursday, Friday or Saturday you could visit the annual festival, which is well-known nationwide for the music, costumes and dance of the local people.

records.definition_text: Your native town or country is the place where you were born.
records.learnerexamples_text: She returned to live and work in her native Japan.; She's a native Californian.; I am good, because in my native country, Austria, I worked in a cinema.

records.definition_text: relating to the first people to live in an area
records.learnerexamples_text: The Aborigines are the native inhabitants of Australia.; the native population; native customs and traditions; I am very happy to tell you about my trip to the Amazon forest native inhabitants museum.

records.definition_text: someone who has spoken a particular language since they were a baby, rather than having learnt it as a child or adult
records.learnerexamples_text: All our teachers are native speakers of English.; a native-speaker dictionary; My knowledge in foreign languages ha[s] to get better and the best way to do [that] is to get in contact with native speakers.

records.definition_text: Something that is natural exists or happens because of nature, not because it was made or done by people.
records.learnerexamples_text: natural ingredients; a natural substance; He died from natural causes.; Floods and earthquakes are natural disasters.; People say that breast-feeding is better than bottle-feeding because it's more natural.

records.definition_text: normal or expected
records.learnerexamples_text: Of course you're upset - it's only natural.;  It's natural that you should feel anxious when you first leave home.;  It's quite natural to experience a few doubts just before you get married.; So, of course, it was quite a natural thing for me to learn [to] driv[e] a car as early as possible, and that was at the age of 18 when one could apply for a driving licence.

records.definition_text: in a normal way
records.learnerexamples_text: Relax and try to behave naturally.; As a result they can't behave naturally at all and become sick.

records.definition_text: as you would expect
records.learnerexamples_text: Naturally, he was very disappointed.; Naturally we had to take his word for it.

records.definition_text: someone's character
records.learnerexamples_text: As a child Juliana had a lovely nature - everyone liked her.;  It's not really in her nature to be aggressive.; He is by nature inclined to be rather lazy.; Jane wasn't very suspicious by nature, but there was something weird in that.

records.definition_text: When children are naughty, or their behaviour is naughty, they behave badly.
records.learnerexamples_text: You naughty boy!; Now that's naughty - you mustn't throw food on the floor!; Our boss treats us all like naughty schoolchildren.; But some naughty students in my class were throwing paper aeroplanes when the teacher was writing something on the board.

records.definition_text: the part of a country's armed forces which is trained to operate at sea
records.learnerexamples_text: My brother is an officer in the Navy.; Gabriel joined the navy in 1997.; a navy ship/vessel; Best of all, not only am I familiar [with the] life-style on a ship but I also know a lot of things about ship[s] because I was in the navy.

records.definition_text: very dark blue
records.learnerexamples_text: He was wearing a navy blue sweater.; I think I will buy [a] navy blue carpet and black and blue furniture.

records.definition_text: close in time
records.learnerexamples_text: He arrived near the end of the lesson.; It was nearer four when we finally arrived.; We can decide which route to take nearer the time.

records.definition_text: close in distance
records.learnerexamples_text: I was standing just near enough to hear what they were saying.; Don't come any nearer.; And they are getting nearer, I must run for my life.

records.definition_text: close in time
records.learnerexamples_text: Her birthday was getting nearer and I still hadn't bought her a present.; As the date of his operation drew near, he became more and more anxious.; I would appreciate very much if you could reply as soon as possible, as the school holiday is drawing near.

records.definition_text: close in distance
records.learnerexamples_text: Where's the nearest post office?; Dear Dan, My friends and I have decided to go to the nearest cinema, the one which is in The Mall, three blocks from here.

records.definition_text: not far away
records.learnerexamples_text: If there's a cafe nearby, we could stop for a snack.; I noticed a policeman standing nearby.; We can go swimming, [and] visit some of the bea[u]tiful castles nearby.

records.definition_text: not far away
records.learnerexamples_text: We stopped at some nearby shops to buy some food.; The nearby towns are lovely, very calm.

records.definition_text: tidy and clean
records.learnerexamples_text: Your house is always so neat - how do you manage it with three children?; She likes everything neat and tidy.; You've got such neat handwriting.; I always go to this restaurant because it's neat and clean.

records.definition_text: used in negatives to mean 'in every case' or 'therefore'
records.learnerexamples_text: That's not necessarily true.; The fact that something is cheap doesn't necessarily mean it's of low quality.; You may love someone without necessarily wanting to marry them.; The most important point in a job interview is to give a good impression, which does not necessarily mean how you look.

records.definition_text: needed in order to achieve something
records.learnerexamples_text: If necessary, we can change the dates of our trip.; We don't want to take any more luggage with us than is necessary.;  I won't stay any longer than necessary.; He lacks the necessary skills for the job.; Is it necessary to give so much detail?

records.definition_text: If something needs something to be done to it, that thing should be done in order to improve it.
records.learnerexamples_text: The car needs to be serviced.; This room needs brightening up a bit.; She needs her hair washing.; It is so beautiful but it needs washing all the time.

records.definition_text: something that is necessary to have or do
records.learnerexamples_text: There's a growing need for cheap housing in the larger cities.; Is there any need to change the current system?; In conclusion, I beli[e]ve that human beings will always have the need for knowledge and entertainment at the same time.

records.definition_text: a thin, pointed metal object with a small hole at one end for thread, used in sewing
records.learnerexamples_text: a needle and thread; It was impossible for me to open the door, it was like [thread]ing a needle with gloves [on].

records.definition_text: the things you need in order to have a good life
records.learnerexamples_text: her emotional needs; The city is struggling to meet the needs of its homeless people.; I love swimming and cycling and that is why I want to ask if there are any facilities that could suit my needs?

records.definition_text: not having enthusiasm or positive opinions about something
records.learnerexamples_text: negative feelings; Many people have a negative attitude towards ageing.; You're so negative about everything!; At the same time there were no negative opinions about the service from the visitors [to] "Fine food".

records.definition_text: A negative effect is bad and causes damage to something.
records.learnerexamples_text: Terrorist threats have had a very negative effect/impact on tourism.; Even if it provides a lot of advantages, this revolution in the world of communication [also] has a negative impact on our society.

records.definition_text: expressing the answer no
records.learnerexamples_text: We received a negative answer to our request.; Museums are the best example to show how life was in the past but when you ask teenagers [whether] they have been in a museum you will get a negative answer.

records.definition_text: with a bad effect
records.learnerexamples_text: They were very negatively affected by the changes.; Despite the huge facilities, technology has affected our lives negatively.

records.definition_text: someone or something that is near or next to someone or something else
records.learnerexamples_text: The French make more films than some of their European neighbours.; Take 5 minutes to discuss this with your neighbour.; As a neighbour of Lithuania and Ukraine we had to learn [the] Russian language.

records.definition_text: an area of a town or city that people live in
records.learnerexamples_text: There were lots of kids in my neighbourhood when I was growing up.; They live in a very well-off neighbourhood.; The place I'm staying in is wonderful, [and] the whole neighbourhood is wonderful.

records.definition_text: near or next to somewhere
records.learnerexamples_text: neighbouring countries/states ; She married a man from the neighbouring village.; We have to do concerts in the neighbouring towns.

records.definition_text: not either of two people or things
records.learnerexamples_text: Luckily, neither child was hurt in the accident.;  Neither of us had ever been to London before.; They gave us two keys, but neither worked. ; "Which one would you choose?" "Neither."; Three years ago, when I was in Japan, my parents were both working and neither of them were at home by the time I g[o]t back from school.

records.definition_text: used to say that a negative fact is also true of someone or something else
records.learnerexamples_text: Jerry doesn't like it, and neither do I.; Her family wouldn't help her and neither would anyone else.; She's not very tall and neither is her husband.; Of course, she never thought those would be the lucky numbers and neither did her husband, so he forgot to ask her about the ticket later.

records.definition_text: used when a negative fact is true of two people or things or when someone or something does not have either of two qualities
records.learnerexamples_text: Neither he nor his mother would talk to the police.; Their performance was neither entertaining nor educational.; I was just having a bath when the lights went out. [...] No lights at all, neither the cooker nor the fridge were working in my flat, so what had happened?

records.definition_text: used when a negative fact is true of two people or things or when someone or something does not have either of two qualities
records.learnerexamples_text: Neither he nor his mother would talk to the police.; Their performance was neither entertaining nor educational.; I was just having a bath when the lights went out. [...] No lights at all, neither the cooker nor the fridge were working in my flat, so what had happened?

records.definition_text: a son of your sister or brother, or a son of the sister or brother of your husband or wife
records.learnerexamples_text: My nephew is 21 today.; I went with my husband, my two sisters and some nieces and nephews.

records.definition_text: the state of being nervous
records.learnerexamples_text: I always suffer from nerves before a match.; I need something to calm my nerves.; I had to calm my nerves.

records.definition_text: worried or anxious
records.learnerexamples_text: He gets very nervous before exams.; I was too nervous to speak.; I was very nervous about driving again after the accident.; She's always been nervous around dogs.; a nervous cough/laugh

records.definition_text: in a worried and anxious way
records.learnerexamples_text: to giggle/laugh nervously ; As always the girls sat down in the fifth row and waited nervously for the event to begin.

records.definition_text: an object that has many holes in it and that is used in many sports and for catching fish
records.learnerexamples_text: a fishing net; a tennis/basketball net; His penalty kick placed the ball firmly in the back of the net.; I have the advantage of being qui[te] tall and therefor[e] I prefer to play at the net.

records.definition_text: a system or group of connected parts
records.learnerexamples_text: a road/rail network; Massive investment is needed to modernise the country's telephone network.; We could reduce our costs by developing a more efficient distribution network.; a network of spies/a spy network; Switzerland is a safe, small and beautiful country [that is] perfect to travel [in], because of the best publi[c] transport network in the world.

records.definition_text: a set of computers that are connected to each other
records.learnerexamples_text: All our offices are on the same network.; [In the future,] the fridge, the television, the stove and the Hi-Fi equipment will be attached to a computer network.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize something negative
records.learnerexamples_text: I never knew you lived around here.; I never knew what happened after I left.

records.definition_text: despite that
records.learnerexamples_text: I knew a lot about the subject already, but her talk was interesting nevertheless.; Both the options you gave seem very interesting. Nevertheless, I get the impression that working with animals is much more fun, don't you think?

records.definition_text: not yet familiar or experienced
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm new to the area.; She's new to the job so you can't expect her to know everything yet.; New staff are given training.; I met a guy called Marc [who] is pretty cool. He is also new to the club.

records.definition_text: recently
records.learnerexamples_text: the newly formed residents' association; Newly-discovered documents cast doubt on the guilt of the two men.; The book is about a newly qualified doctor, Andrew Manson, who starts his career [in] a small town.

records.definition_text: The time when you next do something is the first time you do it again.
records.learnerexamples_text: Could you get some coffee when you next go to the supermarket?; I will talk to you about it much more when I next see you.

records.definition_text: the person or thing that follows the present person or thing
records.learnerexamples_text: Who's next to see the nurse?; Blue roses? Whatever next?

records.definition_text: in the next room, house, or building
records.learnerexamples_text: That's the old man who lives next door to Paul.; Maria didn't understand, but then she realized that the man she was looking for lived next door.

records.definition_text: in the next room, house, or building
records.learnerexamples_text: What are your next-door neighbours like? ; He has just moved from a large city and now he is my new next-door neighbour.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize a positive quality
records.learnerexamples_text: nice and clean; This chair's nice and comfy.; I've just bought a new lamp for my bedroom. [...] I put it by the bed and in front of the door because it's nice and colourful.

records.definition_text: well
records.learnerexamples_text: That table would fit nicely in the bedroom.; His business is doing very nicely.; It is a pleasant, easy book with useful, active vocabulary and short, nicely constructed sentences.

records.definition_text: in a pleasant way
records.learnerexamples_text: She's always very nicely dressed.; If you ask your dad nicely, he might drive you there.; All the rooms are big, clean and nicely decorated.

records.definition_text: a daughter of your brother or sister, or a daughter of your husband's or wife's brother or sister
records.learnerexamples_text: We're taking my niece on holiday with us.; I bought a purple sweater and I want to knit one like mine for my niece.

records.definition_text: a place where you can dance and drink at night
records.learnerexamples_text: We had a meal and then went to a nightclub.; We can visit local pubs or nightclubs which I think you will like.

records.definition_text: entertainment for the night such as bars, clubs, restaurants, and theatres
records.learnerexamples_text: What's the nightlife like around here? ; The nightlife in my country is wonderful!

records.definition_text: a very unpleasant experience
records.learnerexamples_text: Being trapped underwater is my worst nightmare.; The whole journey was a nightmare - we lost our luggage and we arrived two days late.; In a word, [the] holiday became a nightmare: every day we had to buy everything lost by the company.

records.definition_text: a frightening dream
records.learnerexamples_text: a terrifying nightmare; I shouldn't have watched that movie - it'll give me nightmares.; Every night I had a nightmare.

records.definition_text: to move your head up and down as a way of agreeing, to give someone a sign, or to point to something
records.learnerexamples_text: Many people in the audience nodded in agreement.; When I suggested a walk, Elena nodded enthusiastically.; She looked up and nodded for me to come in.; She approached him calmly, showing no signs of nervous[ness] or uncertainty. "Do you have it?" He nodded and shoved his hand into the left pocket of his jacket.

records.definition_text: a lot
records.learnerexamples_text: I've had no end of trouble finding a hotel room.; I had no end of fun when we were going to the beach and the car stopped and we had to go on foot.

records.definition_text: in the past but not now
records.learnerexamples_text: The cinema is no longer used.; She doesn't work here any longer.; The main reason is that my wife got pregnant [and] therefore [a] one-bedroom house is no longer suitable for us.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize that something cannot be changed
records.searchterms_text: matter;matters;no matter how/what/when etc;no matter how/what/when, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: I never manage to lose any weight, no matter how hard I try.; No matter where you are [or] what you do, appar[e]ntly you need electricity.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize that something cannot be changed
records.searchterms_text: no;no matter how/what/when etc;no matter how/what/when, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: I never manage to lose any weight, no matter how hard I try.; No matter where you are [or] what you do, appar[e]ntly you need electricity.

records.definition_text: not any
records.learnerexamples_text: None of us smoke(s).; None of my children has/have blonde hair.; "I'd like some more cheese." "I'm sorry there's none left".; "Have you any idea how much this cost?" "None at all/None whatsoever."; Since none of us had been there before we hired a guide who claimed that he knew English and then we began looking at the ruins.

records.definition_text: If there is no need to do something or no need for something, it is not necessary or it is wrong.
records.learnerexamples_text: There's no need to go to the shops - there's plenty of food in the fridge.; I understand why she was angry but there was no need for that kind of language.; There's no need to shout, for goodness' sake! Just calm down.; He told me that I could trust him with the ticket and that there was no need for me to take it home.

records.definition_text: If there is no need to do something or no need for something, it is not necessary or it is wrong.
records.learnerexamples_text: There's no need to go to the shops - there's plenty of food in the fridge.; I understand why she was angry but there was no need for that kind of language.; There's no need to shout, for goodness' sake! Just calm down.; He told me that I could trust him with the ticket and that there was no need for me to take it home.

records.definition_text: If something someone has said or written is nonsense, it is silly and not true.
records.learnerexamples_text: She talks such nonsense sometimes.; He dismissed the accusations as complete/utter nonsense.; What a load of nonsense!;  It's nonsense to suggest that they could have cheated.; I feel totally disappointed and I would like my money back, because everything [i]n the advertisement was nonsense.

records.definition_text: describes a place where people are not allowed to smoke
records.learnerexamples_text: Let's get a table in the non-smoking area.; You can also choose between a smoking and a non-smoking area.

records.definition_text: used to say that a negative fact is also true of someone else
records.learnerexamples_text: "I don't like cats." "Nor do I."; I've never been to Iceland." "Nor have I."; I can't be at the meeting and nor can Andrew.;  In fact when Mrs. McGillicuddy told the train assist[a]nt about that, he did not believe her. Nor did the Police, [to] whom Mrs. McGillicuddy wrote about what she had seen.

records.definition_text: in the ordinary way that you would expect
records.learnerexamples_text: Both lungs are now functioning normally.; She's behaving perfectly normally for a two-year-old.; But the truth is that those animals are not beh[a]ving normally.

records.definition_text: usually
records.learnerexamples_text: She doesn't normally arrive until ten.; Normally, I plan one or two days ahead.; I normally order fried fish.

records.definition_text: the direction which is between north and east or the northeast part of a country
records.learnerexamples_text: They live in the northeast.; The owner is from the northeast of China.

records.definition_text: in the northeast, or facing towards the northeast
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't really know the northeast part of the country.; You should visit the Northeast Region which is famous for its white sandy beaches which are fringed with coconut trees.

records.definition_text: in or from the north part of an area
records.learnerexamples_text: northern Europe; the Northern Hemisphere; Last Summer I went to Chiang Mai, in northern Thailand with my family.

records.definition_text: the direction which is between north and west or the northwest part of a country
records.learnerexamples_text: The wind is coming from the northwest.

records.definition_text: in the northwest, or facing towards the northwest

records.definition_text: no other thing than

records.definition_text: to see something and be aware of it

records.definition_text: used to say that more than one thing is true

records.definition_text: used to say that more than one thing is true

[T]he only problem is that there are not quite enough tables and chairs for everyone at busy times.

records.definition_text: not before a particular time or event
records.learnerexamples_text: We won't start the meeting until Jeanne is here.; We didn't stop laughing until the movie finished.

records.definition_text: a book that tells a story about imaginary people and events
records.learnerexamples_text: historical/romantic novels; Have you read any of Jane Austen's novels?; His latest novel is selling really well.; Yesterday I was sat on the bench under a tree in that wonderful garden and I was reading an interesting novel by Jane Austen, when a charming [young] boy [came] near to me.

records.definition_text: a person who writes novels
records.learnerexamples_text: His father was a novelist.; My teacher has told me that you are a British novelist who writes crime stories, and you have come to live in our area.

records.definition_text: used to show the length of time that something has been happening, from the time it began until the present
records.learnerexamples_text: I've lived in Cambridge for two years now.; She's been a vegetarian for ten years now.

records.definition_text: as a result of a new situation
records.learnerexamples_text: Now that I've got a car I can visit her more often.; You should help in the house more, now you're older.; She's enjoying the job now that she's got more responsibility.; Now I am in England for fu[r]ther studies, I would be very grateful to you if you will give me the oppo[r]tunity to join your club.

records.definition_text: at the present time, especially when compared to the past
records.learnerexamples_text: Everything seems more expensive nowadays.; Who remembers those films nowadays?; Nowadays, I bake my own bread rather than buy it.; Well, nowadays I hardly ever watch television, as time is something that I really don't have enough [of].

records.definition_text: If something happens now and then, it happens sometimes but not very often.

records.definition_text: relating to the energy that is released when the nucleus of an atom is divided
records.learnerexamples_text: nuclear energy/power; a nuclear power plant; the nuclear industry; Anyway, the manager of that centre called me in order to inform me that I would [be doing] research on nuclear power and atoms.

records.definition_text: relating to weapons that use nuclear power
records.learnerexamples_text: a nuclear war/attack; nuclear disarmament; I think that the car isn't the greatest danger to human life today, because I believe the greatest danger is the nuclear bomb.

records.definition_text: a person, thing, or situation that annoys you or causes problems for you
records.learnerexamples_text: I've forgotten my umbrella - what a nuisance!;  It's such a nuisance having to rewrite those letters.; I hate to be a nuisance, but could you help me?; Local residents claimed that the noise was causing a public nuisance.; It's co[m]fortable, fast and it [avoid]s the nuisance of having to take public transport in the rush hour.

records.definition_text: an amount
records.learnerexamples_text: The number of people killed in road accidents fell last month.;  A small number of children are educated at home.;  A large number of people were contacted.; We are a well-mixed class with equal numbers of boys and girls, all about 20 years old.

records.learnerexamples_text: Does Jake go to a nursery or a childminder?; I enjoy working with children because I was working in a nursery.

records.definition_text: a large tree found in northern countries, or the wood of this tree
records.learnerexamples_text: an oak table/cupboard; There is a very old oak [in the] middle of the garden.

records.definition_text: to do what you are told to do by a person, rule, or instruction
records.learnerexamples_text: The soldiers refused to obey (orders).; They must obey the rules of international law.; People failing to obey the law will be fined.; I have strict parents who tell me what to do and what not to do every day. If I don't obey them, I'll be punished for sure.

records.definition_text: in grammar, the person or thing that is affected by the action of the verb or the person or thing that comes after a preposition
records.learnerexamples_text: In the sentence 'I like ice cream', 'ice cream' is the object of the verb 'like'.

records.definition_text: to feel or say that you do not like or do not approve of something or someone
records.learnerexamples_text: He objects to the label 'magician' which he is often given.; Would anyone object if we started the meeting now?; No-one objected when the boss said it was time to go home.; I would like to object to what the reporter said in his conclusion.

records.definition_text: when someone says that they do not like or approve of something or someone
records.learnerexamples_text: Our main objection to the factory is that it will be noisy.; I have no objections if you want to stay an extra day.; As far as the film programme [is concerned], I have no objections and feel fairly satisfied.

records.definition_text: something that you are trying to achieve
records.learnerexamples_text: Her main/prime objective now is simply to stay in power.; Can the sales force achieve/meet its financial objectives?; Do you think I [will] have [the right] conditions to do the [diving] course and achieve my objectives?

records.definition_text: only influenced by facts and not by feelings
records.learnerexamples_text: I try to be objective when I criticize someone's work.; Friends can be more objective concerning your faults and can give you [a] different point of view.

records.definition_text: something that you do because it is your duty or because you feel you have to
records.learnerexamples_text: If you have not signed a contract, you are under no obligation to pay them any money.; You have a legal obligation to ensure your child receives a proper education.; I think it would be preferable to do [the trip] [i]n July, which is a holiday period and so I won't have any special obligations.

records.definition_text: when someone watches someone or something carefully
records.learnerexamples_text: The doctor wants to keep him under observation for a week.; She has very good powers of observation.; But actually it is boring when you're almost always under observation.

records.definition_text: to watch someone or something carefully
records.learnerexamples_text: The role of scientists is to observe and describe the world, not to try to control it.; He spent a year in the jungle, observing how deforestation is affecting local peoples.; Children learn by observing adults.; To support [the] idea [of] mak[ing] a short video about daily life at our school I have spen[t] some time discussing it with other students, observing and anal[y]sing an av[era]ge day in our school.

records.definition_text: something or someone that you think about all the time
records.learnerexamples_text: an unhealthy obsession with death; her chocolate obsession; He's always wanted to find his natural mother but recently it's become an obsession.; Shopping is an obsession for all of us.

records.definition_text: to get something
records.learnerexamples_text: to obtain permission; First editions of these books are now almost impossible to obtain.; In the second experiment they obtained a very clear result.; Sugar is obtained by crushing and processing sugar cane.; Now, he has obtained [a] permit from other countries to plant sugar in their countries.

records.definition_text: easy to understand or see
records.learnerexamples_text: "How do you know she's not happy?" "It's obvious.";  It's obvious (that) she doesn't like him.; There is no obvious solution.; They have a small child so for obvious reasons they need money.; I know you don't like her, but do you have to make it so obvious?

records.definition_text: in a way that is easy to understand or see

records.definition_text: an important event or ceremony
records.learnerexamples_text: a special occasion; At the wedding he sang a song specially written for the occasion.; I have a suit but I only wear it on special occasions.; The coronation of a new king is, of course, a historic occasion.; Congratulations on the occasion of your wedding anniversary.

records.definition_text: a time when something happens
records.learnerexamples_text: That was a previous/separate occasion.; We met on several occasions to discuss the issue.; I've heard him be rude to her on a number of occasions.; On one occasion our teacher left the class.

records.definition_text: sometimes but not often
records.learnerexamples_text: I see him occasionally in town.; Occasionally I'll have a piece of chocolate, but it's quite rare.; I will need to use the computer to contact my friend on E-Mail and occasionally listen to a couple of CDs.

records.definition_text: to fill or use a place or period of time
records.learnerexamples_text: His book collection occupies most of the room.; All the seats were occupied.; The babies seem to occupy all our time.; An intelligent solution to this is the bicycle, which can be parked almost everywhere and occupies little space.

records.definition_text: to keep someone busy or interested
records.learnerexamples_text: On long car journeys I occupy myself with solving maths puzzles.; The new toys kept the kids occupied for hours.; So in order to keep myself occupied for a while, I went to the restaurant, except it wasn't open.

records.definition_text: to happen, often without being planned
records.learnerexamples_text: An accident involving over ten vehicles has occurred in the east-bound lane.; If any of these symptoms occur while you are taking the medicine, consult your doctor immediately.; Furthermore, I think that most accidents that occur with cars are due to the irrespons[i]bility of some drivers and I think strong measures should be taken in order to punish them.

records.definition_text: the sea
records.learnerexamples_text: to swim in the ocean; It's an island in the middle of the ocean.; These mysterious creatures live at the bottom of the ocean.; It has an ocean view and when I wake up in the morning the sunshine comes [in through the] window, it's the best moment in the day.

records.definition_text: strange or unusual

records.definition_text: used to show who or what does something
records.learnerexamples_text: the works of Shakespeare; the arrival of the rainy season; the music of the flute; They often cover the music of "The Beatles" or "The Rolling Stones".

records.definition_text: showing a reason or cause
records.learnerexamples_text: He died of cancer.; But, three months later, after walk[ing] in the rain he died of pneumonia.

records.definition_text: used after an adjective when judging someone's behaviour
records.learnerexamples_text: It was very nice of you to think of us.; It was a bit mean of him to mention her weight.; Thank you so much for my present. How thoughtful of you.; It was most thoughtful of you to invite us and I warmly appreciate your hospitality.

records.definition_text: If a price has a certain amount of money off, it costs that much less than the usual price.
records.learnerexamples_text: You can get some money off if you pay cash.; There's 40% off this week on all winter coats.; There was $40 or $50 off most jackets in the shop.; He promised me 30% off the price, so I'm going to buy the TV and the CD player from him.

records.definition_text: away from a place or position
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm just off to the shops.; Keep the dog on the lead or he'll just run off.; If we can get off early tomorrow morning we'll avoid most of the traffic.; I'm off now - see you tomorrow.; She's off to Canada next week.

records.definition_text: down or away from a place or position
records.learnerexamples_text: All the leaves had dropped off the tree.; He fell off his bike.; I still remember the way your brother fell off the lad[d]er that day.

records.definition_text: used with actions in which something is removed or removes itself from another thing
records.learnerexamples_text: I can't get the lid off this jar.; Has anyone taken a book off my desk?; Could you cut me a small piece off that white cheese?; Take your feet off the seat.; Next month, I'm going to change my bedroom. I'll take the photographs off the wall.

records.definition_text: near to a building or place
records.learnerexamples_text: an island off the coast of Spain; He spent all night off the coast, (unfinished)

records.definition_text: If food or drink is off, it is not now fresh and good to eat or drink.
records.learnerexamples_text: This milk smells off.; Who knows if the food isn't off?

records.definition_text: If someone such as a doctor or a soldier is off duty, they are not working.
records.learnerexamples_text: What time are you off duty tomorrow?; Sometimes I come off duty at ten p.m.

records.definition_text: a crime
records.learnerexamples_text: Driving without a licence is an offence.; a serious/minor offence; a criminal offence; He committed several serious offences.; It's the third time that he's been convicted of a drug offence.

records.definition_text: when something rude makes someone upset or angry
records.learnerexamples_text: I really didn't mean to cause/give any offence - I was just stating my opinion.; Do you think he took offence at what I said about his hair?; If you don't mind, I'd rather go on my own - no offence, but I think it would be better.; Now, about that organisation of yours. What is it actually doing? No offence, I just wonder are you saving nature or just writing articles about it?

records.definition_text: to give or provide something

records.definition_text: a cheap price or special arrangement for something you are buying

records.definition_text: a police officer

records.definition_text: a person who has a position of authority in an organization
records.learnerexamples_text: a customs/prison officer; I work as [a] customs officer and [in] this job I meet a lot of foreign people every day.

records.definition_text: someone with an important job in a military organization
records.learnerexamples_text: a naval officer; an army officer; He was an officer in [the] army.

records.definition_text: approved by the government or someone in authority

records.definition_text: If something often happens or is often true, it is normal for it to happen or it is usually true.

records.definition_text: belonging to someone or something

records.definition_text: to take part in or become involved in an activity
records.learnerexamples_text: She never participates in any of our discussions, does she?; So, all the students can participate in different activities.

records.definition_text: special, or this and not any other
records.learnerexamples_text: She wanted a particular type of olive oil.; Is there any particular restaurant you'd like to go to?; He wouldn't take just any book - he had to have this particular one!; "Why did you ask?" "Oh, no particular reason, just making conversation."; Are you a fan of a particular team?

records.definition_text: especially, or more than usual
records.learnerexamples_text: Your ideas are particularly helpful.; She didn't seem particularly interested.; "Was the food good?" "Not particularly."; I particularly enjoyed swimming in your new swimming pool.

records.definition_text: to some extent, but not completely
records.learnerexamples_text: The house is partly owned by her father.; He was partly responsible for the error.; I suggest you spend your time partly in the countryside and partly in a city.

records.definition_text: someone who you live with and have a sexual relationship with
records.learnerexamples_text: Partners are not invited to the office party.; Mike had been my partner for 3 years.

records.definition_text: one of two or more people who own a business
records.learnerexamples_text: junior/senior partner; My business partner handles international sales.; Don't spend the evenings with your business partners, but with your women, children and friends.

records.definition_text: when two people or organizations work together to achieve something
records.learnerexamples_text: She's gone into partnership with someone she used to work with.; I really need the money you're offering, mainly to set up that kindergar[t]en school I've told you about, where I would work in partnership with a friend.

records.definition_text: If you work part-time or do part-time work, you work for only some of the day or the week.
records.learnerexamples_text: a part-time job; He works part-time as a waiter.; I can't afford to buy it so I'll look for a part-time job.

records.definition_text: an organization of people who share the same political beliefs and try to win elections
records.learnerexamples_text: a political party; the Green Party; The Labour Party has/have just elected a new leader.; He was elected as party leader in 2001.; They contacted party members from across the nation to ask for their support.

records.definition_text: to go past something or someone
records.learnerexamples_text: I passed him on the stairs this morning.; Cars kept passing us on the motorway.; If you pass a supermarket on the way back, could you get me some milk?; I started to cros[s] the street and then a car passed.

records.definition_text: to give something to someone
records.learnerexamples_text: Could you pass the salt, please?; Gerald passed me the note./Gerald passed the note to me.; For [me to] cover [the] work, can you pass [it] to my friend Jittanun.

records.definition_text: If a period of time passes, it happens.
records.learnerexamples_text: Four years have passed since that day.; Time seems to pass (by) so slowly when you're bored.; Five minutes passed and he didn't come, so I decided to go back inside.

records.definition_text: a successful result in an exam
records.learnerexamples_text: A pass in this exam is above 60%.

records.definition_text: an official document or ticket that allows you to do something
records.learnerexamples_text: a bus/rail pass; a boarding pass; You can buy [a] one-day bus pass and you could visit many monuments and pictures[qu]e places.

records.definition_text: a long, narrow space that connects one room or place to another
records.learnerexamples_text: The bathroom's on the right at the end of the passage.; There's a passage to the side of the house, leading to the garden.; We saw a big house but it was old and locked. We found a secret passage between the trees and we got inside.

records.definition_text: a short part of a book, speech, or piece of music
records.learnerexamples_text: Several passages from the book were printed in a national newspaper before it was published.; She would read a passage for us every night before [we fell] asleep.

records.definition_text: to officially approve of something and make it into a law or rule
records.learnerexamples_text: The government passed a law to restrict the sale of guns.; I hope the government will pass a law which could [control] all these sort of things.

records.base_text: pass around/round sth or pass sth around/round
records.definition_text: to offer something to each person in a group of people
records.searchterms_text: pass;pass around/round sth or pass sth around/round
records.learnerexamples_text: Could you pass these sandwiches round, please?

records.definition_text: to die
records.learnerexamples_text: She passed away peacefully in her sleep.; It was said his father was very ill and his doctor had said his father could pass away in a few months.

records.definition_text: a very powerful feeling, for example of sexual attraction, love, hate, anger or other emotion
records.learnerexamples_text: She saw the passion in his eyes.; Football arouses a lot of passion in fans.; Politics and philosophy were his lifelong passions.; Surfing is my passion.

records.definition_text: having very strong feelings or emotions
records.learnerexamples_text: a passionate speech; a passionate kiss; The child's mother made a passionate appeal for help.; Joe is passionate about baseball.; I wrote a passionate article about how to protect our environment.

records.definition_text: in a way that shows strong feelings or emotions
records.learnerexamples_text: I walked into the room and found them arguing passionately.; Ann has always believed passionately in women's rights.; We met in our favourite pub, we kissed each other passionately like the firs[t] time, and then we sat down.

records.definition_text: A passive verb or sentence is one in which the subject does not do or cause the action but is affected by it.
records.learnerexamples_text: "He was released from prison." is a passive sentence.

records.definition_text: letting things happen to you and not taking action
records.learnerexamples_text: Women at that time were expected to be passive.; Television provides a passive form of entertainment and so just watching it is much easier than reading books which needs concentration.

records.base_text: pass on sth or pass sth on
records.definition_text: to tell someone something that another person has told you
records.searchterms_text: pass;pass on sth or pass sth on
records.learnerexamples_text: Did you pass on my message to Edward?; Lucy asked me to pass on greetings to you.

records.base_text: pass on sth or pass sth on
records.definition_text: to give something to someone else
records.searchterms_text: pass;pass on sth or pass sth on
records.learnerexamples_text: Could you pass the book on to Lara when you've finished with it?

records.definition_text: to become unconscious
records.learnerexamples_text: The heat was too much for me and I passed out.; When she felt a hand on her right shoulder, she passed out.

records.definition_text: to go in a particular direction
records.learnerexamples_text: A plane passed over our heads.; We pass through your village on our way home.; Then we passed through the quiet co[u]ntryside.

records.definition_text: to spend time doing something
records.learnerexamples_text: We passed the time reading and swimming.; What's more, I would have to read to pass the time!

records.definition_text: a secret word that allows you to do something, such as use your computer
records.learnerexamples_text: Key in your password.; It wasn't me, [it] was my brother who stole my password.

records.definition_text: having happened or existed before now
records.learnerexamples_text: past relationships;  I know this from past experience. ; I like the place because it has [nice] people, music and all sorts of things [about] past events.

records.definition_text: above a particular age or further than a particular point
records.learnerexamples_text: This meat is past its sell-by date.; She's past the age where she needs a babysitter.

records.definition_text: used to refer to a period of time before and until the present
records.learnerexamples_text: I've spent the past ten years in and out of jobs. ;  It's been raining for the past three days. ; He was the fifth climber to die on these mountains over the past two days.; Dear Anna, I've just arrived home and couldn't wait to write you to thank you for being so nice, trust[ing] and kind lending me your flat for the past week.

records.definition_text: a set of actions over a period of time, especially ones which lead to a goal or result
records.learnerexamples_text: a career path; The path to success has many difficulties.; Maybe you could talk about your latest book "Murder on Avenue B" or about your path to fame.

records.definition_text: the quality of being able to stay calm and not get angry, especially when something takes a long time
records.learnerexamples_text: You have to have such a lot of patience when you're dealing with kids.; In the end, I lost my patience and shouted at her.; He's a good teacher, but he doesn't have much patience with the slower pupils.; I have patience with animals and care [for] them with love.

records.definition_text: someone who is being treated by a doctor, nurse, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: a cancer patient; I'm a patient of Dr Stephens, please could I make an appointment to see her?; Another good programme is a serial called "House", which is about an e[c]centric doctor who has the incredible flair of knowing which disease patients [have] without examining them.

records.definition_text: having patience
records.learnerexamples_text: Dinner will be ready in half an hour - just be patient!; Be patient with her - she's very young.; She is very patient with us and she tries to explain everything in detail for better understanding.

records.definition_text: in a patient way
records.learnerexamples_text: There was a queue of people waiting patiently for the bus to arrive.; She made her way slowly to the waiting room and patiently waited for the train to arrive.

records.definition_text: a particular way that something is often done or repeated
records.learnerexamples_text: The pattern of family life has been changing over recent years.; Many behaviour(al) patterns have been identified in this study of chimpanzees.; If the alarm-clock had worked, everything would have follow[ed] its usual pattern but this time I woke up too late.

records.definition_text: a design of lines, shapes, colours, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: The carpet was very old and had an unusual pattern.; In my country now legging[s are] the new fashion. Some wear [ones] with stripes, or the black [ones] also ha[ve] a zebra pattern.

records.definition_text: a drawing, shape or set of instructions that helps you to make something
records.learnerexamples_text: a dress/knitting pattern; Approximately three years ago I started to sew my own clothes. I always buy a pattern and follow every instruction given.

records.definition_text: a short period in which something such as a sound or an activity is stopped before starting again
records.learnerexamples_text: There will be a brief pause in the concert while the piano is moved into place.; After a long, awkward pause someone asked a question.; She spoke for three quarters of an hour without a pause.; I would like to correct the journalist [by] saying to him that RADIANT played for 1 hour without any pause.

records.definition_text: to make a CD, DVD, etc. stop for a short time by pressing a button
records.learnerexamples_text: Can you pause the film there, please?; I paused the video I was watching, wondering what that [knocking sound] was.

records.definition_text: to stop doing something for a short time
records.learnerexamples_text: He paused for a moment.; She paused to get her breath back and then carried on jogging.; After a while, she pulled herself together and paused for a minute.

records.definition_text: a path by the side of a road that people walk on
records.learnerexamples_text: The jar slipped from my hand and smashed on the pavement.; I called my friends and asked them if they had found my scarf. Fortuna[ate]ly they ha[d] seen my scarf on the pavement outside the disco.

records.definition_text: the foot of an animal that has claws or nails, such as a cat, dog or bear
records.learnerexamples_text: I found paw prints in the kitchen.; My cat is only 2 years old. She is very beautiful with her long [b]ushy tail and soft paws.

records.definition_text: to give someone money for the work that they do
records.learnerexamples_text: She gets paid twice a month.; Accountancy may be boring but at least it pays well.; Most of these women are very poorly paid and work in terrible conditions.; Those are the first thing[s] I am going to buy when I get paid.

records.definition_text: the money you receive for doing a job
records.learnerexamples_text: Have you had a pay rise recently?; It's a nice job but the pay is appalling.; The pay is good, but have you [got] a car to get everywhere?

records.definition_text: to watch, listen to, or think about something carefully
records.searchterms_text: attention;pay attention (to sth);pay attention to sth
records.learnerexamples_text: You weren't paying attention to what I was saying.; Larry is a very distracted boy. Everybody says that he should pay attention to what he is doing.

records.definition_text: to watch, listen to, or think about something carefully
records.searchterms_text: paid;pay;pay attention (to sth);pay attention to sth;paying;pays
records.learnerexamples_text: You weren't paying attention to what I was saying.; Larry is a very distracted boy. Everybody says that he should pay attention to what he is doing.

records.base_text: pay back sb/sth or pay sb/sth back
records.definition_text: to pay someone the money that you owe them
records.searchterms_text: pay;pay back sb/sth or pay sb/sth back
records.learnerexamples_text: Can you lend me ten pounds? I'll pay you/it back tomorrow.; I put money on the table. If it is not enough, please tell me [and] I'll pay you back.

records.definition_text: an amount of money paid
records.learnerexamples_text: We need a deposit of £165 followed by twelve monthly payments of £60.; When is the first payment due?; Now people can buy or sell things from their home. [T]hey don't have to go to the bank, if they want [to] make a payment.

records.definition_text: the act of paying
records.learnerexamples_text: They will accept payment by credit card.; Usually we ask for payment on receipt of the goods.; Fina[l]ly, we employees have been facing delays on payment of our wages.

records.definition_text: If something that you have done to try to achieve something pays off, it is successful.
records.learnerexamples_text: All your hard work has obviously paid off!; I think people shouldn't underestimate the importance of books and I am sure it will finally pay off!

records.base_text: pay off sth or pay sth off
records.definition_text: to pay all of the money that you owe
records.searchterms_text: pay;pay off sth or pay sth off
records.learnerexamples_text: I've paid off the loan.; I promise you I'll pay off all my phone bills.

records.base_text: pay sb/sth a visit or pay a visit to sb/sth
records.definition_text: to visit a person or place, usually for a short time
records.searchterms_text: paid;pay;pay sb/sth a visit or pay a visit to sb/sth;paying;pays
records.learnerexamples_text: We thought we'd pay Sam a visit while we were in Oxford.; P.S: Wherever you decide to go, do not fail to pay me a visit!

records.definition_text: a round green seed, several of which grow in a pod, eaten as a vegetable
records.learnerexamples_text: frozen/dried peas; pea soup; I had a fish meal with some vegetables: peas, beans, carrots and lettuce.

records.definition_text: calm and quiet
records.learnerexamples_text: You'll need peace and quiet to study.; He says he's at peace when he's walking in the mountains.; Go away and leave us to finish our dinner in peace.; There'll be no peace until she gets what she wants.; I saw a lot of primitive people who live in peace with the rainforest.

records.definition_text: when there is no war, violence or arguing
records.learnerexamples_text: peace talks; a peace agreement; Now that the war is over may there be a lasting peace between our nations.; She's very good at keeping (the) peace within the family.; World peace was being threat[e]ned by the Gulf War, major countries were taking sides and preparing to fight each other, millions of lives were in danger but no one seemed to care enough.

records.definition_text: quiet and calm
records.learnerexamples_text: a peaceful afternoon/place; This village is in a peaceful location with [a] sandy beach.

records.definition_text: without violence
records.learnerexamples_text: a peaceful demonstration/protest; Leipzig is well-known in the world because of the begin[ning] of the peaceful revolution in 1989 in Germany.

records.definition_text: in a peaceful way
records.learnerexamples_text: He died peacefully at home.; There were a beautiful bride and a handsome bridegroom who were sleeping peacefully with smiles on their faces.

records.definition_text: a round fruit with sweet yellow flesh that has a lot of juice, a slightly furry red and yellow skin and a large seed in its centre
records.learnerexamples_text: Would you like peaches and cream for dessert?; I enjoy eating cool summer fruit, such as melon, water-melon, peaches and apricots.

records.definition_text: the top of a mountain, or the mountain itself
records.learnerexamples_text: snow-covered peaks; It is one of the most difficult peaks to climb.; You can walk or ride a horse to reach the peak.

records.definition_text: the highest level or value of something
records.learnerexamples_text: peak travel times; Holiday flights reach a peak during August.; Here we see an athlete at the peak of her fitness and career.; The situation gets worse, especially [during] peak hours, when people go to work or school and when they return home.

records.definition_text: an oval-shaped nut with a thin brown shell
records.learnerexamples_text: peanut oil; salted/dry-roast(ed) peanuts; I went to the supermarket where I bought some peanuts, cheese dip and a bottle [of] soda.

records.definition_text: unusual and strange, sometimes in an unpleasant way
records.learnerexamples_text: She has the most peculiar ideas.; What a peculiar smell!;  It's peculiar that they didn't tell us they were going away.; The video on road accidents made me feel rather peculiar.; Yesterday I had a birthday and my friend Pat suggested that I should visit a fortune-teller. We went along to visit the most peculiar woman I have ever met in my life.

records.definition_text: a part of a machine that you press with your foot to operate or move the machine
records.learnerexamples_text: the brake pedal; This sewing machine is operated by a foot pedal.; He stood up on the pedals of his bike to get extra power as he cycled up the hill.; It has a comfortable seat, big pedals and a [w]onderful inscription "RIDER".

records.definition_text: a person who is walking and not travelling in a vehicle
records.learnerexamples_text: a pedestrian crossing; Many streets are reserved for cyclists and pedestrians.; There aren't cars in the city, because the roads are only for pedestrians.

records.definition_text: to remove the skin of fruit and vegetables
records.learnerexamples_text: Peel and chop the onions.; We are a family of four and everybody peels vegetables, does [the] washing-up and makes coffee.

records.definition_text: a punishment for doing something that is against a law or rule
records.learnerexamples_text: The violation carries a penalty of up to three years in prison.; Currently, ticket holders pay a penalty equal to 25% of the ticket price when they change their flight plans.; Although, the government can [i]ncrease the penalties for neglec[t]ful driving. In this regard, police officers are already paying more attention to drunk drivers.

records.definition_text: an advantage given in some sports to a team or player when the opposing team or player breaks a rule
records.learnerexamples_text: The referee awarded a penalty kick.; After twenty more minutes of playing or I should say fighting, none of us could score and finally the match had to be decided by penalties.

records.definition_text: a large, black and white sea bird that swims and cannot fly
records.learnerexamples_text: A row of penguins stood at the water's edge.; It's wonderful, you can see the whales swimming in the sea, the sea [lions] lying on the beach and the penguins.

records.definition_text: a coin or unit of money with a value of one hundredth of a pound
records.learnerexamples_text: Could you lend me 50 pence/50p?; I found a ten/twenty/fifty pence piece on the ground.; It was [a] two penny coin.

records.definition_text: a sum of money paid regularly by the government or a private company to a person who has stopped working because they are old or ill
records.learnerexamples_text: a pension plan; a state/private pension; He won't be able to draw his pension until he's 65.; Moreover, you'll have to pay attention to your health, if you don't want to die before [you get] your pension.

records.definition_text: a hollow green, red or yellow vegetable
records.learnerexamples_text: red peppers; I eat every [kind] of vegetable - carrots, green peppers...

records.definition_text: for or out of every 100, shown by the symbol %
records.learnerexamples_text: You got 20 percent of the answers right - that means one in every five.; Only 40% of people bothered to vote in the election.; I love colourful clothes and this skirt was [in a] sale so I just had to pay 30 per cent of the old price.

records.definition_text: an amount of something, often expressed as a number out of 100
records.learnerexamples_text: What percentage of women return to work after having a baby?; Interest rates have risen by two percentage points.; If "today's youngster[s]" [are] asked where [they] would like to have lunch, a high percentage of them will probably answer "McDonalds".

records.definition_text: exactly right for someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: You'd be perfect for the job.; The weather's just perfect for a picnic.; The weather was perfect for the cycling holiday.

records.definition_text: in a perfect way
records.learnerexamples_text: The jacket fits perfectly, the skirt not so well.; They're perfectly suited.; I think black is your colour and they'll fit you perfectly!

records.definition_text: used to emphasize the word that follows
records.learnerexamples_text: To be perfectly honest, I don't care any more.; You know perfectly well what the matter is.; I made it perfectly clear to him what I meant.; I was perfectly happy on my own.; I told them I hadn't brought a map because I knew the way perfectly well.

records.definition_text: to entertain people by acting, dancing, singing, playing music, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: She composes and performs her own music.; A major Hollywood star will be performing on stage tonight.; Later a band performs and everybody starts to dance and sing.

records.definition_text: to do a job or a piece of work
records.learnerexamples_text: Computers can perform a variety of tasks.; The operation will be performed next week.; Most of the students performed well in the exam.; The technology of computers can [produce] special effects [i]n films and cartoons, it can also be used to perform some kind[s] of surgery.

records.definition_text: how successful someone or something is
records.learnerexamples_text: The new suits help swimmers to improve their performance.;  High-performance cars are the most expensive.; This was a very impressive performance by the young player, who scored 12 points within the first 10 minutes.; I do some exercises in order to improve my performance in the water.

records.definition_text: acting, dancing, singing, or playing music to entertain people
records.learnerexamples_text: a performance of Arthur Miller's play, 'The Crucible'; She gave a superb performance as Lady Macbeth.; I was sure that the legendary instrument that the great player used during his performances had to be very big, as the box is.

records.definition_text: someone who entertains people by acting, singing, dancing or playing music
records.learnerexamples_text: He's a brilliant performer.; We are going to watch "Bodygu[a]rd", which has so many famous performers.

records.definition_text: a length of time
records.learnerexamples_text: Her work means that she spends long periods away from home.; Unemployment in the first half of the year was 2% lower than in the same period last year.; The study will be carried out over a six-month period.; The house was built during the Elizabethan period.; Hi Jo, I've seen a restaurant [is] looking for a waitress during the period from June to August.

records.definition_text: in school, a division of time in the day when a subject is taught
records.learnerexamples_text: We have six periods of science a week.; After the period, when the bell rang, I stayed in the class [to] ask some questions and my new teacher gave me some explanations.

records.definition_text: lasting or continuing for a long time or forever
records.learnerexamples_text: She is looking for a permanent place to stay.; Are you looking for a temporary or a permanent job?; The disease can cause permanent damage to the brain.; I am a permanent member of [the] Fear factor club.

records.definition_text: always and forever
records.learnerexamples_text: I seem to be permanently broke.; Michael and his family have settled permanently in Brazil.; Although I am not permanently employed, I found it very interesting to help skilled instructors teach other people to swim and surf.

records.definition_text: when you allow someone to do something
records.learnerexamples_text: She gave him permission immediately.; They even have to ask for permission before they go to the toilet.; Official permission has been granted for more building near the river.; The authorities have refused permission for the demonstration to take place.;  Planning permission was refused for the hypermarket after a three-week inquiry.

records.definition_text: to allow something
records.learnerexamples_text: Photography is not permitted inside the museum.; The prison authorities permit visiting only once a month.; The security system will not permit you to enter without the correct password.; My parents permitted me to go!

records.definition_text: relating to or belonging to a particular person
records.learnerexamples_text: I can only speak from my personal experience.; This is a personal opinion/view and not that of the government.; Passengers are reminded to take all their personal belongings with them when they leave the plane.; The only personal belongings he took was a black leather suitcase.

records.definition_text: designed for or used by one person
records.learnerexamples_text: a personal computer/stereo; a personal loan; The activity that I like best is to surf the Web with a powerful personal computer.

records.definition_text: relating to the private parts of someone's life, including their relationships or feelings
records.learnerexamples_text: He has a few personal problems at the moment.; Do you mind if I ask you a personal question?; His resignation was apparently for personal rather than professional reasons.; We know very little about his personal life.; I wanted to see him and talk to him about some personal problems.

records.definition_text: the type of person you are, which is shown by the way you behave, feel and think
records.learnerexamples_text: She has a very warm personality.; He is well qualified for the job, but he does lack personality.; I mean, when she dances, she transmits strength and a big personality.

records.definition_text: a famous person
records.learnerexamples_text: The show is hosted by a popular TV personality.; What is more, you could take part in the festival without paying for it and meet some famous personalities from the world of music.

records.definition_text: used when you give your opinion
records.learnerexamples_text: Personally (speaking), I think the show is going to be a great success.; Personally, I really like green spag[h]etti.

records.definition_text: done by or affecting one person and not by someone else
records.learnerexamples_text: These figures should be correct because I've checked them personally.; He believes that parents should be made personally responsible for their children's behaviour.; At the end of the concert, when it was after midnight and everyone had already left, the group came up to each of us (who helped out) and thanked us personally!

records.definition_text: to make someone agree to do something by talking to them a lot about it
records.learnerexamples_text: If she doesn't want to go, nothing you can say will persuade her.; I persuaded her (that) it was the right thing to do.; He is trying to persuade local and foreign businesses to invest in the project.; Using a bunch of bananas, the zoo-keeper persuaded the monkey back into its cage.; I had to persuade them to let me go and make enquiries.

records.definition_text: to make someone believe that something is true
records.learnerexamples_text: Their argument failed to persuade me.; It's no use trying to persuade him (that) you're innocent.; My friends persuaded me that everythin[g] was going well.

records.definition_text: always believing that bad things are likely to happen
records.learnerexamples_text: The tone of the meeting was very pessimistic.; The doctors are pessimistic about his chances of recovery.; In his book, [the] most important thing is his character. He has never been pessimistic, he has never hated his parents.

records.definition_text: extremely frightened
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm petrified of spiders.; I was petrified as well as confused.

records.definition_text: someone who is trained to prepare or sell medicines
records.learnerexamples_text: The pharmacist gave me some medicine.

records.definition_text: a shop or part of a shop that prepares and sells medicines
records.learnerexamples_text: You could try a hayfever remedy from the pharmacy.; Sometimes such a situation could happen when you need some food or something [from the] pharmacy.

records.definition_text: a stage or period which is part of a longer period
records.learnerexamples_text: The first phase of the project is likely to be completed by August.; We're entering a new phase in international relations.; When I was in my early teens I went through a phase of only wearing black.; Many people disagree about the best phase of a man's life but I defin[i]tely believe that [the] teenage years are the most beautiful of your life and I have many reasons for believing that!

records.definition_text: someone who studies or writes about the meaning of life
records.learnerexamples_text: Plato was a Greek philosopher.; He wasn't a teacher, he wasn't a philosopher, but he was a great artist.

records.definition_text: the study or writing of ideas about the meaning of life, or a particular set of ideas about the meaning of life
records.learnerexamples_text: Descartes is considered by many to be the father of modern philosophy.; We have been enthu[si]astic students of history, literature and philosophy for three years now.

records.definition_text: a copy of a document made with a machine which produces copies of documents using light and electricity
