records.learnerexamples_text: I made several photocopies of my CV and sent them to different companies.; As far as my level of English is concerned, I have obtained my Cambridge Examination and I enclose a photocopy of the certificate.

records.definition_text: to take a picture using a camera
records.learnerexamples_text: I prefer photographing people rather than places.; MacKay was photographed leaving the building.; This city is not big as you know, so we don't have m[any] interesting buildings to be photographed.

records.definition_text: a phrase which consists of a verb in combination with a preposition or adverb or both, which has a different meaning from the meaning of its separate parts
records.learnerexamples_text: 'Look after', 'work out' and 'make up for' are all phrasal verbs.; At my first lesson, we talked together about our past experiences and we learnt some phrasal verbs too (which we really hate!)

records.definition_text: a group of words that are used together, and which often have a particular meaning
records.learnerexamples_text: Here are some phrases that may be useful in your essays.; [A] man dressed in black would ask me: "How many apples are there in the bedroom?" [and] I should answer with a scratch [o]n the nose and the phrase: "Three and seven quarters sir."

records.definition_text: related to the body
records.learnerexamples_text: physical exercise/fitness/strength/disabilities; physical appearance; Eighty kilometres is a pretty long distance and there is a [danger] that our trip would turn out to be a gruelling experience because of physical exhaustion.

records.definition_text: in a way that relates to the body or someone's appearance
records.learnerexamples_text: physically active/fit; Physically I find him very attractive.; The work is physically demanding.; Special holidays are available for physically disabled people.; Most people believe that team sport[s] help children to become healthier, both mentally and physically, but there are those who have objections to this statement.

records.definition_text: to choose something or someone
records.learnerexamples_text: Pick a card from the pack.; She was picked for the Olympic team.; She was picked to play for the team.; [I]n this restaurant, the[re] are all types of pizza [o]n a table and you can pick any pizza you want.

records.definition_text: If you pick flowers or fruit, you take them off a plant or tree.
records.learnerexamples_text: They were picking strawberries for twelve hours a day.; I picked some apples this morning.; Two weeks is quite a long time so I am planning to go cycling [i]n the mountains, gather acorns, pick flowers, go hiking and watch the sun set.

records.definition_text: to choose a person and criticize or treat them unfairly
records.learnerexamples_text: The other boys pick on him because he's so small.; They gave themselves names and acted as gangs rather than just groups of friends, and started picking on younger people, or mem[b]ers of other gang[s], trying to start fights with them.

records.base_text: pick up sth or pick sth up
records.definition_text: to learn a new skill or language by practising it rather than being taught it
records.searchterms_text: pick;pick up sth or pick sth up
records.learnerexamples_text: When you live in a country you soon pick up the language.; I am [a] very good swimmer and I know some basic sailing techniques which I picked up while I was in Canada.

records.definition_text: an idea of what something is like
records.learnerexamples_text: After watching the news, I had a clearer picture of what was happening.; The next day we will go round the area so you will have a general picture in your mind.

records.definition_text: a film
records.learnerexamples_text: Could this be the first animated film to win a best picture award?; Now I can buy the DVD "Star Trek - The Motion Picture".

records.definition_text: an image seen on a television or cinema screen
records.learnerexamples_text: We can't get a clear picture.; Another important point for me is that things like listening [to] music or watching TV sounds better and the pictures on TV are being improved, because the machines [are becoming] better.

records.definition_text: A picturesque place is attractive to look at.
records.learnerexamples_text: the picturesque narrow streets of the old city; Poland is a really nice country, with many historical buildings and picturesque places.

records.definition_text: a type of food made with meat, vegetables, or fruit covered in pastry and baked
records.learnerexamples_text: Would you like some more apple pie?; a chicken and mushroom pie; I like apple pie and ice cream as [a] dessert.

records.definition_text: a single amount of a particular type of thing
records.learnerexamples_text: I have an interesting piece of information/news for you.; She gave me a very useful piece of advice.; You can visit the churches, the ancient bu[i]ldings, and some other interesting places. That's my piece of advice.

records.definition_text: an example of artistic, written or musical work
records.learnerexamples_text: a beautiful piece of music; an orchestral piece; There was an interesting piece on alternative medicine in the newspaper yesterday.; My favourite music is an instrumental piece of music by Vangelis.

records.definition_text: objects positioned one on top of another
records.learnerexamples_text: a large pile of sand; a pile of books; The clothes were arranged in piles on the floor.; It was like finding a needle in a pile of straw.

records.definition_text: If something unpleasant piles up, you get more and more of it.
records.learnerexamples_text: My work's really starting to pile up.; My work [has] piled up and I have to carry on.

records.definition_text: a small, hard piece of medicine that you swallow
records.learnerexamples_text: a sleeping pill; a vitamin pill; My mother takes three or four pills a day.; Jamie's always had trouble swallowing pills.; Don't forget your pills for your allergy.

records.definition_text: a small, thin piece of metal with a sharp point used for temporarily holding pieces of cloth together
records.learnerexamples_text: I'll keep the trouser patch in place with pins while I sew it on.

records.definition_text: to fasten something with a pin
records.learnerexamples_text: We're not allowed to pin anything to/(up) on the walls.; Secondly, we need a big board. Everybody could pin information on it, [for example] the timetable, the menu for the canteen, or information about special events in and around the school.

records.definition_text: a tall tree with long, thin leaves shaped like needles
records.learnerexamples_text: a pine forest; After a few days, we came to a small lake surrounded by pine trees.

records.definition_text: a large fruit with thick skin and sharp leaves sticking out of the top which is sweet and yellow inside
records.learnerexamples_text: pineapple juice;  We ate some slices of pineapple.; [There is] some special fruit [here], like durian, pineapple, banana and so on.

records.definition_text: a measure for liquid equal to about half a litre
records.learnerexamples_text: a pint of milk ; a pint of beer ; I thank everybody, hoping we'll see [each other] in the pub where I'll invite you for a pint of beer.

records.definition_text: a long tube inside which liquid or gas can move through
records.learnerexamples_text: a water/gas pipe; a burst/broken/leaking pipe; A good surprise w[ould] be [if] you told Anna you need her to help to fix the pipe in our house.

records.definition_text: someone who attacks ships and steals from them
records.learnerexamples_text: The pirates held the ship's captain prisoner and demanded money for his release.; I'm crazy about pirates since I watched "Pirates of the Caribbean".

records.definition_text: an area painted with lines for playing particular sports, especially football
records.learnerexamples_text: a football/hockey/cricket pitch; Supporters invaded the pitch.; For example, you can have free access to the football pitch, the basketball court and even to the golf course.

records.definition_text: to choose a place for a tent and put it there
records.learnerexamples_text: We pitched our tent in a field.; After pitching my tent I could not wait to hike the moors.

records.definition_text: a feeling of sympathy and understanding for someone else's unhappiness or difficult situation
records.learnerexamples_text: The girl stood gazing in/with pity at the old lion in the cage.; We took pity on a couple of people waiting in the rain for a bus and gave them a lift.; But the young man insisted so much that I took pity on him and in the end I agreed to help him.

records.definition_text: the seat where you sit in a theatre, a class, a train, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: The children collected their prizes and then went back to their places.;  Could you save me a place near the stage?; We looked for a place to sit and found one.

records.definition_text: an opportunity to study at a college, to join a team, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: She's got a place at university.; She's got a place on on a fine-arts course.; I felt it was my chance so on Monday I ran to the club. [T]here were only 3 places [left], [and] I will begin next Saturday.

records.definition_text: to put something somewhere carefully
records.searchterms_text: place;place sth in/on etc;place sth in/on, etc.;placed;places;placing
records.learnerexamples_text: She placed the letter in front of me.; Suddenly little Sophie, who was chewing a sweet, lifted the lady's hat, took the sweet out of her mouth and placed it on top of the lady's head.

records.definition_text: simple and not complicated
records.learnerexamples_text: a plain style of architecture; He prefers plain food - nothing too fancy.; I like wearing plain cloth[e]s.

records.definition_text: not mixed with other colours, substances, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: plain yoghurt; For the living room, we've chosen a plain carpet and patterned curtains.; The wall didn't have any patterns, nothing but plain light blue. So I've decided to buy some pictures to put on it.

records.definition_text: a drawing of a building, town, area, vehicle, machine, etc. which only shows its shape from above, its size, and the position of important details
records.learnerexamples_text: an architect's plans; a street plan ; a seating plan ; He uses a computer to help him draw 3D plans, ele[c]trical circuit plans and th[at] kind [of thing].

records.definition_text: to think about and decide what you are going to do or how you are going to do something
records.learnerexamples_text: She helped them to plan their route.; If we plan carefully, we should be able to stay within our budget.; She's already planning how to spend her prize money.; Dear Dan, I have planned a wonderful night for us.

records.definition_text: a large, round object in space that moves around the sun or another star
records.learnerexamples_text: the planet Earth/Venus; Might there be intelligent life on other planets?; It's about the planet Mars, because I'm very interested [in] space.

records.definition_text: the activity of thinking about and deciding what you are going to do or how you are going to do something
records.learnerexamples_text: Events like these take months of careful planning.; It seems like you have been doing a lot of planning for our trip next week.

records.definition_text: to put a plant into the ground or into a container of earth so that it will grow
records.learnerexamples_text: We planted trees and bushes in our new garden.; Hyacinth bulbs planted in pots now will flower early in the spring.; The house is beside a small lake and surround[ed] by all sorts of different flowers my aunty had planted.

records.definition_text: to put a bomb somewhere so that it will explode there
records.learnerexamples_text: Rebels had planted several bombs near the base.; As a result, [they] accused him of having planted a bomb in the Airport of Recife, in the city where he lived.

records.definition_text: a raised surface for people to stand on that is higher than the ground
records.learnerexamples_text: a viewing platform; This brilliant young violinist has appeared on concert platforms all round the world.; It was dangerous, but I knew I had do it, bung[ee] jumping! My instructor said 1, 2, 3, and then he said : "Go", so I jumped from the platform where I was standing.

records.definition_text: to be a particular character in a film or play
records.learnerexamples_text: In the film version, Branagh played the part of the father.; The main actor played the part of John, a poor man that becomes rich.

records.definition_text: to compete against a person or team in a game
records.learnerexamples_text: Who are Aston Villa playing next week?; Arsenal are playing against Newcastle in the next round.; Arsenal played against Everton and Arsenal won the game 3[-]1.

records.definition_text: when children enjoy themselves with toys and games
records.learnerexamples_text: a play area; And it has [a] play area for children to enjoy themselves.

records.definition_text: to deceive someone in order to make them laugh
records.learnerexamples_text: I played a trick on her and pretended I'd forgotten her birthday.; She didn't realise they were just playing a joke on her.; His best friend John couldn't put up with Pat always revealing his secrets, so decided to play a trick on him.

records.definition_text: to be one of the people or things that are involved in an event or situation
records.learnerexamples_text: Alcohol plays a part in around 60% of violent crime.; Technology plays an important part in this situation, because I don't think that adults are playing computer games for Batman or Spiderman, for example, but for the special effec[t]s and the gra[phics].

records.definition_text: in a pleasant way
records.learnerexamples_text: They treated me pleasantly enough.; Jacqui was pleasantly surprised to get a B for history.; I was really pleasantly surprised that you're going to spend your summer holiday in Slovakia.

records.definition_text: to make someone feel happy
records.learnerexamples_text: I only got married to please my parents.; He was always a good boy, very friendly and eager to please.; Considering her loneliness, we made every effort to please her and to encourage her, because she was loved by everybody for her gentle, kind and lovely character.

records.definition_text: a feeling of happiness or enjoyment
records.learnerexamples_text: His visits gave his grandparents such pleasure.; Why do so many boys take pleasure in killing insects?; It gave me a lot of pleasure.

records.definition_text: an enjoyable activity or experience
records.learnerexamples_text: It was such a pleasure to meet you.; He wrote an article on the pleasures and pains of camping.; Reading is one of my few pleasures.; It would be a pleasure to have you here in Mexico during your holiday.

records.definition_text: (the state of having) enough or more than enough, or a large amount
records.learnerexamples_text: "Would you like some more coffee?" "No thanks, I've had plenty."; We've got plenty of time before we need to leave for the airport.; They've always had plenty of money.; There's plenty to do here.; There's plenty more beer in the fridge.

records.definition_text: the story of a book, film, play, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: The film has a very simple plot.; The plots of his books are basically all the same.; A film with a good plot, special effects, sound quality and some computer animations can turn into a real experi[e]nce if watched with friends or relatives.

records.definition_text: a plastic or rubber object with metal pins, used to connect electrical equipment to an electricity supply
records.learnerexamples_text: a three-pin/two-pin plug; to fit/change a plug; If a plug is wired incorrectly, it can be dangerous.; We had to check eve[r]y plug, switch, lights.

records.definition_text: something you put in a hole to block it
records.learnerexamples_text: a bath plug

records.definition_text: to connect a piece of electrical equipment to an electricity supply or to another piece of equipment
records.learnerexamples_text: Could you plug the iron in for me?; It allows anybody to call from anywhere without hav[ing] to plug it in a wall!

records.definition_text: someone whose job is to repair or connect water pipes, and things like toilets and baths
records.learnerexamples_text: When is the plumber coming to mend the burst pipe?; In the past I worked as a plumber.

records.definition_text: and also
records.learnerexamples_text: Let's not go on holiday in August - it'll be too hot - plus it'll be more expensive.; I would be more than pleased to receive you at home. We could have a lot of fun, plus, you won't have to pay a thing!

records.definition_text: an advantage or a good feature
records.learnerexamples_text: Your teaching experience will be a plus in this job.; Free accommodation is a plus for me, but there are some points which I want to [find out about].

records.definition_text: a container which is sewn into or onto a bag or fixed to a seat or door in a vehicle
records.learnerexamples_text: Sarah put her maps in the inside/outside pocket of her rucksack.; The safety instructions are in the pocket of the seat in front of you.

records.definition_text: an amount of money given regularly to children by their parents
records.learnerexamples_text: How much pocket money do you get each week?; How much pocket money do you get?

records.definition_text: a piece of writing, especially one which has short lines and uses words that sound similar
records.learnerexamples_text: a book of love poems; This m[y]sterious man used to write a lot of letters and poems to my grandmother.

records.definition_text: someone who writes poems
records.learnerexamples_text: Rimbaud was a nineteenth-century French poet.; Everyone [in] my group knows that I'm quite [a] good poet, so Peter asked me to read some of my poems.

records.definition_text: poems in general as a form of literature
records.learnerexamples_text: modern poetry; I enjoy all kinds of poetry, especially love poetry.; She started writing poetry at a young age.; My town hall organi[z]ed a poetry compet[i]tion.

records.definition_text: an idea, opinion, or fact which someone says or writes
records.learnerexamples_text: I'd like to discuss the first point in your essay.;  He explained his point by drawing a diagram. ;  Could I make a point about noise levels? ; I take your point about cycling, but I still prefer to walk.; Tomorrow I have another class exactly at the time of your class. I can't miss that class because it's a physics class. I know I may miss many important points but I promise you [I will] get the best mark (result) in the next exam.

records.definition_text: a unit used for showing who is winning in a game or competition
records.learnerexamples_text: With 3 games still to play, Manchester United are 5 points ahead.; We were losing [by] 1 point, I ca[ught] the ball and tried to throw it to my partner but...

records.definition_text: the thin, sharp end of something
records.learnerexamples_text: the point of a needle

records.definition_text: an opinion or fact that deserves to be considered seriously, or which other people agree is true
records.learnerexamples_text: "She's always complaining that the office is cold." - "Well, she's got a point."; "How are we going to get there if there are no trains?" - "Good point."; First of all, in your picture you can reveal the style of life of teenagers (I think it is a good point).

records.definition_text: the reason for or purpose of something
records.learnerexamples_text: I'd try to explain to her how I feel but there's no point because she won't listen.; There's no point in inviting her - she never comes to parties.;  What's the point of studying if you can't get a job afterwards?; Obviously, there is no point in saying "famous people have a right to their own live[s]."

records.definition_text: a particular time or stage in an event or process
records.learnerexamples_text: At one point, he seemed to completely forget what he was saying.;  At that point, a soldier opened fire on the car.; It has got to the point where I can't bear to speak to him.; If, at this point, you decide to leave, that is fine.; At one point, I realised that it was 3 a.m. and many people were leaving the disco.

records.definition_text: the mark (.) that is used to separate the two parts of a decimal
records.learnerexamples_text: One mile equals one point six (1.6) kilometres.

records.definition_text: to hold something so that it faces towards someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: He said that the man had pointed a knife at him.; As he got closer, one of the group's members, Paul, pointed a rifle at him.

records.definition_text: If something points in a particular direction, it is turned towards that direction.
records.learnerexamples_text: The road sign points left.; There was an arrow pointing to the door.

records.definition_text: an opinion
records.learnerexamples_text: I can certainly understand her point of view.;  You have to be willing to see other people's points of view.; That is my point of view.

records.definition_text: a way of thinking about a situation
records.learnerexamples_text: From the point of view of personal savings, the cut in interest rates is bad news.; From a medical/scientific point of view, it is an important achievement.; In addition, it is not useful to keep animals in cages even from a scientific point of view.

records.base_text: point out sth or point sth out
records.definition_text: to tell someone about some information, often because they do not know it or have forgotten it
records.searchterms_text: point;point out sth or point sth out
records.learnerexamples_text: He was planning to book a rock-climbing holiday, till I pointed out that Carla is afraid of heights.; I feel I should point out how dangerous it is.; I would like to point out some incorrect information.

records.definition_text: a substance that can make you ill or kill you if you eat or drink it
records.learnerexamples_text: Someone had put poison in her drink.; The third day they were in the forest, Pablo was hurt by a piece of wood with poison on it.

records.definition_text: to try to kill someone by giving them a dangerous substance to drink or eat
records.learnerexamples_text: He tried to poison his wife.; Therefore, Matthew decided to kill Pat. He poisoned Pat by putting poisonous ice-cubes into Pat's wine glass.

records.definition_text: to put poison or a dangerous substance in something
records.learnerexamples_text: They poisoned the city's water supply.; Everyday millions of animals die, millions of acres of forest are burnt, millions of gallons of water are poisoned.

records.definition_text: very harmful and able to cause illness or death
records.learnerexamples_text: poisonous chemicals; Can you tell the difference between poisonous mushrooms and edible varieties?; On the other hand, the people in the future will probably wear clothes to protect themselves from the polluted air and water, the harmful ultra-violet rays from the sun and all the dangerous and poisonous gases or chemicals which [are the] result of a developed country.

records.definition_text: A poisonous animal uses poison in order to defend itself.
records.learnerexamples_text: a poisonous snake; Some of the animals, like poisonous snakes, crocodiles, [and] lions, are kept in special cages.

records.definition_text: a large, white bear that lives in areas near the North Pole
records.learnerexamples_text: Polar bears can be very dangerous.; So it's very difficult to create real-life conditions for some animals, for instance for polar bears and eagles.

records.definition_text: a set of ideas or a plan of what to do in particular situations that has been agreed officially by a group of people, a business organization, a government or a political party
records.learnerexamples_text: They believe that the European Community needs a common foreign and security policy.; What is your party's policy on immigration?; In fact, more and more countries are [creating] new enviro[n]mental policies.

records.definition_text: in a polite way
records.learnerexamples_text: He thanked them politely.; I tried to control myself and started to speak politely and in a friendly way.

records.definition_text: the state of being polite
records.learnerexamples_text: We were impressed by their politeness.; Moreover, I have other qualities such as politeness, thus I am capable of looking after members of the public.

records.definition_text: relating to politics
records.learnerexamples_text: political leaders/parties; Education is back at the top of the political agenda.; I'm very interested in Italian political life, and I want to get news [all the] time.

records.definition_text: someone who works in politics, especially a member of the government
records.learnerexamples_text: Churchill was a distinguished politician.; It was now the third month [since] the gangster had kidnapped her, because of her being the daughter of an important politician.

records.definition_text: ideas and activities relating to how a country or area is governed
records.learnerexamples_text: He has little interest in local politics.;  She's planning to retire from politics next year.; But I'm very interested in politics, so I really enjoy political [programmes] and chat shows.

records.definition_text: to make water, air, soil, etc. dirty or harmful
records.learnerexamples_text: We need a fuel that won't pollute the environment.; Most of them don't pollute the environment, and they don't create traffic jams on the roads.

records.definition_text: damage caused to water, air, etc. by harmful substances or waste
records.learnerexamples_text: air/water pollution;  The book shows simple things you can do to reduce pollution from your car.; The manifesto includes tough measures to tackle road congestion and environmental pollution.; There is less pollution than in the city and [it] is qui[e]ter too.

records.definition_text: an area of water smaller than a lake, often artificially made
records.learnerexamples_text: a duck pond; After that, we'll visit "Suizenji-Park" which is a real Japanese Garden with a pond and many kinds of flowers and trees.

records.definition_text: a game in which two people use long, thin sticks to hit coloured balls into holes around the edge of a table
records.learnerexamples_text: We played pool all evening.; I had a pool table in my bedroom and I had a lot of videogames.

records.definition_text: a small area of water or a small amount of liquid on a surface
records.learnerexamples_text: We dipped our feet in a shallow pool by the rocks. ;  a pool of blood ; When I came into the kitchen, I saw a pool of blood [o]n the floor.

records.definition_text: of very low quality
records.learnerexamples_text: poor health;  Last year's exam results were poor.;  a poor harvest ; But the quality of [the] food was poor.

records.definition_text: not having much skill at a particular activity
records.learnerexamples_text: Her spelling has always been poor.;  Sam's a poor swimmer.; Since I was a teenager, I've often drawn and painted but without any kind of teaching, so my tec[h]nique is poor.

records.definition_text: to go to a particular place
records.learnerexamples_text: Doug's just popped out for a few minutes. ;  I'll pop into the supermarket on my way home. ; Why don't you pop in/over and see us this afternoon?; Who could imagine life without the telephone? Not being able to call your friend and ask if you can pop in for a moment?

records.definition_text: for or involving ordinary people rather than specialists or very educated people
records.learnerexamples_text: popular entertainment/culture; The issue was given full coverage in the popular press.; Due to his studies in Persian folklore and popular culture, he is the progenitor of anthropology in Iran.

records.definition_text: the quality of being liked by many people
records.learnerexamples_text: the increasing popularity of organic food; We agreed that something had to be done to promote the popularity of local films.

records.definition_text: the number of people living in a particular area
records.learnerexamples_text: a growing/shrinking population;  What's the population of Brazil?; With a population [of] about 800 people, that town really surprised me!

records.definition_text: all the people living in a particular area, or all the people or animals of a particular type
records.learnerexamples_text: a 9% rise in the prison population; The dolphin population has been seriously affected by tuna fishing.; Their yellow and black stripe has a mysterious beauty (which is the main reason for the hug[e] decrease [in the] tiger population).

records.definition_text: meat from a pig
records.learnerexamples_text: a pork chop; pork sausages; We ordered pork chops, boiled potatoes, [and] greens.

records.definition_text: a town by the sea or by a river which has a harbour, or the harbour itself
records.learnerexamples_text: a fishing/container port;  the Belgian port of Zeebrugge ; We had a good view of all the ships coming into/leaving port.; The name is very interesting because the hotel is near the port.

records.definition_text: the amount of food served to one person, especially in a restaurant
records.learnerexamples_text: The portions are very generous in this restaurant.; I think you should take [a] packed lunch with you, because the restaurant is far too expensive and the portions are too small.

records.definition_text: a painting, drawing, or photograph of someone
records.learnerexamples_text: a portrait painter; She's commissioned an artist to paint her portrait/paint a portrait of her.; Downstairs we can find pictures [by] old masters and a great portrait of the Spanish King Charles the Third.

records.definition_text: (of places and things) expensive and of high quality
records.learnerexamples_text: a posh hotel; He takes her to some really posh restaurants.; First of all, the 'Kaya' is quite [a] big, posh restaurant [whose] interiors are like [a] traditional Korean house.

records.definition_text: the situation that someone is in
records.learnerexamples_text: In your position, I would probably resign.; She knows the person that owns the club, who decided to organize a private party for her 18th birthday. I wish [I was] in her position.

records.definition_text: the place where something or someone is, often in relation to other things
records.learnerexamples_text: I've found our position on the map.; You've moved the furniture around - the sofa is in a different position.; I like [this restaurant] because of [its] position, the old town, and most of all because the owner is a friend of mine so that the bill is not too expensive for me!

records.definition_text: the way someone is sitting, standing, or lying, or if something is pointing up or down, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: a kneeling position; I go to sleep on my back but I always wake up in a different position.; Keep the bottles in an upright position.; Four hundred kms in that [un]comfortable position was terrible for us.

records.definition_text: the part that someone plays in a game such as football
records.learnerexamples_text: I didn't know you played hockey - what position do you play?; It's a basketball club and all those guys in the club are much bigger than me. At first we talked to each other [about] which position we had to play.

records.definition_text: your level of importance in a company or society
records.learnerexamples_text: the position of women in society; Whether or not you're given a car depends on your position in the company.; Perhaps the style of their dress will indicate their position in society too.

records.definition_text: a job
records.learnerexamples_text: She applied for a position in the firm that I work for.; Dear Mr. Greenfield I am writing in response to the advertisement which I saw published in my local newspaper, as I would like to apply for the position you offer.

records.definition_text: A positive effect is good and makes something better.
records.learnerexamples_text: The improved diet has had a positive effect on his mood.; All the colours and the smell of fresh and dried flowers has such a positive effect on me that life feels great.

records.definition_text: feeling enthusiastic and happy about your life and your future
records.learnerexamples_text: a positive attitude ;  I'm feeling much more positive about things now. ;  We've shown people samples of the product and had a very positive reaction/response. ; She is lovely and she [is] always positive.

records.definition_text: expressing the answer yes
records.learnerexamples_text: We received a positive answer/response from the minister.; I am looking forward to your positive response.

records.definition_text: certain that something is true
records.learnerexamples_text: "Are you sure you saw him?" "Absolutely positive." ;  I'm positive that I switched it off. ; I'm positive that my experience will be useful in another shop like yours.

records.definition_text: in a good or hopeful way
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't respond very positively to being bossed around - it just makes me angry.; Modern technology also affects [my life] positively in the lab I work for.

records.definition_text: something that you own or that you are carrying with you at any time
records.learnerexamples_text: Please remember to take all your personal possessions with you when you leave the aircraft.; Talking about using your possessions, can I use your electronic appliances such as computers [and] CD players while you are away?

records.definition_text: in grammar, a possessive word or form of a word shows who or what something belongs to
records.learnerexamples_text: 'Mine' and 'yours' are possessive pronouns.

records.definition_text: a chance that something may happen or be true
records.learnerexamples_text: The forecast said that there's a possibility of snow tonight.; Is there any possibility (that) you could pick me up from the station?; There is a strong possibility that she was lying.; Then I remembered I had tried [on] some rings one hour before in a shop in the centre of the city. Maybe I had taken it off while I was trying them. It was a possibility!

records.definition_text: something that you can choose to do from a number of options
records.learnerexamples_text: We could take on extra staff - that's one possibility.; "Have you decided what to do?" "No, I'm still considering the various possibilities."; Another possibility is to go to the London Transport Museum, which is very close and free for students.

records.definition_text: If something is possible, it might or might not exist or be true.
records.learnerexamples_text: It's possible (that) Mira might turn up tonight.; "Do you think he'll end up in prison?" "It's very possible."; That's one possible solution to the problem.; I investigate the most urgent environmental problems in our world, and then I [suggest] possible solutions to them.

records.definition_text: used in polite questions
records.learnerexamples_text: Could I possibly borrow your computer? ; Could you possibly lend me your bike for one day?

records.definition_text: used with 'can' or 'could' for emphasis
records.learnerexamples_text: We'll do everything we possibly can to help. ;  I couldn't possibly ask you to do that. ; My opinion is that everyone who possibly can go by bicycle should do that.

records.definition_text: a job in a company or organization
records.learnerexamples_text: Teaching posts are advertised in Tuesday's edition of the paper.; She's held the post for thirteen years.; They have several vacant posts.; In addition, I have worked [in] a similar job so I have already gained the experience needed for the post.

records.definition_text: to leave a message on a website
records.learnerexamples_text: I posted a query about a Chilean novelist.

records.definition_text: someone whose job is to deliver and collect letters and parcels that are sent by post
records.learnerexamples_text: Our postman delivers everything in the morning.; I think a postman brought it.

records.definition_text: to arrange for something to happen at a later time
records.learnerexamples_text: They decided to postpone their holiday until next year.; We've had to postpone going to France because the children are ill.; I'm doing an experiment tomorrow which I can't postpone.

records.definition_text: a round container, usually used for storing things or for cooking
records.learnerexamples_text: a pot of face cream/jam/paint; a flower pot; There's plenty of cupboard space in the kitchen for all your pots and pans.; Fill a large pot with salted water and bring it to the boil.; By the right window there is [a] green plant in [a] pot.

records.definition_text: possible when the necessary conditions exist
records.learnerexamples_text: A number of potential buyers have expressed interest in the company.; Many potential customers are waiting for a fall in prices before buying.; The accident is a reminder of the potential dangers involved in oil production.; As a potential customer, I need some further information.

records.definition_text: someone's or something's ability to develop, achieve or succeed
records.learnerexamples_text: The region has enormous potential for economic development.; I don't feel I'm achieving my full potential in my present job.; You have the potential to reach the top of your profession.; I think this room has got a lot of potential.; The sheer potential for communication it offers is overwhelming.

records.definition_text: possibly
records.learnerexamples_text: Hepatitis is a potentially fatal disease.; This crisis is potentially the most serious in the organization's history.; One must not ignore [the fact] that mobile phones are potentially harmful: scientific experiments tend to show that microwaves produced by phones may cause cancers and tumo[u]rs.

records.definition_text: plates, bowls, etc. that are made from clay
records.learnerexamples_text: They sell pottery and other handmade goods.; You can see very precious pottery and take pictures [of] old goods in antique shop[s].

records.definition_text: the activity or skill of making plates, bowls, etc. from clay
records.learnerexamples_text: I am doing pottery evening classes.; So I suggest we should print new ones with the latest information, for example about our new pottery courses.

records.definition_text: a unit for measuring weight
records.learnerexamples_text: One pound is approximately equal to 454 grams.; One kilogram is roughly the same as 2.2 lbs.; There are 16 ounces in one pound.; Ann's baby weighed eight and a half pounds at birth.

records.definition_text: to hit or beat repeatedly with a lot of force, or to crush something by hitting it repeatedly
records.learnerexamples_text: I could feel my heart pounding as I went on stage to collect the prize.; The city was pounded to rubble during the war.; He pounded on the door demanding to be let in.; Tina's heart began to pound when suddenly, she heard her name being called out loud!

records.definition_text: to make a liquid flow from or into a container
records.learnerexamples_text: I poured the milk into a jug.;  Can I pour you a drink? ; The look on his face stopped me cold, as if someone had just poured a freezing bucket [of water] down my back.

records.definition_text: to rain a lot
records.learnerexamples_text: We can't go out in this weather - it's pouring! ; I real[l]y enjoy shopping, special[l]y in winter time whe[n] the rain is pouring down.

records.definition_text: to flow quickly and in large amounts
records.learnerexamples_text: Blood was pouring from my leg. ; He woke up and cleaned off the blood that poured from his injured eyebrow.

records.base_text: pour sth out or pour out sth
records.definition_text: If you pour out your feelings or thoughts, you talk very honestly about what is making you sad.
records.searchterms_text: pour;pour sth out or pour out sth
records.learnerexamples_text: She listened quietly while he poured out his troubles.; She let me pour out my feelings, a thing I did not do to anyone.

records.definition_text: the condition of being extremely poor
records.learnerexamples_text: Two million people in the city live in poverty.; He emigrated to Australia to escape the poverty of his birthplace.; First of all, I think that our grandparents lived in poverty without amen[i]ties.

records.definition_text: a dry substance made of many small, loose grains
records.learnerexamples_text: curry/chilli powder; A packet of white powder was found and police scientists are analysing it.; Why are there so many adverts for washing powders on TV?; At last I found a box. I put the wasted coffee powder into it and went back to the coffee machine.

records.definition_text: energy, usually electricity, that is used to provide light, heat, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: power cables/lines ;  nuclear power ;  Turn off the power at the main switch. ; From my parents, I found out that there was a power failure.

records.definition_text: control or influence over people and events
records.learnerexamples_text: I've no power over him - he does what he wants to.; People can't be trusted [with] power. [T]hey will always reach for more.

records.definition_text: A powerful person is able to control and influence people and events.
records.learnerexamples_text: a powerful man/woman ; The man worked for a really powerful man, doing the 'dirty work', but, deep inside [he] was a really good person with a sad childhood.

records.definition_text: having a strong effect on people
records.learnerexamples_text: a powerful effect/influence ; The importance of this invention is that the information transmitted on it reaches a lot of people at the same time, so it's a very powerful [method] of co[m]munication in our society.

records.definition_text: having a lot of strength or force
records.learnerexamples_text: a powerful computer/engine/weapon ; The activity that I like best is surf[ing] the Web with a powerful personal computer.

records.definition_text: in a powerful way
records.learnerexamples_text: She kicked the ball so powerfully that it flew over the hedge.; Klaus is a very powerfully-built man .; Mary moved to her aunt's house, an inn, but she had got married to a strange, powerfully-built man.

records.definition_text: relating to experience, real situations or actions rather than ideas or imagination
records.learnerexamples_text: Qualifications are important but practical experience is always an advantage.; The service offers young people practical advice on finding a job.; What's the use of theoretical knowledge that has no practical application?; Before making up my mind, I would like to gain some experience through practical activities.

records.definition_text: almost or very nearly
records.learnerexamples_text: She blamed me for practically every mistake in the report.; These changes would cost us practically nothing.; It's practically impossible for me to get home in less than an hour.; They used to argue all the time and now they've practically stopped talking to each other.; Today it is used [in] practically all spheres and its influence on people is not unnotic[e]able.

records.definition_text: to express admiration or approval about the achievements or characteristics of a person or thing
records.learnerexamples_text: He should be praised for his honesty.; My parents always praised me when I did well at school.; He was highly praised for his research on heart disease.; In fact, my grade was the best in the class and my Math[s] teacher praised me for being so careful and correct.

records.definition_text: a small sea animal which you can eat, and which has a shell and ten legs
records.learnerexamples_text: a prawn sandwich ; Li-Chuong's specialities are sweet and sour pork, prawns and .. rice!

records.definition_text: to hope for something very much
records.learnerexamples_text: We're praying for good weather for tomorrow's cricket match.; I am very di[sa]ppointed with this event and praying that it will happen again next year.

records.definition_text: the words you say to a god
records.learnerexamples_text: a prayer of thanks; She always says her prayers before she goes to sleep.; We thought he'd been killed, but our prayers were answered when he arrived home safely.; I am stopping this letter with lots of love and prayers.

records.definition_text: rare and very valuable
records.learnerexamples_text: a precious vase ; a precious gift;  a precious metal/stone ; I am so sorry because I broke a precious vase you had in your bedroom.

records.definition_text: very important to you
records.learnerexamples_text: a precious moment/memory;  His books are his most precious possessions.; Time is precious - don't waste it.; Love is something precious which we all want to have.

records.definition_text: exact and accurate
records.learnerexamples_text: The precise location of the house is a secret.; He caught me at the precise moment that I fainted.; I would appreciate [it] if you were more precise next time with your report.

records.definition_text: exactly
records.learnerexamples_text: The fireworks begin at eight o'clock precisely.; What do you think the problem is, precisely?; He was born in the countryside, more precisely in Bourgogne, and he had always lived there.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize what you are saying
records.learnerexamples_text: "You look tired - you should go home and rest." - "I'm going to do precisely that."; But it's precisely because of the noise that they're thinking of moving.; Books may not be interactive, but that's precisely where their advantage is.

records.definition_text: to say that an event or action will happen in the future, especially as a result of knowledge or experience
records.learnerexamples_text: It's still not possible to predict the occurrence of earthquakes accurately.; Who could have predicted that within ten years he'd be in charge of the whole company?; The hurricane is predicted to reach the coast tomorrow morning.; No one can predict when/where the disease will strike next.; Now, fully equipped and powerful computers can be so small and mobile that some specialists predict that new devices will replace book[s].

records.definition_text: happening or behaving in a way you expect and not unusual or interesting
records.learnerexamples_text: Comets appear at predictable times.; When I was younger I read many books. I prefer[r]ed m[y]stery stories, but now [they] are very predictable for me.

records.definition_text: when you say what will happen in the future
records.learnerexamples_text: Please don't ask me to make any predictions about tomorrow's meeting.; No one believed her prediction that the world would end on November 12.; But in case my predictions are right, maybe you should buy a new pair of shorts?

records.definition_text: better or more suitable
records.learnerexamples_text: Staying at home is preferable to going out with someone you don't like. ; Surely a diplomatic solution is preferable to war.; I think it would be preferable to do it [i]n July, which is a holiday period.

records.definition_text: if possible
records.learnerexamples_text: Water the plants twice a week, preferably in the morning.; I think you should spend more time with your friends, preferably in the fresh country air.

records.definition_text: when you like something or someone more than another person or thing
records.learnerexamples_text: We have white and brown bread. Do you have a preference? ; Her preference is for comfortable rather than stylish clothes.; I have a preference for sweet food over spicy.; Choosing furniture is largely a matter of personal preference.; On the other hand, those who are in favour of keeping on with traditional education argue that no free [choice] of preferences can be made until one has rec[e]ived a [basic education] involving the study of different fields of knowledge.

records.definition_text: a letter or group of letters added to the beginning of a word to make a new word
records.learnerexamples_text: In the word 'unimportant', 'un-' is a prefix.

records.definition_text: A pregnant woman has a baby developing inside her uterus.
records.learnerexamples_text: to get pregnant; She's five and a half months pregnant.; My mother stopped smoking when she became pregnant.; My sister is pregnant with twins.; She wrote me [the] really nice news that she is pregnant.

records.definition_text: an unfair and unreasonable opinion or feeling, especially when formed without enough thought or knowledge
records.learnerexamples_text: Laws against racial prejudice must be strictly enforced.; He claims that prejudice against homosexuals would cease overnight if all the gay stars in the country were honest about their sexuality.; What is really amazing is that Biko, who is banned but 'free' of any prejudice, who doesn't discriminate [against] anybody, 'frees' Mr Woods (who is not banned) from his narrow-minded and intolerant views and gives another aim to Woods' life.

records.definition_text: the things that you do or the time that you spend preparing for something
records.learnerexamples_text: The teacher didn't seem to have done much preparation for the class.; The team blamed injuries and lack of preparation for their failure to win.; Yasmin assisted in the preparation of this article.; I felt that I improved a lot just in this class, so I think that my preparation for the exam will be really good.

records.definition_text: plans or arrangements that you make to prepare for something
records.learnerexamples_text: wedding preparations; We are making preparations to fly Mr Goodall to the nearest hospital.; Preparations for the opening ceremony are well under way.; I would really like to help you with the preparations the day before but it's impossible for me to come.

records.definition_text: ready to deal with a situation
records.learnerexamples_text: When she called on me, I wasn't prepared.; They were prepared for the worst.; I want to be well prepared for my first [trip] to England.

records.definition_text: done or made earlier
records.learnerexamples_text: The spokesperson read a prepared statement.; More fast-food and prepared meals are available than a few years ago.

records.definition_text: to make yourself ready to deal with a difficult situation
records.learnerexamples_text: Prepare yourself for a shock. ;  You should prepare yourself for a long wait. ; So we bought tickets and prepared ourselves for a difficult [journey].

records.definition_text: in grammar, a word which is used before a noun, a noun phrase or a pronoun, connecting it to another word
records.learnerexamples_text: In the sentences 'We jumped in the lake', and 'She drove slowly down the track', 'in' and 'down' are prepositions.; In my 1st lesson I learned about prepositions, and I think I'm going to continue the class next week.

records.definition_text: a piece of paper on which a doctor writes the details of the medicine or drugs that someone needs
records.learnerexamples_text: a doctor's prescription; a prescription for sleeping pills; The doctor should give you a repeat prescription.; These drugs are only available on prescription.; Prescription charges are rising in June.

records.definition_text: when someone or something is in a place
records.learnerexamples_text: She was anxious about the presence of so many people.; The presence of pollen in the atmosphere causes hay fever in some people.; He's usually quite polite in my presence.; The document was signed in the presence of two witnesses.; Your presence here at the club would be really benefic[ial] for the students.

records.definition_text: in a particular place
records.learnerexamples_text: The whole family was present.; There were no children present.; I'm sorry, tomorrow I can't be present at [your] English class.

records.definition_text: to give, provide or make known
records.learnerexamples_text: The winners were presented with medals.; The documentary presented us with a balanced view of the issue.; He presented the report to his colleagues at the meeting.; It had to be realistic, so when we finished we presented it to the directors of my school.

records.definition_text: to introduce a television or radio show
records.learnerexamples_text: She presents the late-night news.

records.definition_text: to show a new play or film
records.learnerexamples_text: The school is presenting 'West Side Story' this term.; I am writing to complain about the organization of the musical show that the Circle Theatre presented.

records.definition_text: an occasion when prizes, qualifications, etc. are formally given to those who have won or achieved them or the act of giving them
records.learnerexamples_text: The presentation of prizes and certificates will take place in the main hall.

records.definition_text: a talk giving information about something
records.learnerexamples_text: The speaker gave an interesting presentation on urban transport.; I'm going to prepare a presentation about London.

records.definition_text: someone who introduces a television or radio show
records.learnerexamples_text: a news/sports presenter; children's television presenters; Suddenly, a news presenter came on with a unusual message.

records.definition_text: to keep something the same or prevent it from being damaged or destroyed
records.learnerexamples_text: to preserve the environment; We want to preserve the character of the town while improving the facilities.; It is a fundamental necessity for everybody to try to do something in order to preserve the health of our planet.

records.definition_text: the job of being president, or the period when someone is a president
records.learnerexamples_text: He has announced that he is running for the presidency.; She won the presidency by a wide margin.; His presidency finished in 1384 (2005), but Iranians will never forget him.

records.definition_text: the highest political position in some countries, usually the leader of the government
records.learnerexamples_text: President Obama; the President of France; Thank you, Mr/Madam President.; [An]other attraction is our museum that is very famous because many paintings have been bought by important pe[ople] like the President of the United States.

records.definition_text: relating to the president of a country
records.learnerexamples_text: a presidential candidate ; Anyway, now Laura was counting to 10 as her brother was putting a bomb in the presidential car.

records.definition_text: to push something firmly, often without causing it to move permanently further away from you
records.learnerexamples_text: Press the button to start the machine.; He pressed his face against the window.; Press down firmly on the lever.; When you press it, it will say: "Congratulations" to you.

records.definition_text: when someone tries to make someone else do something by arguing, persuading, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: public/political pressure; Teachers are under pressure to work longer hours.; Pressure to abandon the new motorway is increasing.; The government is facing pressure from environmental campaigners.; He only asked her under pressure from his wife.

records.definition_text: a difficult situation that makes you feel worried or unhappy
records.learnerexamples_text: She's got a lot of pressure on her at work just now.; Be nice to him - he's been under a lot of pressure recently.; Can you work well under pressure?; the pressures of work; I have two younger sisters so I think I can cope with the pressure [of] helping out in the summer camps.

records.definition_text: used to say what you think is the likely situation
records.learnerexamples_text: They can presumably afford to buy a bigger apartment.; Presumably he just forgot to send the letter.; First of all, I would recommend depart[ing] at 8 o'clock because it will presumably be less crowded than at 10 o'clock.

records.definition_text: to behave as if something is true when it is not
records.learnerexamples_text: She's not really hurt - she's only pretending.; He pretended (that) he didn't mind, but I knew that he did.; Were you just pretending to be interested?; Of course I was angry - I can't pretend otherwise.; Be calm or at least pretend you are.

records.definition_text: If a place or an object is pretty, it is pleasant to look at.
records.learnerexamples_text: That's a pretty hat you're wearing.;  a pretty little village ; Rabat is the capital of Morocco. There [are] a lot of attractions, like ancient historic sites, sandy beaches, [and a] pretty Moroccan market.

records.definition_text: quite, but not extremely or not completely
records.learnerexamples_text: The house has four bedrooms, so it's pretty big.; I'm pretty sure it was her.; I've got a pretty good idea of how to get there.; The best thing about our club is the table tennis, which I'm getting pretty good at.

records.definition_text: almost
records.learnerexamples_text: I've pretty much finished here.; She knows pretty well everything there is to know on the subject.; You can pretty much tell your mother any problem you have and she'll try her best to help you out.

records.definition_text: to stop something from happening or someone from doing something
records.learnerexamples_text: to prevent accidents/crime;  Members of the public were prevented from entering the building.; As I told you once, I'd like to buy a bookshelf where I can organize my books and prevent them from getting damaged.

records.definition_text: when you stop something from happening or stop someone from doing something
records.learnerexamples_text: crime prevention; The organization is committed to disease prevention and education.; I think prevention is the best medicine.

records.definition_text: existing or happening before something or someone else
records.learnerexamples_text: the previous day/week/month/year;  a previous attempt; I felt my previous class was not suitable for me any longer, [so] I decided to [ask] the administrator to help me to change [to] a higher class.

records.definition_text: before the present time or the time referred to
records.learnerexamples_text: She was previously employed as a tour guide.; I had posted the card two months previously.; Well, first of all I must tell you that I didn't know it previously.

records.definition_text: very valuable
records.learnerexamples_text: a priceless antique/painting ; She had five unique paintings [by] Van Gogh which were priceless.

records.definition_text: a feeling of satisfaction at your achievements or the achievements of your family or friends
records.learnerexamples_text: She felt a great sense of pride as she watched him accept the award.;  The whole community takes pride in the school. ; I take pride in you and your patience.

records.definition_text: the respect that you feel for yourself
records.learnerexamples_text: She has too much pride to accept any help.; Not only did I lose £50, but also some pride and self-respect.

records.definition_text: someone who performs religious duties and ceremonies
records.learnerexamples_text: a Roman Catholic priest; Many in the Anglican Church are still opposed to women priests.; I started to read one of the emails and I couldn't believe what I was reading. One of my best friends had become a priest!

records.definition_text: mainly
records.learnerexamples_text: She's known primarily as a novelist but she also writes poetry.; "The Vagabond Dog" - one of his best short stories - is primarily naturalistic.

records.definition_text: most important
records.learnerexamples_text: Her primary responsibility is to train new employees.; You can listen to music and generally use it for fun but the primary reason that computer[s] were invented was for communication.

records.definition_text: a school for children aged 5-11
records.learnerexamples_text: My daughter is still at primary school. ; We sat at a cafe and talked about our primary school.

records.definition_text: the leader of the government in some countries
records.learnerexamples_text: Yesterday I heard that animal rights activists have met the prime minister: maybe the situation will change.

records.definition_text: the son of a king or queen, or one of their close male relatives
records.learnerexamples_text: Prince Edward; At last, the beast really changed back into a prince.

records.definition_text: the daughter of a king or queen, or one of their close female relatives, or the wife of a prince
records.learnerexamples_text: He was married to a Spanish princess.; My teacher told me that I have to wear a dress like a princess.

records.definition_text: main, or most important
records.learnerexamples_text: That was my principal reason for moving.; He was principal dancer at the Dance Theatre of Harlem.; This is its principal advantage.

records.definition_text: the person in charge of a school or college
records.learnerexamples_text: She is principal of a London school.; Another thing you need to be aware of is that the teachers, the Principal and the whole class will be invited and we want this party to be a success because we deeply respect Mr Brown.

records.definition_text: to produce books, newspapers, magazines, etc., usually in large quantities, using machines
records.learnerexamples_text: Fifty thousand booklets have been printed for the exhibition. ; We should also have a more efficient tourist service - it [is] years since we last printed brochures of our town!

records.definition_text: to include a piece of writing in a newspaper or magazine
records.learnerexamples_text: They printed his letter in Tuesday's paper. ; Please take this into consideration and print a corrected version of the article.

records.definition_text: something that is very important and must be dealt with before other things
records.learnerexamples_text: The management did not seem to consider office safety to be a priority.; My first/top priority is to find somewhere to live.; You have to learn to get your priorities right/straight.; Banks normally give priority to large businesses when deciding on loans.; Official business requirements obviously take/have priority over personal requests.

records.definition_text: a building where criminals must live as a punishment
records.learnerexamples_text: He's spent a lot of time in prison.; She went to/was sent to prison for six months.; They should put him in prison and throw away the key!; a prison cell/sentence; About 3 weeks later, I tried to escape from the prison, but they c[aught] me.

records.definition_text: a person who is kept in prison as a punishment
records.learnerexamples_text: Prisoners climbed onto the prison roof to protest at the conditions inside.; This film dealt with two prisoners that escape from their prison and start to take money from banks (of course not legally!)

records.definition_text: the right to be alone and do things without other people seeing or hearing you
records.learnerexamples_text: I hate sharing a bedroom - I never get any privacy.; The new law is designed to protect people's privacy.; Well, it seems that a young, modern and successful man can have no privacy at all.

records.definition_text: only for one person or group and not for everyone
records.learnerexamples_text: She has a small office which is used for private discussions.; I caught him looking through my private papers.; The sign on the gate said 'Private Property - No Admittance.'; I went there to see what's going on, and the band invited us to their private party.

records.definition_text: describes activities which involve personal matters or relationships and are not connected with your work
records.learnerexamples_text: Apparently in interviews he refuses to talk about his private life.; We talked about the film and also about our work and our private life.

records.definition_text: controlled or paid for by a person or company and not by the government
records.learnerexamples_text: private education/healthcare; a private doctor/dentist; I have been working as an English teacher for small children at a private school for three years.

records.definition_text: in secret, or with only one or two other people present
records.learnerexamples_text: She spoke privately with the manager.; Despite his public support, privately he was worried.; I'll pick you up from the station so we will have the op[p]ortunity to chat privately.

records.definition_text: likely to be true or likely to happen
records.learnerexamples_text: The probable cause of death was heart failure.; An election in June seems increasingly probable.;  It is probable that share prices will fall still further.; Surely the older you are, the less probable it is that you'll choose a bike.

records.definition_text: the official or usual way of doing something
records.learnerexamples_text: The company has new procedures for dealing with complaints.; You must follow correct procedure at all times.; Despite being [a] disorganised procedure, it was successful and many people wanted to attend next year's festival.

records.definition_text: a series of actions that you take in order to achieve a result
records.learnerexamples_text: the peace process; Increasing the number of women in top management jobs will be a slow process.; This decision may delay the process of European unification.; The party has begun the painful process of rethinking its policies and strategy.; Going to court to obtain compensation is a long process.

records.definition_text: a series of changes that happen naturally
records.learnerexamples_text: the ageing process; It's all part of the learning process.; Th[ese] events are not only to entertain students, but they are also a part of the learning process, as by communicating with each other students learn the language.

records.definition_text: to deal with documents in an official way
records.learnerexamples_text: Visa applications take 28 days to process.

records.definition_text: to make or grow something
records.learnerexamples_text: The factory produces about 900 cars a year.; She works for a company that produces electrical goods.;  This plant will produce small yellow flowers in the spring.; She's asked me to produce a report on the state of the project.; In this club we produce and design the school magazine "Freestyle."

records.definition_text: to cause a reaction or result
records.learnerexamples_text: The prime minister's speech produced an angry response from the opposition.; Her remarks produced an awkward silence.; If used on delicate skin, this cream may produce a stinging sensation.; I was fascinated by the perfection of the classic[al] sculptures: they were perfectly proportioned, every part was functional to the beauty of the whole sculpture. It's really different [to] looking at them in a book! I suggest everybody [should go and] look at them: it produces a magic effect!

records.definition_text: someone who controls how a film, play, programme, or musical recording is made
records.learnerexamples_text: a film/Hollywood/movie/record producer; I'm sure they are going to be very interested in your first steps as an actor, but also in your later career as a film producer.

records.definition_text: something that is made or grown to be sold
records.learnerexamples_text: They do a range of skin-care products.; The product is so good it sells itself.; I'm trying to cut down on dairy products.; You can buy leather products too.

records.definition_text: when you make or grow something
records.learnerexamples_text: Sand is used in the production of glass. ; The company's new model will be going into production early next year.; More people can enjoy music than before, because of [the] mass production of recorded music.

records.definition_text: when someone controls how a film, play, programme, or musical recording is made
records.learnerexamples_text: She's hoping to get into television production.; Indeed, Northwood cinema enables people to discover films from all over the world - from a small Brazilian production to a 3 hour Bollywood movie.

records.definition_text: the amount of something that is made or grown by a country or a company
records.learnerexamples_text: We need to increase production by 20%.; Swedish industrial production has fallen steadily this year.; Wheat production has risen over the years.; He became famous because he did a lot of things in this country in a year, like giv[ing] them a good education, [and] increas[ing] their production.

records.definition_text: producing a good or useful result
records.learnerexamples_text: We had a very productive meeting and sorted out a lot of problems. ; Some people think that by keeping animals in [a] zoo we can observe them, and try to understand the way they [live]; of course, you can learn things, but it would be more productive to observe them when they are free.

records.definition_text: producing a large amount of goods, food, work, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: productive land ;  a productive worker ; When the weather is good, I am in the appropriate mood to be productive at work.

records.definition_text: a type of work that needs special training or education
records.learnerexamples_text: What's your profession? ; He's a doctor by profession.; The report notes that forty per cent of lawyers entering the profession are women.; As I look back at my past, [the] most embarrassing moments in my life seem to have something to do with my profession, which is an interpreter from Hungarian.

records.definition_text: the people who do a type of work considered as a group
records.learnerexamples_text: The medical profession has expressed concern about the new drug. ; One day, [when] I had an exam, the examiner asked me questions about the legal profession.

records.definition_text: Someone is professional if they earn money for a sport or activity which most people do as a hobby.
records.learnerexamples_text: a professional footballer/athlete/musician; For example, I met a boy last week and at the end he told me that h[is] father is a professional football player.

records.definition_text: showing skill and careful attention
records.learnerexamples_text: a professional attitude;  He looks very professional in that suit.; My teacher is English, her name is Bronye, she's very professional, and nice.

records.definition_text: relating to a job that needs special training or education
records.learnerexamples_text: Chris, you're a nurse, so can I ask your professional opinion on bandaging ankles?;  You should get some professional advice about your finances.; I want to play safe by saying that I am not an architect, therefore I am not able to give professional advice.

records.definition_text: someone who earns money for doing a sport or activity which most other people do as a hobby
records.learnerexamples_text: a rugby professional ; Finally, I wondered whether it would be possible to explain how long it take[s] an amateur to become a professional. Despite know[ing] almost nothing about tennis I would like to win a championship in the future.

records.definition_text: a teacher of the highest rank in a department of a British university, or a teacher of high rank in an American university or college
records.learnerexamples_text: Professor Stephen Hawking; a professor of sociology; a sociology professor; To put it in a nutshel[l] I was astonished [at] how they weren't able to get on using that assortment of high ranked university professors of social science, and were requiring my help.

records.definition_text: a short description of a person, organization, etc., giving the main details about them
records.learnerexamples_text: He's updated his Facebook profile.; We include a photograph and short profile of all the candidates.; I hope [the] above information suits the profile of [the] person you are looking for [for] the job.

records.definition_text: money that you get from selling goods or services for more than they cost to produce or provide
records.learnerexamples_text: She makes a big profit from selling waste material to textile companies.; Company profits are down on last year's figures.; He sold his house at a huge profit.; Also, supermarket owners have put in a vast amount of money to find out the best way to [display] goods in order to get the most profit.

records.definition_text: resulting in or likely to result in a profit or an advantage
records.learnerexamples_text: Over the years it has developed into a highly profitable business.; It is [a] very profitable business.

records.definition_text: a plan of events or activities with a particular purpose
records.learnerexamples_text: The college offers an excellent social programme.; First of all I have to say that the school social programme was the best and I really enjoyed it.

records.definition_text: when someone writes computer programs
records.learnerexamples_text: We learned how to do programming.; I'm very keen on programming and I have made a lot of small utility programs for both Mac and PC.

records.definition_text: development and improvement of skills, knowledge, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: Technological progress has been so rapid over the last few years.; I'm not making much progress with my Spanish.; I will check new words, the[ir] meanings and pronunciations, to make progress for missed sessions.

records.definition_text: to improve or develop in skills, knowledge, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: My Spanish never really progressed beyond the stage of being able to order drinks at the bar.; I have to warn you than I'm not an expert in terms of musical basics, but I'm eager to learn them because I know no-one can progress without learning them; so the main job will be to do that.

records.definition_text: thinking or behaving in a new or modern way
records.learnerexamples_text: progressive ideas/attitudes; a progressive school; I hear [that] some progressive companies don't really approve of company cars and are trying to keep them to [a] minimum.

records.definition_text: to officially forbid something
records.learnerexamples_text: Motor vehicles are prohibited from driving in the town centre.; The government introduced a law prohibiting tobacco advertisements on TV.; Parking is strictly prohibited between these gates.; Perhaps we should prohibit the traffic and create a new cheap bus service for the inhabitants and the tourists.

records.definition_text: a carefully planned piece of work that has a particular purpose
records.learnerexamples_text: a scientific research project; My next project is decorating the kitchen.; Her latest project is a film based on the life of a nineteenth-century artist.; It is also related to my research project.

records.definition_text: to say that you will certainly do something or that something will certainly happen
records.learnerexamples_text: She promised to write to me every week.; He promised faithfully to call me every week.;  Paul promised me that he'd cook dinner tonight.; "I'll come round and see you every day," she promised.; I promise that I will cover the work that you've done in class and I will send [it] to you the day after.

records.definition_text: to say that you will certainly give something to someone
records.learnerexamples_text: They promised us a reward.;  Grandma's ring was promised to me.; Her parents promised her a new car if she passed her exams.; And as a good friend, he has promised me a[n] invitation to [the] wedding.

records.definition_text: when you say that you will certainly do something
records.learnerexamples_text: I'll tidy my things away tonight - and that's a promise!;  I'm not sure I can do it so I won't make any promises.; Don't forget your promise to not just visit but stay at my place.

records.definition_text: If something promises to be good, exciting, etc., people expect that it will be good, exciting, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: It promises to be a really exciting game.; I'm looking forward to start[ing] this trip with you and Chris. It promises to be very exciting!

records.definition_text: to give someone a more important job in the same organization
records.learnerexamples_text: If I'm not promoted within the next two years, I'm going to change jobs.; She's just been promoted to senior sales rep.; She invited me to a party because her husband had been promoted in his job.

records.definition_text: to advertise something
records.learnerexamples_text: The band is promoting their new album.; At that moment I and a large number of people behind me discovered that I was talking to a person made out of wax. [It] was there to promote the museum.

records.definition_text: when someone is given a more important job in the same organization
records.learnerexamples_text: Did Steve get the promotion he wanted?; The job offers excellent promotion prospects.; I would like to congratulate you [o]n your promotion.

records.definition_text: activities to advertise something
records.learnerexamples_text: a sales promotion;  They're giving away free T-shirts as a special promotion. ; Obviously as sales manager he'll be very involved in the promotion and marketing of the product.; There are different kinds of jobs people do during the festival, e.g. some organisational work, doing promotion for the different events or sell[ing] tickets for the concerts.

records.definition_text: done or acting quickly and without waiting, or arriving at the correct time
records.learnerexamples_text: prompt payment; a prompt reply; His prompt action certainly saved my life.; I look forward to your prompt reply.

records.definition_text: quickly, without delay, or at the arranged time
records.learnerexamples_text: We'll have to leave fairly promptly if we want to catch that train.; We try to answer readers' letters as promptly as we can.; She promised she'd keep it secret and promptly went and told Ben!; It provides a business lunch which is not very expensive and is served promptly.

records.definition_text: a word which is used instead of a noun or a noun phrase
records.learnerexamples_text: Pronouns are often used to refer to a noun that has already been mentioned.; 'She', 'it' and 'who' are all examples of pronouns.

records.definition_text: to make the sound of a letter or word
records.learnerexamples_text: How do you pronounce your surname?; She pronounced his name so badly he didn't even recognise it.; Sade, pronounced shah-day, is a singer.; During the lesson many foreign students discover how to pronounce words in English.

records.definition_text: how words are pronounced
records.learnerexamples_text: Mario's English pronunciation is excellent.; There are two different pronunciations of this word.; My teacher is a friendly young man called Peter. He comes from Scotland and this means that his accent and pronunciation are quite different.

records.definition_text: a fact or a piece of information that shows something exists or is true
records.learnerexamples_text: She showed us her passport as proof of her identity.; Do they have any proof that it was Hampson who stole the goods?; Keep your receipt as proof of purchase.; The smile of a child is the best proof of the utility of zoos.

records.definition_text: correct or suitable
