records.learnerexamples_text: the proper way to do something;  Please put those books back in the proper place.; If you're going to walk those sort of distances you need proper walking boots.; He is unable to speak proper English.

records.definition_text: real and satisfactory
records.learnerexamples_text: his first proper job; I've had sandwiches but I haven't eaten a proper meal.; I [had to] change my previous profession (civil engineer) as I couldn't find a proper job.

records.definition_text: correctly, or in a satisfactory way
records.learnerexamples_text: It's still not working properly.; I'm not properly dressed for this sort of weather.; Come on, Evie, speak properly - you're not a baby any more!; Unfortunately my bicycle is not working properly, so I was just wondering if I could borrow yours[?]

records.definition_text: a word or group of words that is the name of a person or place and always begins with a capital letter
records.learnerexamples_text: 'London' is a proper noun.

records.definition_text: objects that belong to someone
records.learnerexamples_text: lost property; The club does not accept responsibility for loss of or damage to club members' personal property.; Children need to be taught to have respect for other people's property.; When I re[aliz]ed that I had lost it, I went to the lost property point in the shopping centre to ask about it, but they couldn't do anything for m[e].

records.definition_text: a building or area of land
records.learnerexamples_text: He owns a number of properties in the centre of London.; The notice said 'Private Property, Keep Off.'; Every shopkeeper and houseowner should ma[i]ntain their property, looking after gardens and plants that s[u]rround it, trying to keep rub[b]ish out of sight.

records.definition_text: a suggestion for a plan
records.learnerexamples_text: a proposal to raise taxes ;  The proposal for a new sports hall has been rejected. ; There has been an angry reaction to the government's proposal to reduce unemployment benefit.; There was anger at the proposal that a UN peacekeeping force should be sent to the area.; I would like you to consider my proposal [and] give me [your] response as soon as possible.

records.definition_text: when someone asks someone to marry them
records.learnerexamples_text: As a young woman, she received several proposals.; After this, things went perfectly well, and Mary accepted his proposal to marry him.

records.definition_text: to suggest a plan or action
records.learnerexamples_text: I propose that we delay our decision until we have more information. ;  proposed changes; I think [the] most important [thing] is that you understand our language. So I propose that you [attend] a school for the first two month[s].

records.definition_text: to ask someone to marry you
records.learnerexamples_text: He proposed to me on my birthday. ; First he caught everybod[y's] attention and straightaway he proposed marriage to her.

records.definition_text: suggested as an idea or plan
records.learnerexamples_text: The proposed road would cut right through the forest.; I will need information about the price of the proposed vacation.

records.definition_text: to intend to do something
records.learnerexamples_text: They propose to cycle across Europe. ; I propose to build a new hotel following the traditional architecture of the village.

records.definition_text: the possibility that something good might happen in the future
records.learnerexamples_text: Is there any prospect of the weather improving?; Job prospects for graduates in the sciences are good.; We've been warned that there is a prospect of flooding due to the heavy rains.; With our effort, I am sure things will be realize[d] and the prospect is [bright].

records.definition_text: to keep someone or something safe from something dangerous or bad
records.learnerexamples_text: clothing that protects you against the cold; It's important to protect your skin from the harmful effects of the sun.; Public pressure to protect the environment is strong and growing.; Hats protect me from the sun (my skin is very sensitive to the sun) and they are also pretty cool.

records.definition_text: the act of protecting or state of being protected
records.learnerexamples_text: This coat doesn't provide any protection against the rain.; Their tent gave/offered little protection against the severe storm.; New legislation still does not offer adequate protection for many endangered species.; I prefer to be accommodated in a log cabin because it gives better protection against the weather and I can sleep much better in it.

records.definition_text: giving protection
records.learnerexamples_text: protective clothing; a protective mask; Besides, I don't want to wear any protective head-gear, which all the riders are obliged to wear.

records.definition_text: when people show that they disagree with something by standing somewhere, shouting, carrying signs, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: a public protest against the war;  a peaceful/violent protest; I believe that we could force the authorities to do something for us by joining [together] in a very big protest.

records.definition_text: to say something forcefully or complain about something
records.learnerexamples_text: A lot of people protested about the new working hours.; They protested bitterly to their employers, but they wouldn't listen.; A young girl was crying, protesting that she didn't want to leave her mother. ; I'd also like to point out that although the service is pleasant, it's a bit slow, which often makes the customers impatient and leads them to protest.

records.definition_text: to show that you disagree with something by standing somewhere, shouting, carrying signs, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: They're on strike to protest against job losses.; Students were protesting about cuts to the education budget.; Undoubtedly, the human rights' defenders would protest.

records.definition_text: feeling very pleased about something you have done, something you own, or someone you know
records.learnerexamples_text: She was so proud of her son.;  I'm very proud to be involved in this project.; Anyway I am so happy to hear that. I'm really proud of you.

records.definition_text: in a way that shows you are pleased about something you have done, something you own, or someone you know
records.learnerexamples_text: He proudly held out his trophy for us to admire.; There were photographs of all her children proudly displayed on the mantelpiece.; "Congratulations Alison!" her mum said proudly.

records.definition_text: to show a particular result or quality after a period of time
records.learnerexamples_text: The operation proved a complete success.;  The new treatment has proved to be very effective. ; John proved to be a good friend and I really thank him for what he did for me.

records.definition_text: to show that something is true
records.learnerexamples_text: Can you prove that you weren't there?; They proved him innocent/guilty.; That theory was proved false.; He's so aggressive - it's as if he's always trying to prove something.; It was real[l]y stressful because I wanted to prove that the level of my English is high enough for this class but I was too nervous to speak cor[r]ectly.

records.definition_text: to give someone something that they need
records.learnerexamples_text: This booklet provides useful information/advice about local services.; All meals are provided throughout the course.; The restaurant provides excellent service.

records.definition_text: if, or only if
records.learnerexamples_text: He's welcome to come along, provided that he behaves himself.; Finally, provided that you have some money to spend, you can always have a great time strolling through shopping halls.

records.definition_text: relating to the human mind and feelings
records.learnerexamples_text: psychological problems; He claims that the constant aircraft noise has a bad psychological effect on the residents.; We are concerned with the physical and psychological well-being of our employees.; To sum up, taking up team sports [is important] for school children as they are provided with important psychological and social [experiences] vital for their lives.

records.definition_text: in a way that is connected to a person's psychological state
records.learnerexamples_text: psychologically disturbed; It makes us like robots and [we] feel bad psychologically, because we want to be different and free [to wear what we want].

records.definition_text: someone who studies the human mind and human emotions and behaviour, and how different situations have an effect on them
records.learnerexamples_text: a child psychologist; an educational psychologist; Some psychologists claim that forcing pupils to study subjects they don't like can be frustrating for them or even reduce their intellectual potential.

records.definition_text: the scientific study of the way the human mind works and how it influences behaviour, or the influence of a particular person's character on their behaviour
records.learnerexamples_text: She studied psychology at Harvard.; a lecturer in psychology; child psychology; the psychology of the soldier; I think it would be a nice experience for me because I am studying psychology.

records.definition_text: relating to or involving people in general, rather than being limited to a particular group of people
records.learnerexamples_text: Public opinion has turned against him.; Is it really in the public interest to publish this information?; We need to increase public awareness of the disease.; The results will not be made public until tomorrow.; We will not go public with the results until tomorrow.

records.definition_text: provided by the government from taxes to be available to everyone
records.learnerexamples_text: public funds/services/spending; a public library; I've found an advertisement on the noticeboard outside the public library that might interest you.

records.definition_text: a book, magazine, newspaper or document in which information or stories are published
records.learnerexamples_text: Our latest publication is a magazine for surfers.; Dear Sir, I am taking the opportunity to write to you [as] I used your publication "The Student Tourist Guidebook" during my last trip to Lampton.

records.definition_text: the act of making information or stories available to people in a printed form
records.learnerexamples_text: The brochure will be ready for publication in September.; Will you arrange the publication of the names of the winners?; When is the publication date?; First, I would like to thank you for the publication of [this] article.

records.definition_text: advertising or information about someone or something in the newspaper, on television, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: bad/good publicity; We've planned an exciting publicity campaign with our advertisers.; The pop group's arrival by hot-air balloon was just a publicity stunt.; We could also prepare a special publicity campaign because we want all the people in Britain [to] know how wonderful our town is.

records.definition_text: a system of vehicles such as buses and trains which operate at regular times on fixed routes and are used by the public
records.learnerexamples_text: Greater investment in public transport would keep more cars off the roads.; I travelled by public transport.

records.definition_text: to make information available to people, especially in a book, magazine or newspaper, or to produce and sell a book, magazine or newspaper
records.learnerexamples_text: She's just had an article published in their weekend supplement.; The Government publishes figures every six months showing how many people are unemployed.; The names of the winners of the competition will be published in June.; She was only 19 when her first novel was published.; My article was published and I rec[e]ived 500 pounds.

records.definition_text: a company or person who prepares and prints books, newspapers, magazines, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: He works for a publisher in Edinburgh.; I suggest that the music publisher should organise more concerts for us and give us more chances to listen [to] "real music" not just tapes.

records.definition_text: a sweet dish that is usually eaten as the last part of a meal
records.learnerexamples_text: We've got apple pie for pudding.; a sticky toffee pudding; The pudding was delicious.

records.base_text: pull down sth or pull sth down
records.definition_text: to destroy a building
records.searchterms_text: pull;pull down sth or pull sth down
records.learnerexamples_text: They pulled down the warehouse to build a new supermarket.; In addition to that, I'd do [my] very best to persuade the city council to arrange for the old, ugly houses to be pulled down as quickly as possible.

records.definition_text: If a vehicle pulls in or pulls into somewhere, it moves in that direction and stops there.
records.learnerexamples_text: They pulled in at the side of the road.; He killed her and threw her body out of the train not far from the station, when the train [was] pulling in.

records.definition_text: If a vehicle pulls out, it starts moving onto a road or onto a different part of the road.
records.learnerexamples_text: That car pulled out right in front of me.

records.definition_text: a warm piece of clothing which covers the top of your body and is pulled on over your head
records.learnerexamples_text: a black woolly pullover; My favo[u]rite pullover is one with small hearts.

records.definition_text: If a vehicle pulls over, it moves to the side of the road and stops.
records.learnerexamples_text: I was looking for somewhere to pull over so I could look at the map.

records.definition_text: to take hold of something and use physical effort to remove it from somewhere
records.learnerexamples_text: I pulled the plug out.; He pulled off his sweater.; I spent the morning pulling up the weeds in the flowerbeds.; My tv is broken because of my little sister: she pulled out the cable.

records.definition_text: If a vehicle pulls up, it stops, often for a short time.
records.learnerexamples_text: A car pulled up outside the bank and two men got out.; I was walking home late one evening, when a car pulled up alongside me.

records.definition_text: to take hold of something and use effort to move your body forwards or up
records.searchterms_text: pull;pull yourself along/up etc;pull yourself along/up, etc.;pulled;pulling;pulls
records.learnerexamples_text: She pulled herself up the stairs, holding onto the rail.; Rollo and the police ran after him and then Rollo fired wounding Harry, who started to pull himself up the stairs to a manhole above his head and then he died.

records.definition_text: a piece of equipment which is used to cause liquid, air or gas to move from one place to another
records.learnerexamples_text: a water/bicycle pump; a fuel/petrol pump; You need to connect a[n] oxygen pump supplying oxygen [which is] require[d] by goldfish.

records.definition_text: when you hit someone or something with your fist
records.learnerexamples_text: a punch on the nose; He gave me a punch and we started to fight.

records.definition_text: to hit someone or something with your fist
records.learnerexamples_text: He punched him in the stomach.; She start[ed] crying and she punched me!

records.definition_text: the use of punctuation marks in writing so that people can see when a sentence begins and finishes, that something is a question, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: His letter was completely without punctuation.

records.definition_text: to make someone suffer because they have done something bad
records.learnerexamples_text: Those responsible for these crimes must be brought to court and punished.; He punished the class by giving them extra work.; I'll be punished by my parents, because [I told them] a lie.

records.definition_text: when someone is punished
records.learnerexamples_text: He had to stay in his bedroom as a punishment for fighting.; Many people think that the death penalty is too severe a punishment for any crime.; I was punished, nearly expel[led], but Pat didn't receive any punishment.

records.definition_text: a young dog
records.learnerexamples_text: a litter of puppies; I was on the beach when my mobile phone rang. I knew that my mother was going to [tell] me that my puppy [was] dead, [so] I didn't answer the call.

records.definition_text: to buy
records.learnerexamples_text: Tickets must be purchased two weeks in advance.; She purchased her first house with the money.; Of course I was able to purchase a second-hand one but I thought that it was a good investment to have a new computer with up-to-date software.

records.definition_text: something that you buy
records.learnerexamples_text: How do you wish to pay for your purchases?; a major purchase; The other day I was standing in a large department store waiting to pay for a couple of films for my camera when the assistant announced that the computer which controlled the till had stopped working. So there we were: a shop full of customers, money at the ready, waiting to make our purchases.

records.definition_text: the act of buying something
records.learnerexamples_text: New restrictions have been placed on the purchase of guns.; A house is the most expensive purchase that most people ever make.; No purchase is necessary for you to enter this competition.; This product may be frozen. If required, freeze on day of purchase.; Report on the purchase of English videos

records.definition_text: A pure substance is not mixed with anything else.
records.learnerexamples_text: pure gold ; a pure cotton shirt; Its domes are made of pure copper, inside there's a big bell called "Zygmunt".

records.definition_text: used to emphasize that a feeling, quality, or state is completely and only that thing
records.learnerexamples_text: pure coincidence;  Her face had a look of pure delight. ; It switches your mind off and stre[t]ches all your muscles at the same time. It's pure refreshment!

records.definition_text: clean and healthy
records.learnerexamples_text: The mountain air was wonderfully pure.; Tap water is never chemically pure.; The weather is sunny, the gentle breeze is pure and fresh.

records.definition_text: why you do something or why something exists
records.learnerexamples_text: The main purpose of the meeting is to discuss the future of the company. ;  The drug may be legalized for medical purposes. ; a multi-purpose kitchen knife; I think the purpose of it was to make the atmosphere more relax[ed].

records.definition_text: to press something
records.learnerexamples_text: If you push this button, the seat goes back.; I was feeling very angry when I pushed the answer button.

records.definition_text: to move somewhere by moving someone or something away from you
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm sorry - I didn't mean to push in front of you.; She pushed through the crowd.; He pushed past the waiting journalists, refusing to speak to them.; They pushed their way to the front of the queue.

records.definition_text: when you move someone or something by pressing them with your hands or body
records.learnerexamples_text: Get on the swing and I'll give you a push.; I gave the door a hard push, but it still wouldn't open.; The door was open, so I gave it a push.

records.definition_text: to try hard to achieve something or to make someone do something
records.searchterms_text: push;push (sb) for sth/to do sth;push sb for sth/to do sth;pushed;pushes;pushing
records.learnerexamples_text: Local residents are pushing for the road to be made wider.; We had to push them to accept our terms, but they finally agreed to the deal.; Governments should push young artists to get involve[d] in their work.

records.definition_text: to make yourself work very hard in order to achieve something
records.learnerexamples_text: She really pushed herself when she was at school.; Don't push yourself too hard and remember to drink more water.

records.definition_text: to cause someone or something to be in a particular condition or situation
records.learnerexamples_text: What's put you in such a bad mood?; I'm not prepared to put my children at risk.; I'm looking forward to putting my ideas into practice.; He's putting me under pressure to change my mind.; The terrorists were put on trial six years after the bombing.

records.definition_text: to make something stop happening or existing
records.learnerexamples_text: He's determined to put an end to these rumours.; Leg injuries put an end to his athletics career.; Maybe because I needed someone to know, or because I wanted to put an end to that feeling, and [have] a normal life.

records.definition_text: to cause something to stop
records.learnerexamples_text: We must put an end to this violence.; That is all I can say about [what] I have seen [o]n my last visit to the zoo, and in my opinion the authorities have to do something in order to put an end to it.

records.definition_text: to read something and say the words aloud so that other people can hear
records.searchterms_text: read;read out sth or read sth out
records.learnerexamples_text: He read out the names of all the winners.; Michael sat in his favourite chair while his wife read out what had happened.

records.base_text: read over/through sth or read sth over/through
records.definition_text: to read something from the beginning to the end, especially to find mistakes
records.searchterms_text: read;read over/through sth or read sth over/through
records.learnerexamples_text: I read over my essay to check for errors.; I thought my eyes were deceiving me [so] I read the letter over again.

records.definition_text: true and not pretended
records.learnerexamples_text: What was the real reason she didn't come? ;  Is that your real name? ; That is the real reason why I'm going to stay in England longer.

records.definition_text: being the most important or the main thing
records.learnerexamples_text: The real problem, of course, is money.; The real difficulty was the language, because my children don't speak English.; Nowadays people work most of the time with their computers, [and] the internet give[s] them the op[p]ortunity to download whatever they want, even books, but the real problem is that they do not have the time to read them.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize a noun
records.learnerexamples_text: She was a real help. ; It's a real pain he's not available tomorrow.; In the advertisement it says "your perfect evening out", but it was a real disappointment.

records.definition_text: showing things and people as they really are, or making them seem to be real
records.learnerexamples_text: The creatures were all computer-generated but so realistic.; I chose this film because I think it is very realistic.

records.definition_text: accepting the true facts of a situation and not basing decisions on things that will not happen
records.learnerexamples_text: Let's be realistic - we're not going to finish this by Friday. ; We have to be realistic about how much we can afford to pay.;  It isn't realistic  to expect people to work for so little money.; We must be realistic, my friend. Eighty kilometres is a pretty long distance.

records.definition_text: the way things or situations really are and not the way you would like them to be
records.learnerexamples_text: Listening to music is my escape from reality.;  Sooner or later you have to face up to reality.;  He may seem charming but in reality he's actually an unpleasant person.; Finally, your report talks about an audience of less than 2,000 although we were in reality more than 5,000.

records.definition_text: to notice or understand something that you did not notice or understand before
records.learnerexamples_text: I didn't realize how unhappy she was.;  I suddenly realized I'd met her before.; They didn't realise the danger they were in.; Do you realise that this is the third time you've forgotten?; I suddenly realised he was my cousin, Alex.

records.definition_text: used when you are saying what is the truth of a situation
records.learnerexamples_text: He isn't really angry - he's just pretending.; You don't really expect them to refuse, do you?; She said she was twenty eight, but really she's over thirty.; The first lesson was about the present tense and wasn't really difficult for us.

records.definition_text: at the back of something
records.learnerexamples_text: There's a sticker on the rear door/window.; In his rear mirror he saw that all [the] lights on the airfield [were] on again.

records.definition_text: to change the order or position of things
records.learnerexamples_text: I've rearranged the furniture in my office.; Maybe you could rearrange the café to be more classical.

records.definition_text: something that makes it right for you to think or do something
records.learnerexamples_text: I think we have reason to be concerned. ;  There is every reason to believe the project will be finished on time.; She suddenly hit him for no reason.; Animals in zoos are in captivity and not in their natural habitat. They live captured there for no reason, as we could learn about them from books or documentaries [instead].

records.definition_text: quite cheap
records.learnerexamples_text: reasonable prices; Tomatoes are very reasonable at this time of year.; If you are nature lovers, you should visit some small villages where you can find [a] peaceful atmosphere, delicious, fresh food and everything [at a] reasonable price.

records.definition_text: good enough but not the best
records.learnerexamples_text: The service at the hotel is reasonable but don't expect 5-star treatment.;  I'd say her work is of a reasonable standard.; From my Certificates you can see that I speak English very well and that I have [a] reasonable knowledge [of] Italian and Spanish.

records.definition_text: big enough or large enough in number or amount, although not big or not many
records.learnerexamples_text: There were a reasonable number of people there. ;  It's a reasonable salary for that job.; We have a reasonable chance of winning the game.; Some of them have good places for sightseeing and a reasonable [amount of] nightlife.

records.definition_text: fair and showing good judgment
records.learnerexamples_text: It's not reasonable to expect people to work such long hours. ; If you tell him what happened, I'm sure he'll understand - he's a reasonable man.; In my opinion, reasonable rules are important for us but be[ing] too strict will bring stress, w[hi]ch causes kids [to] be afraid of many things.

records.definition_text: based on facts that can be explained
records.learnerexamples_text: There will be a reasonable explanation for all of this. ; I hope you will be able to offer me [a] reasonable explanation [for] these mistakes and report correct information in your newspaper.

records.definition_text: in a fair way, showing good judgment
records.learnerexamples_text: Stop shouting and let's discuss this reasonably.

records.definition_text: good/successful/well, etc. enough but not very good or very well
records.learnerexamples_text: I did reasonably well at school but not as well as my sister.; I noticed the sound system wasn't perfect, but it was reasonably good.

records.definition_text: available at a good price
records.learnerexamples_text: reasonably priced meals; Then in the evenings there are many reasonably priced restaurants, where you can get a nice tasty meal with friends.

records.definition_text: someone who fights against the government in their country, especially a soldier
records.learnerexamples_text: The rebels took over the capital and set up a new government.;  Rebels seized control of the airport.; Suddenly, the police came [o]nto [the train], and killed all [the] rebels.

records.definition_text: to refuse to obey rules that you disagree with or do not like
records.learnerexamples_text: Children often rebel against eating certain foods - Rory won't eat vegetables.; His brother was never kind with her and she always wanted to rebel.

records.definition_text: to build something again that has been damaged or destroyed
records.learnerexamples_text: The cathedral was completely rebuilt in 1425 after it had been destroyed by fire.; It's [a] XIX century construction, but they rebuilt it.

records.definition_text: to make a situation succeed again after something bad caused it to fail
records.learnerexamples_text: The country was still struggling to rebuild its economy after the war.; They had to rebuild their lives after the accident.; Since more and more people in our modern society have been living in a [highly] urbanized environment and they are isolated from the rest of nature, I think it is vital to make every effort to rebuild healthy relationships with nature.

records.definition_text: to remember something
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't recall arranging a time to meet.; Can you recall what happened that night?; I recall that he promised to send the document.; Right now, I can't recall much of that phone call.

records.definition_text: the act of receiving something
records.learnerexamples_text: Items must be returned within fourteen days of receipt.

records.definition_text: happening or starting from a short time ago
records.learnerexamples_text: Is that a recent photo?; Have you been following recent political events?;  In recent years, sales have decreased quite markedly. ; Dear John, Thank you for your recent letter.

records.definition_text: not long ago, or at a time that started not long ago
records.learnerexamples_text: Have you seen any good films recently?; Until very recently he worked as a teacher.; Recently, I've been feeling a bit depressed.; Recently I have been watching a lot of programmes [o]n television.

records.definition_text: the place in a hotel or office building where people go when they arrive
records.learnerexamples_text: Ask for me at reception. ;  a reception area/desk ; When I arrived [at] the hotel I asked the reception to find m[e] a taxi to see the city.

records.definition_text: a formal party that is given to celebrate a special event or to welcome someone
records.learnerexamples_text: a wedding reception ; Next month, I have to fly to London to attend a friend's wedding reception.

records.definition_text: a period when the economy of a country is not successful and conditions for business are bad
records.learnerexamples_text: The latest report confirms that the economy is in recession.; The country is now in the deepest recession for over 40 years.; Now in Japan the recession is getting worse and unemployment [is] increasing.

records.definition_text: a list of foods and a set of instructions telling you how to cook something
records.learnerexamples_text: Do you know a good recipe for wholemeal bread?; For real South Asian food, just follow these recipes.; Actually I am going to bring with me some delicious recipes that you are going to be surprised [by].

records.definition_text: to think that something is probably true
records.learnerexamples_text: I reckon he's going to leave.; How much do you reckon it's going to cost?;  He reckons that he earns more in a week than I do in a month.; What do you reckon about the idea?

records.definition_text: to know someone or something because you have seen, heard or experienced them before
records.learnerexamples_text: I hadn't seen her for 20 years, but I recognized her immediately.;  I recognized her from her picture.; I recognised his voice.; Doctors are trained to recognise the symptoms of different diseases.; I still didn't recognise him and he said that he wanted to tell me something.

records.definition_text: to accept that something is legal, true or important
records.learnerexamples_text: She recognized that she had been partly to blame. ; The international community has refused to recognize the newly independent nation state.;  Smoking is recognised as a leading cause of lung cancer.; Martins hero-worshipped Lime until the moment when he was forced to recognize that his best friend was the worst racketeer imaginable.

records.definition_text: to advise someone that something should be done
records.learnerexamples_text: The report recommended that tourists avoid the region.; I recommend writing your feelings down on paper.; She has been recommended for promotion.; I recommend that you apply to work [at the festival] and you will have a great time!

records.definition_text: to say that someone or something is good or suitable for a particular purpose
records.learnerexamples_text: Can you recommend a good wine to go with this dish? ; Peter had recommended a restaurant to us.; I recommend the city of Porto Alegre.

records.definition_text: a suggestion that someone or something is good or suitable for a particular purpose
records.learnerexamples_text: I bought this book on Andy's recommendation.; The Chef's recommendation is Bulgogi made by beef.

records.definition_text: a piece of advice about what to do in a particular situation
records.learnerexamples_text: The report makes the recommendation that more prisons should be built.;  It's my recommendation that this factory be closed immediately.; I hope my recommendations are helpful, and I [hope] you have a great time!

records.definition_text: to write down information or store it on a computer so that it can be used in the future
records.learnerexamples_text: He recorded details of their conversation in his diary. ; Another way to [highlight] the importance of books is to consider them as the "depots" of wisdom and knowledge that exist and ha[ve] been recorded since the beginning of History.

records.definition_text: a song or music which has been recorded and which is available for the public to buy, or the plastic disk that the music is recorded on
records.learnerexamples_text: I like their new record.; My room is comfortable but a bit untidy around my stereo because in spite of [having] a lot of records and CDs, I don't have any shelf for them so this is why I'm going to buy a new shelf.

records.definition_text: the best, biggest, longest, tallest, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: He ran the 100 metres in 9.79 seconds and broke the world record.;  He holds the world record for 100 metres. ; She set a new European record in the high jump.; [In track and field] he has broken the [current] world record of the 100 met[re] distance!

records.definition_text: information that is written on paper or stored on computer so that it can be used in the future
records.learnerexamples_text: medical/dental records;  My teacher keeps a record of my absences.; This summer has been the hottest on record.; First of all, using [a] computer is most important for me because I can store my personal records such as [my] diary or expenses and I [can] send e-mail[s] to my friends who live abroad.

records.definition_text: a piece of music or a speech which has been recorded onto a disc, tape, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: I bought a recording of Maria Callas singing Verdi.; I've made some recordings for you to listen to.

records.definition_text: the process or business of putting sounds, especially music, onto a disc, magnetic tape, etc., using electronic equipment
records.learnerexamples_text: a recording studio; I loved to sing and I decided to visit all the recording companies.

records.definition_text: to become healthy or happy again after an illness, injury, or period of sadness
records.learnerexamples_text: It takes a long time to recover from surgery. ;  She never recovered from the death of her husband.; Dear Teacher, I'm sorry but I can't be [at] your next class because I'm recovering from [an illness] and my doctor said that I should stay home.

records.definition_text: If a system or situation recovers, it returns to the way it was before something bad happened.
records.learnerexamples_text: The economy was quick to recover after the election. ; Lots of effort ha[s] been put in and finally our economy [is] recover[ing].

records.definition_text: when you feel better or happier again after an illness, injury, or period of sadness
records.learnerexamples_text: She only had the operation last month but she's made a full recovery.; I was sorry to hear that you were ill, and my family and I send you our best wishes for a speedy recovery.

records.definition_text: activities that you do for enjoyment when you are not working
records.learnerexamples_text: Emma's only form of recreation seems to be shopping.;  a recreation area/centre; [Is] there any gym or other recreation facilities available in [the] Magnet Hotel?

records.definition_text: shaped like a rectangle
records.learnerexamples_text: a rectangular patch of grass; Between Rossio and the river there [is] a commercial district laid out in a rectangular pattern, where you can go shopping.

records.definition_text: to collect used paper, glass, plastic, etc., and put if through a process so that it can be used again
records.learnerexamples_text: We recycle all our newspapers and bottles.; The Japanese recycle more than half their waste paper.; I realised that it is very important to recycle.

records.definition_text: Recycled paper, glass, plastic, etc. has been used before and put through a process so that it can be used again.
records.learnerexamples_text: recycled paper/plastic; Using recycled glass and paper not only saves resources, but also a lot of energy.

records.definition_text: when paper, glass, plastic, etc. is put through a process so that it can be used again
records.learnerexamples_text: ways to encourage recycling; a recycling centre; In order to writ[e] this report, I interviewed 50 people in my town near the recycling centre and 50 people on the street.

records.definition_text: to make something less
records.learnerexamples_text: to reduce air pollution;  Prices have been reduced by almost 50 percent.;  The number of employees was reduced from 500 to 300.; Do nuclear weapons really reduce the risk of war?; It is a bit smal[l], but the price was reduced.

records.definition_text: when something is reduced
records.learnerexamples_text: a reduction in traffic; huge price reductions; As for the prices, they are reasonable and you can have a reduction if your group is over 16 pe[ople].

records.definition_text: having lost your job because your employer no longer needs you
records.learnerexamples_text: Half the workforce has been made redundant because of the decline in sales.; She had been made redundant and now, she has no job, no money, no friends and no home.

records.definition_text: a person who is in charge of a sports game and who makes certain that the rules are followed
records.learnerexamples_text: I think the referee made the wrong decision.; Due to my back injur[y], I could not train and play with my team, so it would be a good idea to be a referee.

records.definition_text: a name or book title, etc. in a book or other piece of writing that tells you where information came from
records.learnerexamples_text: There's the usual list of references at the back of the book.; I have information, and historical reference[s] [in] my collection, and I will be glad to share it with other members.

records.definition_text: a letter that is written by someone who knows you, to say if you are suitable for a job or course
records.learnerexamples_text: My old headteacher said he would write/give me a reference.; I am enclosing references from my ex-managers.

records.definition_text: to talk or write about someone or something, especially briefly
records.learnerexamples_text: She didn't once refer to her son.; He always referred to his father as 'the old man'.; In your book you refer to the 'Hotel Astrid' but they decided to close it last year.

records.definition_text: to show or be a sign of something
records.learnerexamples_text: The statistics reflect a change in people's spending habits.; The town's economic success is reflected in its shiny new buildings.; Your description of the people, their everyday life, their characters and their friendliness reflects that you really had an excellent time here.

records.definition_text: If a surface such as a mirror or water reflects something, you can see the image of that thing in the mirror, water, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: He saw himself reflected in the shop window.; We could see a little from the light coming from the moon that [was] reflected in a mirror.

records.definition_text: the image of something in a mirror, on a shiny surface, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: I saw my reflection in the window. ; Have you seen your reflection in a mirror?

records.definition_text: food and drinks that are available at a meeting, event, on a journey, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: Refreshments are available in the lobby.; During the show, we had some refreshments and popcorn.

records.definition_text: someone who has been forced to leave their country, especially because of a war
records.learnerexamples_text: a refugee camp; Thousands of refugees fled across the border.; This year I think I'd rather go to a refugee camp to organise a program for children.

records.definition_text: an amount of money that is given back to you, especially because you are not happy with something you have bought
records.learnerexamples_text: The holiday company apologized and gave us a full refund.; I am expecting a full refund and compensation for the discomfort I have suffered.

records.definition_text: to say that you will not do or accept something
records.learnerexamples_text: I asked him to leave but he refused.;  Cathy still refuses to admit that she was wrong. ; She asked me to lend her some money but I refused.; He's in trouble but he's refused all my offers of help.; We have a competition for the cyclists next Friday and I need to practi[s]e. Unfortunately, I've lost my bike and my Mum refuses to buy a new one.

records.definition_text: to get something back again
records.learnerexamples_text: The government has regained control of the capital.;  It was several hours before he regained consciousness. ; He regained his health in a month, and helped police to capture the loan gang.

records.definition_text: to think of someone or something in a particular way
records.learnerexamples_text: She is generally regarded as one of the greatest singers this century. ;  The plans were regarded with deep suspicion. ; Certainly, riding a bicycle is regarded as a healthy way of travel[l]ing and I do agree with it.

records.definition_text: about
records.learnerexamples_text: The company is being questioned regarding its employment policy.; I apologise to you for missing tomorrow's class as I have to attend a meeting regarding the field trip for our school with the Principal.

records.definition_text: greetings
records.learnerexamples_text: Kind/Best regards;  Give my regards to your mother. ; I hope this information help[s] you to make you[r] decision. Best regards,

records.definition_text: a particular area in a country or the world
records.learnerexamples_text: the semi-desert regions of Australia; the South-west region; The Northeast region is famous for its white sandy beaches which are frin[g]ed with coconut trees.

records.definition_text: relating to a particular area in a country or the world
records.learnerexamples_text: a regional accent/dialect; Among these events, you'll be able to visit the annual regional food festival, in which you'll enjoy some delicious meals [and] stupendous cakes.

records.definition_text: to put information about someone or something, especially a name, on an official list
records.learnerexamples_text: Students have to register for the new course by the end of April.;  Is he registered with the authorities to sell alcohol? ; I registered the car in my name.; I registered for [a] "green card" six months ago.

records.definition_text: when a name or information is recorded on an official list
records.learnerexamples_text: voter registration; We had to pay some money for the registration in the first lesson.

records.definition_text: to feel sorry about a situation, especially something that you wish you had not done
records.learnerexamples_text: If you don't tell her the truth you'll regret it later. ;  I really regret leaving school so young. ;  He began to regret that he hadn't paid more attention in class. ; Is there anything you've done in your life that you regret?; I'm glad to receive your letter and know about your intention to come to Brazil. I think you've made a nice choice and you won't regret it.

records.definition_text: used to say that you are sorry that you have to tell someone about a situation
records.learnerexamples_text: We regret to inform you that the application has been refused. ;  The council regrets that the money is no longer available. ; Dear editor, I regret to inform you about some untru[e] information which w[as] given in [the] last issue of your magazine.

records.definition_text: a feeling of sadness about a situation, often something that you wish you had not done
records.learnerexamples_text: I left school at 16, but I've had a great life and I have no regrets.; My only regret is that we didn't invite James.; The manager expressed regret at the number of staff reductions.;  It is with deep/great regret that I announce Steve Adam's resignation.; Anyway, it was too late for regrets.

records.definition_text: happening or doing something often, especially at the same time every week, year, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: a regular customer; It's recommended that you take regular exercise.; Violence is a regular occurrence in this part of the city.; His girlfriend is a regular member of that new club which I have joined.

records.definition_text: repeated with the same amount of time or space between one thing and the next
records.learnerexamples_text: I suggested that we meet on a regular basis.;  Plant the seedlings at regular intervals.; I'm willing to take care of your telescopes and to carry out [a] service on them at regular intervals so that they will work perfectly for many years.

records.definition_text: following the usual rules or patterns in grammar
records.learnerexamples_text: 'Talk' is a regular verb but 'go' is not.

records.definition_text: being a standard size
records.learnerexamples_text: a burger and regular fries

records.definition_text: at the same time each day, week, month, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: They meet regularly - usually once a week. ; I usually go out with my friends to buy a lot of clothes, regularly at weekends.

records.definition_text: often
records.learnerexamples_text: Accidents regularly occur on this bend.; I know I promised to write to you regularly but I just hadn't [a] spare minu[te] until now.

records.definition_text: an official rule that controls how something is done
records.learnerexamples_text: building/safety/traffic regulations; There are various rules and regulations governing the procedure.; I would like the government to impose strict rules and regulations on capturing animals.

records.definition_text: a time when all the people involved in a play, dance, etc. practise in order to prepare for a performance
records.learnerexamples_text: We only had one rehearsal before the show.; I helped to organise the rehearsals of the different group[s] who were going to play in the concert.

records.definition_text: to refuse to accept or agree with something
records.learnerexamples_text: The United States government rejected the proposal.; The appeal was rejected by the High Court.; The prime minister rejected the suggestion that it was time for him to resign.; [S]he rejected the proposal for a long, long time, [but] she finally married the Crown Prince 6 years ago.

records.definition_text: to not give someone the love or attention they were expecting
records.learnerexamples_text: She felt rejected by her husband.; "So you're Michael, the mis-understood artist, rejected by his family and friends," the man growled.

records.definition_text: to refuse to accept someone for a job, course, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: She applied to Cambridge University but was rejected. ; He applied for a job as a chef, but he was rejected.

records.definition_text: connected
records.learnerexamples_text: We discussed unemployment and related  issues.;  There's been an increase in criminal activity related to drugs.; It is also related to my research project.

records.definition_text: If people are related, they belong to the same family.
records.learnerexamples_text: Of course Elise and Linda are related to each other – they’re cousins.; We're related by marriage only.; Although they're related to each other, they have rather different characters.

records.definition_text: someone who belongs to the same family as you
records.learnerexamples_text: The funeral was attended by friends and relations.;  He's called Ken Russell, no relation to the film director.; I beg[a]n to play against my relations and friends but I soon found that I could [beat] them without any difficulty.

records.definition_text: a connection between two or more things
records.learnerexamples_text: The relation between smoking and lung cancer is well established. ; Another drawback is the relation between space and time.

records.definition_text: the way in which two people or groups of people feel and behave towards each other
records.learnerexamples_text: Relations between the couple are said to be strained.; Britain enjoys friendly relations with Canada.; The second [film] is 'Alice' directed by the world's most respected man within the movie bu[si]ness - of course Woody Allen. Again the good old fellow is totally fascinated by people in general, human relations and reactions.

records.definition_text: the way two people or groups feel about and behave towards each other
records.learnerexamples_text: He has a very good relationship with his father.; Then we studied some phrasal verbs and I was supposed to read a text about feelings and relationships.

records.definition_text: a sexual or romantic friendship
records.learnerexamples_text: Have you had any serious relationships in the past year?;  Are you in a relationship at the moment? ; He told me that he hope[s] that someday we could have a boyfriend-girlfriend relationship for real.

records.definition_text: the way in which two things are connected
records.learnerexamples_text: the relationship between sunburn and skin cancer; The relationship between mind and body has been proved by scientists.

records.definition_text: a member of your family
records.learnerexamples_text: There was a party for friends and relatives.; I haven't got many blood relatives.; All her close/distant relatives came to the wedding.; After that there'll be a big party with all your relatives and friends.

records.definition_text: quite good/bad/cheap, etc. when compared to other similar things
records.learnerexamples_text: Eating out is relatively cheap.;  Students will find the course relatively easy.; First of all, the most favo[u]rable time for me to travel is July, because I am in the final year of University, so I have to attend classes for a thesis almost throughout the year apart from July, when I can take a relatively long summer holiday.

records.definition_text: to become happy and comfortable because nothing is worrying you, or to make someone do this
records.learnerexamples_text: I find it difficult to relax.; After work I relax with a cup of tea and the newspaper.;  The wine had relaxed him and he began to talk.; If you want to relax, Buenos Aires is near a lot of beautiful beaches.

records.definition_text: the feeling of being relaxed
records.learnerexamples_text: He plays the piano for relaxation.; Last week I decided [to] paint it in baby blue, you know I love that colour, in fact somebody told me it was very good for relaxation.

records.definition_text: feeling happy and calm because nothing is worrying you
records.learnerexamples_text: She looked relaxed and happy walking along with her two boys.; He seemed perfectly relaxed and in control of the situation.; It makes me more relaxed.

records.definition_text: A relaxed situation or place is comfortable and informal.
records.learnerexamples_text: There was a very relaxed atmosphere at the party. ; I love this place because [it] has a relaxed atmosp[h]ere and all the staff [are] very friendly.

records.definition_text: making you feel relaxed
records.learnerexamples_text: a relaxing bath; Yoga is a very relaxing activity but not boring at all!

records.definition_text: to make a record or film available for people to buy or see
records.learnerexamples_text: The band's latest album will be released next week.; He has recently released a new CD on which he spent a lot of time and real[l]y made an effort.

records.definition_text: to allow a prisoner to be free
records.learnerexamples_text: Six hostages were released shortly before midday. ; He was released from prison last week.; It all began when I was released from jail, after a two year conviction [for] jewel theft.

records.definition_text: a musical recording which is made available for the public to buy
records.learnerexamples_text: Her latest release, a song about doomed love, she wrote herself.; [This department store] provide[s] the latest cds and dvds, so you are always up to date and never miss new releases.

records.definition_text: related or useful to what is happening or being talked about
records.learnerexamples_text: relevant information;  Education should be relevant to children's needs. ; I had studied psychology but I couldn't find a job relevant to my studies.

records.definition_text: able to be trusted or believed
records.learnerexamples_text: a reliable car; reliable information; Gideon is very reliable - if he says he'll do something, he'll do it.; I got a lot of prizes in school, so I consider myself a hardworking and reliable person.

records.definition_text: the good feeling that you have when something unpleasant stops or does not happen
records.learnerexamples_text: It'll be such a relief when these exams are over. ;  "James can come tonight." "Well, that's a relief!" ; I felt such a sense of relief when we finished the project.; She heard a[n] ambulance siren [in] the distance and with a sigh of relief, she lost consciousness.

records.definition_text: happy that something unpleasant has not happened or has ended

records.learnerexamples_text: He cracked a rib in the accident.; I stayed there for 2 weeks with a broken leg, sore ribs and a couple of scars.

records.definition_text: Rich food has a lot of fat, oil or eggs in it.
records.learnerexamples_text: a rich sauce; The cooking [is] bas[ed] on traditional recipes of Westfalian origin and it is tasty but often very rich!

records.definition_text: containing a lot of something that is important or valuable
records.learnerexamples_text: The region is rich in minerals and coal deposits.;  Both foods are rich in Vitamin C.; The country has vast oil reserves and rich deposits of other minerals.; Their lessons are valuable, rich in knowledge and fun[n]y.

records.definition_text: a journey riding a bicycle, motorcycle, or horse
records.learnerexamples_text: He's gone out for a ride on his bike.; Do you want to come for a ride on my motorbike?; I swam in the sea, sunba[th]ed on the golden beach and had a ride on [a] scooter.

records.definition_text: a journey in a vehicle or train
records.learnerexamples_text: It's a short bus ride to the airport.;  Can I give you a ride to the station? ; He asked me for a ride into town.; On the next day, I went swimming in the lake early in the morning and took a bus ride home after that.

records.definition_text: a machine at a fair which moves people up and down, round in circles, etc as they sit in it
records.learnerexamples_text: She wanted me to go on a ride with her.; I really enjoyed myself a lot. Although I was scared on the rides, in my op[i]nion that funfair we visited was fantastic!

records.definition_text: someone who rides a horse, bicycle, or motorcycle
records.learnerexamples_text: One of the riders was thrown off his horse.; A lot of good riders will come with their horses to take p[art] in a competition.

records.definition_text: very silly
records.learnerexamples_text: I've never heard anything so ridiculous.; I'd look ridiculous in a hat like that.;  It's a ridiculous idea/suggestion.; So, it is just ridiculous to hear that there were fewer than 2000 people there.

records.definition_text: fair or morally acceptable
records.learnerexamples_text: It's not right to criticize him behind his back.; Someone had to tell him - I think you did the right thing.; Was he doing the right thing or he was just making matters worse?

records.definition_text: suitable or best in a particular situation
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm not sure she's the right person for the job. ;  Are we going in the right direction? ; I know that you will make the right choice!

records.definition_text: exactly in a place or time
records.learnerexamples_text: He's right here with me.; I fell asleep right in the middle of her speech.; They live right in the centre of the city.; That's me, right here.

records.definition_text: correctly
records.learnerexamples_text: He guessed right most of the time.

records.definition_text: something that the law allows you to do
records.learnerexamples_text: the right to free speech ;  the right to vote; To sum up, famous people are the same as we are, and we all have the right to lead a private life and no right to break into their privacy.

records.definition_text: morally correct behaviour
records.learnerexamples_text: I've tried to teach them the difference between right and wrong. ; He was raised not knowing the difference between right and wrong.

records.definition_text: immediately
records.learnerexamples_text: Do you want to start right away?; I [would] love to see your new trousers but I'm busy right now.

records.definition_text: in a correct way
records.learnerexamples_text: He is rightly concerned about the situation.; They quite rightly complained to the manager.; If I remember rightly, there were over 5,000.

records.definition_text: something that is the shape of a circle
records.learnerexamples_text: The children sat in a ring around the teacher.; It is forced to jump into a ring of fire, if it does not want to do it, it will be hit.

records.definition_text: the sound a bell makes
records.learnerexamples_text: The ring of the doorbell woke him up.; Walking down the street, he heard a noise: just the ring of the clock tower.

records.definition_text: If something rings, it makes the sound of a bell, and if you ring a bell, you cause it to make a sound.
records.learnerexamples_text: The phone's ringing. ;  I rang the doorbell. ; Me and a few of my friends were having a day off school so we went to a lovely beach by the Danube river, when my phone rang.

records.definition_text: to telephone someone who rang you earlier or to telephone someone for a second time
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm a bit busy - can I ring you back later?; However, I'll ring back to [get more] information.

records.definition_text: to telephone someone
records.searchterms_text: ring;ring (sb) up or ring up (sb);ring sb up or ring up sb
records.learnerexamples_text: Ring Paul up and ask what he's doing tonight.; Whenever I ring up it's always Bill who answers.; Maybe I could ring up one of my friends and c[atch] up [on] the work I will miss.

records.definition_text: to tear quickly and suddenly, or to tear something quickly and suddenly
records.learnerexamples_text: His new trousers ripped when he bent down.;  She ripped her dress getting off her bike. ;  He excitedly ripped open the parcel.; While I was walking I step[p]ed on my dress and ripped it.

records.definition_text: developed enough and ready to be eaten
records.learnerexamples_text: ripe fruit; Those bananas aren't ripe yet - they're still green.; There w[ere] a lot of beautiful, ripe, red strawberries [and] I couldn't resist pick[ing] one of them.

records.definition_text: to move up
records.learnerexamples_text: The balloon rose gently up into the air.

records.definition_text: When the sun or moon rises, it appears in the sky.
records.learnerexamples_text: The sun rises in the East. ; It was very beautiful, especially in the morning when the sun was rising.

records.definition_text: to increase in level
records.learnerexamples_text: rising temperatures ;  Prices rose by 10 percent. ; Inflation is rising by 2.1% a month.; Also, due to global warming, sea levels might rise and [the] risk of flooding will also rise.

records.definition_text: an increase in the level of something
records.learnerexamples_text: a sudden temperature rise; a 5% rise in inflation; August has seen a large rise in the number of unemployed.; There is also a steady rise in underweight [girls] among young girls of today.

records.definition_text: the possibility of something bad happening
records.learnerexamples_text: the risk of heart disease ;  There is a slight risk that the blood could have become infected. ; We want clean rivers and lakes, where you can swim without risk to your health.; It's a low/high-risk strategy.; Nowadays, everything is a risk, even at home we are in danger.

records.definition_text: If you risk something bad, you do something although that bad thing might happen.
records.learnerexamples_text: "It's dangerous to cross here." "I'll just have to risk it."; You shouldn't risk damaging your health.

records.definition_text: If you risk something important, you cause it to be in a dangerous situation where you might lose it.
records.learnerexamples_text: He risked his life to save me. ; She risked her job by giving me that information.; If she had gone home by taxi, she would have not risked her life.

records.definition_text: dangerous because something bad might happen
records.learnerexamples_text: It's risky to buy a car without some good advice.;  Investing in shares is always a risky business.; [Cycling on] this road is a bit risky and demanding so I would agree with Chris [o]n that point.

records.definition_text: to steal from someone or somewhere, often using violence
records.learnerexamples_text: to rob a bank ;  Two tourists were robbed at gunpoint in the city centre last night. ; They robbed the company of £2 million.; About twenty tourists were robbed.

records.definition_text: the crime of stealing from somewhere or someone
records.learnerexamples_text: a bank robbery; The gang admitted they had committed four recent robberies.; He is in prison for armed robbery.; We were fed up with our lives and all the problems we had [so] one of us decided to organize a bank robbery. [At] first we laughed at him because it was such a silly idea but finally it was the only solution for us to become rich.

records.definition_text: a machine controlled by a computer, which can move and do other things that people can do
records.learnerexamples_text: They use robots to spray the cars.; I think there will be tall buildings and [the] population will rise a lot. I think there will be robots too.

records.definition_text: the hard, natural substance which forms part of the Earth's surface, or an area of this substance sticking out of the sea or ground
records.learnerexamples_text: a layer of rock; Mountains and cliffs are formed from rock.; The boat struck a rock outside the bay and sank.; We climbed over the rocks and reached the sea.; There are many wonderful hills, mountains, lakes, caves and rocks.

records.definition_text: a tube-shaped device containing fuel and an engine that pushes a vehicle into space
records.learnerexamples_text: They launched a rocket yesterday.; [With] computers, you can control machines [or] a rocket [or] a satellite.

records.definition_text: an actor's part in a film or play
records.learnerexamples_text: She's got a leading/supporting role in the school play.; He plays the role of a violent criminal.; Jack Nicholson, my favourite actor, plays the main role.

records.definition_text: the job someone or something has in a particular situation
records.learnerexamples_text: What is his role in this project?;  This part of the brain plays an important role in learning. ; Six people have been put on trial for their role in the demonstrations.; In fact, computers play an important role in the office.

records.definition_text: to turn something around itself to make the shape of a ball or tube
records.learnerexamples_text: He was rolling a cigarette.; He rolled the clay into a ball in his hands.; As I got closer, the hedgehog rolled itself up into a ball.

records.definition_text: a small loaf of bread for one person
records.learnerexamples_text: I had a roll with my soup.; We eat ham, cheese, butter and paprika, with [a] roll or bread.

records.definition_text: a piece of film, paper or cloth that is rolled into the shape of a tube
records.learnerexamples_text: a roll of carpet; a toilet roll

records.definition_text: to move somewhere smoothly
records.learnerexamples_text: Tears rolled down her face. ;  His car started rolling down the drive. ; By this time, the rest of us were laughing so [hard that] tears were rolling down our cheeks.

records.definition_text: to move somewhere by turning in a circular direction, or to make something move this way
records.searchterms_text: roll;roll (sth) across/around/over, etc.;roll sth across/around/over etc;roll sth across/around/over, etc.;rolled;rolling;rolls
records.learnerexamples_text: The ball rolled through the goalkeeper's legs.;  She rolled over onto her side. ; The vase rolled off the edge of the table and smashed.

records.definition_text: an exciting relationship of love between two people, often a short one
records.learnerexamples_text: It was just a holiday romance.;  Office romances are usually a bad idea.; I like it very much because it has romance and action, and cats of cours[e].

records.definition_text: relating to feelings of love and affection
records.learnerexamples_text: a romantic dinner for two; And the atmosphere in the evening is so romantic!

records.definition_text: relating to a story about love
records.learnerexamples_text: romantic fiction;  a romantic comedy; It was interesting but romantic novels are my favourite books!

records.definition_text: space for things to fit into
records.learnerexamples_text: Is there enough room for me in the car?; That sofa would take up too much room in the flat.; James took the books off the little table to make room for the television.; In the wardrobe there is no[t] enough room to put all my stuff away.

records.definition_text: someone who you share a room, apartment, etc. with
records.learnerexamples_text: He was my roommate while we were at college. ; I was a student and lived together in a flat with my roommate Claudia.

records.definition_text: the part of a plant that grows under the ground and gets water and food from the soil
records.learnerexamples_text: These plants have really deep roots.; I have gathered over three hundred species: flowers, roots, leaves and others.

records.definition_text: where someone or something originally comes from
records.learnerexamples_text: the roots of modern jazz; I think people should know where our European pop and rock music has its roots.

records.definition_text: very thick string made from twisted thread
records.learnerexamples_text: We tied the boat to a post with a length of rope.; a coil of rope; A few moments later she took out a rope from her backpack.

records.definition_text: a flower with a pleasant smell and thorns, that grows on a bush
records.learnerexamples_text: a rose bush; She sent him a bunch of red roses.; He brought me to a posh restaurant and he gave me a bunch of roses.

records.definition_text: Rotten vegetable or animal substances are decaying.
records.learnerexamples_text: rotten eggs/fruit; I'll tell you something - my freezer still smells of rotten fish.

records.definition_text: A rough surface is not smooth.
records.learnerexamples_text: rough ground; It was a rough mountain road, covered in stones and huge holes.; I went with some people I kn[ew] from bike competitions, and I [was] impressed with how well they can ride a bike on a rough terrain, w[hereas] I had to go carefully in some tracks.

records.definition_text: approximate and not exact
records.learnerexamples_text: Write a rough copy first and check the grammar.;  Can you give me a rough idea of the numbers? ; I lost my personal note-pad where I used to write all my job tasks, my arrangements and the records of my students. I have [even] written the rough copy of some personal letters [there].

records.definition_text: difficult or unpleasant
records.learnerexamples_text: She's having a rough time at work. ; He did the mountain-route last year and he says that even he had a rough time.

records.definition_text: If the sea or weather is rough, there is a lot of strong wind and sometimes rain.
records.learnerexamples_text: The boat sank in rough seas off the Swedish coast. ; I went to the seaside but I was not allowed to bathe for they said that the sea was too rough.

records.definition_text: approximately
records.learnerexamples_text: There has been an increase of roughly 2.25 million.; Roughly speaking, it's 2.25 million.; We have roughly the same tastes.; These are very special cases and roughly speaking, confined to one thing.

records.definition_text: to or in different parts of a place
records.learnerexamples_text: The landlord showed me round the house.; I had to go all round town to find a hotel that was open.; Well, she showed me round her hometown and we did some sight-seeing.

records.definition_text: with a circular movement
records.learnerexamples_text: This switch makes the wheels go round.

records.definition_text: to the opposite direction
records.learnerexamples_text: She looked round. ;  Turn the car round and let's go home. ; I turned round and I saw that the one who was calling me was the singer!!

records.definition_text: from one place or person to another
records.learnerexamples_text: Could you pass these forms round, please?

records.definition_text: moving in a circle without stopping
records.learnerexamples_text: We drove round and round trying to find the hotel.; It's not fun to look at an animal who is bored and only walks round and round.

records.definition_text: the roads or paths you follow to get from one place to another place
records.learnerexamples_text: an escape route; I'm just planning my route.; What's the best route to the station?;  Crowds gathered all along the route to watch the race.; Each cycle route [is] shown in a different colour, so we didn't lose our way.

records.definition_text: the things you regularly do and how and when you do them
records.learnerexamples_text: a daily routine;  He longed to escape the routine of an office job.; There's no set/fixed routine at work - every day is different.; Usually we speak about our daily routine, [and] our plan[s] for the future.

records.definition_text: a straight line of people or things
records.learnerexamples_text: a row of chairs/houses;  My students sit at desks in rows for most of the time.; Two rows of serv[a]nts stood beside the path which was in front of him with [a] red carpet on it.

records.definition_text: a line of seats
records.learnerexamples_text: to sit on the back/front row ;  Isn't that Sophie sitting in the row behind us? ; It is great in my class, there are so many people and they are all nice. I'm sitting in the first row next to Nicole.

records.definition_text: to move a boat or move someone in a boat through the water using oars
records.learnerexamples_text: We rowed to the other side of the lake.; In the end, they had to row all the way back to the beach and it was very late when they got home.

records.definition_text: a loud, angry argument
records.learnerexamples_text: My parents often have rows.;  a blazing row; The sun was shining, the birds w[ere] singing and all the people were happy, but I was very angry because I [had] had a row with my husband.

records.definition_text: relating to a queen or king and their family
records.learnerexamples_text: the royal family; a royal visit; Chris, Anne and I wanted to visit the royal palace.

records.definition_text: to press your hand or a cloth on a surface and move it backwards and forwards
records.learnerexamples_text: She rubbed her hands together to warm them. ;  He rubbed himself dry with a towel. ;  Rub the stain with a damp cloth. ; Paul suddenly saw something. A kind of shadow. He rubbed his eyes but there was nothing.

records.definition_text: a strong material that bends easily, originally produced from the juice of a tropical tree, and used to make tyres, boots, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: shoes with rubber soles; Worst [of] all it seems to me is the way some zoos are regarded as places of entertainment like [a] circus, where the people are encouraged to laugh at animals whe[n] they 'perform their funny tricks' like eating bananas, swinging from rubber tyres and so on.

records.definition_text: things that you throw away because you do not want them
records.learnerexamples_text: Our rubbish gets collected on Thursdays.; Put the empty box in the rubbish bin.; I took some old furniture to the rubbish dump.; While I [was] walking in the rain along the dark and quiet alleys, I heard a weak cry that sound[ed] like a baby [coming] from a corner with rubbish scattered everywhere.

records.definition_text: something that is of bad quality
records.learnerexamples_text: There's so much rubbish on TV. ; I was t[aught] to believe that recorded music was rubbish compar[ed] to live music.

records.base_text: rub out sth or rub sth out
records.definition_text: to remove writing from something by rubbing it with a piece of rubber or with a cloth
records.searchterms_text: rub;rub out sth or rub sth out
records.learnerexamples_text: If your line isn't straight, rub it out and start again.; Moreover, all the bad words written on the building's walls should be rubbed out.

records.definition_text: to move a substance backwards and forwards over a surface so that it covers it and goes into it
records.searchterms_text: -bb-;bb;rub;rub sth into/on etc;rub sth into/on, etc.;rubbed;rubbing;rubs
records.learnerexamples_text: I rubbed some suntan oil on her back. ;  Rub the butter into the flour.

records.definition_text: behaving in a way which is not polite and upsets other people
records.learnerexamples_text: a rude comment/remark;  He complained that a member of staff had been rude to him.;  It would be rude to leave without saying goodbye. ; I thought he [wa]s such a rude man.

records.definition_text: Rude words or jokes relate to sex or going to the toilet.
records.learnerexamples_text: He taught his little sister a lot of rude words.; She just wanted to shout rude words when finally she recognised her father... standing in front of her.

records.definition_text: a soft piece of material used to cover the floor
records.learnerexamples_text: My dog loves lying on the rug in front of the fire.; There is [a] green rug in the middle of the floor.

records.definition_text: the broken parts that are left from an old building after it has been destroyed
records.learnerexamples_text: Thousands of tourists wander around these ancient ruins every year.; After that I'm going to travel to Luxor and see [the] ruins.

records.definition_text: to spoil or destroy something completely
records.learnerexamples_text: They were late and the dinner was ruined.; Her injury ruined her chances of winning the race.; Huge modern hotels have ruined this once unspoilt coastline.; But she didn't keep her promise and she ruined my life.

records.definition_text: an official instruction about what you must or must not do
records.learnerexamples_text: to break the rules;  to obey/follow the rules;  You can't smoke at school, it's against the rules.; There're plenty of rules in my high school.

records.definition_text: a principle of a system, such as a language or science
records.learnerexamples_text: the rules of grammar; We did a little exam about tenses and grammar rules.

records.definition_text: the usual way something is
records.learnerexamples_text: an exception to the rule; I visit my parents on Sunday, as a rule.; As a rule, children who ride bikes change their bike[s] for cars [when they are older] and are pre[pa]red a little [for] how to behave on the road.

records.definition_text: to influence someone's thoughts or actions
records.learnerexamples_text: His life is ruled by the demands of his job.; Our Earth has grown overcrowded and every inch of our life is ruled by computers.

records.definition_text: to be in control of somewhere, usually a country
records.learnerexamples_text: They were ruled for many years by a dictator.; In the late 60s when Greece was ruled by a military government, many young students fled abroad to escape its cruelty.

records.definition_text: a fact that a lot of people are talking about although they do not know if it is true
records.learnerexamples_text: Rumours are going round the school about Mr Mason and his assistant.; Someone has been spreading rumours about me.;  I heard a rumour that you were leaving.; However, the press shouldn't create rumours and hunt those people like animals.

records.definition_text: to organize or control something
records.learnerexamples_text: She ran her own restaurant for five years. ; The social group is run by the residents themselves.; My aunt is always working. She runs her own business.

records.definition_text: If liquid runs somewhere, it flows.
records.learnerexamples_text: Tears ran down her face. ;  Have you got a tissue? My nose is running. ; The warm urine ran through my underwear, [down] my legs and white socks, into my shoes and floated out on the floor.

records.definition_text: If trains or buses are running, they are available to travel on.
records.learnerexamples_text: Trains are still running, despite the snow.; A bus runs three times a day into town.; Buses are running an hour late, because of an earlier accident.; There is an easy way to get to the college: a service bus runs every 15 minutes, [and] the journey takes only 20 minutes.

records.definition_text: If you run a computer program, you use it on your computer.
records.learnerexamples_text: Did you run a virus check this morning? ; At this point the computer is unable to run any program.

records.definition_text: when you move on your feet at a speed faster than walking, especially for exercise
records.learnerexamples_text: We go for/do a three-mile run every evening after work.; If you set off at a run, you'll be exhausted later.; Walking is recognized [as] good exercise, or going for a run.

records.definition_text: in cricket or baseball, a single point
records.learnerexamples_text: to score a run; I liked the competition because both the teams played well and they scored good runs

records.definition_text: to secretly leave a place because you are unhappy there
records.learnerexamples_text: She ran away from home at the age of 13.; At the age of fourteen, she ran away from home.

records.definition_text: to meet someone that you know when you did not expect to meet them
records.learnerexamples_text: I ran into Harry on the train.; We ran into an old friend of mine and we decided to have a coffee together.
