records.definition_text: to accidentally hit something while you are driving a vehicle
records.learnerexamples_text: He lost control of the car and ran into a tree.; I had tried to stop my car next to the road but I ran into a signpost.

records.definition_text: to finish, use or sell all of something, so that there is none left
records.learnerexamples_text: I've run out of money/ideas/patience.; "Have you got any milk?" - "Sorry, I've run out."; Well, I have run out of time, so I have to stop writing.

records.definition_text: If a supply of something runs out, all of it has been used or it is completely finished.
records.learnerexamples_text: The milk has run out.; My patience is beginning to run out.; In addition, if you are at home and something you need has run out or broken, you can go to buy it at any time.

records.base_text: run over sb/sth or run sb/sth over
records.definition_text: to hit someone or something with a vehicle and drive over them, injuring or killing them
records.searchterms_text: run;run over sb/sth or run sb/sth over
records.learnerexamples_text: He was run over by a bus.; After a while, his father vanished and a car ran over John and killed him.

records.definition_text: relating to the countryside and not to towns
records.learnerexamples_text: The area is still very rural and undeveloped.; I live in a rural area far from any village, town, or city.

records.definition_text: to hurry or move quickly somewhere, or to make someone or something hurry or move quickly somewhere
records.learnerexamples_text: We had to rush to catch the bus.;  We rushed out into the street to see what all the noise was.;  The UN has rushed medical supplies to the disaster area.; I rushed to Tom's house, and when I reached it, he received me with a weird smile on his face.

records.definition_text: when you have to hurry or move somewhere quickly
records.learnerexamples_text: Slow down! What's the rush?; Why is it always such a rush to get ready in the mornings?; Everyone seemed to be in a rush.; He was in a rush to get home.; That's because we are always stressed and always in a rush.

records.definition_text: the time when a lot of people are travelling to or from work and so roads and trains are very busy
records.learnerexamples_text: the morning/evening rush hour; I always try to travel outside the rush hours.; During rush hours, you often see cars lined up with just one person inside, each car polluting the environment.

records.definition_text: to do something quickly and enthusiastically
records.learnerexamples_text: His friends rushed to congratulate him after the ceremony.; I was very happy and rushed to talk to them.

records.definition_text: If a skill you had is now rusty, it is no longer good because you have forgotten it.
records.learnerexamples_text: My French is a bit rusty.; However, I am rather "rusty" [at] using the morse code as well as using the codes of communication.

records.definition_text: Rusty metal has rust on its surface.
records.learnerexamples_text: a rusty car/nail; It was very rusty but I repainted it and now it looks like a new bike.

records.definition_text: to tell someone to leave their job, usually because they have done something wrong
records.learnerexamples_text: They sacked her for being late.; He got sacked from his last job.; What's more, I was sacked from my workplace.

records.definition_text: in an unhappy way
records.learnerexamples_text: "He's gone away for six months," she said sadly.; Alice quickly got in the car and waved sadly at her parents while Natalie drove off.

records.definition_text: in a way that is not satisfactory
records.learnerexamples_text: Sadly, the treatment doesn't work for all patients.; If you think she'll let you do that, you're sadly mistaken.; Some forms of entertainment which were popular decades ago have, sadly, disappeared.

records.definition_text: being sad
records.learnerexamples_text: Her sadness at her grandfather's death was obvious.; What can be more real that when your lover is gone or taken away, your own soul is also alone, bitter and dark and there is nothing else than feelings of rev[e]nge, anger, frustration and sadness?

records.definition_text: not harmed or damaged
records.learnerexamples_text: She said that all the hostages were safe.; Suddenly I felt something strange near me, I turn[ed] back quickly and two men were there. They showed me their weapons. Then, I woke up safe in my bed.

records.definition_text: in a safe way
records.learnerexamples_text: We all arrived safely.; Drive safely!; Are the children safely fastened into their car seats?; I think we can safely say they won't find us now.; My friend has come back safely and now a new life [starts for him].

records.definition_text: the state of being safe, or a place or situation where someone or something is safe
records.learnerexamples_text: food/road safety; The hostages were led to safety.;  For your (comfort and) safety, we recommend you keep your seat belt loosely fastened during the flight.; Journalists may enter the danger zone but unfortunately we cannot guarantee their safety.; As the gunman opened fire, they all ran/dived for safety behind trees.

records.definition_text: to control a boat that has no engine and is pushed by the wind
records.learnerexamples_text: He sailed the dinghy up the river.; She sailed around the world single-handed in her yacht.; First of all, we are going to the beach where some sail[o]rs are going to teach us how to sail.

records.definition_text: to travel somewhere on a boat or a ship
records.learnerexamples_text: We sailed to New York.; You know, I've got a boat and if you want, we will be able to spend five days on it. We will sail to the Channel Islands (Jersey, Guernsey, Sark...) .

records.definition_text: When a boat or a ship sails, it travels on the water.
records.learnerexamples_text: The ship was sailing to China.; The boat sailed along/down the coast.; As the battleship sailed by/past, everyone on deck waved.; I started the film and we could all see a ship sailing towards the camera.

records.definition_text: someone who sails ships or boats as their job or as a sport
records.learnerexamples_text: Over 100 sailors took part in the race.; He is a sailor.

records.definition_text: a fixed amount of money that you receive from your employer, usually every month
records.learnerexamples_text: an annual salary of £20 000; His net monthly salary is £1500.; She's on quite a good/decent salary in her present job.; He took a drop in salary when he changed jobs.; a 10% salary increase

records.definition_text: the act of selling something, or the time when something is sold
records.learnerexamples_text: The sale of alcohol is now banned.; The building company gets 10% commission on each house sale.; I haven't made a sale all morning.; We had arranged to meet him at the Ritz restaurant in order to deal [with] the sale of some products.

records.definition_text: the number of items sold
records.learnerexamples_text: Our sales have doubled this year.; You should know that they are getting a marked increase in sales.

records.definition_text: someone whose job is selling things
records.learnerexamples_text: I asked the salesman for advice. ; Sad to say, I have not applied for it again but I did apply for another job as a salesman.

records.definition_text: someone whose job is selling things
records.learnerexamples_text: The saleswoman showed me the car.; Many years ago, when I was seventeen, I was working as a saleswoman [for] a print[er].

records.definition_text: a large, silver fish, or the pink meat of this fish
records.learnerexamples_text: fresh/smoked/tinned salmon; salmon fishing; My favo[u]rite restaurant is Pampa Grill. My favo[u]rite food [there] is the salmon, it's delicious.

records.definition_text: a place where women have their hair cut and put in a style
records.learnerexamples_text: My hairdresser opened her own salon.; I had an appointment at my hairdresser's and late as usual I parked outside the salon on a narrow dead-end-street where it was forbidden to park.

records.definition_text: tasting of or containing salt
records.learnerexamples_text: Is the soup too salty?; On the other hand, [the] Western one gave [good] service but [the] food was oily and salty.

records.definition_text: a small number of people from a larger group that is being tested or considered
records.learnerexamples_text: a random sample of voters; a nationally representative sample of 200 schools; This report is based on a sample of over 50 students.

records.definition_text: a small amount of something that shows you what it is like
records.learnerexamples_text: a free sample of chocolate; She brought in some samples of her work.; samples of carpet/curtain material

records.definition_text: a substance that is found on beaches and in deserts, which is made from very small grains of rock
records.learnerexamples_text: a grain of sand; The children played all day in/on the sand.; coarse/fine sand; We got to a bea[uti]ful beach. The sand looked like gold.

records.definition_text: a light shoe with straps that you wear in warm weather
records.learnerexamples_text: a pair of sandals; In summer, I wear skirts and sandals.

records.definition_text: covered with or containing sand
records.learnerexamples_text: a sandy beach ; We have no mountains in Lithuania, but we have sandy beaches at [the] seaside.

records.definition_text: a piece of equipment that is sent into space around the Earth to receive and send signals or to collect information
records.learnerexamples_text: The World Cup was transmitted around the world by satellite.; satellite television/TV; a TV/weather satellite; To balance this, technology has developed a lot in the last decades and now people can have wild animal[s] inside their homes, [even though] they may be locked up on a CD-Rom or coming in a wave format through the satellite dish.

records.definition_text: a pleasant feeling which you get when you receive something you wanted, or when you have done something you wanted to do
records.learnerexamples_text: She looked at the finished painting with satisfaction.; She got/obtained great satisfaction from/out of helping other people.; For me, job satisfaction is more important than the money.; She had the satisfaction of knowing that she'd done everything she could.; Whatever it [is], it must give us satisfaction.

records.definition_text: good enough
records.learnerexamples_text: We hope very much to find a satisfactory  solution to the problem.; The teachers seem to think his work is satisfactory.; The service is satisfactory.

records.definition_text: pleased because you have got what you wanted, or because something has happened in the way that you wanted
records.learnerexamples_text: Some people are never satisfied!; a satisfied smile; Are you satisfied with the new arrangement?; I must say that I'm very satisfied with [the club].

records.definition_text: to please someone by giving them what they want or need
records.learnerexamples_text: They have 31 flavours of ice-cream - enough to satisfy everyone!; Come on, satisfy my curiosity, what happened last night?; But how can anyone satisfy a wealthy woman like her without giving her an expensive present?

records.definition_text: a deep, metal pan, usually with a long handle and a lid, that is used to cook food in
records.learnerexamples_text: Put the potatoes in a saucepan of boiling water.; The waiters are very polite and the food is so good, specially the fish. You can can see the [chef] with his saucepan, it's very funny!

records.definition_text: a small plate that you put under a cup
records.learnerexamples_text: a cup and saucer; She gave the cat a saucer of milk.

records.definition_text: to stop someone or something from being killed, injured or destroyed
records.learnerexamples_text: Wearing seat belts has saved many lives.; He fell in the river but his friend saved him from drowning.; He had to borrow money to save his business.; He was desperately trying to save their failing marriage.; We all need to do our bit to save the planet.

records.definition_text: to prevent time, money or effort being wasted or spent
records.learnerexamples_text: You'll save time if you take the car.; Thanks for your help - it saved me a lot of work.; More and more people choose to travel by car, because it saves a lot of time comp[ared] to travelling by public transport.

records.definition_text: to prevent a player from scoring a goal
records.learnerexamples_text: He saved two goals in the last minute of the game.

records.definition_text: the money which you keep in an account in a bank or similar financial organization
records.learnerexamples_text: He spent all his savings on an expensive car.; I also spent all my savings [o]n executive-looking clothes.

records.definition_text: to tell someone about a fact, thought, or opinion
records.learnerexamples_text: Did she say where she was going?; Officials refused to say what had happened.; What did they say about the house?; The doctors say (that) it will take him a few weeks to recover.; She didn't say whether she was coming or not.

records.definition_text: to give information in writing, numbers or signs
records.learnerexamples_text: My watch says 3 o'clock.; Can you read what that notice says?; It says in the paper (that) they've found the man who did it.; It says on the bottle to take three tablets a day.; Well yesterday I was reading a new fashion magazine. It says that this summer the best clothes to wear are skirts with different colours!

records.definition_text: to think or believe
records.learnerexamples_text: People/They say (that) he's over 100.; "It's going to be a very hot summer." "So they say."; She is a firm leader, too firm, some might say.; People say that it never rains here.

records.definition_text: when someone can decide something
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't mind what we do - it's your call.; This is my opinon, but it is your call, talk to your parents.

records.definition_text: If something bad that has happened is someone's fault, they are responsible for it.
records.learnerexamples_text: She believes it was the doctor's fault that Peter died.; It's not my fault she didn't come!; "It's my fault" I said and he answered "Never mind, it's all ok".

records.definition_text: the money which a person, company or country has
records.learnerexamples_text: We keep a tight control on the organization's finances.; She needs to sort out her finances.; First of all, we should budget our finances better.

records.definition_text: all of the things that someone has done in their life
records.learnerexamples_text: I knew nothing about his past. ; After the film, we went to a restaurant called Adriano, and as the weather was cool, we had a glass of wine and started asking [about] each other's past.

records.definition_text: the possibility of being successful
records.learnerexamples_text: The course will improve his career prospects.; I could learn many things from picking fruit and vegetables and improve my job prospects.

records.definition_text: the period of time when someone is young
records.learnerexamples_text: I was a fairly good football player in my youth.; I played several kinds of sports during my youth, but now I am not a member of any club.

records.definition_text: the size or level of something
records.learnerexamples_text: We don't yet know the scale of the problem.; Nuclear weapons cause destruction on a massive scale.; My parents used to entertain friends on a large/small scale.; He leads an evil trade: they [carry out] smuggling on a grand scale and use the inn as a store.

records.definition_text: a set of numbers, amounts etc., used to measure or compare the level of something
records.learnerexamples_text: the Centigrade/Fahrenheit scale; How would you rate his work on a scale of 1 to 5?; In brief, I think it would be a very good idea to create a new scale of [salaries] based on our needs, in which doctors would be [higher] than professional footballers.

records.definition_text: how the size of things on a map, model, etc. relates to the same things in real life
records.learnerexamples_text: a scale of 1:50 000; This map is large scale.; Is the bridge drawn to scale?; He was building a scale model of Concorde.; My f[ri]end gave me a 1/72 scale kit of "Supermarine Spitfire" for my birthday.

records.definition_text: a piece of equipment for measuring weight
records.learnerexamples_text: kitchen/bathroom scales

records.definition_text: something that shocks people because they think it is morally wrong
records.learnerexamples_text: a financial/political scandal; Their affair caused/created a scandal in the office.; If there is the slightest suggestion/hint of scandal, the public will no longer trust us.;  It's a scandal (that) children could be treated in this way.; Among them are the increasingly popular reality shows and all the daily news about gossip and scandal.

records.definition_text: a permanent mark left on the body from a cut or other injury
records.learnerexamples_text: an ugly scar; That burn will leave a nasty scar.; David is a tall man with black curly hair, black eyes, a big nose, [a] beard and a scar on his neck.

records.definition_text: frightened or worried
records.learnerexamples_text: He's scared of spiders.; He's scared to tell her what really happened.; I was scared (that) you might not be there.; I was scared stiff.; She had a scared look on her face.

records.definition_text: frightening
records.learnerexamples_text: a scary movie/story; It was quite exciting but a little scary.

records.definition_text: a short part of a film, play, or book in which the events happen in one place
records.learnerexamples_text: the funeral/wedding scene; Juliet dies in Act IV, Scene iii.; If you haven't seen any of th[ese] three "Star Wars" movies, I suggest you do see them tonight or tomorrow. They are great, with [a] lot of action scenes.

records.definition_text: a view or picture of a place, event, or activity
records.learnerexamples_text: Lowry painted street scenes.; scenes of everyday life; There were scenes of great joy as the hostages were re-united with their families.; I like especially the scene of the garden with snow in winter.

records.definition_text: a place where an unpleasant event has happened
records.learnerexamples_text: The police arrived to find a scene of horrifying destruction.; Evidence was found at the scene of the crime.; She managed to recreate the scene of the crime, saying that she had swallowed a fish bone.

records.definition_text: the attractive, natural things that you see in the countryside
records.learnerexamples_text: beautiful/breathtaking/spectacular scenery; They stopped at the top of the hill to admire the scenery.; If I were you, I'[d] go [to] the countryside because it's peaceful, quiet, and the scenery is wonderful.

records.definition_text: a pleasant smell
records.learnerexamples_text: the sweet scent of orange blossom; Flowers are in bloom and their scent triggers my romantic mood.

records.definition_text: to arrange that an event or activity will happen at a particular time
records.learnerexamples_text: The meeting has been scheduled for tomorrow afternoon.; The train is scheduled to arrive at 8.45, but it's running twenty minutes late.; My flight is scheduled to arrive at the airport at 10 o'clock in the morning.

records.definition_text: a plan that gives events or activities and the times that they will happen or be done
records.learnerexamples_text: I have a very busy schedule today.; Will the work be completed on schedule?; Everything went according to schedule.; Firstly, the programme beg[a]n exactly on schedule and the first group were KING CUP, not TORRENTS.

records.definition_text: travelling at a regular time each day or week
records.learnerexamples_text: a scheduled flight

records.definition_text: planned to happen at a particular time or on a particular date
records.learnerexamples_text: This programme will be broadcast half an hour later than the scheduled time.; The scheduled time for the arrival is 5.15 pm.

records.definition_text: an official plan or system
records.learnerexamples_text: a training/housing/play scheme; a pension/savings scheme; There's a new scheme in our town for recycling plastic bottles.; Class sizes will increase under the new scheme.; I reject any other possibilities like building a tunnel or a by-Pass, because compared to the Park and Ride scheme, they would be much too expensive.

records.definition_text: a particular type of science
records.learnerexamples_text: computer science; Chemistry, physics, and biology are all sciences.; advances in medical science; In my class, there were 15 girls and 15 boys, who were studying computer science with me, so I knew everybody.

records.definition_text: stories about life in the future or in other parts of the universe
records.learnerexamples_text: She is a well-known science fiction writer.; Also, I like to watch fantasy and science fiction films.

records.definition_text: relating to science, or using the organized methods of science
records.learnerexamples_text: a scientific discovery/experiment/theory; scientific evidence/research; The project has attracted considerable criticism from the scientific community.; I like programmes about sport and scientific discover[ie]s.

records.definition_text: using scientific methods
records.learnerexamples_text: scientifically proven; It is scientifically pro[v]en and well-known that the gas [releas]ed by cars is toxic and quite dangerous to the environment - specially to the ozone layer.

records.definition_text: someone who studies science or works in science
records.learnerexamples_text: Scientists are working to create a vaccine for the disease.; NASA admitted yesterday they will send a group of highly trained scientists to Mars in the next two years.

records.definition_text: the number of points someone gets in a game or test
records.learnerexamples_text: a high/low score; What's the score?; At half time, the score stood at two all.; The final score was 3-0.; We took 4 or 5 exams that day and my friend, Erick and I studied all night to get the best scores.

records.definition_text: to get points in a game or test
records.learnerexamples_text: He scored just before half-time to put Liverpool 2-1 ahead.; In American football, a touchdown scores six points.; She scored 18 out of 20 in the spelling test.; I almost scored an own goal.

records.definition_text: to rub your skin with your nails, often to stop it itching
records.learnerexamples_text: My skin was so itchy, I was scratching all night.; He was scratching (at) his mosquito bites.; Hannah scratched her head thoughtfully.

records.definition_text: to make a slight cut or long, thin mark with a sharp object on a surface or on your skin
records.learnerexamples_text: I scratched myself on the roses.; We scratched the paintwork trying to get the bed into Martha's room.; People have been scratching their names on this rock for years.; How can this ridiculous man accuse me of scratching his new car, thought Laura.

records.definition_text: a slight cut or a long, thin mark made with a sharp object
records.learnerexamples_text: I've got all these scratches on my arm from the cat.; I should like to join one of those courses to become more 'professional' in how to repair a scratch on the side [of the boat] or a hole in the sail.

records.definition_text: to rub a hard surface with a sharp object, often making a noise
records.learnerexamples_text: The dog's scratching at the door - he wants to be let in.; Something scratched at the door.

records.definition_text: to make a loud, high noise with your voice, or to shout something in a loud, high voice because you are afraid, hurt, or angry
records.learnerexamples_text: A spider landed on her pillow and she screamed.; Through the smoke, the rescuers could hear people screaming for help.; He was screaming in/with pain and begging for anaesthetic.; They screamed with laughter at her jokes.; Ken screamed (out) a warning telling people to get out of the way.

records.definition_text: when someone screams
records.learnerexamples_text: We heard screams coming from their apartment.; Last night, I was cooking and dad was watching tv when, suddenly I heard a scream.

records.definition_text: the words written for and spoken in a film, play, broadcast or speech
records.learnerexamples_text: Bruce Robinson wrote the script for 'The Killing Fields'.; I didn't get involved that much in writing a script because it was very hard and the director wrote most of it but the main idea of the background of the stage was m[ine], and I am very proud of it.

records.definition_text: a piece of art that is made from stone, wood, clay, etc., or the process of making objects like this
records.learnerexamples_text: a wooden sculpture; modern sculpture; Tom teaches sculpture at the local art school.; The museum has several life-sized sculptures of people and animals.; But if you have time, you must visit some cities, like Rome or Florence, because there are many historical buildings and museums, with the most important sculptures and pictures [by] famous artist[s] like Michelangelo or Raffaello.

records.definition_text: an animal with smooth fur that eats fish and lives near the sea
records.learnerexamples_text: We could see seals swimming near the coast.; After leaving the Orkney Islands, we went by boat to [the] Shetland Islands, because we wanted to observe the grey seals with their pups that were [o]n the northwest coast.

records.definition_text: to try to find someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: I've searched my bedroom but I can't find my watch.; He searched in his pockets for some change.; Police are still searching the woods for the missing girl.; He searched (in/through) his pockets for some change.; I've searched high and low , but I can't find my birth certificate.

records.definition_text: to use a computer to find information, especially on the Internet
records.learnerexamples_text: I searched the Internet to find the best prices for flights to Barcelona.; Before you had to go to a lib[r]ary to finish [your] homework. Now, we just search on the internet.

records.definition_text: If the police search a place or a person, they look to see if they are hiding anything illegal, such as drugs.
records.learnerexamples_text: They were searched at the airport.; The men were searched for drugs and then released.; The undercover [patrol] searched our car rather roughly, looking for drugs.

records.definition_text: when you try to find someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: After a long search, they eventually found the missing papers.; The police carried out/conducted/made a thorough search of the house, but they failed to find any drugs.; Joshua instantly thought it could be a bomb, so he organized a search all over the airport.

records.definition_text: when you try to find an answer to a problem
records.learnerexamples_text: the search for happiness; Hemingway fought in the Spanish Civil war and in World War II, always [i]n the search for answers to questions like "... what defines a man", or "... what happens to us in critical situations".

records.definition_text: when you use a computer to find information, especially on the Internet
records.learnerexamples_text: Why not do a search on Google for hotels in the area?; We're doing a computer search for all words beginning with 'high'.; But I think you shouldn't ask me, the best thing is [a] search on the internet, so you can see the photos and choose the option you like mo[st].

records.definition_text: a period of the year when a particular thing happens
records.learnerexamples_text: How long does the dry/hurricane/wet season last?; The British football season begins in August and ends in May.; Once they had finished, Peter kissed his parents and started his journey [on] foot heading towards the stadium, to play the first game of the season.

records.definition_text: one of the four periods of the year: spring, summer, autumn or winter
records.learnerexamples_text: But summer in Poland is as wonderful [a] season as winter!

records.definition_text: relating to or happening during a particular period in the year
records.learnerexamples_text: seasonal vegetables; seasonal farm work; I am a student and during my summer holiday I prefer to do some seasonal work.

records.definition_text: another
records.learnerexamples_text: She is often described as the second Marilyn Monroe.; You really ought to make the most of the opportunity, because you won't get a second chance.; Richard and Liz have a second home in France.; Pay attention to what she's saying because she won't explain it a second time.; I started my new English class last week. I had just finish[ed] my course and that was [a] second chance for me to pick up words so I gave it a go.

records.definition_text: Second is used to show that only one thing is better, bigger, etc. than the thing mentioned.
records.learnerexamples_text: St Petersburg is Russia's second (biggest/largest) city.; Iraq's oil reserves are second only to Saudi Arabia's.; The conditions that these prisoners are kept in are second to none.; Joao Pessoa is the second green[est] city in the world.

records.definition_text: after one other person or thing in order or importance
records.learnerexamples_text: She didn't win the race, but she did come second.; [O]n the other hand, New Zealand came second [for] senior government.

records.definition_text: used to talk about the second in a series of things
records.learnerexamples_text: Second, they failed to send written warning.; Second, the pedestrian area in the commercial centre has to grow, wh[ich] would make this part of the town more pleasant for walking and would improve the opportunities [for] the shops.

records.definition_text: a very short period of time
records.learnerexamples_text: "Come on, hurry up!" "I'll just/only be a second - I've got to lock the back door."; Have you got a second, Paul? I'd like to have a word with you.; It won't take a second .; Wait a couple of/a few seconds before trying again.; A few seconds later, a huge tree beside my house fell down and destroyed most of my house.

records.definition_text: relating to the education of children approximately between the ages of 11 and 18 years old
records.learnerexamples_text: secondary education; Marcus has just started at secondary school.; He is studying at secondary school.

records.definition_text: a school for students aged between 11 and 18
records.learnerexamples_text: My children are both at secondary school now.; They said they chose our school because we are one of the best secondary schools [in] Mexico City. Can you believe that!?

records.definition_text: If something is second-hand, someone else owned or used it before you.
records.learnerexamples_text: second-hand books/clothes; She buys a lot of clothes second-hand.; Personally, I only buy second-hand clothes because in second-hand shops, I really like discover[ing] rare things and funny clothes from the 60s or 70s.

records.definition_text: used for introducing the second reason, idea, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: I want two things: firstly, more money, and secondly, better working hours.; Secondly, I didn't know that you were working in [an] organization which [is] trying to save wildlife, but it sounds very ex[c]iting.

records.definition_text: something that you tell no one about or only a few people
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm having a party for him but it's a secret.; Can you keep a secret?; A close couple should have no secrets from each other.; Aren't you going to let me in on the secret?; She makes no secret of her dislike of her father.

records.definition_text: If something is secret, other people are not allowed to know about it.
records.learnerexamples_text: The President escaped through a secret passage underneath the parliament building.; This is top secret information.; Do you think we'll manage to keep the surprise party secret from Mum until her birthday?; The secret admirer was the guy I liked!

records.definition_text: without allowing other people to know
records.learnerexamples_text: She said she didn't care about it, but I believe she was secretly delighted.; He was convicted on the evidence of secretly recorded telephone conversations.; Then in the evening we'll come to her house secretly. Of course, we should tell her mom everything about this plan.

records.definition_text: one of the parts that something is divided into
records.learnerexamples_text: a non-smoking section in a restaurant; the sports section of the newspaper; the tail section of an aircraft; The poorest sections of the community have much worse health.; It has two floor[s] and is divided into sections, one that is a [general] restaurant and one for vegetarian people.

records.definition_text: safe from danger or harm or not likely to end
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't feel that the house is secure.; Her promotion has made her position in the company more secure.; The museum has been promised £22 million by the government, so its future is relatively secure.; I think homes in the future will be more secure.

records.definition_text: confident about yourself and the situation that you are in
records.learnerexamples_text: I need to feel secure in a relationship.; First of all, you feel secure because you know that all the members of the family love you.

records.definition_text: protection of a person, building, organization or country against threats such as crime or attacks by foreign countries
records.learnerexamples_text: The station was closed for two hours because of a security alert.; Thirty demonstrators were killed in clashes with the security forces over the weekend.; The tighter security measures/precautions include video cameras in the city centre.; The students were deported because they posed a threat to national security.; The proposed national identity card system would help to tighten security against fraud.

records.definition_text: to understand something
records.learnerexamples_text: I see (that) the social club is organising a theatre trip next month.; I see what you mean.; They didn't see the need/any need to notify their members of the changes in writing.; I was surprised that they couldn't see my point of view.; Do you see what I mean?

records.definition_text: to find out information
records.learnerexamples_text: I'll just see what time the train gets in.; Let's see whether there is an early performance on Saturday.; I have looked in my calendar to see what time would be the best for you to come here.

records.definition_text: to imagine or think about something or someone in a particular way
records.learnerexamples_text: She didn't see herself as brave.; It was easy to see the gift as a sort of bribe.; As I see it/things/the situation, we'll have to get extra help.; If I compare the members of my family with these qualities, then I have to say that I don't see them as my best friends.

records.definition_text: a small round or oval object produced by a plant that a new plant can grow from
records.learnerexamples_text: Sow the seeds about 3 cm deep.; This chemical will stop the seeds from sprouting.; [For] several years, I have been very interested in flowers, fresh, dried and artificial and also different kinds of seeds.

records.definition_text: to try to find or get something
records.learnerexamples_text: "Are you actively seeking jobs?" she asked.; Hundreds of dissidents are seeking refuge/asylum in the US embassy.; Legal advice should be sought before you take any further action.; I am seeking employment and [am] interested in your offer.

records.definition_text: to appear to be a particular thing or to have a particular quality
records.searchterms_text: seem;seem happy/a nice person etc;seem happy/a nice person, etc.;seem happy/a nice person, etc. ;seemed;seeming;seems
records.learnerexamples_text: She seemed happy enough.; My new boss seems like a really nice person.; She seemed very friendly.

records.definition_text: to appear to be a particular thing or to have a particular quality
records.searchterms_text: seem;seem like/as if/to etc;seem like/as if/to, etc.;seemed;seeming;seems
records.learnerexamples_text: It seemed like a good idea at the time.; The graphics were so good that the people seemed as if they were real.; There doesn't seem to be any real solution.; I seem to know more about him than anyone else.; I spent four cold days in the mountain[s] and it seemed like winter despite being summer!

records.base_text: see off sb or see sb off
records.definition_text: to go to the place that someone is leaving from in order to say goodbye
records.searchterms_text: see;see off sb or see sb off
records.learnerexamples_text: They came to see me off at the station.; She came to the station to see him off.

records.definition_text: to understand that someone is trying to deceive you
records.learnerexamples_text: It didn't take long for us to see through his charm.

records.definition_text: to deal with a person or task that needs to be dealt with
records.learnerexamples_text: "These letters need posting." "I'll see to them later."; Mrs Chapman asked for some help with the orders - could you see to it?; Please see to it that no-one comes in without identification.; I can see to the children if you want to go out.; If you want to keep an animal happy and healthy, it is also important, in my opinion, to see to it that, for instance, the monkeys have real trees to climb in!

records.definition_text: to take hold of something quickly and firmly
records.learnerexamples_text: I seized his arm and made him turn to look at me.; Besides, I think that the wild beasts have the right to live free and seize their prey in order to feed themselves.

records.definition_text: to do something quickly in order to use an opportunity
records.learnerexamples_text: You need to seize every opportunity.; So we seize the opportunity to go to the sea.

records.definition_text: not often
records.learnerexamples_text: We seldom go out in the evenings.; Alice was a quiet girl, she seldom talked, but he just couldn't stop talking.

records.definition_text: to choose someone or something from a group
records.learnerexamples_text: There was a choice of four prizes, and the winner could select one of them.; A mouse is a device which makes it easier to select different options from computer menus.; How do you select people for promotion?; He was selected to play for Australia at the age of only 18.; The supermarket's policy is to select out the best fruit and discard the rest.

records.definition_text: when someone or something is chosen
records.learnerexamples_text: the selection process ; We need to make a selection from these applicants.; Success is achieved by the careful selection of projects.; The selection of films and plays was well made, but I would have appreciate[d] [it] if there had been more.

records.definition_text: a group of people or things that has been chosen
records.learnerexamples_text: Most schools would have a good selection of these books in their libraries.; The larger shops are able to stock a wide selection of goods.; There is a good selection of bar food.

records.definition_text: being self-confident
records.learnerexamples_text: Since she left home, her self-confidence has grown.; In my opinion, the reason for it is that not many people know how to prepare for [an] interview and gain self-confidence.

records.definition_text: feeling sure about yourself and your abilities
records.learnerexamples_text: He's a very self-confident young man.; So when the day c[a]me, she felt much more self-confident and determined than before.

records.definition_text: caring only about yourself and not other people
records.learnerexamples_text: It's very selfish of him to go away every weekend.; The judge told him: "Your attitude shows a selfish disregard for others."; I found this sport very interesting, because you have to play in a team so you must not be selfish, you have to change your spirit.

records.definition_text: A self-service restaurant or shop is one in which you serve yourself and are not served by the people who work there.
records.learnerexamples_text: It was a cheap, self-service restaurant.; I went to have lunch in a self-service restaurant and in the afternoon I continued my visit.

records.definition_text: to be bought in large numbers
records.learnerexamples_text: His last book sold eight million copies.; The single with her new song sold more than 15 million copies, now she was a powerfull star.

records.definition_text: someone who sells something
records.learnerexamples_text: flower/newspaper/souvenir sellers; Do you think the seller will accept £96 000 for the house?; It was then my mother remembered a toy seller had been selling toys in the place where we had been waiting in the station and that our suitcase[s] must have got mixed up.

records.definition_text: If a supply of something sells out, or if it is sold out, there is no more of that thing to buy.
records.learnerexamples_text: The first issue of the magazine sold out within two days.; All the tickets were sold out and the stadium was nearly full.

records.definition_text: a mark (;) used to separate parts of a sentence, or items in a list which already has commas
records.learnerexamples_text: Use a semicolon to separate the groups of items in your list.

records.definition_text: one of the two games in a sports competition that are played to decide who will play in the final game
records.learnerexamples_text: Who's in the semi-finals?; She's the youngest player ever to get through to a semi-final.; One Sunday morning we had to play the cup semi-final against [our] great rival.

records.definition_text: a meeting of a group of people with a teacher or expert for training, discussion, or study of a subject
records.learnerexamples_text: I attended practically every lecture and seminar when I was a student.; I'm giving a seminar on the latest developments in genetic engineering next week.; a seminar room ; I also need this job because I need money to attend some seminars.

records.definition_text: to make someone go somewhere
records.learnerexamples_text: We're sending the children to stay with my parents for a couple of weeks.; The commander has asked us to send reinforcements.; They've sent their son (away) to school in Scotland.; He was trying to explain but she became impatient and sent him away.; We should buil[d] more schools because we only have one, so we have to send our children away and none of us like that.

records.base_text: send off sth or send sth off
records.definition_text: to send a letter, document or parcel by post
records.searchterms_text: send;send off sth or send sth off
records.learnerexamples_text: Have you sent off your application form yet?

records.base_text: send sth back or send back sth
records.definition_text: to return something to the person who sent it to you, especially because it is damaged or not suitable
records.searchterms_text: send;send sth back or send back sth
records.learnerexamples_text: I had to send the shirt back because it didn't fit me.; I usual[l]y order my clothes [on the] Internet. It's fast, easy and you don't have any problems send[ing] them back if they don't fit.

records.definition_text: having a more important job or position than someone else
records.learnerexamples_text: a senior executive; We work in the same team but she's senior to me.; a senior government minister; She is also extrao[r]dinary in that she graduated from Harvard University and Tokyo University and used to work for the Ministry of the Foreign Affairs as a senior civil servant.

records.definition_text: relating to people who are older
records.learnerexamples_text: You can't use a senior ticket during the rush hour - you have to pay full fare.; When I got to the tickets desk before the show to buy my ticket I asked for a senior discount, and the woman told me there were no discounts available as I read on the advertising.

records.definition_text: a physical feeling, or the ability to physically feel things
records.learnerexamples_text: a burning sensation; I had no sensation of pain whatsoever.; The disease causes a loss of sensation in the fingers.; When I fel[l] into the water, I was shocked. I couldn't move my right leg, the sensation was horrible.

records.definition_text: a strange feeling or idea that you cannot explain
records.learnerexamples_text: I had the odd sensation (that) someone was following me.; Suddenly I had the sensation that something was wrong.

records.definition_text: a lot of excitement, surprise or interest
records.learnerexamples_text: Their marriage caused a sensation.; In the poetry, she expressed her sad feeling, thinking of her brother who was in China as a soldier. It caused a sensation.

records.definition_text: a feeling or understanding about yourself or about a situation
records.learnerexamples_text: Did you get any sense of what they might do?; Living out in the country gave us a great sense of freedom.; I like to see how people fight for the pri[z]e. I like this sense of compet[it]ion that only sport give[s]!

records.definition_text: good judgment, especially about practical things
records.learnerexamples_text: I hope they'll have the (good) sense/have enough sense to shut the windows before they leave.;  There's no sense in waiting - the next train isn't for two hours.; People should have the sense to dispose [of] all the waste properly.

records.definition_text: the ability to do something
records.learnerexamples_text: He's got a good sense of direction and hardly ever uses a map.; good business sense; Animals are part of nature so they must be free [to] go where their sense of direction [leads them].

records.definition_text: one of the five natural abilities of sight, hearing, touch, smell, and taste
records.learnerexamples_text: With her keen sense of smell, she could tell if you were a smoker from the other side of the room.; My cold is so bad I've lost my sense of smell/taste.; You can enjoy a flight with all your five senses.

records.definition_text: one of the possible meanings of a word or phrase
records.learnerexamples_text: They are not immigrants, at least not in any sense that I understand.; The packaging is green - in both senses of the word.; Security defined in the broad/broadest sense of the term means getting at the root causes of trouble and helping to reduce regional conflicts.; The Empress was an ideal lady in every sense of the word.

records.definition_text: showing good judgment
records.learnerexamples_text: a sensible answer/approach/choice/option; a sensible person; I think the sensible thing to do is phone before you go and ask for directions.;  It would be sensible to take an umbrella.; I know it sounds strange but there's a sensible reason: money talks.

records.definition_text: able to react very quickly and easily
records.learnerexamples_text: These scales are very sensitive.; He has a very sensitive nose.; I am very sensitive to noise, especially at night, and tend to catch a cold even in summer.

records.definition_text: easily upset by the things people say or do
records.learnerexamples_text: Her reply showed that she was very sensitive to criticism.; He was very sensitive about his scar and thought everyone was staring at him.; Nowadays we are not so sensitive.

records.definition_text: easy to damage and needing to be protected
records.learnerexamples_text: I have very sensitive skin.

records.definition_text: A sensitive subject or situation needs to be dealt with carefully in order to avoid upsetting people.
records.learnerexamples_text: Sex education and birth control are sensitive issues.; The stolen car contained military documents described as very sensitive.; I knew that I could not cry and shout because it was too important and sensitive [a] problem for us.

records.definition_text: able to understand what people are feeling and deal with them in a way that does not upset them
records.learnerexamples_text: I want a man who's kind and sensitive.; Representatives of the company claim their plan will be sensitive to local needs.; In the movie, he plays a concerned and sensitive father trying to bring up two teenage children on his own.; One thing Bobby is good at is that he is bright and sensitive enough to protect you.

records.definition_text: a punishment that a judge gives to someone who has committed a crime
records.learnerexamples_text: He got a heavy/light sentence.; The offence carries a jail/prison/life/5-year sentence.; This is even worse th[a]n a real life sentence.

records.definition_text: to give a punishment to someone who has committed a crime
records.learnerexamples_text: He was sentenced to life imprisonment.; Soon afterwards he gets imprisoned again and is sentenced to death. Sydney takes his place and is executed instead of him.

records.definition_text: not joined or touching anything else
records.learnerexamples_text: a separate compartment; I try to keep meat separate from other food in the fridge.; But there was no choice, as all my friends that did go were already in separate rooms.

records.definition_text: not affecting or related to each other
records.learnerexamples_text: I've asked him to turn his music down on three separate occasions.; I have my professional life and my private life and I try to keep them separate.; Three youths have been shot and killed in separate incidents this month.; She went to Lisbon, and we [ended up] living separate li[v]es.

records.definition_text: different or new
records.learnerexamples_text: Use a separate sheet of paper.; The art department and the main college are in two separate buildings.; Yesterday I bought a lot [of] presents, so I needed a separate suitcase.

records.definition_text: to divide into parts, or to make something divide into parts
records.learnerexamples_text: I separated the class into three groups.; The north and south of the country are separated by a mountain range.; You can get a special device for separating egg whites from yolks.; The top and bottom sections are quite difficult to separate.; On the other hand, more bins ought to be put in the centre [to] encour[a]ge people to separate their rubbish more carefully.

records.definition_text: to start to live in a different place from your husband or wife because the relationship has ended
records.learnerexamples_text: My parents separated when I was four.; But his parents separated and John didn't see h[is] mother again, as well as his sister, after that day.

records.definition_text: to move apart, or to make people move apart
records.learnerexamples_text: I shall separate you two if you don't stop talking.; Somehow, in the rush to get out of the building, I got separated from my mother.; Perhaps we should separate now and meet up later.; I noticed that there w[ere] some [people] fighting, and we tried to separate them.

records.definition_text: not together
records.learnerexamples_text: Detectives interviewed the men separately.; I tend to wear the jacket and skirt separately rather than as a suit.; I think we'd better deal with these two points separately.; They were living separately and missing each other.

records.definition_text: when two or more people or things are separated
records.learnerexamples_text: During the war, many couples had to face long periods of separation.; After many years, the government finally abandoned its apartheid system of racial separation.; One of the most important project[s] is the separation of the rubbish and I think that it has worked, but it could work better.

records.definition_text: the decision of two people who were married or living together to stop living together
records.learnerexamples_text: They decided on a trial separation.; We lived for a time in peace but our happiness ceased because of his jealousy and fear [of losing] me, which was the cause of our daylong quarrels. There was no solution apart from separation.

records.definition_text: a group of television or radio programmes that have the same main characters or deal with the same subject
records.learnerexamples_text: The footballer Paul Gascoigne is to host a Channel 4 television series on soccer skills.; a comedy series; I missed the second episode of the series so I don't know what's going on now.; I like television series like Smallville.

records.definition_text: several things or events of the same type that come one after the other
records.learnerexamples_text: He's had a series of tests at the hospital but they can't find anything wrong.; She gave a series of lectures at Warwick University last year on contemporary British writers.; The aim of this report is [to] make a series of suggestions on which lessons and other activities should be filmed.

records.definition_text: a set of books published by the same company which deal with the same subject
records.learnerexamples_text: They do a series on architecture throughout the ages.; We read all of Poirot and [the] [Miss] Marple series.

records.definition_text: A serious problem or situation is bad and makes people worry.
records.learnerexamples_text: a serious illness; There were no reports of serious injuries.; The new tax regulations have landed some of the smaller companies in serious trouble.; A shortage of space has become a serious problem in a lot of schools.; He's been taken to hospital where his condition is described as serious but stable.

records.definition_text: A serious person does not laugh often.
records.learnerexamples_text: I remember her as a very serious child.; Well, the new teacher is very serious, but this is ok.

records.definition_text: not joking or intended to be funny
records.learnerexamples_text: Please don't laugh - I'm being serious.; He was wearing a very serious expression and I knew something was wrong.; On the surface it's a very funny novel but it does have a more serious underlying theme.; Is she serious about going to live abroad?; We are taught how to act in both comic and serious parts.

records.definition_text: needing or deserving your complete attention
records.learnerexamples_text: That's an interesting job offer - I'd give it some serious consideration if I were you.; We've got some serious talking to do, you and me.; I think it would be worthwhile to give serious thought to these animals.

records.definition_text: badly or severely
records.learnerexamples_text: seriously ill/worried; He wasn't seriously injured - he just got a few cuts and bruises.; She is seriously ill with cancer.

records.definition_text: in a way that shows that you are not joking
records.learnerexamples_text: Seriously now, did he really say that or are you just being silly?; You're not seriously thinking of leaving, are you?; Seriously, Tom, I have noticed that you get angry very easily since your examinations started.

records.definition_text: someone who works and lives in someone else's house doing their cooking and cleaning, especially in the past
records.learnerexamples_text: They employed more than 50 servants.; In this book, the author [includ]es a detailed description of [the] two main characters: the rich English master PHILEAS FOGG and his French servant PASSEPARTOUT.

records.definition_text: to help customers and sell things to them in a shop
records.learnerexamples_text: Are you being served?; I also learnt a lot about how to serve c[u]st[o]mers and how to use a till.

records.definition_text: a central computer from which other computers get information
records.learnerexamples_text: a network/file server; It was my boss, [who] said "I'm in Australia, and I can't read my e-mail, the server at work crashed.

records.definition_text: a system or organization that provides something that people need
records.learnerexamples_text: the ambulance/health/postal/prison service; They provide a free bus service from the station.; We hope to be operating a normal service as soon as possible.; I told him to phone the after-sales service.

records.definition_text: when people help you and bring you things in a place such as a shop, restaurant, or hotel
records.learnerexamples_text: The only trouble with this café is that the service is so slow.; I think the Cinemark is the best cinema because it has good service and it is cheap.

records.definition_text: an amount of money charged for serving a customer in a restaurant, which is often paid directly to the waiter
records.learnerexamples_text: There is a 10% service charge included in the bill.; Does the bill include service?; The thing which annoyed me the most was [that] they have a 20% service charge, but I refused to pay it because there w[as] no service.

records.definition_text: the armed forces, or work done in the armed forces
records.learnerexamples_text: He joined the air force in 1964 and spent ten years in the service.; Most of my family were in the services.; All men under thirty-five were told to report for military service within three days.; Service personnel are subject to the Official Secrets Act.; He finished his military service, and now he was on his way to his family, who had been waiting for him for a long time.

records.definition_text: a government department that is responsible for a particular area of activity
records.learnerexamples_text: the diplomatic service; the security services; I was employed in the security service.

records.definition_text: a period of time or a meeting arranged for a particular activity
records.learnerexamples_text: The 21-year-old runner twisted his ankle in a training session last Friday.; As the heads of state gathered, the press were allowed in for a photo session.; Last week we had the normal two training sessions and a game against another club.

records.definition_text: If a story, film, etc. is set in a particular time or place, the action in it happens in that time or place.
records.learnerexamples_text: 'West Side Story' is set in New York in the late 1950s.; It was an adventure story and I liked it a lot because it was set in Australia.

records.definition_text: When the sun sets, it moves down in the sky until it cannot be seen.
records.learnerexamples_text: The sun rises in the East and sets in the West.; I loved the thin fog before the sun set.

records.definition_text: to cause something or someone to be in the stated condition or situation
records.learnerexamples_text: It is believed that the building was set on fire deliberately.; She set fire to her neighbour's house.; After years in prison, the men who had wrongfully been found guilty of the bombing were finally set free.; A modern zoo must be [like] a forest, without cages, and the animals must be set free.

records.definition_text: to make a piece of equipment ready to be used
records.learnerexamples_text: The heating is set to come on at 5.00 p.m.; Have you set the video recorder?; I usually set my watch by the time signal on the radio.; He set the alarm for 7.00 a.m.; I had forgotten to set the alarm clock the previous night and by the time I got up it was already 9 o'clock.

records.definition_text: if something is set somewhere, it is in that place or position
records.learnerexamples_text: The campsite is set in the middle of a pine forest.; Our house is set back from the road.; The camp is set in a beautiful place in the heart of nature, with lots of opportunities to get out of the camp if you want to.

records.definition_text: to give someone something to do or achieve
records.learnerexamples_text: Our teacher has set us a lot of homework.; He's set himself the goal/target of making his first million by the time he's 30.; I suggest it [would] be a good idea to set more projections next year.

records.definition_text: a part of a game of tennis
records.learnerexamples_text: They won in straight sets.; Finally we managed to win the [second] set so we were equal.

records.definition_text: the place where a film or play is performed or recorded, and the pictures, furniture, etc. that are used
records.learnerexamples_text: a film set; a stage set; a set designer; They first met on the set of 'Star Wars'.; Her father, John, was a stuntperson and he died in an unfortunate accident while he was perform[ing] [o]n a film set.

records.definition_text: to fix a date or time for something
records.searchterms_text: set;set a date/time (for sth);set a date/time for sth;sets;setting
records.learnerexamples_text: Juan and Maria have set a date for their wedding - it's going to be on August 31.; Has a time been set for the meeting yet?; I'm going to miss your class tomor[r]ow, but we can set a date to cover the work on.

records.definition_text: to do something in a good way so that other people might try to copy you
records.learnerexamples_text: Try to set a good example to the children.; It sets a good example for other museums.

records.definition_text: to do something in a good way so that other people might try to copy you
records.learnerexamples_text: Try to set a good example to the children.; It sets a good example for other museums.

records.definition_text: to establish the best achievement so far in a sport or competition
records.learnerexamples_text: Bolt has set a new world record.

records.definition_text: to start a journey
records.learnerexamples_text: What time will we have to set off for the station tomorrow?; They've just set off on a round-the-world cruise.; We set off [for] home at 5 o'clock.

records.definition_text: to start a journey
records.learnerexamples_text: Martin set out on his cycle ride before dawn.; When do you want to set out?; Next morning I packed my luggage and set out on our trip to France.

records.base_text: set out sth or set sth out
records.definition_text: to give all the details of something, or to explain something clearly, especially in writing
records.searchterms_text: set;set out sth or set sth out
records.learnerexamples_text: All the project costs are set out in this document.; She gave a presentation setting out the company's future plans.; But first of all I will set out briefly the reasons that made me take the final decision.

records.definition_text: to allow someone to leave prison or to allow a person or animal to escape
records.learnerexamples_text: He opened the cage and set the birds free.; To sum up, animals should be set free and live as they should live in nature.

records.definition_text: the position of a house or other building
records.learnerexamples_text: Their cottage is in a beautiful rural setting.; [It is] a beautiful setting with old architecture, trees and glittering water.

records.definition_text: the time and the place in which the action of a book, movie, play, etc. happens
records.learnerexamples_text: The play has its setting in a wartime prison camp.; The setting of "The Third Man" is Vienna after the Second World War.

records.definition_text: to start living somewhere that you are going to live for a long time
records.learnerexamples_text: After they got married, they settled in Brighton.; He travelled around Europe before finally settling in Rome.; I can understand why you have decided to settle near the Loire Valley, which is one of the greatest part[s] of France.

records.definition_text: to decide or arrange something
records.learnerexamples_text: Right, that's settled. We're going to Spain.; They haven't yet settled when the wedding is going to be.; "The tickets are £40 each." "Well, that settles that then - I can't afford that much."; I'd like to get this matter settled once and for all.; The details of the contract have not yet been settled.

records.definition_text: to become familiar with a place and to feel happy and confident in it
records.learnerexamples_text: She quickly settled down in her new house/job/school.; He seemed to be such a nice guy and I was very happy to find you [have] settled down so well in your new life.

records.base_text: set up sth or set sth up
records.definition_text: to formally establish a new company, organization, system, way of working, etc.
records.searchterms_text: set;set up sth or set sth up
records.learnerexamples_text: A committee has been set up to organize social events in the college.; She plans to set up her own business.; They've set up a fund for victims of the earthquake.; It is such a beautiful country that I wanted to stay there and set up a business.

records.base_text: set up sth or set sth up
records.definition_text: to arrange for an event or activity to happen
records.searchterms_text: set;set up sth or set sth up
records.learnerexamples_text: We need to set up a meeting to discuss the proposals.; The government has agreed to set up a public enquiry.; I suggest we try to set up a meeting with people from city hall, and give them all the right arguments.

records.definition_text: extremely bad
records.learnerexamples_text: a severe chest infection/leg injury/toothache; This is a school for children with severe learning difficulties.; In parts of Africa there is a severe food/water shortage.; There is expected to be a severe frost tonight.; Their life was a severe financial struggle, and Tom's dream was to run somewhere far away.

records.definition_text: a severe person is unfriendly or very strict
records.learnerexamples_text: She had her hair tied back in a severe style.; The teacher was a small, severe man.; Jane Eyre is sen[t] away to [a] school for orphans. [...] The atmosphere in school is no better, with little food and severe teachers.

records.definition_text: very seriously
records.learnerexamples_text: Their daughter was severely injured in a car accident.; severely disabled; Job opportunities are severely limited/restricted at the moment.; In spite of trying to repair it, it is still severely damaged.

records.definition_text: to make or repair clothes by joining pieces of cloth using a needle and thread
records.learnerexamples_text: My grandmother taught me to sew.; I made this skirt just by sewing two pieces of material together.; She sews all her children's clothes.; He sewed the badge neatly onto his uniform.; Well, I used to sew my clothes on my own.

records.definition_text: sexual activity between people
records.learnerexamples_text: Sex before/outside marriage is strongly disapproved of in some cultures.; She was complaining about all the sex and violence on television.; She'd been having sex with a colleague at work for years.; Most young people now receive sex education at school.;  unprotected sex

records.definition_text: the state of being either male or female
records.learnerexamples_text: What sex is your cat?; Some tests enable you to find out the sex of your baby before it's born.; The teacher gave me the application form about my name, age, sex, nationality and address.

records.definition_text: relating to the activity of sex
records.learnerexamples_text: a sexual relationship; Most people remember their first sexual experience.; Before continuing with the story I would like to remind [you] that having sexual relationships was common to everybody in Brave New World.

records.definition_text: attractive or exciting in a sexual way
records.learnerexamples_text: sexy underwear; He's very sexy.; Richard was only wearing Levis Jean[s] and a white T shirt but looked so sexy and handsome.

records.definition_text: an area where there is no light from the sun and so it is darker and not as hot
records.learnerexamples_text: I'd prefer to sit in the shade.; The sun was hot, and there were no trees to offer us shade.; The children played in/under the shade of a large beach umbrella.; The shade from huge trees kept me cool and fresh.

records.definition_text: a colour, especially when referring to how dark or light it is
records.learnerexamples_text: a pale/dark shade of grey; Not only was it a beautiful day but the sky was a magnificent shade of blue as well.

records.definition_text: a dark area made by something that is stopping the light
records.learnerexamples_text: The tree had cast a long shadow.; The children were playing, jumping on each other's shadows.; Jamie followed his mother around all day like a shadow.; This corner of the room is always in shadow.; Suddenly I saw a shadow and as I turned over I noticed that something was moving in the trees.

records.definition_text: to move backwards and forwards or up and down in quick, short movements, or to make something or someone do this
records.learnerexamples_text: A young boy climbed into the apple tree and shook the branches so that the fruit fell down.; Babies like toys that make a noise when they're shaken.; The explosion shook buildings for miles around.; She shook her hair loose from its ribbon.; Every time one of these big trucks goes through the village, all the houses shake.

records.definition_text: If you are shaking, your body makes quick short movements, or you feel as if it is doing so, because you are frightened or nervous.
records.learnerexamples_text: She was shaking as she opened the letter.; Her voice shook as she spoke about the person who attacked her.; I was shaking in my shoes/boots about having to tell Dad what I'd done.; I was shaking like a leaf before my exam.; She understood that it was absolutely foolish of her to stand [t]here shaking with fear.

records.definition_text: to hold someone's hand and move it up and down when you meet them for the first time, or when you make an agreement with them
records.learnerexamples_text: The two leaders smiled and shook hands for the photographers.; I shook hands with him.; I felt embarras[s]ed when all my friends thought they were my friends, so [they] all sh[ook] hands with them ex[c]ept me.

records.definition_text: to move your head from side to side to mean 'no'
records.learnerexamples_text: I asked him if he wanted to come and he just shook his head.; He just looked at me shaking his head and got into his car and drove off.

records.definition_text: not deep
records.learnerexamples_text: The stream was quite shallow so we were able to walk across it.; She told her children to stay in the shallow end (of the swimming pool).; Fry the onions in a shallow pan.; These beech trees have shallow roots.; A heavy body plunged into the shallow water of harbo[r] No 14.

records.definition_text: the physical form of something made by the line around its outer edge
records.learnerexamples_text: a circular/rectangular shape; You can recognize trees by the shape of their leaves.; Very few people are really happy with their body shape.; These bricks are all different shapes.; Kim's birthday cake was in the shape of a train.

records.definition_text: If two or more people or things share a feeling, quality or experience, they both or all have the same feeling, quality or experience.
records.learnerexamples_text: We share an interest in sailing.; All hospitals share some common characteristics.; I don't share your views/beliefs.; Management and the union both share in the responsibility for the crisis.; She knew that he was the person she wanted to share her life with.

records.definition_text: If two or more people share an activity, they each do some of it
records.learnerexamples_text: Shall we share the driving?; We shared the preparation for the party between us, so it wasn't too much work.; Ask your employer and other colle[a]gues to share the work.

records.definition_text: a part of something that has been divided
records.learnerexamples_text: The total bill comes to £80, so our share is £20.; We must make sure that everyone gets equal shares of the food.; The party's share of the vote fell from 39% to 24%.; She's not doing her share of the work.; We must all accept some share of the responsibility.

records.definition_text: a large fish with very sharp teeth
records.learnerexamples_text: a great white shark; The movie 'Jaws' is about a man-eating shark.; By the way, this ocean was full of sharks, our guide said.

records.definition_text: having a very thin or pointed edge that can cut things
records.learnerexamples_text: a sharp knife; sharp teeth/claws/fingernails; The point of this pencil isn't sharp enough.; My heart was broken by a knife, a sharp, hot knife, but I don't feel pain, I don't feel anything, I just want to die and forget about everything.

records.definition_text: quick to notice and understand things
records.learnerexamples_text: a sharp mind; She is an elderly woman who seems to be very weak but with an extrem[e]ly sharp mind.

records.definition_text: quickly and suddenly
records.learnerexamples_text: Inflation has risen/fallen sharply.; His health improved/deteriorated sharply this week.; In the last few years, the trend of owning a mobile phone has increased sharply.

records.definition_text: to cut hair off your face or body with a razor
records.learnerexamples_text: John has to shave twice a day.; I always shave my legs in the bath.; Do you shave under your arms?; When my dad shaved his beard (off), he looked ten years younger.; The other men shave the man who is getting married.

records.definition_text: a small building, usually made of wood, used for storing things
records.learnerexamples_text: a garden shed; a tool/bicycle shed; It was hidden in a shed that hardly anybody ever entered.

records.definition_text: a large piece of cloth put on a bed to lie on or under
records.learnerexamples_text: I've put clean sheets on the bed.; I have a big bed with silk sheets.

records.definition_text: the hard outer covering of some creatures and of eggs, nuts, or seeds
records.learnerexamples_text: Brazil nuts have very hard shells.; A piece of shell fell into the cake mixture.; the shell of a snail/crab/tortoise; a shell necklace; Mainly I collect books, postcards, dolls, silver bracelets and sea shells.

records.definition_text: a place that protects you from bad weather or danger
records.learnerexamples_text: an bomb shelter; We all ran to hide [in] the little shelter we had built.

records.definition_text: protection from bad weather or danger
records.learnerexamples_text: We took shelter from the rain in a doorway.; John told me it was a [place] where we could find shelter.

records.definition_text: a period of work in a place such as a factory or hospital, or the people who do that work
records.learnerexamples_text: As the night shift leave/leaves, the day shift arrive/arrives.; Are you on the night shift or the day shift ?; I worked there in two shifts, in the mornings and in the evenings, for approximately 8-10 hours a day.

records.definition_text: to produce bright light
records.learnerexamples_text: The sun was shining brightly through the window.; Is that light shining in your eyes?; The weather was good and the sun was shining.

records.definition_text: A shiny surface is bright because it reflects light.
records.learnerexamples_text: beautiful shiny hair; shiny black shoes; a shiny silver dollar; I prefer shiny tops and blue trousers.

records.definition_text: to shake because you are cold or frightened
records.learnerexamples_text: She shivered with cold.; The poor dog - it's shivering!; She was shivering not only because of the cold, but also because she had no idea what she was going to tell him.

records.definition_text: a big, unpleasant surprise
records.learnerexamples_text: We got a nasty shock when he gave us the bill.; Her death came as a terrible shock to him.; They are still in shock from the accident.; I was in shock. I read the letter again and again, the last part of the text said 'Don't forget'.

records.definition_text: to surprise and upset someone
records.learnerexamples_text: The advertisements were designed to shock - that was the whole point of the campaign.; I think it shocks him to hear women talking about sex.; The news of the accident shocked the family deeply.; They hardly could believe it, although that American woman always wants to shock them...

records.definition_text: very surprised and upset
records.learnerexamples_text: After his announcement, there was shocked silence.;  We were shocked to see smoke pouring out of the roof.; I was surprised and shocked.

records.definition_text: offensive, upsetting or immoral
records.learnerexamples_text: The sex scenes in the book were considered very shocking at the time when it was published.; There are few crimes more truly shocking than the murder or abuse of children.; The news was shocking but at the same time this fact will change our life.

records.definition_text: to injure or kill a person or animal by firing a bullet from a gun at them
records.learnerexamples_text: If he's not armed, don't shoot.; The kids were shooting arrows at a target.; She was shot three times in the head.; A policeman was shot dead in the city centre last night.; The troops were told to shoot to kill.

records.definition_text: to try to score points in sports such as football by hitting, kicking, or throwing the ball towards the goal
records.learnerexamples_text: He shot from the middle of the field and still managed to score.; A[fter] I shot my first goal for this team they started to talk to me.

records.definition_text: when a gun is fired, or when someone is injured or killed by a bullet from a gun
records.learnerexamples_text: We heard some shooting in the night.; There have been a number of shootings in the capital this week.; He liked shooting very much and once [he went] [in]to the forest he didn't come back.

records.definition_text: to buy things in shops
records.learnerexamples_text: I like to shop at Harrods for clothes.; If I'm just shopping for food, I tend to go to the local supermarket.; I'd like to go out with you to shop [for] clothes.

records.definition_text: someone who owns or manages a small shop
records.learnerexamples_text: Local shopkeepers say business is good at the moment.; One of the major disadvantages is that the shopkeepers would have to work [until] midnight or perhaps on bank holidays.

records.definition_text: the area of land along the edge of the sea or a lake
records.learnerexamples_text: You can walk for miles along the shore.; The boat was about a mile from/off (the) shore when the engine suddenly died.; We were on the fourth floor, where you can see the se[a] shore and also the mountains behind.

records.definition_text: describes a name that is used as a shorter form of a name
records.learnerexamples_text: Her name's Jo - it's short for Josephine.; Her name's Josephine, or Jo for short.; There is even a strange disease called Chronic Fatigue Syndrom[e] (CFS for short).

records.definition_text: when there is not enough of something
records.learnerexamples_text: There's a shortage of food and shelter in the refugee camps.; The long hot summer has led to serious water shortages.; Due to a shortage of teachers in summer I can [only] take holiday in July.

records.definition_text: soon
records.learnerexamples_text: We will shortly be arriving in King's Cross Station.; I look forward to hear[ing] from you shortly.

records.definition_text: a short time after or before something
records.searchterms_text: shortly;shortly afterwards shortly after/before sth;shortly afterwards; shortly after/before sth;shortly afterwards; shortly after/before sth
records.learnerexamples_text: I got home at midnight and James arrived shortly afterwards.; Shortly after you left, a man came into the office looking for you.; Shortly afterwards, the door bell rang.

records.definition_text: lasting a short time, or relating to a short period of time
