records.learnerexamples_text: short-term memory; a short-term weather forecast; Setting up restricted areas for animals is a nice idea, but due to the overall pol[l]ution, [it is] only a short-term solution.

records.definition_text: when a bullet is fired from a gun
records.learnerexamples_text: He fired four shots at the car as it drove off.; Suddenly he heard a shot and the lights went out.

records.definition_text: when someone tries to score points in sports such as football by hitting or throwing the ball
records.learnerexamples_text: And that was a great shot by Lineker!; Nadal's forehand shot down the line won him the match.; I enjoy this sport because it forces me to improve my self control when playing: if I miss a shot, I have to stay very calm because it's the best way to achieve the next shot.

records.definition_text: a photograph
records.learnerexamples_text: I got/took some really good shots of the harbour at sunset.; [A] few months ago I had [the] chance to work abroad and see some of the Middle Eastern countries, where I took a lot of good shots.

records.definition_text: used to say or ask what is the correct or best thing to do
records.learnerexamples_text: "Should I apologize to him?"; Where should we meet tonight?; There should be an investigation into the cause of the disaster.; I should have written to her but I haven't had any time.; It's getting cold in here. Should I turn the heat up?

records.definition_text: used to say that you expect something to be true or that you expect something to happen
records.learnerexamples_text: My dry cleaning should be ready this afternoon.; If you follow these directions, you shouldn’t have any trouble finding our house.; I wonder what's happened to Annie. She should be here by now.; That should be enough food for five people.; I have invite[d] all his friends, [so] we should be 28 people.

records.definition_text: one of the two parts of your body where your arms join your neck
records.learnerexamples_text: I rested my head on her shoulder.; Then she put her arm round my shoulder and gave me a kiss.; She glanced nervously over her shoulder to make sure no one else was listening.; The name of the movie was Ghost ship. It was a horror movie but it was so boring [that] she slept on my shoulder.

records.definition_text: when you say something very loudly or make a very loud sound with your voice
records.learnerexamples_text: He heard an angry shout.; shouts of anger; The only noise we could hear was the shouts of the hero[e]s fighting with terrible monsters coming from space...

records.definition_text: to give information in a book, on a website, on a piece of equipment, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: The pictures show two types of holiday. Talk to your partner about which you would prefer and why. ; The right-hand dial shows the temperature, and the left-hand one shows the air pressure.; On this map, urban areas are shown in grey.; The latest crime figures show a sharp rise in burglaries.; Secondly, I'd like to tell you that the website is good, but it does not provide all the information we need, [as] it only shows the times of the films for that day and they usually change at the weekends.

records.definition_text: If numbers, results, facts, etc. show something, they prove that it is true.
records.learnerexamples_text: Research shows that 40% of the programme's viewers are aged over 55.; Sales figures showed a significant increase last month.; She has shown herself (to be) a highly competent manager.; His diaries show him to have been an extremely insecure person.; The diaries show (that) he was very insecure.

records.definition_text: to express a feeling so that other people are able to notice it
records.learnerexamples_text: He finds it difficult to show affection.; She showed enormous courage when she rescued him from the fire.; You should show your parents more respect/show more respect to your parents.; I think a face can show so much and some day I [hope] I could be[come] a photographer.

records.definition_text: an event at which a group of similar things are brought together for the public to see
records.learnerexamples_text: a fashion/flower show; There were some amazing new cars at the motor show.; They put on a show of his work at the National Museum of American Art.; I do not know if it is possible to make any change[s], but we saw an ad in "Time Out" magazine last week about a fashion show which we would like to see.

records.definition_text: a short period of rain
records.learnerexamples_text: You're soaked! Did you get caught in the shower?; There will be thundery/wintry showers over many parts of the country.; Well the weather was really good during the morning [but] [there were] some showers during the afternoon.

records.definition_text: to wash standing under a shower
records.learnerexamples_text: We all showered before breakfast.; Singing is a hobby of mine but unfortunately I can only do it when I'm showering or cleaning up my flat.

records.definition_text: to try to make people admire your abilities or achievements in a way which other people find annoying
records.learnerexamples_text: She only bought that sports car to show off and prove she could afford one.; He's always showing off to his classmates.; You can even show off a bit to your relatives and friends.

records.definition_text: to go with someone and show them a place
records.learnerexamples_text: Alejandro offered to show her around Mexico City.; My friend Daniel showed me round the club house.

records.base_text: show sb what to do/how to do sth
records.definition_text: to teach someone how to do something by explaining it or by doing it yourself while they watch
records.searchterms_text: show;show sb what to do/how to do sth;showed;showing;shown;shows
records.learnerexamples_text: She showed me how to use the new computer system.; Have you shown him what to do?; Before the performance I introduced the spectators to their seats and then a[n] instructor showed me how to [operate] the spotlights.

records.definition_text: to arrive somewhere
records.learnerexamples_text: I invited him for eight o'clock, but he didn't show up until nine-thirty.; We were expecting thirty people to come, but half of them never showed up.; I took him to his father and then my friend, Maria, showed up.

records.definition_text: to become smaller, or to make something smaller
records.learnerexamples_text: Your sweater will shrink if you wash it at too high a temperature.; The company's profits have shrunk from £5.5 million to £1.25 million.; After 5 seconds I started shrinking until I was as small as the smallest toe on my foot.

records.definition_text: closed
records.learnerexamples_text: I suspected something was wrong when I noticed her curtains were still shut at lunchtime.

records.definition_text: When a shop, restaurant, etc. is shut, it has stopped serving customers and does not allow people to enter it.
records.learnerexamples_text: The post office will be shut now.; On the advertis[e]ment it also said you could visit [the] restaurant after the show, and that is what I did, but when I got there it was shut for no reason.

records.definition_text: to stop talking or making a noise, or to make someone do this
records.learnerexamples_text: I wish you'd shut up for a moment and listen to what the rest of us have to say.; Just shut up and get on with your work!; My dad never stops talking. It's impossible to shut him up!; You must still remember that time we walked along the street, singing blues and rock, it's incredible the way that people shouted at us to shut up.

records.definition_text: If a computer or machine shuts down or someone shuts it down, it stops operating.
records.searchterms_text: shut;shut (sth) down or shut down (sth);shut sth down or shut down sth
records.learnerexamples_text: Make sure you shut down your computer before you leave.; The crew shut down the right-hand engine of the aircraft.; I was as happy as a lark. I shut down the computer and I called my m[u]m to tell her about the good news.

records.definition_text: If a business or organization shuts down or someone shuts it down, it closes.
records.searchterms_text: shut;shut (sth) down or shut down (sth);shut sth down or shut down sth
records.learnerexamples_text: The company plans to shut down four factories and cut 10 000 jobs.; A great [number] of zoos ought to be shut down.

records.definition_text: not confident, especially about meeting or talking to new people
records.learnerexamples_text: He was too shy to ask her to dance with him.; She gave a shy smile.; Children are often shy of/with people they don't know.; The deer were shy and hid behind some trees.; I was a little shy at first, but I ended up talking too much!

records.definition_text: when you are ill
records.learnerexamples_text: There's a lot of sickness around this winter.; She's had three weeks off for sickness this year.; The simpl[e] joy and happiness will help you to feel in good shape and keep away any sickness.

records.definition_text: the area next to something
records.learnerexamples_text: I have a small table at/by the side of my bed.; He stood at/by her side as she welcomed the guests one by one.; Linda is by my side right now and she asks [me to] send you a warm hug.

records.definition_text: part of a situation that can be considered or dealt with separately
records.learnerexamples_text: She looks after the financial side of things.; Finally, I think for me the most important [thing] is to enjoy life - don't be worried [about] little things and always find the funny side of each situation.

records.definition_text: a part of someone's character
records.learnerexamples_text: She has a very practical side.; In fact the film describes the actions of this politi[c]ian, also saying something not very "Politically Correct", but true: he reveals that no one is always good, everyone has a dark hidden side.

records.definition_text: one of the people or groups who are arguing, fighting, or competing
records.learnerexamples_text: Whose side is he on?; Whenever we argue he always takes Alice's side .; This is a war which neither side can win.; Don't be angry with me - I'm on your side.; I hope you'll be on my side.

records.definition_text: a way of considering something, especially when there is disagreement about it
records.learnerexamples_text: There are at least two sides to every question.; I've listened to your side of the story, but I still think you were wrong to do what you did.; This shows the other side of technology.

records.definition_text: If two things or people are side by side, they are next to each other.
records.learnerexamples_text: We sat side by side on the sofa.; It is not rare to see two people walking side by side, both talking on the phone.

records.definition_text: to breathe out slowly and noisily, often because you are annoyed or unhappy
records.learnerexamples_text: She sighed deeply and sat down.; "I wish he was here," she sighed.; Having solid ground beneath her feet again she sighed with relief for having survived this adventure.

records.definition_text: the sound that is made when someone sighs
records.learnerexamples_text: He read the letter and gave a deep sigh.; I entered the house with a deep sigh!

records.definition_text: the ability to see
records.learnerexamples_text: If your sight is poor, you should not drive a car.; The old woman has lost her sight.; She had lost her sight although doctors didn't know if it was forever.

records.definition_text: the area that it is possible for you to see
records.learnerexamples_text: You should always keep sight of your bags while you're at the airport.; I dare not let the children out of my sight in this park.; The police officer was hidden out of sight behind a tree.; The castle came into sight as we went round a bend in the road.; We're looking for a house which is within sight of the mountains.

records.definition_text: something which shows that something is happening or that it exists or is true
records.learnerexamples_text: Flowers are the first sign of Spring.; His inability to handle the situation is a sure sign of weakness.; The fact that he's eating more is a sign that he's feeling better.; There's no sign of progress with the building work.; Billy's work at school has shown signs of improvement this year.

records.definition_text: a movement you make to give someone information or tell them what to do
records.learnerexamples_text: She pointed to her watch as a sign that it was getting late and she wanted to leave.; She made/gave a sign to her husband to stop talking.; The priest made the sign of the cross when he entered the church.; She looked at Paul and made a strange sign with her fingers.

records.definition_text: a written or printed mark which has a standard meaning
records.learnerexamples_text: + and - are mathematical signs.; £ is the sign for the British pound.

records.definition_text: to write your name on something to show that you wrote/painted, etc. it or to show that you agree to it
records.learnerexamples_text: to sign a letter/form/cheque/contract/agreement; Sign here, please.; He signed his name at the end of the letter.; He signed himself 'Mark Taylor'.; She said the painting was by Picasso, but it wasn't signed.

records.definition_text: a movement, light, or sound which gives information, or tells people what to do
records.learnerexamples_text: At a signal from their teacher, the children all held up their flags.; Don't move until I give the signal.; The firework was a signal that the festival had started.; The police officer gave us a signal to stop.; The signal for a race to start is often the firing of a gun.

records.definition_text: a series of light waves or sound waves which are sent to a radio, television, mobile phone, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: I can't get a phone signal here.; On the other hand you can face problems with signal transmission.

records.definition_text: your name written by yourself, always in the same way, usually to show that something has been written or agreed by you
records.learnerexamples_text: Please put your signature in this box.; I thought it was a joke but when I saw the signature I knew it was for real.

records.definition_text: important or noticeable
records.learnerexamples_text: There has been a significant increase in the number of women students in recent years.; These measures will save a significant amount of money.; The talks between the USA and Russia were very significant for the relationship between the two countries.; One of the most significant invention[s] is [the] computer.

records.definition_text: in a way that is easy to see or by a large amount
records.learnerexamples_text: My piano playing has improved significantly since I've had a new teacher.; Also, with today's machines, factories have significantly increased their production.

records.definition_text: a sign by the side of the road that gives information about routes and distances
records.learnerexamples_text: Look out for the signpost to the airport.; There were no signposts and there was no one to ask where he could find a place to stay.

records.definition_text: to arrange to do an organized activity
records.learnerexamples_text: I've signed up for evening classes at the local college.; If you are interested in other activities, just sign up for them [on] the notice board.

records.definition_text: when there is no sound
records.learnerexamples_text: The three men ate in silence.; A loud crash of thunder broke the silence of the night.; I suppose that you want to relax [o]n your holiday and so I suggest you visit the Alps - [some] beautiful countryside where you can relax, walk and enjoy the silence and nature.

records.definition_text: a period of time in which there is complete quiet or no speaking
records.learnerexamples_text: There were long silences during the discussion.; The progress of the story is very slow, but the author is descri[b]ing hard conditions, hard characters [and] long silences, which is quite t[y]pical of his way [of writing].

records.definition_text: without any sound
records.learnerexamples_text: The empty house was completely silent.; The countryside, like Chianti, is peaceful and silent.

records.definition_text: without talking
records.learnerexamples_text: She whispered a silent prayer that her wounded brother would not die.; The police officer told the criminal that he had the right to remain silent.; The minister was silent on/about his plans for the future.; Arthur has always been the strong, silent type.; When they were there, Aunt Patience was obliged by her husband to go to her room and remain silent.

records.definition_text: without making any noise
records.learnerexamples_text: She wept silently as she read the letter.; He silently vowed to take revenge.; After waiting silently for two minutes, she dropped the phone.

records.definition_text: a type of cloth which is light and smooth
records.learnerexamples_text: a silk dress; a silk shirt; Normally, I would prefer my blouses to be made of cotton or silk, as these materials make me [feel] comfortable.

records.definition_text: showing little thought or judgment
records.learnerexamples_text: Don't do that, you silly boy!; a silly mistake; It was silly of you to go out in the sun without a hat.; I feel silly in this dress.; They had some very silly games.

records.definition_text: small and not important
records.learnerexamples_text: She gets upset over such silly things.; Pe[o]ple are so worried about silly things, about how to make money or how to be popular and they forget about what really matters.

records.definition_text: If something or someone is similar to another thing or person, they have many things the same, although they are not exactly the same.
records.learnerexamples_text: My father and I have similar views on politics.; I bought some new shoes which are very similar to a pair I had before.; Paul is very similar in appearance to his brother.; I can understand how you are feeling because at our age, every teenager has similar problems.

records.definition_text: when two things or people are similar, or a way in which they are similar
records.learnerexamples_text: I can see the similarity between you and your mother.; The book bears several striking similarities to last year's bestseller.; Another similarity between the two was their appearance.

records.definition_text: plain or not complicated
records.learnerexamples_text: a simple life; a simple black dress ; We had a simple meal of bread and cheese.; You can eat simple food and drink good local wine.

records.definition_text: used to describe the one important fact, truth, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: We didn't go swimming for the simple reason that the water was too cold.; I'm very fond of working with animals, and the simple reason is that I'm plan[n]ing to become a vet.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize what you are saying
records.learnerexamples_text: We simply don't have the time.; You look simply beautiful in that dress.; The hunger in parts of Africa is terrible - there's (quite) simply no other word for it.; It's said that most of the centre's sports facilities are very expensive, [but] that is simply not true.

records.definition_text: only
records.learnerexamples_text: A lot of people miss out on this opportunity simply because they don't know about it.; I am very interested in fashion, simply because it is a style, an attitude, a way of life.

records.definition_text: in a way which is not complicated or difficult to understand
records.learnerexamples_text: He explained it as simply as he could, but the class still didn't understand.; Try to organize your work as simply as possible.

records.definition_text: at the same time
records.learnerexamples_text: Two children answered the teacher's question simultaneously.; The floods of information pour towards you and go through your brain simultaneously.

records.definition_text: from a time in the past until a later time or until now
records.learnerexamples_text: He's been much happier since he started his new job.; I've known Tim since he was seven.; I was really surprised when I read the e-mail because I haven't heard from you since I visited you last year.

records.definition_text: from a time in the past until a later time or until now
records.learnerexamples_text: Emma went to work in New York a year ago, and we haven't seen her since.; He started working for the company when he left school, and has been there ever since.; I've long since forgotten any Latin I ever learned.; It was my grandmother who introduced me to teddy bears and she wanted me to love them as she did. When she died, I got all her bears and have been taking care of them ever since.

records.definition_text: because
records.learnerexamples_text: Since we've got a few minutes to wait for the train, let's have a cup of coffee.; Since my mother has surgery tomorrow, I will not [be able to] come to your class.

records.definition_text: only one
records.learnerexamples_text: There was a single light in the corner of the room.;  Not a single person offered to help her.; You haven't been listening to a single word I've been saying.; The night was calm and not a single sound was disturbing her.

records.definition_text: a ticket for a journey that is from one place to another but not back again
records.learnerexamples_text: Could I have a single to Edinburgh, please?

records.definition_text: someone who has a child or children, but no wife, husband or partner living with them
records.learnerexamples_text: Many single parents find it difficult to get a job.; The number of single-parent families dependent on the state has risen enormously in recent years.; She's a single parent, with 3 children from Australia but she's gorgeous.

records.definition_text: a single ticket takes you to a place, but not back again
records.learnerexamples_text: I've only got a single ticket.; Suddenly I was asked to show my single ticket.

records.definition_text: to go down or make something go down below the surface of water or a soft substance and not come back up
records.learnerexamples_text: The Titanic was a passenger ship which sank to the bottom of the ocean in 1912.; The legs of the garden chair sank into the soft ground.; Enemy aircraft sank two battleships.; The dog sank its teeth into the ball and ran off with it.; They w[ere] travelling on the very big ship called "Titanic", [and] the ship sank.

records.definition_text: to move or make something move to a lower position or level
records.learnerexamples_text: The sun glowed red as it sank slowly below the horizon.; Student numbers have sunk considerably this year.; Dora's face grew pale and she sank [into] a chair.

records.definition_text: used as a formal and polite way of speaking to a man, especially one who you are providing a service to or who is in a position of authority
records.learnerexamples_text: Would you like to see the menu, sir?; "Did you hear what I said?" "Yes, sir."; Suddenly, the man with the hat, sunglasses, and mask came to me and sa[id] "sir, what is your name?"

records.definition_text: a woman married to your brother, or the sister of your husband or wife
records.learnerexamples_text: My sister-in-law is a great cook. ; So, I and a sister-in-law had to stay with our little sons without any entertainment at the hotel.

records.definition_text: to take a test or exam
records.learnerexamples_text: I had to sit an exam the next day.; Visiting you in July is just perfect because schools will have closed and I will have already sat my exams at the English school.

records.definition_text: a place where something is, was, or will be built, or where something happened, is happening, or will happen
records.learnerexamples_text: a building site; The council haven't yet chosen the site for the new hospital.; This is the site of the accident.; I work as a civil engineer on a site.

records.definition_text: the set of things that are happening and the conditions that exist at a particular time and place
records.learnerexamples_text: the economic/political situation; Her news put me in a difficult situation.; "Would you get involved in a fight?" "It would depend on the situation."; I'll worry about it if/when/as the situation arises.; It was a weird situation.

records.definition_text: to sit or stand with your body vertical
records.learnerexamples_text: Stand up straight and put your shoulders back!; She tried to sit up straight and quickly realised all her mus[c]les were stiff from non activity.

records.definition_text: to move using skates
records.learnerexamples_text: The ice on the river is thick enough to skate on/across/over.; We skated [for] two or three hours.

records.definition_text: the structure made of all the bones in the body of a person or animal

records.learnerexamples_text: She was invited to speak at a conference in Madrid.; [O]n behalf of all its members, I would like to invite you to speak at one of our meetings.

records.definition_text: to talk about something
records.learnerexamples_text: He refused to speak about the matter in public.; In the interview she spoke of her sadness at her mother's death.; They filmed the headmistress of our school. She spoke about the school's activities.

records.definition_text: someone who can speak English/French, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: He's a fluent Russian speaker.; I think I'm going to be an English speaker sooner than I expected.

records.definition_text: someone who makes a speech to a group of people
records.learnerexamples_text: a good public speaker; Please join with me in thanking our guest speaker tonight.; The speaker told me many things about feeding birds.

records.definition_text: to speak in a louder voice so that people can hear you
records.learnerexamples_text: Could you speak up? We can't hear at the back.; First of all, I read it far too fast and in a voice that was hardly a[udi]ble, and people started to shout that they couldn't hear me and that I should speak up; it was terrible!

records.definition_text: different from normal things, or used for a particular purpose
records.learnerexamples_text: You need to use a special kind of paint.; Some of the children have special educational needs.; Full details of the election results will be published in a special edition of tomorrow's newspaper.; Firefighters use special breathing equipment in smoky buildings.; He stepped into a small, handmade, wooden canoe - it['s] call[ed] Hakaro. It's a special kind of canoe.

records.definition_text: treatment that is better than usual
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't expect special treatment - I just want to be treated fairly.; As you know, an Austin Healey needs special treatment.

records.definition_text: someone who has a lot of experience, knowledge, or skill in a particular subject
records.learnerexamples_text: a software specialist; She's a specialist in modern French literature.; She's a specialist in childhood illnesses.; a leading cancer/eye specialist; Now, fully equipped and powerful computers can be so small and mobile that some specialists predict that new devices will replace [the] book.

records.definition_text: to spend most of your time studying one particular subject or doing one type of business
records.learnerexamples_text: She's hired a lawyer who specializes in divorce cases.; a restaurant that specialises in seafood; I enjoy working in general medicine, but I hope to be able to specialize in the future.; Some specialise in acting and others [work] back stage like adjusting the sound or light and preparing the outfits.

records.definition_text: for a particular purpose
records.learnerexamples_text: I came here specially to see you.; She has a wheelchair that was specially made for her.; The opera 'Aida' was specially written for the opening of the Cairo opera house in 1871.; I'm thinking [of] get[ting] a beautiful long black wool[l]en coat specially made for you.

records.definition_text: a price which is lower than usual
records.learnerexamples_text: There's a special offer on sunglasses this week.; Unfortunately, they have stopped their special offer "1 month [for Euro] 100" and I know that you want to stay fit. As soon as they make a new offer I will let you know and then you [can] join us!

records.definition_text: a group of plants or animals which share similar characteristics
records.learnerexamples_text: Mountain gorillas are an endangered species.; Over a hundred species of insect are found in this area.; Then I wrote an article about saving endangered species.

records.definition_text: used to refer to a particular thing and not something general
records.learnerexamples_text: English for specific purposes; The disease seems to be specific to certain types of plant.; Is there anything specific you want from the shops?; We need to see animals, study them, and in some cases find out why specific types of animals can't live in the nature which we have spoiled.

records.definition_text: to state or describe something clearly and exactly
records.learnerexamples_text: He said we should meet but didn't specify a time.; The peace treaty clearly specifies the terms for the withdrawal of troops.; The newspaper report did not specify how the men were killed.; My contract specifies (that) I must give a month's notice if I leave my job.; The loan must be repaid within a specified period/by a specified date.

records.definition_text: extremely good, exciting, or surprising
records.learnerexamples_text: a spectacular view; The show was a spectacular success.; He scored a spectacular goal in the second half.; There was a spectacular sunset last night.; It is located in a tall building and has a spectacular view.

records.definition_text: someone who watches an event, sport, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: They won 4-0 in front of over 40 000 cheering spectators.; At midnight sharp, fireworks covered the concert hall and I, as well as the rest of [the] spectators, felt the excitement and delight I've never felt before.

records.definition_text: someone's ability to talk, or an example of someone talking
records.learnerexamples_text: Children usually develop speech in the second year of life.; People who suffer a stroke may experience a loss of speech.; Some expressions are used more in speech than in writing.; The reason why I de[c]ide[d] to join [the] English class is because of my English speech, I should talk more fluently but I'm trying my best.

records.definition_text: a formal talk given usually to a large number of people on a special occasion
records.learnerexamples_text: I had to give/make a speech at my brother's wedding.; The Governor of New York delivered a rousing speech to the national convention.; He gave the after-dinner speech .; Did you hear her acceptance speech at the Oscars ceremony?; I suggest that if you want to invite someone to give a speech, you have to invite athletes.

records.definition_text: very fast movement
records.learnerexamples_text: I get a real thrill from speed.; He put on a sudden burst of speed.; Both cars were travelling at speed when the accident happened.; Every summer I go to watersports because I like water. I'm very good at swimming and I like the speed of some watersports.

records.definition_text: how fast something moves or happens
records.learnerexamples_text: high/low speed; He was travelling at a speed of 90 mph.; The car has a top speed of 155 miles per hour.; You should lower/reduce your speed as you approach a junction.; On a clear, straight road you can gather/pick up speed.

records.definition_text: a substance made from a plant, which is used to give a special taste to food
records.learnerexamples_text: Cinnamon, ginger and cloves are all spices.; Spices are widely used in South Asian cooking.; It's very delicious with some spices and many kinds of salad.

records.definition_text: containing spices which have a strong, hot flavour
records.learnerexamples_text: Do you like spicy food?; I don't like spicy food, it's not good for my stomach.

records.definition_text: a small creature with eight long legs which catches insects in a web
records.learnerexamples_text: a spider's web; She is afraid of spiders.

records.definition_text: to pour liquid or another substance somewhere without intending to, or to fall or flow out of a container in a way that is not intended
records.learnerexamples_text: I spilt coffee on my silk shirt.; You've spilt something down your tie.; Let's see if I can pour the juice into the glass without spilling it.; He dropped a bag of sugar and it spilt all over the floor.; Then I'm going to buy [a] new [r]ug, because [a] few days ago, I spilled [some] ju[i]ce.

records.definition_text: a vegetable with large, dark green leaves and a strong taste
records.learnerexamples_text: spinach lasagne/salad; The embarrassing moment came when I saw the first dish: carrots with spinach!

records.definition_text: the way people think and feel about something
records.learnerexamples_text: The players have a very strong team spirit.; As rock musicians in the 1960s, they were very much part of the spirit of the age/times.; We acted in a spirit of cooperation.; In addition to [that], you should invite athletes who have experience in sports to speak about team spirit and the role that sports [have] in our life.

records.definition_text: a form of a dead person such as a ghost
records.learnerexamples_text: an evil spirit; I thought the house could have ghosts or spirits and because of this, I tried to convince myself that it ha[d] been [my] imagination, but suddenly the lights went out.

records.definition_text: relating to deep feelings and beliefs, especially religious beliefs
records.learnerexamples_text: Traditional ways of life fulfilled both economic and spiritual needs.; I'd like to get in contact with the amazing spiritual life in [India]. There is no other country in the world with so many different religions and sects.

records.definition_text: If a liquid splashes or you splash a liquid, drops of it hit or fall on something.
records.learnerexamples_text: Water was splashing from a hole in the roof.; Unfortunately some paint splashed onto the rug.; She splashed her face with cold water.; But in some towns we stayed [in], there were public swimming pools so we could even splash in the water.

records.definition_text: the sound of something falling into or moving in water
records.learnerexamples_text: They sat listening to the splash of raindrops on the lake.; [M]y friend, the mechanic Alex, heard a strang[e] noise, a very powerful splash in the sea, [and] a lot of water came into the boat.

records.definition_text: to move in water so that drops of it go in all directions
records.learnerexamples_text: The children splashed about in the puddles.; So we were splashing around and then went to dry ourselves.

records.definition_text: to divide into smaller parts or groups, or to divide something into smaller parts or groups
records.learnerexamples_text: The prize was split between Susan and Kate.; Split the aubergines in half and cover with breadcrumbs.; The teacher split the children (up) into three groups.; In my opinion we might just split a full-time salary.

records.definition_text: If two people who have a romantic relationship split up, they finish their relationship.
records.learnerexamples_text: She's just split up with her boyfriend.; I asked her about the family and about her. She had recently split up with her boyfriend, Joe.

records.definition_text: to stop something from being enjoyable or successful
records.learnerexamples_text: He tried not to let the bad news spoil his evening.; I haven't seen the film, so don't spoil it for me by telling me what happens.; You'll spoil your appetite for dinner if you have a cake now.; And perhaps it [will] rain and spoil your holiday.

records.definition_text: to give money to someone to support an activity, event, or organization, sometimes as a way to advertise your company or product
records.learnerexamples_text: The team is sponsored by JVC, so the players wear the letters JVC on their shirts.; Eva said she was doing a ten-mile walk for charity and asked if I'd sponsor her for £1 a mile.; The whole [event] is organized by university students and is sponsored by local firms.

records.definition_text: a person or organization that gives money to support an activity, event, etc
records.learnerexamples_text: All the major theatres now have sponsors, especially for high-cost productions.; Last but not least I am also very keen o[n] supporting the club in general, like finding a sponsor or becoming a member of the board.

records.definition_text: relating to sports
records.learnerexamples_text: sports equipment; He only reads the sports section of the newspaper.; You should go there because in a big school there are more possibilities of making new friendships and you can choose [from] a wide range of sports activities.

records.definition_text: a small, round mark which is a different colour to the surface it is on
records.learnerexamples_text: He had a spot of grease on his tie.; I wore that skirt with the green spots.; This lamp is green with yellow spots on it and in my opinion it's perfect for my room.

records.definition_text: a place
records.learnerexamples_text: This looks like a nice spot for a picnic.; Lake Frene is just a lake, there's nothing to do and it's a crowded spot.

records.definition_text: an unpleasant, small, red mark on your skin
records.learnerexamples_text: He suffered badly with spots as a teenager.

records.definition_text: to see or notice something or someone
records.learnerexamples_text: I've just spotted Malcolm - he's over there, near the entrance.; If you spot any mistakes in the article just mark them with a pencil.; The police spotted him driving a stolen car.; I soon spotted what was wrong with the printer.; The policewoman spotted that I hadn't got my seat belt on and signalled me to stop.

records.definition_text: liquid in a container which forces it out in small drops
records.learnerexamples_text: hair spray; spray paint; Actually, there was an attempt to cut down on using and producing sprays which destroy the ozon[e] layer.

records.definition_text: to force liquid out of a container in many small drops
records.learnerexamples_text: The fields are sprayed with pesticides.; She sprayed a little perfume on her wrists.; Vandals had sprayed graffiti on the wall.; I quickly helped [the] others to decorate the hall - we blew up as many balloons as we c[ould] and sprayed them with gold and silver.

records.definition_text: If information spreads, or if someone spreads it, it is communicated to many people.
records.learnerexamples_text: News of his victory spread quickly.; Have you been spreading gossip about them again?; The news spread all over the village.

records.definition_text: to gradually affect a larger area
records.learnerexamples_text: The fire spread very rapidly because of the strong wind.; It started off as cancer of the liver but it spread to other areas of the body.; It seemed that the fire might spread more.

records.definition_text: to cover an area
records.learnerexamples_text: The suburbs spread for miles in every direction.; Our offices are spread (out) over a very wide area.; It has about 500 [in]habitants, who live in 128 houses, which are spread over a big area.

records.definition_text: when something moves to cover a larger area or affect a larger number of people
records.learnerexamples_text: Jazz records fostered the spread of American culture.; More should be done to stop the spread of this disease.; It is true that these days people have much more choice in entertain[ment], the spread of computers and video games is just one example.

records.definition_text: If people spread out, they move from being close together in a group to being in different places across a larger area.
records.learnerexamples_text: They spread out to search the whole area.; They don't dare to spread out in the space.

records.definition_text: a chart produced on a computer which helps you to do business calculations and planning
records.learnerexamples_text: She prepared a spreadsheet with the new sales information.; I would be very interested in joining your club, in order to learn how to use basic software like word processing, spreadsheet or database software.

records.definition_text: someone who secretly tries to discover information about a person, country, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: His father was a British spy.; It's a spy story.

records.definition_text: to push someone or something into a small space
records.learnerexamples_text: The kids were all squashed into the back seat.; My idea of fun is not getting up at seven o'clock in the morning to take a bus where we are squashed by lots of rude people we don't even know.

records.definition_text: to crush something into a flat shape
records.learnerexamples_text: He accidentally sat on her hat and squashed it.

records.definition_text: a sport in which two people hit a small rubber ball against the four walls of a room
records.learnerexamples_text: a game of squash; a squash court/racket; In the club you can play golf, tennis, squash and football.

records.definition_text: to press something firmly
records.learnerexamples_text: She squeezed his hand and said goodbye.; Cut the lemon in half and squeeze the juice into the bowl.; Once he had finished cleaning the floor, he squeezed the cloth out.; He reloaded the gun, took aim and then squeezed the trigger.; It must have been nine o'clock and I was there, sitting [i]n my armchair, squeezing a cushion in my arms.

records.definition_text: to succeed in getting someone or something into a small space or object, often by pushing or forcing
records.searchterms_text: squeeze;squeeze (sb/sth) in/squeeze (sb/sth) into sth;squeeze (sb/sth) in/squeeze (sb/sth) into sth ;squeeze sb/sth in/squeeze sb/sth into sth;squeeze sb/sth in/squeeze sb/sth into sth
records.learnerexamples_text: The car's quite full, but we could manage to squeeze another couple of people in.; I must have put on a lot of weight over Christmas because I can only just squeeze into my jeans.; At the end of the day, I would not only be carrying [a] pile of shopping bags but also trying to squeeze in between other passengers on the train on my way home.

records.definition_text: to push a knife into someone
records.learnerexamples_text: She was stabbed in the arm.; The victim had been stabbed to death.; She raised the knife high in the air and stabbed it right into her stomach.

records.definition_text: a period of development, or a particular time in a process
records.learnerexamples_text: The project is in its final stages and should be completed by August.; They did the last stage of their journey on foot.; Our marriage is going through a difficult stage at the moment.; Their youngest child is at the stage where she can say individual words but not full sentences.; I'm not tired at the moment but I will need a rest at some stage during the walk.

records.definition_text: a dirty mark on something that is difficult to remove
records.learnerexamples_text: a blood/grass stain; You can remove a red wine stain from a carpet by sprinkling salt over it.; I realised that I had a stain on my trousers.

records.definition_text: a large table or a small shop with an open front from which goods are sold in a public place
records.learnerexamples_text: In the village market, the stalls are piled high with local vegetables.; You know, there's a big commercial square near my house where traders, along with shops, set up stalls every day and sell an enormous variety of lifestyle products ranging from CDs and instruments to furniture and clothes.

records.definition_text: to put a mark on an object either by printing on it or pushing into it with a small tool
records.learnerexamples_text: It is necessary to stamp your passport.; Every carton of yoghurt is stamped with a sell-by date.; There was only a small sign stamped on the door, saying that it was "closed for repairs".

records.definition_text: a level of quality, especially a level that is acceptable
records.learnerexamples_text: a high standard of service; low safety standards; His work was below standard.; She sets very high standards for herself.; This essay is not of an acceptable standard - do it again.

records.definition_text: usual rather than special, especially when thought of as being correct or acceptable
records.learnerexamples_text: White is the standard colour for this model of refrigerator.; These are standard procedures for handling radioactive waste.; The metre is the standard unit for measuring length in the SI system.; It should be a standard price.

records.definition_text: how much money and comfort someone has
records.learnerexamples_text: a low/high standard of living; I think we would have a better standard of living if we had this situation.

records.definition_text: to move a short distance away from something or someone
records.learnerexamples_text: Please stand back - then all of you will be able to see what I'm doing.

records.definition_text: to continue to support or help someone who is in a difficult situation
records.learnerexamples_text: She has vowed to stand by her husband during his trial.; And I promise I'll stand by you.

records.definition_text: to support or represent a particular idea or set of ideas
records.learnerexamples_text: This party stands for low taxes and individual freedom.; The Brandenburger Tor stands for freedom and unity.

records.definition_text: If one or more letters stand for a word or name, they are the first letter or letters of that word or name and they represent it
records.learnerexamples_text: 'GMT' stands for Greenwich Mean Time.

records.definition_text: to be very easy to see or notice
records.learnerexamples_text: The bright blue letters really stand out on the page.; Why wasn't that money spent in trying to make them more bearable to [look at], [rather] than making them stand out even more?

records.definition_text: to be much better than other similar things or people
records.learnerexamples_text: One candidate stood out from the rest.; Those small fishing villages will always stand out in my memory.

records.definition_text: to be in or to put something in a particular place or position
records.searchterms_text: stand;stand (sth) in/against/by, etc. sth;stand sth in/against/by etc sth;stand sth in/against/by, etc. sth;standing;stands;stood
records.learnerexamples_text: His walking stick stood by the door.; You'll have to stand the sofa on its end to get it through the door.; The room was empty except for a wardrobe standing in one corner.; As he stepped forward I knelt down and pulled his leg, so that he fell over and hit a small table standing beside the sofa.

records.definition_text: to defend or support a particular idea or a person who is being criticized or attacked
records.searchterms_text: stand;stand up for sth/sb;stand up for sth/sb
records.learnerexamples_text: It's high time we all stood up for our rights around here.; Don't be bullied, learn to stand up for yourself and what you believe in.; He decides to stand up for black rights and becomes an important leader.

records.base_text: stand up sb or stand sb up
records.definition_text: to fail to meet someone you have arranged a romantic meeting with
records.searchterms_text: stand;stand up sb or stand sb up
records.learnerexamples_text: I was starting to think I'd been stood up when he arrived.

records.definition_text: If a film, play, etc. stars someone, or if someone stars in a film, play, etc., they are the main actor in it.
records.learnerexamples_text: Ben Kingsley starred in the film 'Gandhi'.; Fowles's novel 'The French Lieutenant's Woman' was turned into a film starring Meryl Streep.; As we both love romantic comedy, we decided to see Notting Hill [together], which starred Julia Roberts and Hugh Grant.

records.definition_text: to look at someone or something for a long time and not move your eyes
records.learnerexamples_text: Don't stare at people like that, it's rude.; Chuck sat quietly for hours staring into the distance, thinking of what might have been.; David had seen her once before in a park, staring at him.

records.definition_text: to begin to happen or to make something begin to happen
records.learnerexamples_text: A new series of wildlife programmes has started on Monday evenings.; Police believe the fire was started by arsonists.; The Council has started another programme as well which calls people to collect the rubbish in their own street one weekend in every month.

records.definition_text: If a business or other organization starts, or if someone starts one, it is created and starts to operate.
records.learnerexamples_text: She started her own software company.; A lot of new restaurants have started up in the region.; It was the first time in many years he had the opportunity or time to think over his situation and life. He had started his company fifteen years ago and had been successful.

records.definition_text: If you start a machine or an engine, you switch it on, and if a machine or engine starts, it begins to work.
records.learnerexamples_text: The car wouldn't start.; Do you know how to start the lawn mower?; The car would not start and it was impossible to get a taxi because it was Saturday evening, so the only thing we could do was to run all the way to the school.

records.definition_text: the beginning of something
records.learnerexamples_text: We were doubtful about the product's usefulness from the start.; They announced the start of a new commercial venture.; The weather was good at the start of the week.; The event got off to a shaky/poor start with the stage lights failing in the first few minutes.; That was a bad start [to] my holidays!

records.definition_text: to begin by doing something, or to make something begin by doing something
records.searchterms_text: start;start (sth) off or start off(sth);start sth off or start offsth
records.learnerexamples_text: She started off the meeting with the monthly sales report.; I'd like to start off by thanking you all for coming today.; We started off the trip by driving to the foot of the mountain, where there was a village.

records.definition_text: ill or dying because there is not enough food
records.l_topic_text_text: body and health, food and drink
records.learnerexamples_text: starving people; What shocked me most was the misery and poverty: thousands of homeless people roaming the streets starving and cold.

records.definition_text: very hungry
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm absolutely starving.; I've always been greedy, but [at] that moment, while my Chemistry teacher was explaining a difficult lesson, I was really starving.

records.definition_text: the condition that something or someone is in
records.learnerexamples_text: The building is in a terrible state.; She was found wandering in a confused state (of mind).; Give me the keys - you're in no fit state to drive.; After the accident I was in a state of shock.; I came home to an unhappy state of affairs.

records.definition_text: to officially say or write something
records.learnerexamples_text: Our warranty clearly states the limits of our liability.; Union members stated (that) they were unhappy with the proposal.; Please state why you wish to apply for this grant.; Children in the stated areas were at risk from a lack of food, the report said.; Dear Mr Thomas, I've read your advertis[e]ment in [the] last issue of "The Traveller", [where] you state that you are looking for people to work on your campsites with English-speaking tourists.

records.definition_text: provided, created or done by the state
records.learnerexamples_text: state education/industries; state control; state funding/pensions; In general, the rules at private schools are much [strict]er than the ones at state schools.

records.definition_text: something that someone says or writes officially
records.learnerexamples_text: The government is expected to issue a statement about the investigation to the press.; He produced a signed statement from the prisoner.; We were not surprised by their statement that the train services would be reduced.; Dear Editor Referring to your article of today, I want to correct some statements [made].

records.definition_text: a company that broadcasts television or radio programmes
records.learnerexamples_text: a radio/television station; The reception is not very good - try to tune in to another station.; Last week I was [listen]ing to my favorite radio station and they announced a new sports club.

records.definition_text: a collection of facts in the form of numbers that shows information about something
records.learnerexamples_text: Statistics show/suggest that women live longer than men.; According to official statistics, the Japanese work longer hours than workers in most other industrialized countries.; According to statistics based on the questionnair[e], the majority of students feel the most enthusiasm for [their] English class.

records.definition_text: a model that looks like a person or animal, usually made from stone or metal
records.learnerexamples_text: a statue of a boy; They planned to put up/erect a statue to the President.; After, we passed in front of the statue of the president.

records.definition_text: to continue to be in a particular state
records.learnerexamples_text: The supermarket stays open late.; I was tired and couldn't stay awake.; Put a lid on the pan so the food will stay hot.; They stayed friends after their divorce.; Some people prefer to stay dry [rather] than be caught by the rain.

records.definition_text: a period of time that you spend in a place
records.learnerexamples_text: Did you enjoy your stay in Tokyo?; Dear Candie, I have just arrived here on my holiday. I'm in Cannes, in the south of France. [I]t's a lovely place, [and] I'm enjoying my stay so much.

records.definition_text: to not leave a place when other people leave it
records.learnerexamples_text: He stayed behind after class to speak to the teacher.

records.definition_text: to stay in your home
records.learnerexamples_text: Let's stay in tonight and watch a video.; I went with my friend, Marina, because she was not having classes any more, and she was bored of staying in [and] doing nothing.

records.definition_text: to not come home at night, or to go home late
records.learnerexamples_text: Our cat usually stays out at night.; My mum won't let me stay out late.; Firstly, I like it so much because we have no school and we can stay out for as long as we want.

records.definition_text: to spend the night somewhere instead of returning to your home or continuing your journey
records.learnerexamples_text: Why don't you stay over and drive back in the morning? ; We stay[ed] over in a hotel and the next morning Tom brought me home.

records.definition_text: to go to bed later than usual
records.learnerexamples_text: We stayed up (late) to watch a film.; In Vegas, we were staying up all night gambling.

records.definition_text: at a gradual, regular rate
records.learnerexamples_text: Prices have increased steadily since the war.;  In the past people didn't read books all the time. Neither did their kids at school. Today they read even less books but the number of copied and read articles or book extracts ha[s] increased steadily.

records.definition_text: happening at a gradual, regular rate
records.learnerexamples_text: The procession moved through the streets at a steady pace.; Orders for new ships are rising, after several years of steady decline.; Over the last 10 years, he has produced a steady flow/stream of articles and papers.; Progress has been slow but steady.; There is also a steady rise in underweight [young girls] today.

records.definition_text: still and not shaking
records.learnerexamples_text: You need steady hands to be a dentist.; Make sure you hold the ladder steady.; I know very well you have steady nerves but what is strong can turn weak as well.

records.definition_text: the ability to be calm in difficult situations
records.learnerexamples_text: You need a cool head and steady nerves for this job.; I know very well you have steady nerves but what is strong can become weak as well.

records.definition_text: the hot gas that is produced when water boils
records.learnerexamples_text: Steam rose from the simmering stew.; a steam engine; the age of steam; The pump is driven by steam.; I've been interested in trains, in particular steam trains, since my childhood.

records.definition_text: a very strong metal made from iron, used for making knives, machines, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: steel pipes; a stainless steel sink; The object that I would choose is without any doubt my Katana, my Japanese Sword. It is a weapon that reminds me of my childhood games. I also like the form, and the cool steel of the blade.

records.definition_text: A steep slope, hill, etc. rises quickly.
records.learnerexamples_text: a steep slope; It's a steep climb to the top of the mountain, but the view is worth it.; The castle is set on a steep hill/hillside.; But the slope was terribly steep and I didn't dare to ski down.

records.definition_text: to control the direction of a vehicle
records.learnerexamples_text: She carefully steered the car around the potholes.; This car is very easy to steer.; After an hour she could keep [her] balance but she still had problems steering, but that didn't matter.

records.definition_text: a wheel that you turn to control the direction of a vehicle
records.learnerexamples_text: He took both hands off the steering wheel.; After leaving your house on Monday morning, I gripped the steering wheel, fixed my eyes firmly on the road, and bravely drove my way up to Scotland.

records.definition_text: one of the movements you make with your feet when you walk
