records.definition_text: a way of designing hair, clothes, furniture, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: She's had her hair cut in a really nice style.;  the latest styles; The classic black dress is always in style.; And they like the same style of clothes as I [do].

records.definition_text: a way of doing something that is typical of a particular person, group, place, or period
records.learnerexamples_text: a style of painting/writing; Jon has an interesting hands-on style of management.; I love Hip Hop music. This style of music is my life.

records.definition_text: the quality of being attractive and fashionable or behaving in a way which makes people admire you
records.learnerexamples_text: She's got style.; But when he came back, his popularity was increased. That's reasonable, because he's got style, he is authentic and brill[i]ant.

records.definition_text: fashionable and attractive
records.learnerexamples_text: a stylish black suit; The film's direction is subtle and stylish.; I pay attention to fashionable and stylish clothes, of course, if they don't seem strange [or] unus[u]al.

records.definition_text: the person or thing which performs the action described by the verb
records.learnerexamples_text: 'Bob' is the subject of the sentence 'Bob threw the ball'.

records.definition_text: what someone is writing or talking about
records.learnerexamples_text: Our subject for discussion is homelessness.; She has made a series of documentaries on the subject of family relationships.; She likes swimming and practising yoga. In fact, this was the subject of our first lesson.

records.definition_text: to send a document, plan, etc. to someone so that they can consider it
records.learnerexamples_text: Applications must be submitted before January 1st.; The developers submitted building plans to the council for approval.; According to my friends and professors, I am hardworking and never fail to submit my essays on [time].

records.definition_text: a solid, liquid, or gas
records.learnerexamples_text: an organic/chemical substance; a dangerous substance; What sort of substance could withstand those temperatures?; Chemical substances are added to our food.

records.definition_text: large in amount
records.learnerexamples_text: a substantial sum of money; The first draft of his novel needed a substantial amount of rewriting.; The findings show a substantial difference between the opinions of men and women.;  The taxis: Considerin[g] that you are willing to spend quite a substantial amount of money, this is the best transport one can get.

records.definition_text: to use someone or something instead of another person or thing
records.learnerexamples_text: You can substitute oil for butter in this recipe.; Dayton was substituted for Williams in the second half of the match.; [M]y opinion is that we shouldn't substitute one for the other, but read one and watch [the] other.

records.definition_text: a thing or person that is used instead of another thing or person
records.learnerexamples_text: Tofu can be used as a meat substitute in vegetarian recipes.; Vitamins should not be used as a substitute for a healthy diet.; I had been looking forward to seeing his performance for ages, so as soon as I realized there was a substitute on the stage, I was really disappointed.

records.definition_text: an area on the edge of a large town or city where people who work in the town or city often live
records.learnerexamples_text: Box Hill is a suburb of Melbourne.; We drove from middle-class suburbs to a very poor inner-city area.; Peterhof is only a small suburb of St. Petersburg and it is not famous [for] its nightlife.

records.definition_text: a passage under a road or railway for people to walk through
records.learnerexamples_text: We could take the subway.; I began to walk along that narrow and dark subway.

records.definition_text: to achieve what you are trying to achieve
records.learnerexamples_text: Lucy has the skill and determination to succeed.; She finally succeeded in passing the exam.; You need to be pretty tough to succeed in today's business world.; I hope I will succeed [in] the P.E.T.

records.definition_text: when you achieve what you want to achieve
records.learnerexamples_text: The success of almost any project depends largely on its manager.; I've been trying to persuade her to take on more staff, but so far without success.; I'm not having much success in communicating with him at the moment.; The success rate for this operation is very low.; I searched in the taxi-cab and in the company with no success.

records.definition_text: something that has a good result or that is very popular
records.learnerexamples_text: Both films have been a big/huge box-office success in this country.; She's keen to make a success of this project.; That salmon dish was a success, wasn't it?; And lastly the rest of the space we can use for further information and details about the history of our school and our successes in the past.

records.definition_text: achieving what you want to achieve
records.learnerexamples_text: a successful operation; My second attempt at making pizza was more successful.; This year's harvest was one of the most successful since the record crop of 1985.; I am very happy every time I return from a successful shopping-tour.

records.definition_text: having achieved a lot or made a lot of money through your work
records.learnerexamples_text: a successful businesswoman; a successful career; He runs a very successful computer business.; I would like to finish by asking Mr. Smith to talk a bit about his life and his successful career.

records.definition_text: very popular
records.learnerexamples_text: a successful film; He's the author of several hugely successful children's books.; I suppose the facts about your film career, especially about your first film and [your] most successful film would be pretty interesting [as well].

records.definition_text: in a way that is successful
records.learnerexamples_text: A number of patients have been successfully treated with the new drug.; As you can see, I managed to do the project successfully.

records.definition_text: used to refer to something or someone that you were just talking about, or something or someone of that type
records.learnerexamples_text: It's difficult to know how to treat such cases.; I tried to tell her in such a way that she wouldn't be upset.; Moreover we can plan different events where we invite people who aren't members [and] we can use such events [to bring in] new members.

records.definition_text: done or happening quickly and unexpectedly
records.learnerexamples_text: His sudden death at the age of 53 came as a terrible shock to her.; There was a sudden change in their plans.; And Angie's leaving work in two weeks? It's a bit sudden, isn't it.; After arriving in Vienna, Martins was really shocked when he got to know about his friend's sudden death.

records.definition_text: quickly and unexpectedly
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't remember much about the accident - it all happened so suddenly.; I suddenly realized how late it was.; I was just drifting off to sleep when suddenly I heard a crash outside.; Suddenly a dog appeared in front of us.; Suddenly a car appeared at the end of the street.

records.definition_text: to experience pain or unpleasant emotions
records.learnerexamples_text: She really suffers in the winter when it's cold and her joints get stiff.; I think he suffered quite a lot when his wife left him.; If you're not happy with it, you should complain. Don't just suffer in silence.; I am sure it w[ould] suffer living in a small flat in a big city, with no park nearby to go [to] every day for a walk.

records.definition_text: to experience something bad
records.learnerexamples_text: The party suffered a crushing defeat in the last election.; Twenty-five policemen suffered minor injuries during the protest.; The city suffered another blow last month with the closure of the local car factory.; If you will insist on eating three helpings of dessert, I'm afraid you'll have to suffer the consequences!; When you're working such long hours, it's almost inevitable that your marriage will start to suffer.

records.definition_text: to have an illness or other health problem
records.learnerexamples_text: She suffers from severe depression.; She's been suffering from cancer for two years.; The doctors told my parents that my aunt was suffering from cancer so they had to stay with her.

records.definition_text: when someone experiences pain or unpleasant emotions
records.learnerexamples_text: The war will cause widespread human suffering.; There had been too much suffering for days, months, years.

records.definition_text: as much as is necessary
records.learnerexamples_text: This recipe should be sufficient for five people.; It was thought that he'd committed the crime but there wasn't sufficient evidence to convict him.; To resolve that, try to have a sufficient amount of sleep so that both your body and mind will keep fit.

records.definition_text: a group of letters that you add to the end of a word to make another word
records.learnerexamples_text: The suffix '-ness' added to the end of the word 'sweet' forms the word 'sweetness', changing an adjective into a noun.

records.definition_text: to express an idea or plan for someone to consider
records.learnerexamples_text: I suggest (that) we wait a while before we make any firm decisions.; Liz suggested (that) I try the shop on Mill Road.; He suggested having the meeting at his house.; I also suggest you should go to the Alps because there [is] a lot of beautiful scenery and if it's winter there are many place[s] to ski.

records.definition_text: to say that someone or something is suitable for something
records.learnerexamples_text: to suggest someone for a job; Can you suggest a good hotel?; Might I suggest a white wine with your salmon, sir?; I suggest the "Renoir".

records.definition_text: to make something seem likely to be true
records.learnerexamples_text: There's no absolute proof, but all the evidence suggests (that) he's guilty.; Something about what he said suggested that he wasn't happy.; So animals cannot be [as] unhappy as the topic suggests.

records.definition_text: an idea or plan that someone suggests
records.learnerexamples_text: We don't know where to eat out tonight - have you got any suggestions?; Clara made some very helpful suggestions.; They didn't like my suggestion that we should all share the cost.; I have a few favourite restaurants that I tend to go back to, but I'm always open to new suggestions.; Now I wan[t] to give you some suggestions that will be useful for you.

records.definition_text: when you intentionally kill yourself
records.learnerexamples_text: to attempt/commit suicide; The suicide rate among men between the ages of 16 and 25 has risen alarmingly.; Many suicides occur in prisons.; The savage thinks he can change it but fails and commits suicide by hanging himself.

records.definition_text: to make someone look more attractive
records.learnerexamples_text: You should wear more red - it suits you.; Short skirts don't really suit me - I haven't got the legs for them.; They usually wear casual clothes such as jeans, T-shirts and trainers, because they believe that th[ese] kind[s] of clothes suit them best.

records.definition_text: to be convenient or suitable for a particular person, situation or occasion
records.learnerexamples_text: We could go now or this afternoon - whatever time suits you best.; The city lifestyle seems to suit her - she's certainly looking very well.; "How about eight o'clock outside the cinema?" "That suits me fine."; If you find it difficult to arrange your visit for these two dates, please let us know which other Sunday would suit you most.

records.definition_text: acceptable or right for someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: Is the film suitable for children?; It's a nice enough dress but it's not really suitable for a wedding.; I think they are more suitable for boys than for girls.

records.definition_text: in a way that is acceptable or right
records.learnerexamples_text: a suitably qualified person; Was he dressed suitably?; Nevertheless, a lot of people think animals are not suitably looked after - they have to live in small [space]s and, moreover, the weather [is] often rather different from [w]hat animals are used to.

records.definition_text: an amount of money
records.learnerexamples_text: Huge sums of money are spent on national defence.; On retirement, he will receive the sum of £50 000 from the company.; My poor aunt Yutta [h]as died and she's left me a big sum of money.

records.definition_text: a short, clear description that gives the main facts or ideas about something
records.learnerexamples_text: He gave a brief summary of events.; Below is a summary of the most relevant points and recommendations.

records.definition_text: to describe briefly the most important facts or characteristics of something
records.searchterms_text: sum;sum up (sth/sb) or sum (sth/sb) up;sum up sth/sb or sum sth/sb up
records.learnerexamples_text: The purpose of the conclusion is to sum up the main points of your essay.; To sum up, young people are interested in many things but in my opinion, music, TV and clothes are issues about which they care more than others.

records.definition_text: to sit or lie in the sun so that your skin becomes brown
records.learnerexamples_text: We spent the day sunbathing on the beach.; The weather is very good here, so I hope [to] go to the beach with my mother in the mornings to sunbathe.

records.definition_text: the light from the sun
records.learnerexamples_text: The garden was bathed in sunlight.; There are many sources of light in this world such as sunlight, moonlight, [and] candle light. [...] Nowadays, the electric light has becom[e] part of our lives, especially [at] night.

records.definition_text: when the sun appears in the morning and the sky becomes light
records.learnerexamples_text: I always get up before sunrise.; I have also decided to buy something new. I would like to have a poster, maybe a big black and white photo or a picture of a sunrise, what do you think about that?

records.definition_text: when the sun disappears in the evening and the sky becomes dark
records.learnerexamples_text: They close the park at sunset.; We can go to Focone Beach, where the sunset is so beautiful.

records.definition_text: the light and heat that come from the sun
records.learnerexamples_text: The children were out playing in the sunshine.; You know I love sunshine. It's my [energy source].

records.definition_text: excellent
records.learnerexamples_text: He is a superb dancer.; Taylor scored a superb goal at the end of the first half.; My homemade pizzas are superb, although I say it myself, and I would like to make one for the two of us.

records.definition_text: used to describe things that cannot be explained by our knowledge of science or nature
records.learnerexamples_text: supernatural powers/forces; The book consists of six completely different 'ghost stories' which involve ghosts and supernatural phenomena, something that attracts young readers.

records.definition_text: to watch a person or activity to make certain that everything is done correctly, safely, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: The UN is supervising the distribution of aid by local agencies in the disaster area.; The children play while two teachers supervise.; Our main activity will be to supervise the 8 to 12 year [old]s during those activities.

records.definition_text: a person or company that provides something that people want or need
records.learnerexamples_text: They used to be a leading supplier of military equipment.; I have been employed by the Swedish fruit supplier "Northern Fruit Corp.'' for the last 6 years.

records.definition_text: an amount of something that is available for use
records.learnerexamples_text: a supply of water; Our food supplies were running out.; In London, demand for cheap housing far outstrips supply.; Please send me a list of [the] clothes [needed] and/or supplies.

records.definition_text: to provide things that people want or need, often over a long period of time
records.learnerexamples_text: to supply food/drugs to people; Electrical power is supplied by underground cables.; Three people have been arrested for supplying arms to the terrorists.; At the beginning of term, students are supplied with a list of books that they are expected to read.; I would be able to supply you with [a] reference from my employer.

records.definition_text: to like a particular sports team, often going to see their matches
records.learnerexamples_text: Which team do you support?; Also I saw another programme, it was talking about the history of Barcelona football club. I liked it very much because this is the team that I support.

records.definition_text: to look after someone by paying for their food, clothes, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: He has a wife and four children to support.; Sara has to work hard to support her family.

records.definition_text: to help someone, often when they are having problems
records.learnerexamples_text: Alcoholics Anonymous is a group which supports people who are trying to stop drinking too much alcohol.; My family has always supported me in whatever I've wanted to do.; All [Mum and Dad] can do is support him in this next step of his life.

records.definition_text: to agree with an idea, group, or person
records.learnerexamples_text: Do you support their views on nuclear weapons?; The majority of people in the town strongly support the plans for a new sports centre.; I support this idea because I believe that [it] is the [only] way to stop the traffic in cities.

records.definition_text: to give encouragement or financial help to someone or something because you want them to succeed
records.learnerexamples_text: I think it's important to support local businesses by buying locally.; The drug company is supporting cancer research.; These films are more attractive for older viewers and support the local film business.

records.definition_text: help or encouragement given to someone when they are having problems
records.learnerexamples_text: Carol gave me a lot of support when I lost my job.; She's been a great support to my mum since my dad died.; Mother needs our support now and I'll go as soon as I can

records.definition_text: agreement with an idea, group or person
records.learnerexamples_text: Environmental groups are fast gaining support among young people.; Is there much public support for the proposal?; Support for the party leader has declined in recent weeks.; I signed a petition in support of the human rights campaign.; Dear Julian, I wanted to tell you that you have my moral support.

records.definition_text: the money someone needs in order to buy food and clothes and pay for somewhere to live
records.learnerexamples_text: He is dependent on his father for support.; Re[cei]ving my pocket money las[t] week, I was thinking what would happen if I lo[st] my father's support.

records.definition_text: someone who likes a particular sports team and wants them to win
records.learnerexamples_text: Manchester United supporters; Thousands of supporters have travelled to London for the cup final.; I'm a great supporter of Milan as you know, so you can imagine how I feel now.

records.definition_text: someone who supports a particular idea, group or person
records.learnerexamples_text: He is one of the Prime Minister's strongest supporters within industry.; According to supporters of Animal Rights, people wouldn't like being kept in zoos.

records.definition_text: used to show that you believe something is very likely
records.learnerexamples_text: Surely they'd have called us by now to say they're not coming.; Surely you are interested in how we spent the rest of our holiday?

records.definition_text: used to express surprise that something has happened or is going to happen
records.learnerexamples_text: Surely you don't expect me to believe that?; Surely he wasn't expecting us to pay the whole amount?; Surely it doesn't mean that they have learnt the exciting news?

records.definition_text: to ride on a wave as it comes towards land, while standing or lying on a special board
records.learnerexamples_text: I spent the summer learning how to surf.; I really enjoy[ed] learning how to surf, it was terrific.

records.definition_text: the top or outside part of something
records.learnerexamples_text: The sun was reflected on the surface of the water.; Tropical rainforests used to cover 10% of the Earth's surface.; The marble has a smooth, shiny surface.; Neil Armstrong was the first person to set foot on the surface of the moon.; When we came back to the surface we just looked like real miners.

records.definition_text: what someone or something seems to be like when you do not know much about them
records.learnerexamples_text: On the surface, he seemed very pleasant.; Miss Marple on the other hand is an old, nervous but gentle lady on the surface but inside that head of hers there is a brain [as] sharp as a knife, cutting through the mysteries she [is] involved in.

records.definition_text: a place where doctors or other medical workers treat people
records.learnerexamples_text: What time does the surgery open?; As she walked into the doctor's surgery, she began to explain her problem to the doctor and that she couldn't stand the idea of lice inhabiting her head.

records.definition_text: when a doctor cuts your body open and repairs or removes something
records.learnerexamples_text: heart surgery; The patient had/underwent surgery on his heart.; He made a good recovery after surgery to remove a brain tumour.; My mother had to go through gall-stone surgery in Finland, where she was spending her holiday.

records.definition_text: the feeling that you get when something happens that you did not expect
records.learnerexamples_text: He looked at her in/with surprise.; He agreed to everything, (much) to my surprise.; He stared at me in surprise and didn't say anything.

records.definition_text: to make someone feel surprise
records.learnerexamples_text: The news surprised everyone.; It doesn't surprise me that she wants to leave.; It won't surprise anyone to learn that the offer has been rejected.; Then I saw a blue light that surprised me, I was scared. [A] strange creature was standing in front of me. [I]t was fat and ugly and then it tried to grab me...

records.definition_text: not expected and making someone feel surprised
records.learnerexamples_text: He gave a rather surprising answer.;  It's hardly/not surprising (that) you're putting on weight, considering how much you're eating!; I must say that it's surprising to find you agreeing with me for once.; That was a little bit surprising because I'm pretty small and it's hard for me to find clothes that really fit me!

records.definition_text: unexpectedly or in a way that is unusual
records.learnerexamples_text: The restaurant turned out to be surprisingly cheap.; Not surprisingly, the jury found them guilty.; Surprisingly, I met a friend of mine from primary school.

records.definition_text: to be or go everywhere around something or someone
records.learnerexamples_text: Snow-capped mountains surround the city.; Early this morning, armed police surrounded the house in north London.; Gwen sat at her desk, surrounded by books and papers.; She said that she wanted to die surrounded by the people she loved.; The place I've enjoyed [most] is a small lake surrounded by very [tall] trees and a lot of bushes.

records.definition_text: in a position around something
records.learnerexamples_text: A lot of the children at the school do not live in the town, but come in from the surrounding countryside.; If all of you would help by using these facillities, our village could be very attractive to people from surrounding villages, which could be very good for the economy of our village.

records.definition_text: the place where someone or something is and the things that are in it
records.learnerexamples_text: beautiful/pleasant surroundings; Have you got used to your new surroundings?; Some butterflies blend in with their surroundings so that it's difficult to see them.; The larger animals who [are]n't threaten[e]d should li[v]e in their natural surroundings.

records.definition_text: an examination of opinions, behaviour, etc., made by asking people questions
records.learnerexamples_text: A recent survey found/showed that 58% of people did not know where their heart is.; They are conducting/carrying out/doing a survey.; I have made a little survey on the subject of my report and I have [found] that most of the pupils of our school consider that the region and the area around [the] school should be filmed first.

records.definition_text: when someone or something continues to live or exist, especially after a difficult or dangerous situation
records.learnerexamples_text: The doctors told my wife I had a 50/50 chance of survival.; His main concern is to ensure his own political survival.; For many animals zoos are [their] only hope for survival: for example, [the] Chinese panda or white eagle.

records.definition_text: to continue to live or exist, especially after almost dying or being destroyed
records.learnerexamples_text: The baby was born with a heart problem and only survived for a few hours.; These plants cannot survive in very cold conditions.; The front passengers were lucky to survive the accident.; The family are struggling to survive on very little money.; They struggle to survive.

records.definition_text: someone who continues to live after almost dying because of an accident, illness, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: Rescuers have given up hope of finding any more survivors.; He was the sole survivor of the plane crash.; She's a cancer survivor/a survivor of cancer.; We were the only survivors.

records.definition_text: to think that something is probably true, or is likely to happen
records.learnerexamples_text: They suspected (that) he was lying.; I suspect she won't come - she's very busy.; "Do you think she'll have told them?" "I suspect not/so.";  He apologised, but he had some family problems and in fact he couldn't come. I suspect that's his mother - he didn't [say] clearly.

records.definition_text: to think that someone may have committed a crime or done something bad
records.learnerexamples_text: No one knows who killed her, but the police suspect her husband.; The police suspect him of carrying out two bomb attacks.; But other people were suspected of having killed them.

records.definition_text: someone who may have committed a crime
records.learnerexamples_text: He's the prime suspect in the murder case.; He had never thought that Doctor Quimper might [have] been a suspect, as well.

records.definition_text: to not allow someone to go to work or school for a period of time because they have done something wrong
records.learnerexamples_text: She was suspended from school for fighting.; He was suspended for four matches after arguing with the referee.; The director decided to suspend the girl because she had be[en] rude.

records.definition_text: a belief or idea that something may be true
records.learnerexamples_text: I have a suspicion that he only asked me out because my brother persuaded him to.; I asked my mother what had happened and she confirmed my suspicions.

records.definition_text: not trusting someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: Many of them remain suspicious of journalists.; My mother has a very suspicious nature.; He gave me a suspicious look.; Paul was suspicious and asked her if she was alright. [Jane] replied with a yes, but she looked nervous. She went quickly upstairs and came back holding a baby in her arms. She told him that this baby was theirs.

records.definition_text: making you feel that something illegal is happening or that something is wrong
records.learnerexamples_text: suspicious behaviour/circumstances; His wife became suspicious after finding blood in their car.; The fire at the bank is being treated as suspicious.;  It's a bit suspicious that no one knows where he was at the time of the murder.; There's a suspicious-looking van parked at the end of the road.

records.definition_text: in a way that shows that you do not trust someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: He looked at her suspiciously.; He sniffed the soup suspiciously.; The old man, who was going upstairs, stopped and looked at us very suspiciously.

records.definition_text: to move your throat in order to make food or drink go down
records.learnerexamples_text: My throat is so sore that it really hurts when I swallow.; The snake swallowed the bird whole.; When Mrs McGillicuddy was upstairs, she swallowed a fish bone.

records.definition_text: a large, white bird with a long neck which lives on lakes and rivers
records.learnerexamples_text: We saw two swans gliding down the river with their signets.; The ugly duckling became a beautiful swan.

records.definition_text: to use language which people think is rude or offensive
records.learnerexamples_text: It was a real shock, the first time I heard my mother swear.; When the taxi driver started to swear at him, he walked off.; When I heard the ringing of the phone I became so furious that as soon as I answered the phone, I started swearing at it.

records.definition_text: to make a serious promise
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't know anything about what happened, I swear (it).; She swore blind (that) she didn't know what had happened to the money.; New gang members must swear to obey the gang leaders at all times.; In some countries, witnesses in court have to swear on the Bible.; That day I swore to myself that I would never trust anybody again.

records.definition_text: the salty colourless liquid that comes through your skin when you are hot, nervous or ill
records.learnerexamples_text: The sweat was pouring off me ten minutes into the game.; By the time we'd climbed to the top of the hill, we were covered in sweat.; She wiped the beads of sweat from her forehead.; Pearls of sweat appeared on her foreh[e]ad.

records.definition_text: to produce liquid through your skin because you are hot, nervous or ill
records.learnerexamples_text: The room was hot and I was starting to sweat.; The prisoners were sweating with fear.; I began to sweat and my fear changed to panic when we opened a door.

records.definition_text: a piece of clothing made of soft cotton which covers the top of your body and is pulled on over your head
records.learnerexamples_text: She was dressed casually in jeans and a sweatshirt.; Well, I'm always wearing tight-fitting, blue jeans, I really love them as they're always in fashion, and if it's cold, a v-neck, long sleeved sweatshirt.

records.definition_text: to clean the floor using a brush
records.learnerexamples_text: I've swept the floor.; He swept up the pieces of broken glass.; I found your watch yesterday, while I was sweeping the floor.

records.definition_text: kind and friendly
records.learnerexamples_text: It was really sweet of you to help.; Thank you ever so much for the present you've sent me! It was really sweet of you.

records.definition_text: someone who is swimming or who can swim
records.learnerexamples_text: Oliver is a very strong swimmer.; He is the best swimmer in the club, much faster than I could [ever] be.

records.definition_text: a chair hanging on two ropes that children sit on and swing backwards and forwards
records.learnerexamples_text: Jake wanted me to push him on the swing.; Do you remember the swing by the big tree in my garden?

records.definition_text: to move smoothly backwards and forwards, or to make something do this
records.learnerexamples_text: He walked briskly along the path swinging his rolled-up umbrella.; When Mary ent[e]red the bar, the room was empty and there was a rope swinging from a beam.

records.definition_text: to change from one thing to another
records.learnerexamples_text: She started studying English at college, but switched to Business Studies in her second year.; He's just switched jobs.; For many years I had created my system under MS-DOS (Disk Operating System), but two years ago I switched and since the[n] I've worked with Unix.

records.definition_text: a small object that you push up or down with your finger to turn something electrical on or off
records.learnerexamples_text: a light switch; Can you flip the switch?; Then I turned off the switch until the end of the day.

records.base_text: switch off sth or switch sth off
records.definition_text: to turn off a light, television, etc. by using a switch
records.searchterms_text: switch;switch off sth or switch sth off
records.learnerexamples_text: Remember to switch the computer off.; I was sad and tried to call her, [but] it was not possible because her mobile phone was switched off.

records.base_text: switch on sth or switch sth on
records.definition_text: to turn on a light, television, etc. by using a switch
records.searchterms_text: switch;switch on sth or switch sth on
records.learnerexamples_text: Could you switch the light on?; We will switch on a light and will sing "Happy Birthday" and the party will begin.

records.definition_text: larger than usual
records.learnerexamples_text: a bruised, swollen face; I cried almost all day and wanted to go home as quick[ly] as possible but suddenly, someone took a photograph of me with swollen eyes.
