records.definition_text: a particular point of the day, week, month, year, etc. that is suitable for a particular activity, or at which something is expected to happen
records.learnerexamples_text: holiday time; party time; When would be a good time for me to call you?

records.definition_text: a number of minutes, hours, days, etc. that is available for something or that is needed for something
records.learnerexamples_text: If I have time, I'll call Sam.; Have you got time for a quick drink after work?; I'd like to learn to sail, but I haven't the time.; I haven't got time to go to the shops today.; She ran out of time and didn't finish the last question.

records.definition_text: a period in history
records.learnerexamples_text: Charles Dickens' novel "A Tale of Two Cities" is set at the time of the French Revolution.;  In/During medieval times, women thought to be witches were burnt at the stake.;  In times gone by, all crops were harvested by hand.; He is widely regarded as one of the best writers of modern/our times.; We sat and talked about old times.

records.definition_text: to measure how long it takes for something to happen or for someone to do something
records.learnerexamples_text: It's a good idea to time yourself while you do the exercises.

records.definition_text: multiplied by
records.learnerexamples_text: What is eight times fourteen?

records.definition_text: a list of times when buses, trains, etc. arrive and leave
records.learnerexamples_text: Do you have a Birmingham to London train timetable that I could borrow?

records.definition_text: a list of dates and times that shows when things will happen
records.learnerexamples_text: The timetable for our trip to Paris includes visits to Notre Dame, the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre.; Here is the timetable of events for the day.; Could you kindly send me some information about the activities and timetable of the club?

records.definition_text: the time when something happens
records.learnerexamples_text: "Are we early?" "No, your timing is perfect - dinner is almost ready."; [The] timing was perfect, the car was waiting for us [and] it was really easy.

records.definition_text: a metal container with a lid that you keep food or other substances in
records.learnerexamples_text: a biscuit tin; a tin of paint; Meanwhile it was 11.15 p.m. and I [had] just asked my husband to take away the tins [of] paint from the stairs when suddenly the lights went out.

records.definition_text: a metal container in which food is sold
records.learnerexamples_text: a tin of beans; piles of soup tins; The only thing I have is a tin of beans and a laser gun stolen from one of the cyborguards.

records.definition_text: extremely small
records.learnerexamples_text: the baby's tiny hands; a tiny little cottage; I was a tiny bit late.; I got a small cottage in a tiny village, called San Bernardino.

records.definition_text: a piece of useful advice
records.learnerexamples_text: He includes a few tips on growing vegetables.; She's given me a number of useful gardening tips.; Dear Julie, Sam, and Max I'm just writing to give you guys some tips about your trip to Brazil.

records.definition_text: an extra amount of money that you give to a driver, someone working in a restaurant, etc to thank them
records.learnerexamples_text: a 15% tip; He gave the porter a tip.; Have you left a tip for the waiter?; You could also work in a pub or in a restaurant, the advantage there is get[ting] extra money besides the agreed salary, because customers give tips.

records.definition_text: the state of being tired
records.learnerexamples_text: He said that it was tiredness that led him to make the mistake.; I was overtaken by a sudden wave of tiredness.; I felt so relaxed and my tiredness disappeared almost entirely.

records.definition_text: bored or annoyed by something that has happened too often
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm tired of listening to her problems.; I never get tired of watching this film, I really love it!

records.definition_text: making you feel tired
records.learnerexamples_text: I've had a very tiring day.; Looking after three kids is extremely tiring.; The only bad thing is that the trip was a bit tiring.

records.definition_text: a soft piece of paper that you use for cleaning your nose
records.learnerexamples_text: I have some tissues in my bag.; P.S. Bring tissues because you won't stop crying when you watch the film.

records.definition_text: the name of a book, film, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: The title of Evelyn Waugh's first novel was 'Decline and Fall'.; And this next record is the title track on the album 'The Red Shoes'.; I can't remember the title of the movie.

records.definition_text: used to show the position of someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: She stood with her back to the window. ; I had my back to them, so I couldn't see what they were doing.; John's standing to the left of Adrian in the photo.; The Yorkshire Dales are twenty miles to the north of the city.; My town is situated to the south of Paris.

records.definition_text: used to say who is treated in a particular way or who or what is affected by something
records.learnerexamples_text: What have you done to your hair?; Her evidence was very helpful to the police.; She was very kind to us.; The waiter was really kind to us. We gave him the key of the car and he drove us home.

records.definition_text: used to show a relationship with someone
records.learnerexamples_text: I've been married to Peter for nine years.; She was an assistant to the chief executive.; She's 38 years old and she's married to a Spanish engineer.

records.definition_text: used to compare two things
records.learnerexamples_text: I prefer football to cricket. ; She's earning a reasonable wage, but nothing to what she could make in a big company.; I prefer homemade food to re[s]taurant meals.

records.definition_text: used to say where something is fastened or connected
records.learnerexamples_text: The paper was fastened to the wall with tape.; A fast rail service connects us to the city.; My mouth became so dry that my tongue stuck to my palate.

records.definition_text: until a particular time, state or level is reached
records.learnerexamples_text: It's only two weeks to Christmas.; Unemployment has risen to almost eight million.; She nursed me back to health.

records.definition_text: used in phrases which show a range
records.learnerexamples_text: There must have been thirty to thirty-five people there.

records.definition_text: mainly
records.searchterms_text: extent;to a great/large etc extent;to a great/large, etc. extent
records.learnerexamples_text: Their anger was to a large extent justified.; As we all know, TV, video and cinema have replaced books to an enormous extent.

records.definition_text: at the start of a situation
records.learnerexamples_text: To begin with, the two girls got on well.; It wasn't stunningly beautiful, but a bed and a bathroom is really all we need[ed] to begin with!

records.definition_text: used to give the first important reason for something
records.learnerexamples_text: To begin with, we can't afford to move.; To begin with, it doesn't pollute and I think it's time we started thinking about [the] environment.

records.definition_text: used to express your real opinion
records.learnerexamples_text: To be honest, I didn't really enjoy the party. ; To be honest with you, I don't think it will be possible.; To be honest, I do hate shopping for clothes.

records.definition_text: used to give exact details about something
records.learnerexamples_text: We met in 1994 - on October 1st to be precise. ; There was a good turnout for the meeting - twelve of us to be precise.; It's in Central London, to be precise.

records.definition_text: up to the present time
records.learnerexamples_text: This is her best work to date.; I enclose a copy of my curriculum vitae, which will give you further details about my career to date.

records.definition_text: up to the present time
records.learnerexamples_text: This is her best work to date.; I enclose a copy of my curriculum vitae, which will give you further details about my career to date.

records.definition_text: in the period of time that is happening now
records.learnerexamples_text: Today, people are much more concerned about their health than they were in the past.; Today we cannot go to a place without se[e]ing a computer.

records.definition_text: the period of time that is happening now
records.learnerexamples_text: With today's technology almost anything seems possible.; However, technology has made immense steps forward and the cars of today come close to perfection.

records.definition_text: one of the hard, flat parts on top of the end of your toes
records.learnerexamples_text: I need to cut my toenails.

records.definition_text: at the same time
records.learnerexamples_text: Everyone seemed to arrive together.; We can deal with the next two items on the list together.; He came to my house early in the morning and then we left together.

records.definition_text: used to say that two or more things are joined to each other, mixed with each other, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: She tied the two pieces of rope together.; Could you add these figures together for me?; You mix all the dry ingredients together before you add the milk.; You could stick that back together with a bit of glue.; I like both flavours separately but I don't like them together.

records.definition_text: combined
records.learnerexamples_text: Together they must earn over ninety thousand dollars a year.; The money that I owe you for the telephone together with the rent equals £300.; When you ride a bike on the main road, it's very dangerous to breath[e] the dirty air - together with the gases from the cars.

records.definition_text: to accept or allow something although you do not like it
records.learnerexamples_text: I will not tolerate that sort of behaviour in my class.; We will not tolerate racism of any sort.; He couldn't tolerate anybody disturbing childrens' lives for the sake of money, because he was a very moral man.

records.definition_text: to make a situation more difficult, unpleasant, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: To make matters worse, our car broke down!; To make matters worse, the newspaper said they only played for thirty-five minutes.

records.definition_text: to make a situation more difficult, unpleasant, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: To make matters worse, our car broke down!; To make matters worse, the newspaper said they only played for thirty-five minutes.

records.definition_text: to make a situation more difficult, unpleasant, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: To make matters worse, our car broke down!; To make matters worse, the newspaper said they only played for thirty-five minutes.

records.definition_text: a place where a dead person is buried, usually with a stone structure
records.learnerexamples_text: He is buried in a marble tomb.; My father opened it slowly and we saw a huge marble tomb behind it.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize that you are giving your own opinion
records.learnerexamples_text: To my mind, the play was rather disappointing.; To my mind, The Picture of Dorian Gray is probably his best novel.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize that you are giving your own opinion
records.learnerexamples_text: To my mind, the play was rather disappointing.; To my mind, The Picture of Dorian Gray is probably his best novel.

records.definition_text: a unit for measuring weight, equal to 1016 kilograms in the UK and 907 kilograms in the US
records.learnerexamples_text: They generated nearly 6 tons of rubbish.; It was at this point I saw a twenty ton lorry speeding towards them.

records.definition_text: the quality of a sound, especially of someone's voice
records.learnerexamples_text: I tried to use a sympathetic tone of voice.; It wasn't so much what she said that annoyed me - it was her tone.; Paul, the leader of the group, shouted: "Keep quiet" and he went on [in] a quiet tone: "They want this kind of reaction, they want to frighten us...

records.definition_text: an electronic sound made by a telephone
records.learnerexamples_text: a dialling tone; Quickly, a man got the phone [and was] trying [to] call the police but there was no tone.

records.definition_text: the large soft piece of flesh in the mouth which you can move and which you use for tasting, speaking, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: I burnt my tongue on some soup last night.; My mouth became so dry that my tongue stuck to my palate.

records.definition_text: a lot of something
records.learnerexamples_text: We've got tons of things to do before they arrive.; There were tons of handmade items!

records.definition_text: used to say that you are sorry about a situation
records.learnerexamples_text: "He didn't get the job." "Oh, that's too bad."; Too bad you couldn't be here.

records.definition_text: used to say that you are sorry about a situation
records.learnerexamples_text: "He didn't get the job." "Oh, that's too bad."; Too bad you couldn't come to my party.

records.definition_text: a piece of equipment that you use with your hands in order to make or repair something
records.learnerexamples_text: power tools; The only tools you need for this job are a hammer and a screwdriver.; And, of course, she got a set of excellent tools and I won only one thing: a tube of model[l]ing glue.

records.definition_text: a thing that helps you to do a particular activity
records.learnerexamples_text: Computers are an essential tool for modern scientists.; From my personal experience, I can also say that a personal computer is also an amazing tool.

records.definition_text: a substance that you use to clean your teeth
records.learnerexamples_text: Put a small amount of toothpaste on the brush. ; Modern technology [has] changed our li[v]es in many ways. When I have to wake up earlier, I use my alarm clock, [and] if I have to [brush] my teeth, I use my toothbrush with a little toothpaste.

records.definition_text: a piece of clothing worn on the upper part of the body
records.learnerexamples_text: a black/striped top; I need a top to go with these trousers.; I like wearing formal clothes but at a party I usually wear jeans and a nice top.

records.definition_text: at the highest part of something
records.learnerexamples_text: There's a dirty mark on the top left-hand corner of the photo.; The offices are on the top floor of the building.; He was standing on the top rung of a ladder.; My bedroom is quite big and on the top floor.

records.definition_text: in the position of being most important or successful
records.learnerexamples_text: She came top in the maths test.

records.definition_text: the best, most important, or most successful
records.learnerexamples_text: He's one of the country's top athletes. ; So what would be your top choice for a holiday?; As a chess player, he's among the top 10% in the country.; top jobs; top universities

records.definition_text: a subject that you talk or write about
records.learnerexamples_text: Our discussion ranged over various topics, such as climate change and nuclear weapons.; Do you know that food is one of my favourite topics of conversation?

records.definition_text: a small electric light that you hold in your hand
records.learnerexamples_text: She shone the torch into the dark room.; After fifteen minutes of walking, we got into a cave. It was dark, so we [turned on] our torches.

records.definition_text: an extremely strong and dangerous wind that blows in a circle and destroys buildings as it moves along
records.learnerexamples_text: A tornado had swept through the north of the state, causing terrible destruction.; The storm was getting very wild outside, she wasn't sure if it [was] a real tornado, she had never seen one, but somehow she could sense the danger.

records.base_text: to some extent/to a certain extent
records.definition_text: in some ways
records.searchterms_text: extent;to some extent/to a certain extent
records.learnerexamples_text: To some extent, she was responsible for the accident.; I agree with you to a certain extent.; To a certain extent, this point of view seems to be very respectable.

records.definition_text: used before saying the first thing in a list of things
records.learnerexamples_text: To start with, we need better computers. Then we need more training.; There is some information I should tell you about. To start with, the T.V repairman didn't come on Wednesday morning as expected.

records.definition_text: the amount you get when you add several smaller amounts together
records.learnerexamples_text: That figure at the bottom of the column is the total.;  A total of 21 horses were entered for the race.; We made £700 in total, over three days of trading.; My holiday started from last Sunday morning for a total of ten days.

records.definition_text: including everything
records.learnerexamples_text: the total cost; Total losses were $800.; The total cost was only £60, including lunch, and I think it was worth every penny of it.

records.definition_text: extreme or complete
records.learnerexamples_text: total silence; The whole evening was a total disaster.; That's total rubbish.; The room was in total darkness and I couldn't hear anything.

records.definition_text: completely
records.learnerexamples_text: They're totally different.; I'd totally forgotten I'd arranged to meet her.; I totally agree with you.; But in the new class, it is totally different.

records.definition_text: used to say that you think that something is true, but cannot be sure
records.searchterms_text: knowledge;to (the best of) my knowledge;to the best of my knowledge
records.learnerexamples_text: To the best of my knowledge, she's never worked abroad.; Besides, to the best of my knowledge, nowhere in the city can [you] try such lovely mushrooms.

records.definition_text: to put your hand on something
records.learnerexamples_text: That paint is wet - don't touch it.; He touched the girl on the arm to get her attention.; Suddenly, someone touched my arm and I screamed.

records.definition_text: If two things touch, they are so close to each other that there is no space between them.
records.learnerexamples_text: These two wires must not touch. ; Out of the blue, I felt the wheels touching the ground.

records.definition_text: to affect your emotions, especially so that you feel pleased or a little sad
records.learnerexamples_text: I was deeply touched by her letter.; Her stories are based on real life, so they're not only easy to read but also touch our hearts.

records.definition_text: the ability to feel things by putting your hand on them
records.learnerexamples_text: the sense of touch; The material was soft to the touch.

records.definition_text: when you put your hand or finger on something
records.learnerexamples_text: I felt the touch of his hand on my face.; At the touch of a button, the door opened.; In a shopping centre you may search [for] something for hours, but [on the] internet you can find everything with the touch of a button.

records.definition_text: difficult
records.learnerexamples_text: He's had a tough time at work recently. ;  We've had to make some tough decisions. ; Homeless people are facing a tough winter.; You know it was really a very tough decision for me.

records.definition_text: Tough people are mentally strong and not afraid of difficult situations.
records.learnerexamples_text: You have to be tough to be successful in politics.; It is about a tough old fisherman from Cuba who sails out alone in a small boat to fish.

records.definition_text: describes food that is difficult to cut or eat
records.learnerexamples_text: This steak is very tough.; Your pork chop was as tough as old boots and the salad dressing was sour!

records.definition_text: to go on a tour somewhere
records.learnerexamples_text: We spent a month touring (around/round) Kenya.; The New Zealand team will be touring in Europe this winter.; The band are currently touring to promote their new album.; She and her husband came over [to] England for [a] short stay and are touring Europe [on] a second honeymoon as [it's the] 10th anniversary of their marriage.

records.definition_text: the business of providing services for tourists, including organizing their travel, hotels, entertainment, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: Tourism is Venice's main industry.; These beautiful old towns have remained relatively untouched by tourism.; As you know, Peru is one of the countries with [the] most tourism around the world.

records.definition_text: a competition with a series of games between many teams or players, with one winner at the end
records.learnerexamples_text: a tennis/chess/golf tournament; They were defeated in the first round of the tournament.; I met him at a basketball tournament and his name is Mark.

records.definition_text: in the direction of someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: She stood up and walked towards him.; He leaned towards his wife and whispered, "Can we go home soon?"; She kept glancing towards the telephone.; We took the train from Paris to Bordeaux, and from there we started to cycle towards the sea.

records.definition_text: in relation to something or someone
records.learnerexamples_text: They've always been very friendly towards me.; He feels a lot of anger towards his father.; She always has a positive attitude towards life.; His parents were very cold towards me.

records.definition_text: a very tall, narrow building, or part of a building
records.learnerexamples_text: the Eiffel Tower; There's a clock on the church tower.; He works in an office tower in downtown San Francisco.; I think that, first of all, we should visit our capital because it has many old towers, castles and churches, which you have to see.

records.definition_text: poisonous
records.learnerexamples_text: toxic chemicals/fumes/waste; Paris throws out billions of tons of toxic gases into the atmosphere, and in the summer months, [it]'s wrapped in a veil of toxic haze, from power station[s], factory chimneys, and from the exhausts of cars and lorries on the streets.

records.definition_text: proof that someone or something was in a place
records.learnerexamples_text: There was no trace of her anywhere.; When she moved out, she left no trace of having been there.; He seems to have disappeared without trace.; There were no traces of anything alive nearby.

records.definition_text: a narrow path or road
records.learnerexamples_text: We followed a dirt track off the main road. ; However, on the second day, the sun appeared, and we went [o]n a mountain track.

records.definition_text: a path, often circular, used for races
records.learnerexamples_text: a race track; The runners are now on their final lap of the track.; There are 3 football fields, 4 basketball fields, an athletic[s] track, 4 tennis fields, and a bar [and] changing rooms.

records.definition_text: one song or piece of music on a CD, record, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: The album includes four previously unreleased tracks.; It is a really good idea to give every CD a book containing information about every track on [the] disc and about [the] performance.

records.definition_text: a sport in which people compete with each other by running a race on a specially prepared circular path
records.learnerexamples_text: a track event; Since that time I have been reading every article about track and field.

records.definition_text: a mark or line of marks left on the ground or on another surface by an animal, person or vehicle which has moved over it
records.learnerexamples_text: Police found tyre tracks in the mud.; The hunters followed the tracks of the deer for hours.; The burglars were careful not to leave any tracks behind them.; I [saw] some tracks on the floor. I went to the bedroom and near the bed I [saw] a big cat with its kittens.

records.definition_text: loose, comfortable trousers and a top, especially worn for exercising
records.learnerexamples_text: He was wearing a tracksuit and trainers.; I also like wearing tracksuits, because they are very soft and warm.

records.definition_text: the buying and selling of large numbers of goods or services, especially between countries
records.learnerexamples_text: The country's trade in manufactured goods has expanded in the last ten years.; They rely heavily on trade with Europe.; The two countries have signed a trade agreement for one year only.; You know, I work in a foreign trade company so I have to be well dressed.

records.definition_text: someone's job, especially one which needs skill in using their hands
records.learnerexamples_text: He's a builder by trade. ; He left school at 15 to learn a trade.; At the age of 15 he [left] school and started to learn a trade.

records.definition_text: to buy and sell goods or services, especially between countries
records.learnerexamples_text: For centuries, Native Americans traded with European settlers.; The company has been trading in oil for many years.; The two countries have become close trading partners.; Our books are traded right across Asia.; His story is interest[ing]: he first worked in a little shop in Bourges and started trading in France, then in Europe, [and] in Asia.

records.definition_text: a custom or way of behaving that has continued for a long time in a group of people or a society
records.learnerexamples_text: Fireworks have long been an American tradition on the Fourth of July.; There's a long/strong tradition of dance in St Petersburg.; We decided to break with tradition this year and go away for Christmas.; Nevertheless, Leipzig has always been an attractive town for tourists, because of its well-known fair and its cultural traditions.

records.definition_text: following the customs or ways of behaving that have continued in a group of people or society for a long time
records.learnerexamples_text: traditional farming methods; The dancers were wearing traditional Hungarian dress/costume.; She's very traditional in her ideas.; If you come to visit me, I'll invite you to "La Provincana" to have traditional Argentinian food.

records.definition_text: according to tradition or in a traditional way
records.learnerexamples_text: Chestnuts are traditionally eaten at Christmas.; Traditionally, the company's main markets have been Britain and the US.; You will be able to try our special sau[sages], produced traditionally in our city!

records.definition_text: a line of cars, trucks, etc. that are moving slowly or not moving at all
records.learnerexamples_text: They got stuck in a traffic jam.; Cities are always crowded; there are lots of traffic jams, so they are very polluted.

records.definition_text: an event or situation which is very sad, often involving death
records.learnerexamples_text: His life was touched by hardship and personal tragedy.; They had only recently arrived in London when tragedy struck - their son was killed in a traffic accident.; The people who cause those tragedies are irresponsible drivers.

records.definition_text: very sad, often involving death and suffering
records.learnerexamples_text: Her tragic death at the age of 36 shocked the world.; He was killed in a tragic accident.; Hospital authorities admitted that a tragic error had taken place.; For instance, the tragic death of Princess Diana is an example of what a journalist must not do.

records.definition_text: a path through the countryside, often made or used for a particular purpose
records.learnerexamples_text: a forest/mountain trail; After 6 miles of the trail we decided to stop and put our blanket on the ground.

records.definition_text: to practise a sport or exercise, often in order to prepare for a sporting event, or to help someone to do this
records.learnerexamples_text: He's been training hard for the race for several weeks now. ; She told me that they are training for a tournament which is in about four weeks.

records.definition_text: to teach someone how to do something, usually a skill that is needed for a job
records.learnerexamples_text: We are training all our staff in how to use the new computer system. ;  The aid workers trained local people to give the injections. ; I think I could be suitable for the job because I have some experience [of] training people.

records.definition_text: to learn the skills you need to do a job
records.learnerexamples_text: He trained as a lawyer in Vienna. ; For example, one of my father's friends who was trained as a computer engineer received the only job vacancy for economy-related work in a very good company just because he graduated from the best university in Taiwan.

records.definition_text: a person who teaches skills to people or animals and prepares them for a job, activity or sport
records.learnerexamples_text: a teacher trainer; a fitness trainer; They showed pictures of the horse and its trainer.; The trainer is O.K., too, and he told me that I can play in the team in four to five weeks.

records.definition_text: the process of learning the skills you need to do a particular job or activity
records.learnerexamples_text: a training course; a teacher-training college; New staff have/receive a week's training in how to use the computers.; I decided to join the new class because I [am] tak[ing] training in broadcasting now, so I need to improve my English.

records.definition_text: preparation for a sport or competition
records.learnerexamples_text: football training; After the training, the team invited me to the club party next weekend.

records.definition_text: to move someone or something from one place to another
records.learnerexamples_text: He has been transferred to a psychiatric hospital.; Police are investigating how £20 million was illegally transferred from the Trust's bank account.; The aim is to transfer power/control/responsibility to self-governing regional councils.; The person described himself as a financial officer of a South African government and needs a contact person in Switzerland to transfer [the] sum of 200 million dollar[s].

records.definition_text: to change to a different job, team, place of work, etc., or to make someone do this
records.learnerexamples_text: After a year he transferred to University College, Dublin.; Some very high-profile British players have transferred to clubs abroad.; He threatened to give up football if his club didn't transfer him.; I'm talking about Michael Ballack, who was transferred to the Chelsea soccer team at the beginning of this season.

records.definition_text: when something or someone moves or is moved from one place, position, etc. to another
records.learnerexamples_text: the transfer of information; Black's transfer to an Italian football club came as a shock to Coventry supporters.; Most of the transfers are controlled by computers.

records.definition_text: to change something completely, usually to improve it
records.learnerexamples_text: Within weeks they had transformed the area into a beautiful garden.; The reorganization will transform the British entertainment industry.; Well th[ese] are some ideas that could help transform the cinema with the extra money that is available.

records.definition_text: A transitive verb always has an object.
records.learnerexamples_text: Transitive verbs, such as 'put', are marked [T].

records.definition_text: to change written or spoken words from one language to another
records.learnerexamples_text: We were asked to translate a list of sentences.; She works for the EU, translating from English into French.; I was ashamed because I needed someone to translate [everything] that the people said to me.

records.definition_text: something which has been translated from one language to another, or the process of translating
records.learnerexamples_text: It's a translation from the original Spanish.; In the second paper they are asked to do a translation.; Much of the beauty of the rhymes is lost in translation.; We [did] some translations and wrote [a] few letters.

records.definition_text: If a substance or object is transparent, you can see through it very clearly.
records.learnerexamples_text: Grow the bulbs in a transparent plastic box, so the children can see the roots developing.; We loved [it] there, because the sky was [a] clear blue and the sea was transparent.

records.definition_text: a vehicle or system of vehicles, such as buses, trains, aircraft, etc. for getting from one place to another
records.learnerexamples_text: investment in public transport ; Do you have your own transport?; Bicycles are a cheap and efficient form of transport.; We'll stay in a hostel [be]cause it's cheap and we'll use public transport.

records.definition_text: to move people or goods from one place to another
records.learnerexamples_text: The goods are packed in boxes and transported overseas.; The pipeline was constructed to transport oil to ports on the coast.; Such heavy items are expensive to transport by plane.; At first we chase them in the forests and then put them in small and narrow boxes to be transported to a zoo.

records.definition_text: when people or goods are moved from one place to another
records.learnerexamples_text: the transport of live animals; The company will arrange transport from the airport.; In addition to that, a car is more suitable for the transport of goods.

records.definition_text: a piece of equipment for catching animals
records.learnerexamples_text: a mouse trap; The fox got its foot caught in a trap.; Angel's horse hurt its leg in a trap for foxes.

records.definition_text: a dangerous or unpleasant situation which is difficult to escape from
records.learnerexamples_text: The undercover agents went to the house knowing that it might be a trap.; She's too clever to fall into the trap of doing any unpaid work.; With this trap Miss Marple reveals Dr. Quimper's real motive and has him arrested by the police.

records.definition_text: to move or go from one place to another
records.learnerexamples_text: Supersonic planes can travel faster than the speed of sound.;  News of the accident travelled fast.; [In the film,] there were a lot of space-shuttles that travelled around stars and planets.

records.definition_text: the activity of travelling
records.learnerexamples_text: air/space travel; business travel; We share a love of literature, food and travel.; I heard on the travel news that there'd been an accident.; In the travel industry they are looking for Advanced English.

records.definition_text: someone whose job is making travel arrangements for people
records.learnerexamples_text: She worked for many years as a travel agent.; I am living with a family in London which the travel agent recommended [to] me.

records.definition_text: someone who travels
records.learnerexamples_text: This hotel is for serious travellers, rather than tourists on two-week package holidays.; Singapore - 'The Island of Paradise' - is a place travellers from all around the world would not want to miss.

records.definition_text: a flat object, usually with raised edges, used for carrying food and drinks
records.learnerexamples_text: She was carrying a tray of drinks.; Our table had to be cleaned up, so I took a couple of trays, crossed the room and put the trays [o]nto a shelf.

records.definition_text: very valuable things, usually in the form of a store of precious metals, precious stones or money
records.learnerexamples_text: Stories about pirates often include a search for buried treasure.; When they opened up the tomb they found treasure beyond their wildest dreams.; It was said that King Arthur had hid[d]en his treasure in a cave near his castle and he was the only [one] who knew where [it] was located.

records.definition_text: to behave towards or deal with someone in a particular way
records.learnerexamples_text: My parents treated us all the same when we were kids.; He treated his wife very badly.; They treat her like one of their own children.; She felt she'd been unfairly treated by her employer.; I'll treat them like my own son and daughter.

records.definition_text: to give medical care to someone for an illness or injury
records.learnerexamples_text: He is being treated for a rare skin disease.; Western medicine tends to treat the symptoms and not the cause.; I have also worked for the "Red Cross" so I know how to treat injuries, if someone gets hurt.

records.definition_text: to consider something in a particular way
records.learnerexamples_text: He treated my suggestion as a joke.; It was [a] horrible experience, beli[e]ve me, but now we treat it as an adventure.

records.definition_text: to do or buy something special for someone
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm going to treat them to dinner at that new restaurant.; There is one nice pub, of course I'll treat you!

records.definition_text: the use of drugs, exercises, etc. to cure a person of an illness or injury
records.learnerexamples_text: free dental treatment; Perhaps it's time to try a new course of treatment.; This disease doesn't generally respond to treatment.; There are various treatments for this complaint.; For instance, if I had a child who need[ed] special medical treatment and I [was] rich then it would make me very happy to be able to pay for an expensive operation and to see my child growing up.

records.definition_text: the way you deal with or behave towards someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: There have been complaints about the treatment of prisoners.; Peter gets special treatment because he knows the boss.; My pet doesn't need special treatment. All it needs is care and love.

records.definition_text: when you go on a long, difficult journey on foot
records.learnerexamples_text: We want to go trekking in the Himalayas.; I hear she's going to Africa for some trekking.

records.definition_text: to shake slightly, usually because you are cold, frightened, or very emotional
records.learnerexamples_text: When he came out of the water, he was trembling with cold.; Her bottom lip trembled and tears welled up in her eyes.; His voice started to tremble and I thought he was going to cry.; It was Tuesday the 13th and the fact that I was very superstitious made me tremble with fear.

records.definition_text: extremely good
records.learnerexamples_text: I think she's doing a tremendous job. ; He's been a tremendous help.; I think it would be a tremendous idea to work with you.

records.definition_text: very large, great, strong, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: a tremendous amount of money ; I think I certainly could live without watching television for a week, but it would put a tremendous strain on my everyday life.

records.definition_text: very or very much
records.learnerexamples_text: They've worked tremendously hard.; We all enjoyed ourselves tremendously.; I enjoyed it tremendously.

records.definition_text: a general development or change in a situation or in the way that people are behaving
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm not familiar with the latest trends in teaching methodology.; The trend at the moment is towards a more natural and less made-up look.; Surveys show a trend away from home-ownership and towards rented accommodation.; There's been a downward/upward trend in sales in the last few years.; So the most important thing [about] shopping is that you can talk about the [lat]est news with your friend and look for the newest trends.

records.definition_text: a legal process to decide if someone is guilty of a crime
records.learnerexamples_text: The two men are now on trial for attempted murder.; He will be taken to the US to stand trial.; Trial by jury is a fundamental right.; It was a very complicated trial that went on for months.; the trial proceedings

records.definition_text: a flat shape with three straight sides
records.learnerexamples_text: an equilateral triangle; There's a small triangle of land to one side of the house.; On the right, two cherry trees and an apple tree are placed [in the] shape [of] a triangle.

records.definition_text: a group of people who live together, usually in areas far away from cities, and who share the same culture and language and still have a traditional way of life
records.learnerexamples_text: a tribe of Amazonian Indians; the Masai tribe; Then I went South to Mali and visited the Dagan tribe whose mythology and rituals interest me a great deal.

records.definition_text: something you do to deceive or cheat someone, or to make someone look stupid as a joke
records.learnerexamples_text: She played a really nasty trick on me - she put syrup in my shampoo bottle!; It's a bit of trick photography - she's meant to look like she's walking on water.; At my first lesson, Jim decided to play a trick [on] us!

records.definition_text: something that is done to entertain people and that seems to be magic
records.learnerexamples_text: a card trick; My niece likes to do magic tricks for us.; She [did] some magic tricks.

records.definition_text: an effective or quick way of doing something
records.learnerexamples_text: What's the trick to getting this chair to fold up?; On page 21, twenty tricks to speed up your beauty routine.; I like all kinds of sports: swimming, volleyball, football, bowling, golf, and so on. I hope that [by] joining your club I will learn all the rules and tricks of these sports.

records.definition_text: to deceive someone
records.learnerexamples_text: They tricked him into signing the papers.; After they explained everything to him, he then knew he was being tricked by them.

records.definition_text: difficult to deal with or do
records.learnerexamples_text: Those bird models are quite tricky to make, aren't they?; I'm in a tricky situation really - whatever I do I'll offend someone.; I think Chris is more sensitive than you and she has taken into account how tricky that route could turn out [to be].

records.definition_text: to fall or almost fall because you hit your foot on something when you are walking or running
records.learnerexamples_text: Careful you don't trip over the cat!;  He tripped on a stone and hurt his ankle. ; We got in the house and it was so dark in there that I couldn't see anything. Then I tripped over a box, I believe.

records.definition_text: small and not important
records.learnerexamples_text: It's a fairly trivial offence.; It may seem trivial to you but it matters to me.; Sexual harassment in the workplace is not a trivial matter.; All this may seem trivial [and] unimportant to an ordinary man addicted to [his] TV set.

records.definition_text: a metal object with two or four wheels that you push or pull to transport large or heavy objects on
records.learnerexamples_text: a shopping/supermarket trolley; The hospital is so overcrowded that some patients are being treated on trolleys in the corridors.; Sometimes customers' trolleys run into each other and they have to wait ages to go through check-[out].

records.definition_text: a prize, such as a silver cup, that you get for winning a race or competition
records.learnerexamples_text: He's an excellent snooker player, but he's never won a major trophy.; The Duchess of Kent will be presenting the trophies.; How about organising some competitions with pri[z]es, like a trophy??

records.definition_text: from or in the hottest parts of the world
records.learnerexamples_text: a tropical island/region/climate; a tropical storm; She specialises in tropical medicine.; The Amazon river basin contains the world's largest tropical rainforest.; There were special tropical flowers from Brazil and East Asia.

records.definition_text: when you use extra time or energy to do something
records.learnerexamples_text: He took the trouble to write to each of them personally. ;  "Would you like to have a meal with us?" "Only if it's not too much trouble." ; I could give you a lift - it's no trouble.; I hope it's not too much trouble and I swear I will not break anything again.

records.definition_text: problems, difficulties, or worries
records.learnerexamples_text: Parents often have trouble finding restaurants that welcome young children.; The form was terribly complicated and I had a lot of trouble with it.; The trouble started when my father came to live with us.; I should get it finished over the weekend without too much trouble.;  I'd like to go to the party, but the trouble is my parents won't let me.

records.definition_text: a difficult, unpleasant or dangerous situation
records.learnerexamples_text: The company was in serious trouble with massive debts.; He got into financial trouble after his divorce.; The marriage ran into trouble because of her husband's heavy drinking.; She opened her eyes and saw that she was in serious trouble because it was much to[o] late.

records.definition_text: when you have done something wrong and are likely to be punished
records.learnerexamples_text: Her children are always in trouble. ;  They got into trouble with the police. ; He's never been in trouble with his teachers before.; She'll be in big trouble if she's late again.; It's a great way of getting kids off the street and keeping them out of trouble.

records.definition_text: a situation in which people are fighting or arguing
records.learnerexamples_text: The trouble started after a group of drunken football fans started to throw bottles.; Listen, I don't want any trouble in here, so please just finish your drink and leave.; When we arrived, there had been two men eating on the table just next to us, but they had disap[p]eared when the trouble started.

records.definition_text: a large road vehicle for carrying goods from place to place
records.learnerexamples_text: The road was completely blocked by an overturned truck.; a truck driver; My bed[room] ha[s] drawings of trucks and motorbike[s].

records.definition_text: real
records.learnerexamples_text: true love; a true friend; The true horror of the accident did not become clear until the morning.; The film we saw was so nice. It [was] about true friends.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize a description of something
records.learnerexamples_text: This is a truly remarkable achievement.; It was a truly terrifying experience.; Those concerts are truly eye-opening.

records.definition_text: a metal musical instrument that you play by blowing into it and pressing buttons to make different notes
records.learnerexamples_text: Liz used to play the trumpet.; I play the guitar and John plays the trumpet.

records.definition_text: the thick stem of a tree that the branches grow from
records.learnerexamples_text: The trunks of these trees can be more than two metres wide.; Paula found a small hole in the trunk, just near Laura's feet.

records.definition_text: to believe that someone is good and honest and will not harm you, or that something is safe and reliable
records.learnerexamples_text: My sister warned me not to trust him.; Trust me - I know about these things.; I trust her to make the right decision.; That man is not to be trusted.; I wouldn't trust him with my car.

records.definition_text: the belief that you can trust someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: a relationship based on trust and understanding; We were obviously wrong to put our trust in her.; He's in a position of trust.; Now the trial is starting and, as a result, I have lost trust in my friends.

records.definition_text: the quality of being true
records.learnerexamples_text: There may be some truth in what she says.; There is no truth in the reports of his resignation.; And yet what he says contains at least a grain of truth.; My humble opinion is that this statement is absolute, even though there is a great deal of truth behind it.

records.definition_text: to do, test, taste, etc. something to discover if it works or if you like it
records.learnerexamples_text: I tried that recipe you gave me last night. ;  He tried the door, but the handle was broken. ;  Why don't you try using a different shampoo? ; You should try Hungarian food.

records.definition_text: an attempt to do something
records.learnerexamples_text: They might just have a place left on the course - why don't you give it a try?; Give it here - I'll have a try.; You could ask him if he's willing - it's worth a try.; This will be her third try at jumping the bar.; I can assure that you will like it, so give it a try.

records.base_text: try out sth or try sth out
records.definition_text: to use something to discover if it works or if you like it
records.searchterms_text: try;try out sth or try sth out
records.learnerexamples_text: Why don't you try out your new racket?; We're going to try out that Italian restaurant tonight.; Moreover we have a riding school for those that want to try out this experience.

records.definition_text: a long, thin container for a soft substance, that you press to get the substance out
records.learnerexamples_text: a tube of toothpaste ; And, of course, she got a set of excellent tools and I won only one thing: a tube of modelling glue.

records.definition_text: a pipe made of glass, plastic, metal, etc., especially for liquids or gases to flow through
records.learnerexamples_text: Gases produced in the reaction pass through this tube and can then be collected.; I threw the tube into the river.

records.definition_text: a large sea fish, or the meat from this fish
records.learnerexamples_text: I had a tuna sandwich for lunch.; I'll make tuna with tomatoes, it's delici[o]us.

records.definition_text: a long passage under the ground or through a mountain
records.learnerexamples_text: The train went into the tunnel.; Unfortunately, the tunnel was closed so I just had to continue walking on the pathway.

records.definition_text: a bird that looks like a large chicken, or the meat of this bird
records.learnerexamples_text: We had turkey for dinner.; I asked for a turkey pie [but] they gave me a beef pie, so they change[d] it for me.

records.definition_text: to move your body so that you are facing a different direction
records.learnerexamples_text: Ricky turned and saw Sue standing in the doorway. ; She put out the light, turned over and went to sleep.; I turned around and looked into the eyes of my favourite football player Timo Hildebrand.

records.definition_text: to move something round so that it faces a different direction
records.learnerexamples_text: Ella turned the cup to hide the crack in it.; I turned it over in my hands and looked at it quite carefully.

records.definition_text: to move a page in a book or magazine in order to see the next one
records.learnerexamples_text: Now turn the page, please, and start Exercise 2.; He turned over two or three pages.; Now turn to page 23 and look at the first paragraph.; Television helps a lot to make our life easier. But, where is the poetry of handling a book? Yes, there is a lot of poetry, first you handle it, you turn the pages, second you can read any passage, where and when you want.

records.definition_text: to move around a central point in a circle, or to make something do this
records.learnerexamples_text: Turn the steering wheel as quickly as you can. ; The Earth turns on its axis once every 24 hours.; The wheels started to turn (round).; She turned the door knob and quietly opened the door.; It's not like sitting on a bike and just turning the pedals, in this case you work only your legs.

records.definition_text: the time when you can or must do something, usually before or after someone else
records.learnerexamples_text: Is it my turn yet?; It's your turn to do the washing up!; In this game if you give the wrong answer you have to miss a turn.; I really enjoy[ed] the holidays in England with you, so now it's my turn to invite you to come to my country, Peru.

records.definition_text: a change in the direction in which you are moving or facing
records.learnerexamples_text: a left/right turn; We got as far as the school, and there we had to make a right turn.

records.definition_text: to become blue, cold, nasty, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: The sky turned black and it started to rain. ; The weather has suddenly turned cold.; When I refused to pay, he turned nasty.; She turned pale and started to shiver.; His friends began to laugh and my face turned red.

records.base_text: turn down sb/sth or turn sb/sth down
records.definition_text: to refuse an offer or request
records.searchterms_text: turn;turn down sb/sth or turn sb/sth down;turn down sb/sth or turn sb/sth down
records.learnerexamples_text: He offered her a trip to Australia but she turned it/him down.; He turned down the job because it involved too much travelling.; I hope you don't turn down my invitation.

records.base_text: turn down sth or turn sth down
records.definition_text: to reduce the level of sound or heat that something produces
records.searchterms_text: turn;turn down sth or turn sth down;turn down sth or turn sth down
records.learnerexamples_text: I asked him to turn down the heating.; Actually, as I know nothing about instruments, the only thing I could do was just turn the volume up and down.

records.definition_text: a corner where one road meets another
records.learnerexamples_text: Take the first turning on the left.; Then, take the second turning on the left and go along that road until you get to the roundabout.

records.definition_text: to happen in a particular way or to have a particular result, especially an unexpected one
records.learnerexamples_text: The bomb warning turned out to be a false alarm.; How did the recipe turn out?; But unfortunately, my experience of seeing the musical show named "Over the Rainbow" in your Circle Theatre turned out to be rather disappointing.

records.definition_text: to be known or discovered finally and surprisingly
records.learnerexamples_text: It turned out that we'd been to the same school.; It turned out that Corey was organizing the concert and he asked me and three of my friends if we wanted to help.

records.definition_text: If people turn out for an event, they go there.
records.learnerexamples_text: Thousands of people turned out to welcome the England team home.; Over 800 people turned out for the protest.; On top of that, there were more than 5,000 people who had turn[ed] out [for] the festival!

records.definition_text: to change and become someone or something different, or to make someone or something do this
records.searchterms_text: turn;turn (sb/sth) into sb/sth;turn (sb/sth) into sb/sth ;turn sb/sth into sb/sth;turn sb/sth into sb/sth
records.learnerexamples_text: The council was hoping to turn a children's home into a residence for adolescent girls.; The town turned from a small seaside resort into a major commercial centre when oil was discovered.; After midnight it turns into a club where you can dance [to] any kind of music.

records.definition_text: to return in the direction you have come from, or to make someone do this
records.learnerexamples_text: They had to turn back because of the bad weather.; As we were walking along we came across a river we couldn't pass, so we turned back.

records.definition_text: to ask a person or organization for help or support
records.learnerexamples_text: Eventually she turned to her aunt for help.; Her family lived a long way away, and she had no one to turn to.; People were very friendly and there was always someone to turn to in case of trouble.

records.definition_text: to arrive or appear somewhere
records.searchterms_text: turn;turn up (somewhere);turn up (somewhere) ;turn up somewhere;turn up somewhere
records.learnerexamples_text: Do you think many people will turn up?; She turned up at my house late one night.; A few minutes later two security men turned up.

records.base_text: turn up sth or turn sth up
records.definition_text: to increase the level of sound or heat that a machine produces
records.searchterms_text: turn;turn up sth or turn sth up
records.learnerexamples_text: Could you turn the heating up, please?; In addition to that, my neighbour is always organizing part[ie]s during the week. He stay[s up] with his friends till late and they turn the music up.

records.definition_text: someone who teaches one person or a very small group of people
records.learnerexamples_text: a private tutor; We could afford t[rips] abroad, modern labour-saving devices and private tutors.

records.definition_text: one of two children who are born to the same mother at the same time
records.learnerexamples_text: My sister has twin sons.; a twin sister; I have twin cousins there and I love them [very] much.

records.definition_text: bent so that the original shape is changed or destroyed
records.learnerexamples_text: a twisted tree trunk; a twisted ankle; twisted metal; When I got there, a very nice nurse told me that I['ve] got a twisted ankle and I [can]not walk for one week!

records.definition_text: at a particular time in the future
records.searchterms_text: away;two weeks/five hours etc away;two weeks/five hours, etc. away
records.learnerexamples_text: My English exam's only a week away and I haven't even started to prepare.; Christmas is just a few months away, and I do not inten[d] to spend it all alone like in the past few years, so I am writing to invite you [to] my real Christmas party without my parents.

records.definition_text: to write something using a keyboard
records.learnerexamples_text: She asked me to type a couple of letters.; He can type very quickly.; I was typing away into the early hours of the morning just to get the thing finished.; I'm typing this email to ask your permission to borrow your bicycle.

records.definition_text: having all the qualities you expect a particular person, object, place, etc to have
records.learnerexamples_text: I must look like the typical tourist with my shorts and my camera.; This sort of hot and spicy food is very typical of the food in the south of the country.; Typical symptoms would include severe headaches, vomiting and dizziness.; This film is a typical horror film.

records.definition_text: used for saying what usually happens
records.learnerexamples_text: Typically, a doctor will see about thirty patients a day.; Tickets for such events will typically cost around thirty dollars.; The climate of Brazil is typically tropical so the weather is gorgeous.

records.definition_text: in a way that shows all the characteristics that you would expect from the stated person, thing or group
records.learnerexamples_text: She has that reserve and slight coldness of manner which is typically English.; Paul, in typically rude fashion, told him he was talking rubbish.; Your wife really made an effort to cook me typically English dishes.

records.definition_text: better, greater or worse than all similar things
records.learnerexamples_text: Climbing Mount Everest is the ultimate challenge.; the ultimate luxury cruise; For me, rats are the ultimate horror.; Being on the road is always better than the arrival, so this journey would be the ultimate journey for me as well.

records.definition_text: too bad to be allowed to continue
records.learnerexamples_text: The water contains unacceptable levels of pollution.; I find that sort of behaviour completely unacceptable.; The unions have described the latest pay offer as unacceptable.; So I waited for 45 minutes until the show started. [T]hat is an unacceptable delay.

records.definition_text: not beautiful or nice to look at
records.learnerexamples_text: I felt old and unattractive.; Their new building is very unattractive.; This information is useful for [a person] who thinks his/her body is unattractive.

records.definition_text: impossible to buy or get
records.learnerexamples_text: The book is unavailable in Britain.; The third point was that the discount[ed] tickets were unavailable.

records.definition_text: not knowing about something
records.learnerexamples_text: He was unaware that the police were watching him.; I was quite unaware of the problem.; Although you may be an expert in one subject you can be unaware [of] some basics in others.

records.definition_text: too painful or unpleasant for you to continue to experience
records.learnerexamples_text: The heat was almost unbearable.; Life can be very difficult, almost unbearable sometimes.

records.definition_text: extremely bad or good and making you feel surprised
records.learnerexamples_text: It's unbelievable how lucky she's been.; You've had such bad luck - it's unbelievable.; The food is unbelievable and I'm sure you'll love it.

records.definition_text: not probable and difficult to believe
records.learnerexamples_text: I found most of the characters in the play totally unbelievable.; They made up unbelievable stories which almost made them cry in the end.

records.definition_text: not sure or not able to decide about something
records.learnerexamples_text: She's uncertain whether to go to New Zealand or not.; Bridie was uncertain about meeting him.; [There are] things that I am uncertain about, and [that I would] be grateful if you c[ould] explain.

records.definition_text: not known or fixed, or not completely certain
records.learnerexamples_text: New arrivals face an uncertain future.; The political outlook is still uncertain.; Please do not bother posting them since we do not have a zip code where I live, and they might get lost with our uncertain Post Service.

records.definition_text: staying the same
records.learnerexamples_text: The area has remained virtually unchanged in fifty years.; All the big and small things which defin[e] people's personal environment will be left nearly unchanged - the furniture, the pictures on the wall.... I suppose our future homes will be a mix of new technologies and good old tradition.

records.definition_text: not easy to understand
records.learnerexamples_text: The situation at the moment is unclear.; It's unclear what actually happened that night.; It's unclear whether he arrived before or after the shot was fired.; If something is unclear please give me a call.

records.definition_text: not feeling comfortable and pleasant, or not making you feel comfortable and pleasant
records.learnerexamples_text: I've eaten so much, I'm really quite uncomfortable.; These shoes are really uncomfortable.; The thing[s] I most hate wearing are shirts, I think they're very uncomfortable.

records.definition_text: in a state as though you are sleeping, for example because you have been hit on the head
records.learnerexamples_text: She was hit on the head by a stone and knocked unconscious.; In the morning, Mrs Crozier went to visit Miss Appleford in number 42 only to find her lying on the floor unconscious.

records.definition_text: a noun which does not have a plural form and cannot be used with 'a' or 'one'
records.learnerexamples_text: 'Information' and 'furniture' are uncountable nouns.

records.definition_text: in a particular state or condition
records.learnerexamples_text: The President is under pressure to resign. ; Under no circumstances should the festival become too specialized.; I am used to working under pressure.

records.definition_text: being affected by something at the present time
records.learnerexamples_text: The town is once again under attack.; The cause of the fire is still under investigation.;  A new 16-screen cinema is under construction.;  Several different plans are under discussion.; We are working hard to get the situation under control.

records.definition_text: being dealt with successfully
records.learnerexamples_text: Don't worry - everything's under control.; "Everything is under control," said the captain.

records.definition_text: to fail to understand how large, strong, or important something is
records.learnerexamples_text: Many people underestimate the cost of owning a car.; We shouldn't underestimate the part that exercise plays in good health.; The report also seemed to underestimate the number of people that had attended.

records.definition_text: below the surface of the ground
records.learnerexamples_text: an underground cave/passage; Some animals, such as moles, live underground.; As it was expected, Harry was seen, and then he went underground t[h]rough a tunnel which crossed from the inner city to the Russian zone.

records.definition_text: below the surface of the ground
records.learnerexamples_text: an underground cave/passage; Some animals, such as moles, live underground.; As it was expected, Harry was seen, and then he went underground t[h]rough a tunnel which crossed from the inner city to the Russian zone.

records.definition_text: to draw a line under a word or sentence, especially in order to show its importance
records.learnerexamples_text: All the technical words have been underlined in red.; And, another disadvantage in my opinion is that is more difficult to underline or to write some notes if you study from the computer.

records.definition_text: to emphasize the truth or importance of something
records.learnerexamples_text: The report underlines the need for more teachers in schools.; It is true that museums do not show the past as well as they could, but we must underline that they are always good enough if we are really interested in knowing about our past.

records.definition_text: under or below something
records.learnerexamples_text: The tunnel goes right underneath the city.; They found a bomb underneath the car.; She was dressed like a princess, after spending the whole day looking for an appropriate dress, which she finally managed to find underneath her bed.

records.definition_text: under or below
