records.definition_text: a piece of underwear that covers the area between your waist and the top of your legs
records.learnerexamples_text: I need some new underpants.; Was that woman me, standing there in those ugly-looking underpants, but with a smart sports bra, with everybody laughing around her?

records.definition_text: to know how someone feels or why they behave in a particular way
records.learnerexamples_text: I don't understand James sometimes.; I understand why she's so angry.; Maybe now you can understand why I hate shopping. kisses,

records.definition_text: An understandable feeling or action is one that you would expect in that particular situation.
records.learnerexamples_text: "I still feel really angry about it." "That's understandable."; Their refusal to help is perfectly/completely understandable, considering the circumstances.; I guess they wouldn't give me permission [to stay] at a female friend's home, but that's understandable.

records.definition_text: knowledge about a subject, situation, etc. or about how something works
records.learnerexamples_text: She doesn't have any understanding of politics.; My understanding of the agreement is that they will pay £50, 000 over two years.; It was my understanding that she would come alone.; It was my understanding that discounts were available on the tickets, as the advertisement showed, but there were no discounts.

records.definition_text: sympathy
records.learnerexamples_text: Thank you for your understanding - I do appreciate it.; Thank you for your understanding.

records.definition_text: showing sympathy for someone's problems
records.learnerexamples_text: Fortunately, my boss is very understanding.; They are famous, but they need to be alone sometimes. I think [the] media must be more understanding.

records.definition_text: under the surface of water
records.learnerexamples_text: an underwater camera; Seals can hear very well underwater.; If you have diving equipment, you will spend a very good time underwater.

records.definition_text: the clothes that you wear next to your skin, under your other clothes
records.learnerexamples_text: They sell a wide range of underwear.; If I see some nice underwear, I will buy it too.

records.definition_text: to open something that is tied or fastened
records.learnerexamples_text: I took off my hat and undid my coat.;  Can you undo this knot for me?; Can someone help me to undo my seat belt?

records.definition_text: to make a computer get rid of the last change you made to a document and make it the way it was before
records.learnerexamples_text: You need to undo that change.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize that something is true
records.learnerexamples_text: Stress has undoubtedly contributed to her illness.; This trip will undoubtedly be a wonderful experience.

records.definition_text: to remove your clothes or someone else's clothes
records.learnerexamples_text: She undressed the children and put them to bed.; The chair is for my clothes when I undress.

records.definition_text: not wearing any clothes
records.learnerexamples_text: I got undressed and went to bed.; We got undressed quicker than ever and ran into the waterfall.

records.definition_text: worried because you think something bad might happen
records.learnerexamples_text: I feel a bit uneasy about her travelling alone.; Anyway I was getting uneasy because of all that silence, so I began to sing.

records.definition_text: not having a job that provides money
records.learnerexamples_text: He's been unemployed for over a year.; I have been unemployed for four months.

records.definition_text: the number of people who are unemployed
records.learnerexamples_text: a rise/fall in unemployment; Unemployment has fallen/risen again for the third month in a row.; Later, after a discussion about unemployment, we did reading, writing and listening.

records.definition_text: not expected
records.learnerexamples_text: His death was completely unexpected.; Last week I had an unexpected visit from my best friend - Mark.

records.definition_text: in a way or at a time that is not expected
records.learnerexamples_text: Retail sales unexpectedly fell last month.; He called in quite unexpectedly last week.; He called me really unexpectedly at work, and told me to go [to] his office at once.

records.definition_text: not treating people in a equal way
records.learnerexamples_text: an unfair system; The test was unfair because some people had seen it before.; He [always] gave me horrible marks and was very unfair.

records.definition_text: not true and morally wrong
records.learnerexamples_text: It's unfair to blame Roger for everything.; Furthermore, it's unfair [to] say that there is nothing to do in the evenings, because there is lots to do.

records.definition_text: in an unfair way
records.learnerexamples_text: His employers treated him very unfairly.; Your report not only gave wrong information to your readers but also criti[c]ized a music festival unfairly.

records.definition_text: not known to you
records.learnerexamples_text: I noticed several unfamiliar faces in the meeting room.; His name was unfamiliar to me.; On the other hand, you may not like some dishes, because they may be unfamiliar to you.

records.definition_text: not fashionable or popular at a particular time
records.learnerexamples_text: This kind of cooking is very unfashionable now.; I think that museums became a little bit unfashionable [as a] way of knowing or showing something.

records.definition_text: not healthy because you do too little exercise
records.learnerexamples_text: I really must do some exercise - I'm so unfit.; I was interested in practicing some sport, because I was feeling quite unfit.

records.definition_text: not suitable or good enough
records.learnerexamples_text: The building was declared unfit for human habitation.; Cars also emit carbon monoxide and make the air unfit to breath[e].

records.definition_text: Something that is unforgettable is so good, interesting, etc. that you remember it for a long time.
records.learnerexamples_text: Seeing Niagara Falls was an unforgettable experience.; I've just arrived home and I'd like to thank you for the unforgettable weekend.

records.definition_text: used to show that you wish something was not true or had not happened
records.learnerexamples_text: an unfortunate mistake; It was so unfortunate that she lost her job just as her husband became ill.; It is unfortunate that he couldn't inform you about the conference.

records.definition_text: unlucky
records.learnerexamples_text: One unfortunate person failed to see the hole and fell straight into it.; He was always an unfortunate person, because bad things happen[ed] to him all the time.

records.definition_text: not friendly
records.learnerexamples_text: I found her rather unfriendly.; My last teacher was very unfriendly.

records.definition_text: the state of being unhappy
records.learnerexamples_text: Her unhappiness was obvious to everyone.; They feel very unhappy living in a zoo, since for them it is like a prison, and their unhappiness can bring about their death.

records.definition_text: not satisfied
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm unhappy about the situation.; We were very unhappy with the service at the hotel.; I'm still unhappy about my present accommodation [for] the following reasons.

records.definition_text: likely to become ill or likely to damage your health
records.learnerexamples_text: He has a very unhealthy lifestyle.; The city is unsafe and unhealthy because [of] the pollution and the violence.

records.definition_text: not wanting to help someone, in a way that seems unfriendly
records.learnerexamples_text: The taxi driver was rude and unhelpful.; However, The Taverna has no uniform and the waiters there are sometimes pushy and unhelpful.

records.definition_text: not important
records.learnerexamples_text: Staffing is still a relatively unimportant issue compared to the other problems that we're facing.; Pat told him some unimportant things such as she learnt to swim at the age of five or that she loved ants.

records.definition_text: not interested
records.learnerexamples_text: He's completely uninterested in politics.; He is uninterested in his father['s] money.

records.definition_text: not interesting
records.learnerexamples_text: His later work is uninteresting in comparison with his first novel.; My neighbours are particularly uninteresting, they bore me stiff!

records.definition_text: when two or more countries, groups, etc. join together to make one country, group, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: the European Union; Meanwhile, the debate on European political and monetary union continues.

records.definition_text: an organization that represents people who do a particular job
records.learnerexamples_text: a teachers'/firefighters' union; Otherwise there will be some problems with trade unions.

records.definition_text: unusual and special
records.learnerexamples_text: Do not miss this unique opportunity to buy all six pans at half the recommended price.; First of all, I would like to tell you that I really enjoyed my stay and it was a unique experience for me.

records.definition_text: different from everyone and everything else
records.learnerexamples_text: Everyone's fingerprints are unique.; Every book is unique because every writer is unique, with his own style and his own character.

records.definition_text: a single thing or a separate part of something larger
records.learnerexamples_text: The first year of the course is divided into four units.; Each unit of the course book focuses on a different grammar point.; I'm sorry but I can't come [to] tomorrow's class because my father [had a] car crash and I have to take care [of] him but don't worry I can do the unit of my workbook and do the exercise.

records.definition_text: joined together as a group, organization, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: The whole village was united in their grief.; It was the first film festival to take place in a united Germany.; Despite all these advantages, I deeply miss the times [when] I had almost no technological facilities, but a very happy and united family.

records.definition_text: If people are united, they all agree about something.
records.learnerexamples_text: On the issue of education the party is united.; We have the authority to make changes, that is if we stand united.

records.definition_text: relating to everyone in the world, or to everyone in a particular group
records.learnerexamples_text: a universal truth; Food is a subject of almost universal interest.; The new reforms have not met with universal approval within the government.;  Kittens and puppies have an almost universal appeal. ; I think [the film] Yasujino Ozo has something universal in [relation to] our daily life, a kind of feeling or emotion.

records.definition_text: slightly cruel
records.learnerexamples_text: an unkind remark;  I didn't tell her the truth because I thought it would be unkind. ; His daughter-in-law was most unkind towards him.

records.definition_text: not famous
records.learnerexamples_text: an unknown actor; Two unknown actors were being filmed while they were acting.

records.definition_text: not known
records.learnerexamples_text: The exact number of people carrying the virus is unknown.; Unknown to me, she'd organized a party for my birthday.; There w[ere] few words and the address was unknown.

records.definition_text: except if
records.learnerexamples_text: I won't call you unless there are any problems.; You can't get a job unless you've got experience.; Unless you call me to say you're not coming, I'll see you at the theatre.; I never go shopping unless it's necessary.

records.definition_text: different from someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: The furniture was unlike anything she had ever seen.; Dan's actually quite nice, unlike his father.; Unlike you, I'm not a great dancer.; In fact the Hotel Astrid is now closed so I had to stay at the Riverside Hotel, [whi]ch offers great savings for students, unlike the Hotel Royal [whi]ch is quite expensive.

records.definition_text: not likely
records.learnerexamples_text: It's unlikely that we'll see them again.;  We might see them there but it's fairly unlikely.; He's unlikely to arrive before midday.; Unfortunately, it is very unlikely that I would be able to go and collect the keys at that time, because I have arranged an appointment with my doctor to see him about my leg.

records.definition_text: without any limits
records.learnerexamples_text: a service that offers unlimited Internet access; Moreover, who has the freedom to buy [whatever they need] with an unlimited budget?

records.definition_text: to open something which is locked using a key or an electronic device
records.learnerexamples_text: They haven't unlocked the computer room yet.; She unlocked the door and went in.

records.definition_text: having or causing bad luck
records.learnerexamples_text: They played well and were unlucky to lose.;  Some people think it's unlucky to walk under ladders. ; I'm going to tell you a story of an unlucky man.

records.definition_text: not normal or right
records.learnerexamples_text: an unnatural silence; unnatural conditions; Animals live in unnatural conditions, and die early.

records.definition_text: describes something that could be avoided or that is not needed
records.learnerexamples_text: You don't want to make any unnecessary car journeys in this weather.; The aim is to kill the animal as quickly as possible without causing unnecessary suffering.; Don't waste too much time with unnecessary TV shows or computer games.

records.definition_text: to remove things from a suitcase, bag or box
records.learnerexamples_text: I haven't even had time to unpack my bag/case/clothes/suitcase.; After I unpacked, I asked if I c[ould] have a guide to show me [around the] town.

records.definition_text: not enjoyable or pleasant
records.learnerexamples_text: an unpleasant experience/smell; On top of that, if you stay in the countryside, you will avoid the smog and the noise of the city, which are very unpleasant!

records.definition_text: disliked by most people
records.learnerexamples_text: Night flights from the airport are deeply unpopular.; The government is becoming increasingly unpopular.; In addition, the outdoor swimming pool, sup[p]osedly unpopular, happens to be constantly full of people, since waterpolo classes are given for free and there is a bar just next to it.

records.definition_text: changing so much that you do not know what will happen next
records.learnerexamples_text: The weather there can be a bit unpredictable - one minute it's blue skies and the next minute it's raining hard.; The hours in this job are very unpredictable - you sometimes have to work late at very short notice.; By that time I was nervous because there were too many unpredictable things [happening].

records.definition_text: not thinking about what is likely to happen or what you can really do
records.learnerexamples_text: I think these sales forecasts are unrealistic, considering how slow sales are at present.;  It's unrealistic to expect an answer before next week.; There must be an alternative to today's zoo, some may suggest a release of all confined animals, but I realise that is unrealistic.

records.definition_text: not fair or acceptable
records.learnerexamples_text: unreasonable behaviour/demands;  It seems unreasonable to expect one person to do both jobs.; So it's unreasonable to think that a country can base its scholastic system only on the few things that students like.

records.definition_text: not able to be trusted or depended on
records.learnerexamples_text: The trains were noisy, dirty, and unreliable. ; This article has 4 main errors which makes it unreliable and I am disappointed [in] it.

records.definition_text: not good enough
records.learnerexamples_text: We had a rather unsatisfactory meal.; It was a great idea, but I think I need to make some points about the things that I found unsatisfactory.

records.definition_text: not achieving what was wanted or intended
records.learnerexamples_text: They made several unsuccessful attempts to reach the men.; His application was unsuccessful.; We tried very hard to score a second goal but all our effo[rt]s were unsuccessful.

records.definition_text: not acceptable or right for someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: The software blocks material that is unsuitable for children.; If the date of [the] meeting is unsuitable for you, just inform me.

records.definition_text: not certain or having doubts
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm a bit unsure about what to do.;  I was unsure of the directions.; I was unsure what/how to tell them.; As I have not been there before, I am rather unsure of what to wear.

records.definition_text: not tidy
records.learnerexamples_text: an untidy room; She's really untidy at home.; Now we need to buy some drawers to put our clothes away, which are for the moment kept in our suitcase and look very untidy!

records.definition_text: to open a knot or something that has been tied with a knot
records.learnerexamples_text: I untied my shoelaces and kicked off my shoes.; She tried to untie the ropes but they were too strong.

records.definition_text: continuing to happen before a particular time or event and then stopping
records.learnerexamples_text: Hadn't we better wait until Antony arrives?; I waited until they'd gone before I started clearing up.;  Whisk the egg whites until they look white and fluffy.; I had always wanted to travel by plane to another country but I [di]dn't have the op[p]ortunity until I was eleven years old.

records.definition_text: as far as
records.learnerexamples_text: Go straight on until you reach the roundabout and then take the second exit.; On the second day, we cycled [for] approximately 4 hours until we reached a beautiful castle.

records.definition_text: bigger, stronger, better, etc. than is normal
records.learnerexamples_text: unusually warm weather; On you[r] free afternoon I suggest you visit our local museum, which is unusually large for such a small town.

records.definition_text: ill
records.learnerexamples_text: to feel/look unwell; I won't be able to go to your English class tomorrow morning because my sister is unwell and I will have to stay with her.

records.definition_text: not wanting to do something
records.learnerexamples_text: A lot of people are unwilling to accept change.; I was unwilling to face the truth and the reality that my best friend had already left me.

records.definition_text: not in bed
records.learnerexamples_text: I stayed up all night finishing this report.; That night we were up until late talking and after a couple of days she left.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize that an action or process is complete
records.learnerexamples_text: Come on, Maria, drink up your lemonade.; By the time we left, she had bought up half of the shop.; Anna, I broke one of your beautiful vase[s] accidentally when I was trying to clean up the house one evening.

records.definition_text: to a greater degree, amount, volume, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: Please speak up, I can't hear you.; The fire heats the room up within minutes.; The cost of car insurance is up, but not very much.; Moreover the microphone suddenly wouldn't work anymore, and even though I desperately tried to speak up, people began to lose interest in both my speech and me and simply started to talk to each other instead.

records.definition_text: rising and falling
records.learnerexamples_text: They were jumping up and down with impatience.; Well, you should be bouncing up and down with joy (just kidding)!

records.definition_text: from one end to the other and back again
records.learnerexamples_text: They were running up and down the corridors.; Almost a thousand people [were] running up and down the ballroom shouting in panic: "Who's got matches?" "Turn the lights on!"

records.definition_text: the way that your parents look after you and the things that they teach you when you are growing up
records.learnerexamples_text: a middle-class/religious upbringing; She had a very strict upbringing.; Now, as a grown-up person, I am trying to evaluate [my] upbringing objectively.

records.definition_text: to add new information
records.learnerexamples_text: The website has just been updated.; We'll update you on this news story throughout the day.; Besides, I can also always update my knowledge by visiting the information and new technology websites on the Internet from time to time.

records.definition_text: to make something more modern
records.learnerexamples_text: They need to update their image.; On the other hand, the movies shown are updated regularly, I guess that part is under control.

records.definition_text: a new form of something which existed at an earlier time
records.learnerexamples_text: a software update;  It's an update of an old 60's movie.

records.definition_text: new information
records.learnerexamples_text: I'll need regular updates on your progress.; Television offers different program[me]s, such as documentaries, program[mes] on culture and updates on [the] news.

records.definition_text: a piece of software or equipment that improves the quality, power or usefulness of a computer or machine
records.learnerexamples_text: a hardware upgrade; The upgrade to version 5.0 costs £395.

records.definition_text: to improve something so that it is of a higher quality or is a newer model
records.learnerexamples_text: to upgrade a computer; The system has been upgraded.; The computer [has] upgraded most existing inventions, and made them more efficient, faster and [more] user friendl[y].

records.definition_text: to send a computer program or a document electronically from your computer, using the Internet
records.learnerexamples_text: All the files have been uploaded to the server.; You should upload it [to] the website.

records.definition_text: on
records.learnerexamples_text: Upon her head she wore a black velvet hat.; Please report to the reception desk upon arrival.; He answered with a smile upon his face, 'As I just told everybody else, you will have the results by the end of June.'

records.definition_text: at a higher position or level than something else
records.learnerexamples_text: the upper lip/body; The office block's upper floors were being repainted.; I am doing the upper intermediate level and last summer I was in London [for] three months.

records.definition_text: straight up or vertical
records.learnerexamples_text: Please return your seats to an upright position and fasten your seat belts.; Immediately the pilot informed the passengers that the weather conditions were not good and [told us] to fasten our seatbelt, put the seat upright and [ado]pt the emergency position.

records.definition_text: to make someone feel unhappy or worried
records.learnerexamples_text: The phone call had clearly upset her.; It still upsets him when he thinks about the accident.; Don't upset yourself by thinking about what might have happened.; This really upset me as no notice w[as] given before the show.

records.definition_text: an illness in the stomach
records.learnerexamples_text: I had an upset stomach after I ate that fish.; I wasn't feeling well at all with an upset stomach and headache.

records.definition_text: having the part which is usually at the top turned to be at the bottom
records.learnerexamples_text: Turn the jar upside down and shake it.; The plane was flying upside down at high speed.; One car landed on its side and the other was upside down.; The furniture was upside down and neither money nor cash were left.

records.definition_text: on or at a higher level of a building
records.learnerexamples_text: an upstairs window; Suddenly, Robert [and I] heard a strange noise coming from an upstairs room but we kept on reading quietly.

records.definition_text: any amount or number under 10, 20, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: We can invite up to 65 people.; A wedding can cost up to 10,000 SFr.

records.definition_text: partly
records.learnerexamples_text: What he says is true up to a point.; I agree up to a point with the statement give[n], but if the journalists [di]dn't follow them, people wouldn't know [so] much about them.

records.definition_text: modern, recent or containing the latest information
records.learnerexamples_text: Great care is taken to keep our database up to date.; Furthermore, the website is not always up to date.

records.definition_text: modern, recent, or containing the latest information
records.learnerexamples_text: The website contains up-to-date information on live football matches.;  The Internet keeps us up to date. ; It is essential to have an up-to-date dictionary.; I will write more later - I do need to give you up-to-date information on my love life!

records.definition_text: until a particular time
records.learnerexamples_text: You can call me up until midnight.; The party will be in my house up to 1:00 a.m., then we will go to Jean's house.

records.definition_text: belonging or relating to a town or city
records.learnerexamples_text: urban areas; urban development; We are generally more interested in [an] urban lifestyle than [living in] the countryside.

records.definition_text: very important and needing you to take action immediately
records.learnerexamples_text: an urgent message; He's got to sign that paper - will you tell him it's urgent?; Many people are in urgent need of food and water.; I want to apologise for missing tomor[r]ow's class, because I have to attend an urgent family meeting at my grandparents' house.

records.definition_text: in a way that is urgent
records.learnerexamples_text: Help is urgently needed.; I have e-mailed you to tell you that I need your bicycle urgently.

records.definition_text: to take an amount from a supply of something
records.learnerexamples_text: Taking a shower uses less water than having a bath.; These bulbs use a lot of electricity.; The equipment in the kitchen is very old and use[s] a lot of electricity and gas.

records.definition_text: to say or write a particular word or phrase
records.learnerexamples_text: 'Autumn' is used in British English and 'fall' in American English.

records.definition_text: a purpose for which something is used
records.learnerexamples_text: A food processor has a variety of uses in the kitchen.; I'd have no use for a boat.; Don't throw that cloth away, you'll find a use for it one day.; We need computers in many places, and [for] many uses today.

records.definition_text: one of the meanings of a word, or the way that a particular word is used
records.learnerexamples_text: Can you list all the uses of the word 'point'?

records.definition_text: If something used to happen or a situation used to exist, it happened regularly or in the past but it does not happen or exist now.
records.learnerexamples_text: She used to live in Detroit.; He used to be a pilot.; You don't come and see me like you used to.; When we were younger, we didn't used to drink coffee.; It's an American film about a girl that used to live in Africa.

records.definition_text: If something is useless, it does not work well or it has no effect.
records.learnerexamples_text: This umbrella's useless - there's a big hole in it.;  It's useless arguing with her.; I started digging, but it was useless.

records.definition_text: someone who uses a product, machine or service
records.learnerexamples_text: drug users; Unemployed people are the main users of this advice centre.; When you log in, you will be asked for your user name and password.; I would like to meet other experienced computer users in order to share programs as well as tips and tricks about programming.

records.base_text: use up sth or use sth up
records.definition_text: to finish a supply of something
records.searchterms_text: use;use up sth or use sth up
records.learnerexamples_text: Don't use up all the milk, we need some for breakfast.; The Earth's resources are being used up at an alarming rate.; It saves time which would be used up [by] doing housework such as laundry, cleaning and ironing.

records.definition_text: normal and happening most often
records.learnerexamples_text: I went to bed at my usual time.; You'll find the box in its usual place.; There was more rain than usual this summer in the mountain areas.; We are going to meet at 5 pm at the station and then go for a pizza - you know where, the usual place "Pizza Express".

records.definition_text: A vacant job is available for someone to do.
records.learnerexamples_text: The assistant marketing post is vacant - why don't you apply?; Therefore, I believe I am suitable for your vacant position.

records.definition_text: Somewhere that is vacant is available because it is not being used.
records.learnerexamples_text: a vacant building; The room next to ours is vacant at the moment.; You see, we have plenty of vacant rooms so you would not cause any trouble.

records.definition_text: based on good reasons or facts that are true
records.learnerexamples_text: a valid excuse/reason; a valid argument/criticism; My ideas might be different from yours, but they're equally valid.; You could hardly think of Dr Quimper as guilty, because every one of the Crackenthorpe family had a valid reason to kill.

records.definition_text: officially or legally acceptable
records.learnerexamples_text: The ticket is valid for three months.; My passport is valid for another two years.; You need to enter a valid password.; Is this offer valid for the weekends, as well?

records.definition_text: an area of low land between hills or mountains, often with a river running through it
records.learnerexamples_text: the Nile Valley; the Thames valley; There was snow on the hill tops but not in the valley.; My home town is situated in a valley.

records.definition_text: Valuable objects are worth a lot of money.
records.learnerexamples_text: valuable paintings; These antiques are extremely valuable.; So as you can imagine, not only is the ring valuable but it also means a lot to me since it makes me remember Brazil!

records.definition_text: Valuable information, advice, etc. is very helpful or important.
records.learnerexamples_text: He was able to provide the police with some valuable information.; This trip will allow me to gain valuable knowledge and experience.

records.definition_text: how much money something could be sold for
records.learnerexamples_text: The new road has affected the value of these houses. ; She had already sold everything of value that she possessed.; Cars quickly go down in value.; The value of the pound fell against other European currencies yesterday.; "Well, there was nothing of value in [the suitcase]," my mother remarked, but I was close to tears.

records.definition_text: how useful or important something is
records.learnerexamples_text: The documents are of great historical value.; The necklace had great sentimental value.; I was really sad because th[ese] shoes had a lot of sentimental value for me, and they were made of genuine le[a]ther!

records.definition_text: to consider something important
records.learnerexamples_text: I've always valued her advice.; I will learn how other people live and I will also learn to value the things I have.

records.definition_text: the beliefs people have about what is right and wrong and what is most important in life, which control their behaviour
records.learnerexamples_text: family/moral/traditional values; A tragedy occurs which causes Andrew to rediscover his moral values.

records.definition_text: a vehicle that is used for carrying things but which is smaller than a truck
records.learnerexamples_text: a delivery van; a van driver; I looked in my mirror and saw [a] white van.

records.definition_text: to disappear suddenly
records.learnerexamples_text: The sun vanished behind the clouds.; The child vanished while on her way home from school.; I [went after] the thief but he vanished into the crowd.

records.definition_text: a difference in amount or quality
records.learnerexamples_text: variations in price/temperature; There was some variation in the quality of the prints.; Apart from this, there is very little variation in temperature between day and night.

records.definition_text: consisting of many different things or types
records.learnerexamples_text: a varied diet; a long and varied career; Remember you should always eat a varied diet.

records.definition_text: the quality of often changing or of being made of many different things
records.learnerexamples_text: Factory work often lacks variety.; I think you need a bit more variety in your diet.; You know, I like variety a lot and don't like my friends to see me with [the same] clothes.

records.definition_text: If things of the same type vary, they are different from each other.
records.learnerexamples_text: Car prices vary greatly/widely across Europe.; The samples varied in quality but were generally acceptable.; The price of the dishes varies.

records.definition_text: to change or to cause something to change
records.learnerexamples_text: Temperatures vary depending on/according to the time of year.; I try to vary what I eat.; To vary the pictures of cultural events, I would recommend [visiting] the Wednesday market, which starts at 8 am.

records.definition_text: a container that you put flowers in
records.learnerexamples_text: a glass vase; a vase of flowers; Yesterday I went to a shopping centre with my mother, and bought a small desk, a radio, a vase, and a small s[ofa].

records.definition_text: extremely big
records.learnerexamples_text: a vast amount/sum of money; vast areas of forest; The vast majority of pupils attend state schools.; Among the vast choice of interesting buildings to photograph I can name the "National Portrait Museum", a huge building in renaissance style, [and] the old "Castle of Sforza", built in the eleventh century.

records.definition_text: someone who does not eat meat or fish
records.learnerexamples_text: Of the four million people who have become vegetarians in Britain, nearly two-thirds are women.; I've heard that even the non-vegetarian food is good there, but I'm a vegetarian.

records.definition_text: not eating, containing or using meat or fish
records.learnerexamples_text: All her children are vegetarian.; vegetarian cooking/food; a vegetarian dish/meal; She's recently gone/become vegetarian.; Do you like vegetarian food?

records.definition_text: something such as a car or bus that takes people from one place to another, especially using roads
records.learnerexamples_text: The driver of the vehicle was unhurt.; Sometimes I watch programmes about cars and other vehicles, because I'm keen on them.

records.definition_text: a place where a sports game, musical performance, or special event happens
records.learnerexamples_text: The hotel is an ideal venue for conferences and business meetings.; The stadium has been specifically designed as a venue for European Cup matches.; This festival has already got [a] good reputation as [an] alternative venue for both artists and audience.

records.definition_text: one of the parts that a song or poem is divided into
records.learnerexamples_text: I only know the first verse of the poem.; Each verse was sung as a solo and then everyone joined in on the chorus.; But I was so puzzled that when I tried to sing, I couldn't remember a word of the verse I had written.

records.definition_text: one form of something that is slightly different to other forms of the same thing
records.learnerexamples_text: An English-language version of the book is planned for the autumn.; The original version of the film is much better.; a new/updated version; Who has never said that the original book was better than the film version?

records.definition_text: someone whose job is to give medical care to animals that are ill or hurt
records.learnerexamples_text: Helen is training to become a vet.; Sorry Mr Smith but I'[ll miss] tomorrow's class as I have to go to the vet with my dog.

records.definition_text: going through or stopping at a place on the way to another place
records.learnerexamples_text: The train to Utrecht goes via Amsterdam.; Two years ago I travel[l]ed to Canada via Italy.

records.definition_text: using a particular machine, system or person to send or recieve something
records.learnerexamples_text: Reports are coming in via satellite.; I only found out about it via my sister.; I hate shopping via [the] internet.

records.definition_text: someone who has suffered the effects of violence, illness or bad luck
records.learnerexamples_text: victims of crime; The children are the innocent victims of the fighting.; The new drug might help save the lives of cancer victims.; His wife was his last victim.

records.definition_text: when you win a game, competition, election, fight, war, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: Phoenix managed a 135-114 victory over Denver. ; Grant won/achieved/gained a comfortable/easy victory over Cooper in yesterday's match.; This result is a victory for democracy.; They were all celebrating their victory with a gorgeous dinner.

records.definition_text: a short video recording that you can see on a website
records.learnerexamples_text: The website has several video clips of Murray's recent matches.; It shows how a band or a singer do their video clips.

records.definition_text: your opinion
records.learnerexamples_text: We have different views about/on education.;  In my view, her criticisms were justified.; I take the view that everyone should be free to decide for themselves.; It's my view that everyone should have the right to choose. ; We had a friendly exchange of views.

records.definition_text: how well you can see something from a particular place
records.learnerexamples_text: We had a great view of the procession.; Don't stand in front of me - you're blocking my view of the stage.; She turned a corner, and disappeared from view.; In a few seconds, he disappear[ed] out of my view.

records.definition_text: someone who watches a television programme
records.learnerexamples_text: Millions of viewers will be watching this match.; He's an extraordinary person and TV viewers will love him because of his good sense of humo[u]r and his honesty.

records.definition_text: a sour liquid that is used in cooking, often made from wine
records.learnerexamples_text: red wine vinegar

records.definition_text: when someone tries to hurt or kill someone else
records.learnerexamples_text: an act of violence ;  A number of people were killed in the violence.; Violence against women has increased in recent years.; The recent outbreak of violence in the region is very disturbing.; Today, it is important that children and teenagers do something with their free time and do not get in contact with criminality and violence.

records.definition_text: involving violence
records.learnerexamples_text: a violent crime;  a violent protest; His films tend to be very violent.; Some say that television can affect people in bad ways and sometimes causes violent incidents.

records.definition_text: using force to hurt or attack someone else
records.learnerexamples_text: a violent criminal; He shouts a lot but I don't think he's ever been physically violent towards her.; Now Mary knew what happened at Jamaica Inn and it was very dangerous for her because her uncle was a violent man.

records.definition_text: in a way that involves violence
records.learnerexamples_text: He often behaved violently and they were terrified of him.; He claimed to have been violently assaulted while in prison.; Sometimes they behave violently because of their [imprison]ment.

records.definition_text: using computer images and sounds that make you think an imagined situation is real
records.learnerexamples_text: a virtual art gallery online; However, I go far away from my family and other people and have virtual relationships.

records.definition_text: almost
records.learnerexamples_text: I've virtually finished.; Their twins are virtually identical.; That wine stain on my shirt has virtually disappeared.; Virtually everyone today can go out and buy their own personal computer.

records.definition_text: in a way that uses computer images and sounds that make you think an imagined situation is real
records.learnerexamples_text: Nowadays all these things can be experienced virtually.; I also have the possibility of making new friends: I can connect to a special site which will enable me to [meet people] virtually.

records.definition_text: when a computer produces images and sounds that make you think an imagined situation is real
records.learnerexamples_text: virtual reality games; virtual reality software; Magnificent scientific pro[j]ects are done by computers, [as well as] daily shopping, com[m]unication with people in other parts of the world, games, getting any kind of information and, soon, virtual reality!

records.definition_text: a program that is secretly put onto a computer in order to destroy the information that is stored on it
records.learnerexamples_text: My computer has been behaving oddly and I suspect it's a virus.; That document was a "virus" and erased all my documents [o]n my computer.

records.definition_text: an infectious organism too small to be seen that causes disease, or an illness that it causes
records.learnerexamples_text: a flu virus; I don't know exactly what's wrong with her - I think it's some sort of virus.; My "friend" Pat told everybody that my brother died and that he died because he got a virus - that's why I didn't have friends because all the people thought that I had the virus too.

records.definition_text: an official mark in your passport which allows you to enter or leave a particular country
records.learnerexamples_text: We travelled to Argentina on a tourist visa.; Tomorrow I am not going to attend [the] class because I have to apply for my visa at 9.00.

records.definition_text: able to be seen
records.learnerexamples_text: You should wear something light-coloured when you're cycling at night so that you're more visible.; The fire was visible from five kilometres away.; There are few visible signs of the illness that kept her in hospital for so long.; The comet should be visible to the naked eye.; He waited curiously for her to become visible through the fog, which seemed to have [become] denser in the last few seconds.

records.definition_text: an idea or image in your mind of what something could be like in the future
records.learnerexamples_text: a vision of a better society; We see in his novels his grim vision of the future.; All in all, I think you must write a new report to apologize for having been so pessimistic and having given such a bleak vision of this Festival.

records.definition_text: the ability to see
records.learnerexamples_text: He has poor vision in his left eye.; Her hands were sweating and her vision had become a blur because of the tension in the air.

records.definition_text: when you visit a place or a person
records.learnerexamples_text: the President's visit to Argentina; I think I'll pay a visit to the hairdresser's while I'm in town.; We had a visit from the school inspector last week.; The problem is that my mother arranged a visit [to] the doctor, and after that [to] the dentist.

records.definition_text: relating to seeing
records.learnerexamples_text: The film has some powerful visual effects.; It also provides a clear idea of how people's lives were in a particular period by showing us the visual images of that time.

records.definition_text: necessary or extremely important
records.learnerexamples_text: Tourism is vital to the country's economy.; The kidney plays a vital role/part in the removal of waste products from the blood.;  It's absolutely vital that you follow the instructions exactly.; If you don't mind I would like to ask you some vital questions.

records.definition_text: one of a group of natural substances that you need to be healthy
records.l_topic_text_text: body and health, food and drink
records.learnerexamples_text: a vitamin pill; Oranges are full of vitamin C.; On the one hand, we eat a lot of sweet [or] fat food, which lack[s] vitamins.

records.definition_text: A vivid colour is very bright.
records.learnerexamples_text: She was wearing a vivid pink shirt.; Students would like to have some vivid colours or pictures on the walls but the best solution would be to repaint the walls.

records.definition_text: Vivid descriptions or memories produce strong, clear images in your mind.
records.learnerexamples_text: He gave a very vivid account/description of life in Havana.; I still have a very vivid memory of the evening.; She has a very vivid imagination.; Each memory is still so vivid.

records.definition_text: in a vivid way
records.learnerexamples_text: I vividly remember my first day at school.; She could vividly remember the last time he hurt her, only then it was with a razor.

records.definition_text: the sounds that are made when people speak or sing
records.learnerexamples_text: She has a very loud/quiet/soft voice.; a clear/deep voice; You could tell from her voice that she wasn't pleased.; She lowered her voice to a whisper.;  Could you please keep your voices down?

records.definition_text: a mountain with a large hole at the top which sometimes explodes and produces hot, melted rock and smoke
records.learnerexamples_text: an extinct/active volcano;  Erupting volcanoes discharge massive quantities of dust into the atmosphere.; Finally, I think that a good place to go is Santorini, a beautiful island which has a volcano.

records.definition_text: the number or amount of something, especially when it is large
records.learnerexamples_text: I was put off by the volume of work involved.; The volume of traffic in the city is causing problems.; Nowadays, marketing volume is rapidly increased in Internet business, according to one of [the] major newspaper[s].

records.definition_text: the level of sound produced by a television, radio, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: Could you turn the volume up/down, please.; After we went to the disco and we danced together, but the volume of the music was too high to talk!

records.definition_text: a person who does something, especially helping other people, willingly and without being forced or paid to do it
records.learnerexamples_text: a Red Cross volunteer ; The charity relies on volunteers to run the office and answer the telephones.; Well the concert was Friday night and I went there with the Red Cross volunteers, did you know I'm one of them?

records.definition_text: when someone shows their choice or opinion in an election or meeting by writing a cross on an official piece of paper or putting their hand up
records.learnerexamples_text: He lost the election by twenty votes.; The suggestion was approved, with 25 votes in favour, and 7 against.; She cast her vote for the Green Party.; [T]he one who get[s] the most votes will get 1000 Baht as first prize.

records.definition_text: to show your choice or opinion in an election or meeting by writing a mark on an official piece of paper or by putting your hand up
records.learnerexamples_text: Who did you vote for?;  The unions voted against strike action.;  Staff have voted to accept the pay offer. ; She was too young to vote in the national election.; The committee voted on the proposal, and accepted it.

records.definition_text: a way of making a decision by asking a group of people to vote
records.learnerexamples_text: We called a meeting in order to take a vote on the issue.

records.definition_text: a speech sound that you make with your lips and teeth open, shown in English by the letters a, e, i, o, or u
records.learnerexamples_text: A short vowel is a short sound as in the word 'cup'.; A long vowel is a long sound as in the word 'shoe'.; [In the game,] he let the student[s] cho[o]se [a] vowel or consonant.

records.definition_text: a long journey, especially by ship, or in space
records.learnerexamples_text: Cook's voyage to Australia; Besides, I have a good command of French and I speak English fluently, which might be also useful during the voyage around the world.

records.definition_text: the amount of money a person regularly receives for their job
records.learnerexamples_text: weekly wages; He earns/gets good wages at the factory.; a very low/high wage; the minimum wage; an hourly/daily/weekly wage

records.definition_text: the part of the body above and slightly narrower than the hips
records.learnerexamples_text: a small/narrow/tiny/large waist; These trousers are a bit tight around my waist.; She has a 26-inch waist.; Chris was holding his arm tight[ly] around Claire's waist.

records.definition_text: when you stay in one place until someone or something arrives, or someone or something is ready for you
records.learnerexamples_text: a long wait; well worth the wait; We had a three-hour wait before we could see the doctor.; The long wait for the doctor/to see the doctor really made me anxious.

records.definition_text: said in order to interrupt someone, or to get their attention or when you have suddenly thought of something important
records.learnerexamples_text: Wait a minute - I've just had an idea.; Oh! Wait a minute...

records.definition_text: said in order to interrupt someone, or to get their attention or when you have suddenly thought of something important
records.learnerexamples_text: Now, wait a moment - I don't agree with that.; Wait a minute - I've just had an idea.; Oh! Wait a minute...

records.definition_text: said in order to interrupt someone, or to get their attention or when you have suddenly thought of something important
records.learnerexamples_text: Now, wait a moment - I don't agree with that.

records.definition_text: to stop sleeping or to make someone else stop sleeping
records.learnerexamples_text: Please wake me early tomorrow.; Hey Dan, I didn't want to wake you, that's why I left this note.

records.definition_text: a long, thin piece of wood that you use when you are walking/playing hockey, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: She uses a walking stick.; I am very sad, because I have lost my hockey stick and it was very special to me; a very famous player [gave] it to me as a present.

records.definition_text: to walk with someone in order to guide them or keep them safe
records.learnerexamples_text: He walked me to my house.; Then we went to the bar beside the restaurant to have a last drink and he walked me home.

records.definition_text: to walk with a dog to give the dog exercise
records.learnerexamples_text: I walk the dog twice a day.; Well, I suppose in my opinion you should walk the dog three times a day.

records.definition_text: to walk around slowly in a relaxed way or without any clear purpose or direction
records.learnerexamples_text: We spent the morning wandering around the old part of the city.; He was here a moment ago but he's wandered off somewhere.; If you can't afford it you can just wander around the city and enjoy meeting people.

records.definition_text: a room or area in a hospital, where people receiving treatment stay
records.learnerexamples_text: She's in a ward on the fourth floor.; I spent two days alone in a ward [in] Biarritz's hospital.

records.definition_text: a large cupboard for keeping clothes in
records.learnerexamples_text: She was showing me her new built-in/fitted wardrobes.; I want to sell a wooden wardrobe, because I've bought a new one.

records.definition_text: friendly and loving
records.learnerexamples_text: They're a very warm family.; He has a lovely warm smile.; I'd like to give a warm welcome to our guests this evening.; He is warm and friendly.

records.definition_text: to become warm or make something become warm
records.learnerexamples_text: You're so cold - come and warm your hands by the fire.; Your supper's just warming through in the oven.; We can warm (up) the room quite quickly with this electric fire.; After they save[d] me, I put those gloves on to warm my hands.

records.definition_text: in a way that keeps you warm
records.learnerexamples_text: You're not dressed warmly enough - put a sweater on.

records.definition_text: in a friendly or loving way
records.learnerexamples_text: He shook my hand warmly.; He embraced me warmly and whispered 'You wouldn't have believed me.'

records.definition_text: a friendly and loving quality in someone or something
records.learnerexamples_text: I still remember the warmth of their welcome.; They gave us so much when we were children, their love and their warmth, and now it is up to us to stay with them and give back the love we [recei]ved.

records.definition_text: the heat that is produced by something
records.learnerexamples_text: I've put a T-shirt on under my sweater for extra warmth.; We lay down on the sand enjoying the warmth of the sun and listening to the birds.

records.definition_text: to make someone realise a possible danger or problem, especially one in the future
records.learnerexamples_text: We were warned not to eat the fish.; Have you warned them (that) there will be an extra person for dinner?; I was warned against/off going to the east coast because it was so full of tourists.; This particular curry is extremely hot - be warned!; Put that ball down and come over here, Laura - I'm warning you!

records.definition_text: something that tells or shows you that something bad may happen
records.learnerexamples_text: There's a warning on the cigarette packet that says 'Tobacco seriously damages health'.; The bombs fell completely without warning.; Just a word of warning - restaurants in this area can be very expensive.; The government have today issued a warning about the dangers of sunbathing.; Without any warning he pushed [me].

records.definition_text: a black and yellow flying insect that can sting you
records.learnerexamples_text: There's a wasps' nest in that old tree.; a wasp sting ; We were sitting in the garden and suddenly a wasp entered my T-shirt.

records.definition_text: an unnecessary or wrong use of money, substances, time, energy, abilities, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: That meeting achieved absolutely nothing - it was a complete waste of time.; She's been unemployed for two years and it's such a waste of her talents.; This food mixer's been a total waste of money - we never use it.; I don't [watch] m[uch] television because I think it's a waste of time.

records.definition_text: unwanted matter or material of any type, often that which is left after useful substances or parts have been removed
records.learnerexamples_text: Britain produces 20 million tonnes of household waste each year.; He opposes any kind of nuclear waste being dumped at sea.; Oil spills are common, as is the dumping of toxic waste.; What I did to get it was send them an article based on some possible solutions to the problem of nuclear waste in my local area.

records.definition_text: Waste material is no longer needed and can be got rid of.
records.learnerexamples_text: The Japanese recycle more than half of their waste paper.; In addition, some waste materials are carried to the incinerator where they are burnt completely at very high temperatures.

records.definition_text: to use too much of something or use something badly when there is a limited amount of it
records.learnerexamples_text: You waste a lot of water by having a bath instead of a shower.; Come on, let's get started - we've wasted enough time already.; Don't waste your money on me, love, keep it for yourself.; It's nice to hear that you want to go to Colombia and I'm really happy because I can tell you all the details so you won't waste time and money.

records.definition_text: to be careful about something
records.learnerexamples_text: I have to watch my weight now I'm not doing so much sport.; Watch how you cross the road!; Watch (that) you don't get glue on your fingers, won't you?; Watch what you're doing with that knife, Jim, it's sharp.; The odd glass of wine is fine but watch what you [eat].

records.definition_text: to be careful
records.learnerexamples_text: "Watch out!" he shouted, but it was too late - she had knocked the whole tray of drinks on the floor.; I definitely know that having a cat brings inconvenience, you have to watch out for your curtains, it can scratch your sofa or your hand, but these are so few problems in comparison [with] all the affection [it] can give you.

records.definition_text: to pour water on to plants or the soil that they are growing in
records.learnerexamples_text: I've asked my neighbour to water the plants while I'm away.; I cleaned [the flat] every day and watered your flowers.

records.definition_text: water, especially from a river or stream, dropping from a higher to a lower point, sometimes from a great height
records.learnerexamples_text: We walked for an hour and arrived at the waterfall.

records.definition_text: not allowing water to go through
records.learnerexamples_text: Canvas boots are all right but they're not as waterproof as leather.; Probably warm jumpers and a waterproof coat would do, don't you think so?

records.definition_text: to raise your hand and move it from side to side in order to attract someone's attention or to say goodbye
records.learnerexamples_text: I waved to/at him from the window but he didn't see me.; She was so annoyed she wouldn't even wave us goodbye/wave goodbye to us.; She waves her hands about/around a lot when she's talking.; She waved at me and I smiled.

records.definition_text: a line of higher water which moves across the surface of an area of water, especially the sea
records.learnerexamples_text: At night, I listened to the sound of the waves breaking/crashing against the shore.; I already know you surf and the waves at Reserva will be huge this weekend [so] we will surely surf together.

records.definition_text: the pattern in which some types of energy, such as sound, light and heat, are spread or carried
records.learnerexamples_text: radio waves; Indeed, it is thought that using a mobile phone may cause brain damage owing to magnetic waves.

records.definition_text: the direction in which something is facing or travels
records.learnerexamples_text: "Which way does the room face?" "North."; This bus is going the wrong way.; Which way up should this box be?; The numbers are the wrong way round - it should be 71, not 17.; Although he had told us he knew this address, he went [the] wrong way.

records.definition_text: a distance or a period of time
records.learnerexamples_text: We walked a long way yesterday.; The holidays seem like they're a long way away/off.; I like this best because [it] is not a long way from home.

records.definition_text: used to refer to people generally
records.learnerexamples_text: The world in which we live today is very different.; Why can't we live without computers?

records.definition_text: not physically strong
records.learnerexamples_text: It's not surprising you feel weak if you haven't eaten properly for days.; I felt so weak that I wasn't able to tidy and wash up.

records.definition_text: not good at something
records.learnerexamples_text: She reads well but her spelling is weak.; Listening is my weak point so I have to improve.

records.definition_text: not powerful, or not having a strong character
records.learnerexamples_text: a weak leader/government/king; At the beginning of the story, [Mary] seemed to be a weak person, but in the end she demonstrated that she could overcome her fears in order to protect someone.

records.definition_text: containing little taste or alcohol
records.learnerexamples_text: weak coffee/beer

records.definition_text: difficult to see or hear
records.learnerexamples_text: He spoke in a weak voice.; I could hardly see with the weak light of the candle and I couldn't remember the last time I had used it.

records.definition_text: when someone or something is not strong or powerful
records.learnerexamples_text: Asking for help is not a sign of weakness.; I believe that I'll be able to cover my physical weakness with my experience and knowledge.

records.definition_text: a particular part or quality of someone or something that is not good or effective
records.learnerexamples_text: There are definite weaknesses in their security arrangements.; His main weakness as a manager is his inability to delegate.; The later novels show none of the weaknesses of his earlier work.; However, I have to complain about a few weaknesses in this festival.

records.definition_text: a large amount of money or valuable possessions that someone has
records.learnerexamples_text: During a successful business career, she accumulated a great amount of wealth.; On the other hand, having a mobile phone can also create social distinctions between people as it can [be] a sign of wealth.

records.definition_text: rich
records.learnerexamples_text: He's a very wealthy man.; With its natural resources it is potentially a very wealthy country.; But how can anyone satisfy a wealthy woman like her without giving her an expensive present?

records.definition_text: any object used in fighting or war, such as a gun, bomb, sword, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: chemical/nuclear/biological weapons; The youths were dragged from their car and searched for weapons.; Technology is used [to] create new types of weapons.

records.definition_text: to arrange or grow your hair in a particular way
records.learnerexamples_text: She usually wears her hair in a ponytail.;  I now wear my long hair loose and I dyed it black.

records.definition_text: If a feeling or effect wears off, it gradually disappears.
records.learnerexamples_text: The injection the dentist gave me is starting to wear off.; And Jim, has his pas[s]ion for you finally worn off?

records.base_text: wear sb out or wear out sb
records.definition_text: to make someone extremely tired
records.searchterms_text: wear;wear sb out or wear out sb
records.learnerexamples_text: Standing up all day is wearing me out.; This does not mean that we have to spend hours in the gym and get home worn out.

records.definition_text: to use something so much that it is damaged and cannot be used any more, or to become damaged in this way
records.searchterms_text: wear;wear (sth) out or wear out (sth);wear sth out or wear out sth
records.learnerexamples_text: He's already worn out two pairs of shoes this year.; My shoes are worn out too! I have to get new ones.

records.definition_text: a description of what the weather will be like
records.learnerexamples_text: Have you heard the weather forecast for tomorrow?; The weather forecast is not so good for the next two days: rain and wind.

records.definition_text: a type of net made by a spider to catch insects
records.learnerexamples_text: a spider's web; On the way coming back to [the] hotel I almost got lost because the underground was like a spider['s] web.

records.definition_text: a camera that records moving pictures and sounds and allows these to be shown on the Internet as they happen
records.learnerexamples_text: I see my grandchildren via the webcam.

records.definition_text: a marriage ceremony and any celebrations such as a meal or a party that follow it
records.learnerexamples_text: a wedding cake/dress/invitation/present/reception; Do you know the date of Cathy and Matthew's wedding?; It was their twenty-fifth wedding anniversary last week.; Some couples prefer to [have] a traditional wedding in an old village.

records.definition_text: to consider something carefully, especially in order to make a decision
records.learnerexamples_text: He needs to weigh up the pros and cons of going to college.; Having weighed the pros and cons, I thought you [ought] to be conscious of the fact that... you're working too hard.

records.definition_text: to have a heaviness of a stated amount, or to measure the heaviness of an object
records.learnerexamples_text: How much do you weigh?; She weighs herself every week on the scales in the bathroom.; Your luggage must be weighed before it is put on the aircraft.; You can [see] monkeys that weigh only 100g.

records.definition_text: the amount that something or someone weighs
records.learnerexamples_text: He's about average height and weight.; I need to lose a bit of weight.; Graham's put on a lot of weight recently.; These drugs can cause patients to gain weight.; So let me describe Fabian: he has brown hair and his weight is about 75 kg.

records.definition_text: the quality of being heavy
records.learnerexamples_text: The shelf collapsed under the weight of the books.; The weight of the snow broke the branches of the trees.

records.definition_text: something that is heavy
records.learnerexamples_text: Try not to lift heavy weights.; I lift weights twice a week at the gym.; [...] my long training periods in lifting weights.

records.definition_text: very strange and unusual, unexpected or not natural
records.learnerexamples_text: Her boyfriend's a bit weird but she's all right.; That's weird - I thought I'd left my keys on the table but they're not there.; There is nothing to rival the weird and wonderful things that come out on the streets at carnival time.; She was hearing all sorts of weird noises.

records.definition_text: to greet someone who has arrived in a place
