records.learnerexamples_text: This problem needs to be dealt with without delay.; Firstly, the programme began on time at midday without delay.

records.definition_text: immediately
records.learnerexamples_text: This problem needs to be dealt with without delay.; Firstly, the programme began on time at midday without delay.

records.definition_text: relating to a particular thing
records.learnerexamples_text: I am writing with respect to your letter of 24 June.; With respect to the ages of the members, they are between fifteen and twenty years old.

records.definition_text: relating to a particular thing
records.learnerexamples_text: I am writing with respect to your letter of 24 June.; With respect to the ages of the members, they are between fifteen and twenty years old.

records.definition_text: using something
records.searchterms_text: help;helps;with the help of  sth;with the help of sth
records.learnerexamples_text: We managed to assemble the table with the help of the instructions. ; The film was full of special effects created with the help of computer graphics, [and] it was very good.

records.definition_text: a person who sees an event happening, especially a crime or an accident
records.learnerexamples_text: Police are appealing for witnesses to the accident to come forward.; According to (eye) witnesses, the robbery was carried out by two teenage boys.; Furthermore, the witness was assassinated.

records.definition_text: to see something happen, especially an accident or crime
records.learnerexamples_text: Did anyone witness the attack?; Finally, if you witness an accident you can inform the police quickly, which can save lives.

records.definition_text: using words in a clever and funny way
records.learnerexamples_text: a witty comment/remark; He was witty and very charming.; I have read it many times and [the] author's witty remarks and elegant style have always been a source of entertainment to me.

records.definition_text: a wild animal of the dog family
records.learnerexamples_text: Wolves hunt in groups known as packs.; We could hear wolves howling in the distance.; Before we knew it, Nick leap[t] onto the wolf and they started to fight.

records.definition_text: used in phrases, at the beginning of a request, to make it more formal and polite
records.learnerexamples_text: I wonder - could you help me carry these books?; I wonder whether you could pass me the butter?; I was wondering if you could give me some information about places to visit in the area?; I wonder if there is a way that I would be able to cover the work I have missed?

records.definition_text: to ask yourself questions or express a wish to know about something
records.learnerexamples_text: Hadn't you better phone home? Your parents will be wondering where you are.; He's starting to wonder whether he did the right thing in accepting this job.; Will this turkey be big enough for eight, I wonder?; "Have you decided where you're going next summer?" "I've been wondering about going to Florida."; You might wonder why I decided to do so.

records.definition_text: a painting, book, piece of music, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: The museum has many works by Picasso as well as other modern painters.; the complete works of Shakespeare; We agreed that something had to be done to promote the popularity of local films, some of them being great works of art.

records.definition_text: when you use physical or mental effort to do something
records.learnerexamples_text: Carrying heavy loads around all day is hard work.; I can certainly do a report for you but it will be a lot of work.; The lessons are very good but the teacher is going very quickly. It will be hard work.

records.definition_text: If something works, it is effective or successful.
records.learnerexamples_text: Her plan to increase sales worked.; The tablets will start to work in a few minutes.; I changed cars several times to fool the police. It worked very well.

records.definition_text: to try hard to achieve something
records.learnerexamples_text: You need to work at improving your writing.; In my opinion, this is the part our college has to improve and to work at.

records.definition_text: relating to your job
records.learnerexamples_text: a 37-hour working week ; working hours; Working conditions in the mill have hardly changed over the last twenty years.; She has a difficult working relationship with many of her staff.; As you know, I work in [a] bank, so I have to [dress] smartly during working hours.

records.definition_text: to spend time repairing or improving something
records.learnerexamples_text: Tim loves working on old cars.; I believe that it would be best to paint a picture of me in the garage working on my new car.

records.definition_text: a period of physical exercise
records.learnerexamples_text: a light workout; Are there many fitness-cent[res] where we can practise our daily workout?

records.definition_text: to exercise in order to improve the strength or appearance of your body
records.learnerexamples_text: Heidi works out in the gym two or three times a week.; At the time I use[d] to work out and I [saw] that he was looking [at] me while I was doing my exercises.

records.definition_text: If a problem or a complicated situation works out, it ends in a successful way.
records.learnerexamples_text: We were worried that the event would be disorganized, but it all worked out in the end.; I hope you follow my instructions and you'll see how everything works out fine.

records.base_text: work sth out or work out sth
records.definition_text: to do a calculation to get an answer to a mathematical question
records.searchterms_text: work;work sth out or work out sth
records.learnerexamples_text: We need to work out the total cost of the project.; I had to work out all my figures two times to make sure that my accounts were accurate.

records.definition_text: the people and things that are involved in a particular activity or subject
records.learnerexamples_text: the entertainment world; the world of politics; Well, as you know, I'm not very interested in the fashion world, so I rarely spend much time shopping for clothes.

records.definition_text: existing or happening in all parts of the world
records.learnerexamples_text: a worldwide success; An increase in average temperature by only a few degrees could cause environmental problems worldwide.; You can visit the main monuments of Paris, known worldwide, like Notre-Dame Cathedral or the Eiffel Tower, built in 1903.

records.definition_text: a small creature with a long, thin, soft body and no legs
records.learnerexamples_text: Blackbirds eat worms, insects, and berries.; Fishing is my hobby and that's why I bought these plastic worms, that are not [very] good - it's better to use live worms!

records.definition_text: to make someone feel anxious because of problems or unpleasant things that might happen
records.learnerexamples_text: It worries me that he hasn't phoned yet.; The lack of rain is starting to worry people.; Unemployment is increasing too, and today, it worries every single citizen of the world, specially the ones who live in [a] third world country.

records.definition_text: a problem that makes you feel anxious
records.learnerexamples_text: health/financial worries; Keeping warm in the winter is a major worry for many old people.; My worries proved to be wrong.

records.definition_text: when you are anxious about something
records.learnerexamples_text: She's been sick with worry.; Unemployment, bad health - all sorts of things can be a cause of worry.; You really need to spend a whole month without any kind of worry.

records.definition_text: making you feel unhappy and afraid
records.learnerexamples_text: It's a very worrying situation.; But the most worrying thing about this matter is you.

records.definition_text: comparative of badly
records.learnerexamples_text: He did worse than he was expecting in the exams.; He was treated much worse than I was.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize how unpleasant, difficult, severe, etc. something is becoming
records.learnerexamples_text: The economic climate is getting worse and worse.; The traffic situation in all big towns is getting worse and worse, so that bicycles or public transport must become more attractive.

records.definition_text: the most unpleasant or difficult thing, person, or situation
records.learnerexamples_text: That was the worst I've seen him play in several years.; This situation was the worst I have lived [through].

records.definition_text: (superlative of badly) the most badly
records.learnerexamples_text: Small businesses have been worst hit by the recession.; Roads in the Tayside region were worst affected by the snow.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize the worst thing, situation, etc.
records.learnerexamples_text: We had no food or light, but worst of all, we had no water.; And worst of all, her mother had been always against that relationship and had given her advice many times.

records.definition_text: useful and enjoyable, despite needing a lot of effort
records.learnerexamples_text: She considers teaching a worthwhile career.; The time and expense involved in keeping up to date with all the changes has been worthwhile.; If you need him on this project, you've got to make it financially worthwhile for him.; It's a worthwhile trip. You'll have the op[p]ortunity to visit beautiful places and learn lots of history.

records.definition_text: used to say what might happen if something else happens
records.learnerexamples_text: What would you do if you lost your job?; They knew there would be trouble unless the report was finished by the next day.; I was just wondering if you would ask me that, because if you didn't, I would - I just love shopping!

records.definition_text: used as the past form of 'will' to talk about what someone was willing to do or what something was able to do
records.learnerexamples_text: The car wouldn't start this morning.; I asked her to talk to him, but she wouldn't.; My parents wouldn't let me stay in a hotel alone.

records.definition_text: used as the past form of 'will' to talk about what someone said or thought
records.learnerexamples_text: Archie said he would see his brother tomorrow.; They thought that she would never recover.; He said to me he would like to come back soon.

records.definition_text: used to talk about a situation that you can imagine happening
records.learnerexamples_text: It would be lovely to go to New York.; It would be great to join you and your friends in the mountains.

records.definition_text: used to talk about things that happened often in the past
records.learnerexamples_text: He would always turn and wave at the end of the street.; Since my childhood I have always been fond of swimming. I would usually spend my summer holidays on a campsite near a river with my family.

records.definition_text: used when you are politely requesting something
records.learnerexamples_text: I would appreciate it if you could let me know in advance whether or not you will be coming.; I would really appreciate a positive answer from your side.

records.definition_text: used to show that you prefer to have or do one thing more than another
records.learnerexamples_text: I'd much rather go out for a meal than stay in and watch TV. ; I would rather not tell him.; I'd rather watch something funny, like a sitcom.

records.definition_text: used to show that you prefer to have or do one thing more than another
records.learnerexamples_text: I'd rather have a beer.; Which would you rather do - go swimming or play tennis?; Wouldn't you rather finish it tomorrow?

records.definition_text: used to request something politely
records.learnerexamples_text: Would you mind sharing a room?; Would you mind if I called you, to know what I've missed?

records.definition_text: used to request something politely
records.learnerexamples_text: Would you mind sharing a room?; Would you mind if I called you, to know what I've missed?

records.definition_text: an injury, especially one that is made with a knife or bullet
records.learnerexamples_text: a gunshot wound; a chest/leg wound; a flesh wound; Rollo discovered that his best friend was implicated in the penicillin racket: the racketeer would put sand into penicillin without worrying about the great suffering that they caused to people who needed penicillin for their wounds.

records.definition_text: to injure someone, especially with a knife or gun
records.learnerexamples_text: The police chief was badly wounded in the explosion.; Harry was wounded on his leg.

records.definition_text: to cover someone with material in order to protect them
records.learnerexamples_text: She wrapped the baby in a blanket.; He wrapped a towel around his shoulders.; After a few seconds I gathered my wits and wrapped the towel around myself again.

records.definition_text: to cover or surround something with paper, cloth or other material
records.learnerexamples_text: She wrapped the present and tied it with ribbon.; Wrap the chicken in foil and cook it for two hours.

records.base_text: wrap sth up or wrap up sth
records.definition_text: to fold paper, cloth, etc. around something to cover it
records.searchterms_text: wrap;wrap sth up or wrap up sth
records.learnerexamples_text: Have you wrapped up Jenny's present?; It was wrapped up in paper with a red ribbon.

records.definition_text: the part of the body between the hand and the arm
records.learnerexamples_text: I sprained my wrist playing squash.;  I fell [o]n [some] stair[s] and hurt my wrist.

records.definition_text: to create a book, story, article, etc. or a piece of music
records.learnerexamples_text: He's writing a book on Colombia.; She writes for Time magazine.; Walton wrote the Cello Concerto in 1956.; Stephen King wrote this book.

records.definition_text: a person who writes books or articles to be published
records.learnerexamples_text: a travel/sports/fiction/crime writer; She is a well-known writer of children's books.; The last book I read was a true story written by a young South-American writer.

records.base_text: write sth down or write down sth
records.definition_text: to write something on a piece of paper so that you do not forget it
records.searchterms_text: write;write sth down or write down sth
records.learnerexamples_text: Did you write Jo's phone number down?; I wrote the address down and left the restaurant.

records.definition_text: the way that someone writes
records.learnerexamples_text: Do you recognise the writing on the envelope?

records.definition_text: the activity of creating pieces of written work, such as books, stories, poems, etc., or the written work of one person or a group of people
records.learnerexamples_text: I did a course in creative writing.; She is studying women's writing of the 1930s.; Black humo[u]r is a distinguishable feature of his writing.

records.definition_text: expressed in writing, or involving writing
records.learnerexamples_text: written instructions; a written exam; I would like you to tell me what subject you're teaching tomorrow and the pages of the homework, so I can do the written test [in the] next class.

records.definition_text: If something is wrong, there is a problem.
records.learnerexamples_text: You've been quiet all evening. Is there anything wrong?; What's wrong?; There's something wrong with my computer.; I didn't kn[o]w him, so I thought that there was something wrong.

records.definition_text: not considered morally acceptable by most people
records.learnerexamples_text: Children should be taught that violence is wrong.;  It is wrong to tell lies.; What's wrong with having a bit of fun?; To sum up, I think it is wrong to keep animals in zoos.

records.definition_text: not correctly
records.learnerexamples_text: It has been said - wrongly - that Americans hate government.; Equally, the point about 'staying' is erroneous: we stayed at Riverside Hotel instead of Hotel Astrid, [which] closed last year, [and] Hotel Royal [was] wrongly [described as having] 'special rates' for students.

records.definition_text: a photograph that shows the inside of your body
records.learnerexamples_text: They took an X-ray of his leg.; I was with my last patient trying to operate [on] his damage[d] tooth when I realized the X-Ray was on the wrong side and that I wasn't working on the damage[d] tooth.

records.definition_text: a boat with sails and sometimes an engine, used for either racing or travelling on for pleasure
records.learnerexamples_text: a luxury yacht; a yacht club; The class of boat that best fits my physical condition is the one called [S]nipe, that seems to be available at your yacht club.

records.definition_text: a unit of measurement equal to three feet or approximately 91.4 centimetres
records.learnerexamples_text: The garden is about 100 yards long.; I'm not a fitness maniac and I don't go to a shop which is 50 yards away from my house just to buy a newspaper, but if you go to school, why not go by bike[?]

records.definition_text: to take a deep breath with your mouth wide open, because you are tired or bored
records.learnerexamples_text: I can't stop yawning - I must be tired.; I think that the maths lesson is the most suitable one to be recorded. Watching ourselves yawning and nearly asleep would really reflect how boring maths [is].

records.definition_text: to shout something very loudly
records.learnerexamples_text: Our neighbours were yelling at each other this morning.; The child yelled out in pain.; "Just get out of here!" she yelled.; "Cut," yelled the director.

records.definition_text: a loud shout
records.learnerexamples_text: Suddenly there was a loud/great yell from the bathroom.; Suddenly a big yell came out of my throat.

records.definition_text: used to connect two words, phrases, or clauses when the second part adds something surprising to the first part
records.learnerexamples_text: simple yet effective; I agree it's unlikely, yet she knows what she's talking about.; It was huge and yet gracious.

records.definition_text: again after something has happened or been done many times before
records.learnerexamples_text: The bus was late yet again.; Tom, thank you so much yet again for your interest. This talk is very important to me and to count on you is an honour for our college.

records.definition_text: again after something has happened or been done many times before
records.learnerexamples_text: The bus was late yet again.; Tom, thank you so much yet again for your interest. This talk is very important to me and to count on you is an honour for our college.

records.definition_text: a set of exercises for the mind and body, based on the Hindu religion
records.learnerexamples_text: She does yoga three times a week. ; We do yoga in a heated room so we sweat a lot.

records.definition_text: used to emphasize what you are saying, or used before you start to talk about someone or something, or used as something to say while you are thinking what to say next
records.learnerexamples_text: I'm not stupid, you know!; You know the bookshop next to the bank? Well, it's closing down.; It's, you know, supposed to be a surprise on her birthday.

records.base_text: You must be joking!/ You're joking!
records.definition_text: something you say to show that you are surprised by what someone has said, or do not believe it is true
records.searchterms_text: joke;joked;jokes;joking;you must be joking!/ you're joking!;you must be joking/ you're joking
records.learnerexamples_text: "He spoke to me in French." "You're joking! Really?"; One television set in my house? You must be joking! We need four televisions!

records.definition_text: used to say that something could be possible although it does not seem likely
records.learnerexamples_text: You never know - you might win the lottery.; You never know, maybe I'll find something interesting and I'll change my point of view.

records.definition_text: belonging or relating to people generally
records.learnerexamples_text: Of course you want the best for your children.; Garlic is good for your blood.; Riding [a] bicycle is a good [way of maintaining] personal fitness and doesn't harm your health either.

records.definition_text: the first language that you learn
records.learnerexamples_text: French is his native tongue.; My native language is Russian but I speak English fluently and I have been learning Latin for two years.

records.definition_text: used to give special emphasis to the subject of the sentence
records.learnerexamples_text: If you yourself ever need help, would you know where to get it?; If you are thinking of taking it up yourself always do [a] warm-up exercise before you run, don't go too fast at the beginning, and don't overdo it.

records.definition_text: used when both the subject and object of the verb are 'you', and 'you' is also being used to refer to people generally
records.learnerexamples_text: You tell yourself everything's all right but you know it's not really.; You help yourself by doing some exercise.

records.definition_text: used to end a formal letter to someone whose name you do not know
records.learnerexamples_text: Yours faithfully, Katherine Smith; Yours faithfully, SAMSON LAM (READER)

records.definition_text: used to end a formal letter to someone whose name you do not know
records.learnerexamples_text: Yours faithfully, Katherine Smith; Yours faithfully, SAMSON LAM (READER)

records.definition_text: used at the end of formal letters where you know the name of the person you are writing to
records.learnerexamples_text: Yours sincerely, Emma Clarke.; I'm going to ask Tom for the [work] I will miss. Yours sincerely,

records.definition_text: used at the end of formal letters when you know the name of the person you are writing to
records.learnerexamples_text: Yours sincerely, Emma Clarke.; I'm going to ask Tom for the [work] I will miss. Yours sincerely,

records.definition_text: used to end a letter
records.learnerexamples_text: I look forward to hearing from you. Yours truly, Taylor Champinski.; Dear Clyde, . . . I hope my advice helps you [with] your decision. Yours truly,

records.definition_text: young people generally
records.learnerexamples_text: the youth of today; a youth club; Finally I decided to join a new youth club in my town.

records.definition_text: an African animal like a horse with black and white lines
records.learnerexamples_text: We saw a zebra in the distance.; Otherwise there would be many children and grown-ups who [would have] never seen an elephant, a tiger, a zebra etc.

records.definition_text: the temperature at which water freezes in degrees centigrade
records.learnerexamples_text: The temperature is expected to drop to ten degrees below zero tonight.; We have to learn that [it] is not natural for a lion [to live] in a country where, in winter, [the] temperature can fall below zero.

records.definition_text: a thing for fastening clothes, bags, etc. consisting of two rows of very small parts that connect together
records.learnerexamples_text: to do up/undo a zip; I can't open my bag - the zip has stuck.; Suddenly the zip of my new dress broke.

records.definition_text: an area where a particular thing happens, that is used for a particular purpose, or where there are particular rules
records.learnerexamples_text: an earthquake zone; a nuclear-free zone; He was charged with driving 75 mph in a 55 mph zone.; The UN Security Council has established a no-fly zone.; It is a very clean city with a lot of car-free zones.
